title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄序
庚午秋八月天下當復貢士
于鄉今
皇上龍飛之第二科也方
建元初屬大比期
皇上冀得真才任使首
詔下有司釐正文體諸不應經義
===
浮蔓者黜之天下士蒸蒸嚮
風至是復從禮官議申飭約
束而限之言法視昔加密矣
維時御史蒙詔奉
上命來按閩部祗承
德意惟慎惟虔乃博訪四方文學
之臣以禮聘機暨教授夏大
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄序

庚午秋八月，天下當復貢士于鄉，今皇上龍飛之第二科也。方建元初，屬大比期，皇上冀得真才任使，首詔下有司，釐正文體，諸不應經義、浮蔓者黜之。天下士蒸蒸嚮風。至是，復從禮官議，申飭約束，而限之言法，視昔加密矣。

維時，御史蒙詔奉上命來按閩部，祗承德意，惟慎惟虔，乃博訪四方文學之臣，以禮聘機暨教授夏大
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the gengwu year [1570], the time had come once again for the provinces throughout the empire to recommend scholars through the Provincial Examination. This was the second examination cycle since His Majesty ascended the throne. At the beginning of his reign, the triennial examination fell due. Hoping to obtain men of genuine talent to employ in service, His Majesty first issued an edict to the responsible authorities to rectify literary style: writings that failed to accord with the meaning of the classics or were superficial and verbose were to be rejected. Scholars throughout the empire responded with growing enthusiasm. Now, following further deliberations by the ritual officials, the regulations were reiterated and reinforced, and restrictions imposed on expression; these were more exacting than before.

At this time, Censor Meng Zhao came by imperial command to inspect Fujian. Reverently receiving His Majesty’s benevolent intentions, he proceeded with utmost care and devotion. He sought widely among officials of literary learning from all quarters and courteously invited me, Ji, together with Instructor Xia Da…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
勳爲考試官敎授吳希旦學
正黃自任龍養性敎諭李明
通王汝振朱繼魯趙友仁許
嘉榮爲同考試官各以其經
至屆期以左布政使陳典右
布政使周賢宣司提調按察
使陳一松僉事王圻司監試
===
其餘百執事咸慎遴以充而
御史寔監臨焉御史率諸大
夫文學集于庭揚觶矢言曰
上臣事君以人舉非其人惟
爾不任如人臣之義何諸大
夫文學罔不懍懍改色惕慮
而後卽事於是進提學副使
punctuated:
勳爲考試官，敎授吳希旦、學正黃自任、龍養性、敎諭李明通、王汝振、朱繼魯、趙友仁、許嘉榮爲同考試官，各以其經至。屆期，以左布政使陳典、右布政使周賢宣司提調，按察使陳一松、僉事王圻司監試。其餘百執事，咸慎遴以充，而御史寔監臨焉。
御史率諸大夫文學集于庭，揚觶矢言曰：「上臣事君以人，舉非其人，惟爾不任，如人臣之義何？」諸大夫文學罔不懍懍改色惕慮，而後卽事。於是進提學副使
translation_en:
…Xia Daxun as Examiner; Wu Xidan, Instructor in a prefectural school; Huang Ziren and Long Yangxing, Instructors in subprefectural schools; and Li Mingtong, Wang Ruzhen, Zhu Jilu, Zhao Youren, and Xu Jiarong, Instructors in county schools, were appointed Associate Examiners. Each came to examine in his respective Classic. When the appointed time arrived, Chen Dian, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Zhou Xianxuan, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, were assigned to serve as Proctors; Chen Yisong, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Wang Qi, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, were assigned to oversee the examination. All the remaining functionaries were carefully selected for their posts, while the Censor himself served as Supervising Official.
The Censor led the assembled officials and scholars into the courtyard. Raising a ceremonial wine cup, he solemnly declared: “The highest ministers serve their sovereign by recommending worthy men. If you recommend unsuitable men, you yourselves are unfit for your responsibilities. How would that accord with a minister’s duty?” Every official and scholar grew solemn, changed countenance, and reflected anxiously; only then did they take up their duties. Thereupon they admitted those selected by the Vice Surveillance Commissioner for Education…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
周弘祖所選士二千七百有
奇三試之登其雋者九十人
并梓其文以
獻
制也機以職事當僭言于首簡機
聞之易曰君子藏器於身待
時而動夫士伏處嵓巖之下
===
冥摉墳典誦法孔孟席珍以
待聘孰不思表見所志徼尺
寸之功於當世哉然而出潛
遘會有時存焉時不可强也
是故君子恥懷寶以傲世而
亦不能違時以就功尺蠖附
於飛龍蒼蠅致乎千里時也
punctuated:
周弘祖所選士二千七百有奇，三試之，登其雋者九十人，并梓其文以獻，制也。
機以職事當僭言于首簡。機聞之，《易》曰：「君子藏器於身，待時而動。」夫士伏處嵓巖之下，冥摉墳典，誦法孔孟，席珍以待聘，孰不思表見所志，徼尺寸之功於當世哉？然而出潛遘會，有時存焉，時不可强也。是故君子恥懷寶以傲世，而亦不能違時以就功。尺蠖附於飛龍，蒼蠅致乎千里，時也。
translation_en:
…the more than 2,700 scholars selected by Zhou Hongzu were examined in three sessions, and ninety of the most outstanding were placed on the successful list. Their writings were also printed from woodblocks for presentation to the throne, as prescribed by established regulations.
By virtue of my official duties, I, Ji, must presume to offer some words on the opening pages. I have heard it said in the Book of Changes: “The gentleman keeps his abilities within himself and waits for the proper time to act.” Scholars dwell in seclusion among the crags, searching deeply into ancient books and classics, reciting and taking as their models Confucius and Mencius, and treasuring their learning as they await an invitation to serve. Who among them does not wish to make his aspirations manifest and seek to accomplish even some small service in the world of his day? Yet emerging from seclusion and encountering an opportunity depend upon the proper time, and that time cannot be forced. Thus the gentleman is ashamed to hoard his treasures and disdain the world, yet neither can he act against the times to achieve success. An inchworm clings to a flying dragon; a fly is carried a thousand li: it is opportunity that makes this possible.

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
我
皇上聖神天縱
嗣登寶曆
總乾綱
親儒碩
從言速於轉圜
求賢徵於夢賚野無佚才
===
朝無素飽
仁恩所被薄海內外罔不磅礴四
塞
文明熈洽之運誠千載而一時也
夫時者士之所遭所以利見
展錯以顯洩其平生之藏者
也諸士際斯時應賢科之選
punctuated:
我皇上聖神天縱，嗣登寶曆，總乾綱，親儒碩，從言速於轉圜，求賢徵於夢賚，野無佚才，朝無素飽。仁恩所被，薄海內外，罔不磅礴四塞。文明熈洽之運，誠千載而一時也。
夫時者，士之所遭，所以利見展錯，以顯洩其平生之藏者也。諸士際斯時，應賢科之選，
translation_en:
Our Emperor, endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom and divine understanding, has succeeded to the imperial throne. He holds the sovereign reins and draws eminent Confucian scholars close to him. He accepts counsel more swiftly than a ball turns, and his search for worthy men finds its token in a dream-bestowed gift. No talent remains overlooked in the countryside, and none at court eats without earning his keep. Wherever his benevolence and grace extend, throughout the realm and beyond its shores, they spread abundantly in every direction. This age of flourishing culture and harmonious prosperity is truly an opportunity encountered but once in a thousand years.
An opportune time is what a scholar encounters: it enables him advantageously to appear in public life and put his abilities into practice, bringing forth what he has stored up throughout his life. You scholars have met with such a time and answered the call for selection through the examination for worthy men …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
策名
天府揚于王路其所遭甚偉乃
其所素具先資以成信者則
何以哉機謬從諸文學後縱
觀閩士所爲文其指遠其詞
達其言必稱先王其揆事曲
而中其上下今古博雅而裁
===
蔚乎華國之昌言一陶鎔
聖化而軌于正者也機亟讀亟收
之以告御史使偕計吏誠器
之矣而諸士其何以器于世
乎夫天球河圖寶刀大弓商
彝周鼎薦清廟侈國寶天下
之珍器□上也其次若簠簋
punctuated: 策名天府，揚于王路，其所遭甚偉。乃其所素具，先資以成信者，則何以哉？機謬從諸文學後，縱觀閩士所爲文，其指遠，其詞達，其言必稱先王，其揆事曲而中，其上下今古，博雅而裁，蔚乎華國之昌言，一陶鎔聖化而軌于正者也。機亟讀亟收之，以告御史，使偕計吏，誠器之矣。而諸士其何以器于世乎？夫天球、河圖、寶刀、大弓、商彝、周鼎，薦清廟，侈國寶，天下之珍器□上也。其次若簠簋
translation_en:
…to have their names inscribed in the celestial repository and to rise upon the royal path: magnificent indeed is the opportunity they have encountered. Yet what have they long possessed that first furnished the basis for establishing their credibility [?]? I, Ji, have undeservedly followed in the company of learned men and have surveyed the writings of the scholars of Fujian. Their purport is far-reaching, their expression lucid; their words invariably invoke the former kings. Their assessment of affairs is finely discriminating and apt; they range through past and present with broad learning, elegance, and discernment. These splendid pronouncements bring lustre to the realm: all have been moulded by the sage ruler’s transforming influence and brought onto the proper course. I, Ji, eagerly read and selected them, reporting them to the Censor so that these scholars might accompany the tribute officials to the capital. Truly, I have esteemed them as worthy vessels. Yet how will these scholars serve as useful vessels in the world?
Consider the celestial jade sphere, the River Chart, the treasured blade, the great bow, the ritual vessels of Shang, and the cauldrons of Zhou. Presented in the pure ancestral temple, they enhance the splendour of the state’s treasures and rank highest [?; one character illegible] among the precious vessels of the world. Next come such vessels as the fu and gui for sacrificial grain…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
卮匜筐筥鬵鍑爲品不同皆
可以適世用而敝帚鉛刀則
視之爲贅物矣夫士之器亦
有類乎是者是不可以不辨
也機之執策進諸士也始而
喜已而大懼何也機駑槧士
也幸而與於校士之役又幸
===
而祗役於閩閩才藪也羣千
百士之秀焉拔其尤茲人文
之極選也藉是可以報
天子矣故喜抑機之所以進諸士
也文也文可以信諸士乎否
也今天下之士習偽矣緣飾
詩書以游言譁衆者其詞理
punctuated: 卮、匜、筐、筥、鬵、鍑，爲品不同，皆可以適世用，而敝帚、鉛刀則視之爲贅物矣。夫士之器亦有類乎是者，是不可以不辨也。機之執策進諸士也，始而喜，已而大懼，何也？機，駑槧士也，幸而與於校士之役，又幸而祗役於閩。閩，才藪也，羣千百士之秀焉，拔其尤，茲人文之極選也。藉是可以報天子矣，故喜。抑機之所以進諸士也，文也。文可以信諸士乎？否也。今天下之士習偽矣，緣飾詩書以游言譁衆者，其詞理
translation_en:
…cups, pouring vessels, square and round baskets, cauldrons and cooking pots differ in kind, yet all can serve practical needs in the world; a worn-out broom or a leaden knife, however, is regarded as a useless encumbrance. The capacities of scholars likewise resemble these things, and one must distinguish among them.

When I, Ji 機, took up the examination scripts to advance these scholars, I was at first delighted, but afterward greatly afraid. Why? I am a plodding man of letters [?], fortunate to have participated in the work of examining scholars, and fortunate again to have discharged this duty in Fujian. Fujian is a gathering place of talent. To assemble the outstanding men among its hundreds and thousands of scholars and select the very best is to make the choicest selection of literary talent. Through this I could repay the Emperor; hence my delight.

Yet the means by which I advanced these scholars was their writing. Can their writing establish their trustworthiness? No. Nowadays scholars throughout the realm are practiced in deception. Those who embellish their words with the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, using glib discourse to impress the crowd—their language is coherent…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
綴緝纖華以詭世巧售者其
詞澤剽竊異端以隱義誑俗
者其詞奥若是者皆足以炫
有司之目而或未之辨焉機
所以鰓鰓焉懼也嗟乎三代
而下取士代更自科目之制
起俶儻魁壘之佐鮮不羔鴈
===
於文藝文之貴乎世也久矣
自夫士以僞售於是庸之而
違試之罔功則雖雕龍吐鳳
燁然照世無裨實用君子弗
尚也諸士既裒然以文舉矣
由是而砥節礪躬亮工楨
國于以樹俶儻魁壘之烈光助
punctuated: 綴緝纖華以詭世巧售者，其詞澤；剽竊異端以隱義誑俗者，其詞奥。若是者，皆足以炫有司之目，而或未之辨焉，機所以鰓鰓焉懼也。嗟乎！三代而下，取士代更。自科目之制起，俶儻魁壘之佐，鮮不羔鴈於文藝。文之貴乎世也久矣！自夫士以僞售，於是庸之而違，試之罔功，則雖雕龍吐鳳，燁然照世，無裨實用，君子弗尚也。諸士既裒然以文舉矣，由是而砥節礪躬，亮工楨國，于以樹俶儻魁壘之烈，光助
translation_en:
…Those who stitch together delicate embellishments to deceive the world and artfully gain acceptance have polished diction; those who plagiarize heterodox teachings to obscure right principles and beguile ordinary people have abstruse diction. All such writings can dazzle the eyes of the responsible officials, who may fail to discern their true nature. This is why I, Ji, am so anxiously afraid.

Alas! Since the Three Dynasties, methods of selecting officials have changed from age to age. Since the examination system arose, scarcely any outstanding and imposing minister has been recruited with ceremonial gifts except through literary accomplishment. Literature has long been prized in the world! Yet once scholars gain acceptance through deception, they prove wanting when employed and achieve nothing when put to the test. Though their writing may carve dragons and utter phoenixes, brilliantly illuminating the world, it contributes nothing to practical service, and the gentleman does not esteem it.

You scholars have now distinguished yourselves and been selected through your writing. Proceed from this to temper your integrity and discipline yourselves, discharge your duties faithfully and serve as pillars of the state, thereby establishing outstanding and imposing achievements and lending lustrous support to…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
太平施令聞無窮不亦偉乎是
又安可讓也夫閩奠在南服
山海之奧區也靈氣鬱發人
文昭宣爰稽往牒才哲項背
相望而龜山延平考亭數先
生者又以身任濂洛道統之
傳析微闡晦六經於是大明
===
今之緝藻橫塾褒衣膠序者
孰不嚌其菁華而窺其堂奧
其淵源蓋與海內學士異矣
夫求珠赤水斲玉崑崙市駿
大宛他郡國非無是三者而
必於赤水崑崙大宛乎稱焉
則其產良也道南一脈比跡
punctuated:
太平，施令聞無窮，不亦偉乎？是又安可讓也？夫閩奠在南服，山海之奧區也。靈氣鬱發，人文昭宣。爰稽往牒，才哲項背相望，而龜山、延平、考亭數先生者，又以身任濂洛道統之傳，析微闡晦，六經於是大明。

今之緝藻橫塾、褒衣膠序者，孰不嚌其菁華而窺其堂奧？其淵源蓋與海內學士異矣。夫求珠赤水，斲玉崑崙，市駿大宛，他郡國非無是三者，而必於赤水、崑崙、大宛乎稱焉，則其產良也。道南一脈，比跡
translation_en:
…great peace and spread a good reputation without end: would this not be magnificent? How, then, could one yield this responsibility to others? Min lies firmly in the southern domains, a region of secluded mountains and seas. Its spiritual vitality flourishes abundantly, and its cultural achievements shine forth. Examining the records of the past, we find talented and wise men following one another in close succession. Moreover, such masters as Guishan, Yanping, and Kaoting personally undertook to transmit the orthodox succession of the Way from Lian and Luo. They elucidated subtleties and brought obscurities to light, so that the Six Classics became fully understood.

Among those today who weave literary embellishments in the schools [?] and wear broad scholarly robes in the academies, who has not tasted these masters’ finest essence and glimpsed the inner chambers of their learning? The sources of their learning surely differ from those of scholars elsewhere in the realm. Now, one seeks pearls in Chishui, works jade from Kunlun, and buys fine steeds in Dayuan. It is not that other regions lack these three things; yet Chishui, Kunlun, and Dayuan are invariably named in connection with them because their products are excellent. The lineage of the Way transmitted southward, following in the footsteps of…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
鄒魯非閩產邪諸士挾所產
之良以售于有司有司採而
進之以應
聖世之求譬之沒赤水之淵陟崑
崙之巔涉大宛之澤百珍千
騎畢陳於前殫精竭智惟瓌
瑋奇麗是收而其贋且似者
棄之若土苴勿顧也於乎盛
矣諸士出而珪璋治世驅騁
千里使天下後世指以爲隋
珠卞璧龍媒然而終免於贋
且似焉之誚有司藉以休榮
渥甚機之懼可少釋也已唐
陸贄有言上不負天子下不
punctuated: 鄒魯，非閩產邪？諸士挾所產之良，以售于有司；有司採而進之，以應聖世之求。譬之沒赤水之淵，陟崑崙之巔，涉大宛之澤，百珍千騎畢陳於前，殫精竭智，惟瓌瑋奇麗是收，而其贋且似者，棄之若土苴，勿顧也。於乎，盛矣！諸士出而珪璋治世，驅騁千里，使天下後世指以爲隋珠、卞璧、龍媒，然而終免於贋且似焉之誚。有司藉以休榮渥甚，機之懼可少釋也已。唐陸贄有言：「上不負天子，下不
translation_en:
…Zou and Lu—does this not originate in Fujian? These scholars bring the excellence native to their land to offer to the responsible officials, who select and advance them to answer the needs of this sagely age. It is like plunging into the depths of the Chishui, ascending the summit of Kunlun, or traversing the marshes of Dayuan: a hundred treasures and a thousand steeds are all arrayed before one. Exhausting our concentration and judgment, we accept only what is magnificent, extraordinary, rare, and beautiful; counterfeits and mere look-alikes we discard like dirt and straw, without another glance. Ah, how splendid!

When these scholars go forth, serving the well-governed age as precious jade tablets and galloping a thousand li, may all the world and later generations point to them as the pearl of Sui, the jade disc of Bian, and dragon steeds, and may they forever escape the reproach of being counterfeits or mere look-alikes. The responsible officials would thereby receive abundant glory and honor, and my own apprehensions—I, Ji—might be somewhat relieved. Lu Zhi of the Tang said: “Above, do not fail the Son of Heaven; below, do not…”

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
負所學斯言古今韙之爾諸
士淑艾儒先兢兢於當世之
務則既學之素矣當
文明熙洽之朝抱其器以出行列
明廷交戟之下
聖天子將器其才而使之諸士其
厚自重惜以仰答
===
當宁以懋揚其素所蘊蓄者乎詩
曰藹藹王多吉士維君子使
媚于天子媚于天子而後可
以稱不負矣諸士勗諸是役
也提督巡撫右僉都御史何
寛輯寧疆宇文敎弘敷前提
督南贛今巡撫湖廣右僉都
punctuated:
負所學。」斯言古今韙之。爾諸士淑艾儒先，兢兢於當世之務，則既學之素矣。當文明熙洽之朝，抱其器以出，行列明廷交戟之下，聖天子將器其才而使之。諸士其厚自重惜，以仰答當宁，以懋揚其素所蘊蓄者乎！詩曰：「藹藹王多吉士，維君子使，媚于天子。」媚于天子而後可以稱不負矣。諸士勗諸！

是役也，提督巡撫右僉都御史何寛，輯寧疆宇，文敎弘敷；前提督南贛、今巡撫湖廣右僉都
translation_en:
…fail what one has learned.” These words have been esteemed as right in ancient times and today. You gentlemen have been nurtured by earlier Confucian scholars and have applied yourselves conscientiously to the affairs of the present age: this is already the foundation of your learning. In a reign of cultural brilliance, prosperity, and harmony, you will bring forth your abilities and take your places beneath the crossed halberds of the illustrious court. The sagely Son of Heaven will employ you according to your talents. You gentlemen should hold yourselves in the highest regard and cherish your worth, thereby answering the sovereign’s favor and fully displaying what you have long cultivated within yourselves! The Book of Odes says: “Abundant indeed are the king’s many worthy men; they are gentlemen fit for employment, pleasing to the Son of Heaven.” Only after pleasing the Son of Heaven can you be said not to have failed him. Exert yourselves, gentlemen!

For this examination, He Kuan, Supreme Commander, Grand Coordinator, and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, brought peace and concord to the territory and widely extended literary education. The former Supreme Commander of Nan-Gan, now Grand Coordinator of Huguang and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
御史張翀風敎丕宣章縫仰
止今提督南贛右僉都御史
殷從儉憲令初頒士心聿勸
鎮守總兵官署都督同知李
錫揚威茂績雅意尚文左參
政熊琦右參政顧問副使陳
紹登黃宸參議劉志伊李紀
===
僉事蘇愚徐作王錫命顧養
謙副總兵官仍管參將事張
元勳遊擊將軍金科署都指
揮僉事狄從夏朱玨王克振
白瀚紀田義咸贊襄于外弼
成
盛典副使柴淶則以遷秩行亦始
punctuated: 御史張翀，風敎丕宣，章縫仰止。今提督南贛右僉都御史殷從儉，憲令初頒，士心聿勸。鎮守總兵官署都督同知李錫，揚威茂績，雅意尚文。左參政熊琦、右參政顧問、副使陳紹登、黃宸、參議劉志伊、李紀、僉事蘇愚、徐作、王錫命、顧養謙、副總兵官仍管參將事張元勳、遊擊將軍金科、署都指揮僉事狄從夏、朱玨、王克振、白瀚、紀田義，咸贊襄于外，弼成盛典。副使柴淶則以遷秩行，亦始
translation_en:
…Censor Zhang Chong broadly spread moral instruction, and the scholars looked up to him. Yin Congjian, the present Supreme Commander of Nan-Gan and Right Assistant Censor-in-chief, had only just promulgated his directives, yet scholars were already encouraged. Li Xi, the Regional Commander stationed here and Acting Vice Commissioner-in-chief, displayed military might and achieved distinguished results; his cultivated inclinations favored literary learning.

Xiong Qi, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; Gu Wen, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; Chen Shaodeng and Huang Chen, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Liu Zhiyi and Li Ji, Administration Assistant Commissioners; Su Yu, Xu Zuo, Wang Ximing, and Gu Yangqian, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; Zhang Yuanxun, Vice Regional Commander, concurrently administering the duties of Assistant Regional Commander; Jin Ke, Mobile Corps Commander; and Di Congxia, Zhu Jue, Wang Kezhen, Bai Han, and Ji Tianyi, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners—all provided support from outside the examination compound and helped bring this grand ceremony to completion. Surveillance Vice Commissioner Chai Lai departed upon promotion, but also, at the outset…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
隆慶四年福建鄉試
監臨官
巡按福建監察御史蒙詔〔廷綸廣東番禺縣人壬戌進士〕
提調官
福建等處承宣布政使司左布政使陳典〔子厚保定中衛中所人庚戌進士〕
福建等處承宣布政使司右布政使周賢宣〔仲含江西萬安縣人癸丑進士〕
監試官

===

河南汝寧府儒學敎授帥機〔惟審江西臨川縣人戊辰進士〕
直隸松江府儒學敎授夏大勳〔謙甫廣東饒平縣人丙午貢士〕
同考試官
江西南昌府儒學敎授吳希旦〔左卿直隸歙縣人壬子貢士〕
山東青州府莒州儒學學正黃自任〔伊吾湖廣黃岡縣人乙卯貢士〕
直隸蘇州府太倉州儒學學正龍養性〔順甫江西吉水縣人甲子貢士〕
河南河南府登封縣儒學敎諭李明通〔貞守雲南石屏州人壬子貢士〕
浙江紹興府諸曁縣儒學敎諭王汝振〔憐甫江西安福縣人戊午貢士〕
punctuated:
隆慶四年福建鄉試。

監臨官：巡按福建監察御史蒙詔〔廷綸，廣東番禺縣人，壬戌進士〕。

提調官：福建等處承宣布政使司左布政使陳典〔子厚，保定中衛中所人，庚戌進士〕。福建等處承宣布政使司右布政使周賢宣〔仲含，江西萬安縣人，癸丑進士〕。

監試官：福建等處提刑按察司按察使陳一松〔宗岩，廣東海陽縣人，丁未進士〕。福建等處提刑按察司僉事王圻〔元翰，直隸上海縣籍，嘉定縣人，乙丑進士〕。

考試官：河南汝寧府儒學敎授帥機〔惟審，江西臨川縣人，戊辰進士〕。直隸松江府儒學敎授夏大勳〔謙甫，廣東饒平縣人，丙午貢士〕。

同考試官：江西南昌府儒學敎授吳希旦〔左卿，直隸歙縣人，壬子貢士〕。山東青州府莒州儒學學正黃自任〔伊吾，湖廣黃岡縣人，乙卯貢士〕。直隸蘇州府太倉州儒學學正龍養性〔順甫，江西吉水縣人，甲子貢士〕。河南河南府登封縣儒學敎諭李明通〔貞守，雲南石屏州人，壬子貢士〕。浙江紹興府諸曁縣儒學敎諭王汝振〔憐甫，江西安福縣人，戊午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Fujian Provincial Examination, fourth year of Longqing (1570).

Supervising Official:
Meng Zhao, Investigating Censor on inspection duty in Fujian, courtesy name Tinglun, was from Panyu County, Guangdong, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the renxu year.

Proctors:
Chen Dian, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Fujian, courtesy name Zihou, was from the Central Battalion of Baoding Central Guard and a metropolitan graduate of the gengxu year.
Zhou Xianxuan, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Fujian, courtesy name Zhonghan, was from Wan'an County, Jiangxi, and a metropolitan graduate of the guichou year.

Examination Monitoring Officials:
Chen Yisong, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian, courtesy name Zongyan, was from Haiyang County, Guangdong, and a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.
Wang Qi, Assistant Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian, courtesy name Yuanhan, was registered in Shanghai County, Zhili, and originally from Jiading County. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.

Examiners:
Shuai Ji, Professor of the Confucian School of Runing Prefecture, Henan, courtesy name Weishen, was from Linchuan County, Jiangxi, and a metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.
Xia Daxun, Professor of the Confucian School of Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Qianfu, was from Raoping County, Guangdong, and a tribute student (gongshi) of the bingwu year.

Associate Examiners:
Wu Xidan, Professor of the Confucian School of Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, courtesy name Zuoqing, was from She County, Zhili, and a tribute student of the renzi year.
Huang Ziren, Instructor of the Confucian School of Ju Subprefecture, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, courtesy name Yiwu, was from Huanggang County, Huguang, and a tribute student of the yimao year.
Long Yangxing, Instructor of the Confucian School of Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Shunfu, was from Jishui County, Jiangxi, and a tribute student of the jiazi year.
Li Mingtong, Instructor of the Confucian School of Dengfeng County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, courtesy name Zhenshou, was from Shiping Subprefecture, Yunnan, and a tribute student of the renzi year.
Wang Ruzhen, Instructor of the Confucian School of Zhuji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, courtesy name Lianfu, was from Anfu County, Jiangxi, and a tribute student of the wuwu year.

punctuated:

translation_en:

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
福州府同知張敏德〔遜時江西萬安縣人己未進士〕
泉州府同知丁一中〔少鶴直隸丹陽縣人監生〕
漳州府同知李畿嗣〔明卿湖廣蘄水縣人壬戌進士〕
福州府推官李一中〔時卿直隸建德縣人戊辰進士〕
彌封官
汀州府同知賀幼殊〔子英湖廣湘鄉縣人壬子貢士〕
泉州府通判陳嘉謨〔益卿湖廣湘鄉縣人己酉貢士〕
泉州府推官李燾〔若臨廣東河源縣人戊辰進士〕
福州府長樂縣知縣蔣以忠〔伯孝直隸常熟縣人戊辰進士〕
===
建寧府甌寧縣知縣羅徵竹〔庭猗江西吉水縣人戊辰進士〕
建寧府崇安縣知縣余乾貞〔秉智浙江遂安縣人戊辰進士〕
興化府仙遊縣知縣關玉成〔少抑廣東南海縣人辛酉貢士〕
謄錄官
建寧府同知周祈〔敬仲湖廣蘄州人壬子貢士〕
興化府推官邵城〔惟衛浙江鄞縣人戊辰進士〕
福州府閩縣知縣許子良〔直夫浙江仁和縣人戊辰進士〕
福州府候官縣知縣詹世用〔汝賢江西弋陽縣人戊辰進士〕
福州府福清縣知縣陳大猷〔鳴翊廣東南海縣人戊辰進士〕
punctuated:
福州府同知張敏德〔遜時，江西萬安縣人，己未進士〕。泉州府同知丁一中〔少鶴，直隸丹陽縣人，監生〕。漳州府同知李畿嗣〔明卿，湖廣蘄水縣人，壬戌進士〕。福州府推官李一中〔時卿，直隸建德縣人，戊辰進士〕。

汀州府同知賀幼殊〔子英，湖廣湘鄉縣人，壬子貢士〕。泉州府通判陳嘉謨〔益卿，湖廣湘鄉縣人，己酉貢士〕。泉州府推官李燾〔若臨，廣東河源縣人，戊辰進士〕。福州府長樂縣知縣蔣以忠〔伯孝，直隸常熟縣人，戊辰進士〕。建寧府甌寧縣知縣羅徵竹〔庭猗，江西吉水縣人，戊辰進士〕。建寧府崇安縣知縣余乾貞〔秉智，浙江遂安縣人，戊辰進士〕。興化府仙遊縣知縣關玉成〔少抑，廣東南海縣人，辛酉貢士〕。

謄錄官：

translation_en:

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
君子學以致其道
知遠之近知風之自知微之顯
孟子曰言近而指遠者善言也守約而施
博者善道也君子之言也不下帶而道
存焉君子之守脩其身而天下平
易
象曰天行健君子以自彊不息
===
惠我德大得志也
夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業也知崇禮卑
崇效天卑法地
天地之大德曰生聖人之大寶曰位
書
帝曰夔命汝典樂教胄子直而温寬而栗
剛而無虐簡而無傲詩言志歌永言聲
依永律和聲八音克諧無相奪倫神人
以和
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

君子學以致其道。

知遠之近，知風之自，知微之顯。

孟子曰：「言近而指遠者，善言也；守約而施博者，善道也。君子之言也，不下帶而道存焉。君子之守，脩其身而天下平。」

易

象曰：「天行健，君子以自彊不息。」

惠我德，大得志也。

夫易，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。

天地之大德曰生，聖人之大寶曰位。

書

帝曰：「夔，命汝典樂，教胄子，直而温，寬而栗，剛而無虐，簡而無傲。詩言志，歌永言，聲依永，律和聲。八音克諧，無相奪倫，神人以和。」
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The gentleman learns in order to realize his Way.

Know how what is distant lies in what is near; know whence the wind comes; know how what is subtle becomes manifest.

Mencius said: “Words that are close at hand yet point far afield are good words. Holding to what is concise yet applying it broadly is a good Way. The gentleman’s words do not go below his sash, yet the Way is present in them. What the gentleman holds to is cultivating his own person, and thereby all under Heaven is brought to peace.”

Book of Changes

The Commentary on the Images says: “Heaven moves with vigor; the gentleman accordingly strengthens himself without cease.”

“They cherish my virtue”: this means fully attaining one’s aspirations.

The Changes is that by which the sages exalt their virtue and extend their undertakings. Knowledge is lofty; ritual is humble. What is lofty emulates Heaven; what is humble takes Earth as its model.

The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called giving life; the great treasure of the sage is called his position.

Book of Documents

The emperor said: “Kui, I command you to take charge of music and instruct the sons of the nobility to be upright yet gentle, broad-minded yet dignified, firm without being harsh, and straightforward without being arrogant. Poetry expresses intent; song prolongs the words; the tones follow their prolongation; the pitch standards harmonize the tones. When the eight kinds of musical instruments can sound in harmony without disrupting one another’s proper order, spirits and human beings are thereby brought into harmony.”

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
沿于江海達于淮泗
俾萬姓咸曰大哉王言又曰一哉王心
徽柔懿恭懷保小民惠鮮鰥寡自朝至于
日中昃不遑暇食用咸和萬民
詩
七月在野八月在宇九月在戶
駕彼四牡四牡奕奕赤芾金舄會同有繹
鳳凰于飛翽翽其羽亦集爰止藹藹王多
吉士維君子使媚于天子鳳凰于飛翽
===
翽其羽亦傅于天藹藹王多吉人維君
子命媚于庶人鳳凰鳴矣于彼高岡梧
桐生矣于彼朝陽菶菶萋萋雝雝喈喈
有秩斯祜申錫無疆
春秋
春王正月公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯
許男曹伯侵蔡蔡潰遂伐楚次于陘〔僖公四年〕
冬公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒
子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子
punctuated:
沿于江海，達于淮泗。
俾萬姓咸曰：「大哉王言！」又曰：「一哉王心！」
徽柔懿恭，懷保小民，惠鮮鰥寡，自朝至于日中昃，不遑暇食，用咸和萬民。

詩
七月在野，八月在宇，九月在戶。
駕彼四牡，四牡奕奕。赤芾金舄，會同有繹。
鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦集爰止。藹藹王多吉士，維君子使，媚于天子。鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦傅于天。藹藹王多吉人，維君子命，媚于庶人。鳳凰鳴矣，于彼高岡。梧桐生矣，于彼朝陽。菶菶萋萋，雝雝喈喈。
有秩斯祜，申錫無疆。

春秋
春，王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡。蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。〔僖公四年〕
冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子
translation_en:
…Proceed along the Yangzi River and the sea, reaching the Huai and Si rivers.
Let all the people say, “Great are the king’s words!” And again, “Undivided is the king’s heart!”
Admirably gentle and nobly reverent, he cherished and protected the common people and showed kindness to the widowed and bereft. From morning until the sun declined past noon, he had no leisure to eat; thus he brought all the people into harmony.

Book of Odes
In the seventh month, [the crickets] are in the fields; in the eighth month, beneath the eaves; in the ninth month, at the door.
They harness those four stallions; the four stallions are splendid. In red knee-aprons and gold-adorned shoes, they attend the assemblies in an unbroken succession.
The phoenixes fly, their wings rustling; they gather here and alight. In abundant array, the king has many worthy officers. These gentlemen he employs, and they are dear to the Son of Heaven. The phoenixes fly, their wings rustling; they rise to the heavens. In abundant array, the king has many worthy men. These gentlemen he commissions, and they are dear to the common people. The phoenixes call upon that high ridge. The wutong trees grow on its sun-facing slope. Luxuriant and flourishing are the trees; harmonious and clear are the birds’ calls.
Abundant is this blessing, bestowed again without limit.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the Duke [of Lu] joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao in invading Cai. Cai collapsed. They then attacked Chu and encamped at Xing. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕
In winter, the Duke [of Lu] joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi 杞, the Viscount of Xiao Zhu, and the heir apparent of Qi 齊…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
光伐鄭十有二月巳亥同盟于戲〔襄公〕
〔九年〕夏公會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷
〔定公十年〕
六月齊侯來獻戎捷〔莊公三十有一年〕
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕夏曹公孫會
自鄭出奔宋〔昭公二十年〕
五月公及諸侯盟于皐鼬〔定公四年〕
禮記
本仁以聚之播樂以安之
===
詩云肅雝和鳴先祖是聽夫肅肅敬也雝
雝和也夫敬以和何事不行
子曰君子不以辭盡人故天下有道則行
有枝葉
孚尹旁達信也
第貳場
論
聖人一天人贊化育之道
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
punctuated:
光伐鄭。十有二月，巳亥，同盟于戲。〔襄公〕〔九年〕夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。〔定公十年〕
六月，齊侯來獻戎捷。〔莊公三十有一年〕
晉欒書帥師救鄭。〔成公六年〕夏，曹公孫會自鄭出奔宋。〔昭公二十年〕
五月，公及諸侯盟于皐鼬。〔定公四年〕
禮記
本仁以聚之，播樂以安之。
《詩》云：「肅雝和鳴，先祖是聽。」夫肅肅，敬也；雝雝，和也。夫敬以和，何事不行？
子曰：「君子不以辭盡人，故天下有道，則行有枝葉。」
孚尹旁達，信也。
第貳場
論
聖人一天人、贊化育之道。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
translation_en:
…Guang attacked Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the sihai day [?], they jointly entered into a covenant at Xi. 〔Duke Xiang〕〔Ninth year〕 In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu. 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding〕
In the sixth month, the Marquis of Qi came to present spoils of victory over the Rong. 〔Thirty-first year of Duke Zhuang〕
Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng. 〔Sixth year of Duke Cheng〕 In summer, Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Zheng to Song. 〔Twentieth year of Duke Zhao〕
In the fifth month, the duke and the feudal lords entered into a covenant at Gaoyou. 〔Fourth year of Duke Ding〕
Record of Rites
Take benevolence as the foundation for gathering the people together, and spread music to bring them peace.
The Book of Odes says: “Reverently and harmoniously they sing together; the ancestors listen.” Reverence signifies respect; harmony signifies concord. With respect and concord, what undertaking could fail?
The Master said: “The gentleman does not judge a person entirely by his words. Thus, when the Way prevails throughout the world, conduct has branches and leaves.”
The radiance of jade, extending in every direction, represents trustworthiness.
Second Session
Discourse
The way by which the sage unites Heaven and humanity and assists the transforming and nourishing processes of creation.
Imperial Edict, Patent of Appointment, and Memorial 〔One question from among these categories [?]〕

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔〔建元元年〕
擬唐以陸贄爲中書侍郎同平章事誥〔貞元八年〕
擬
大閱禮成廷臣
賀表
判語〔五條〕
官員赴任過限
===
監臨勢要中鹽
術士妄言禍福
承差轉雇寄人
軍民約會詞訟
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問帝王居萬民之上父天而爲之子則敬
天勤民豈非至重至重者哉敬天莫大
郊祀勤民莫大籍田往無論已
punctuated:
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔〔建元元年〕。
擬唐以陸贄爲中書侍郎同平章事誥〔貞元八年〕。
擬大閱禮成廷臣賀表。

判語〔五條〕
官員赴任過限。
監臨勢要中鹽。
術士妄言禍福。
承差轉雇寄人。
軍民約會詞訟。

第叁場
策〔五道〕
問：帝王居萬民之上，父天而爲之子，則敬天勤民，豈非至重至重者哉？敬天莫大郊祀，勤民莫大籍田，往無論已，
translation_en:
Compose a decree in the name of the Han emperor calling for the recommendation of men who are worthy and good, upright and correct, and who will speak frankly and remonstrate fearlessly. 〔First year of Jianyuan [140 BCE].〕
Compose a letter of appointment in the name of the Tang emperor appointing Lu Zhi as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery. 〔Eighth year of Zhenyuan [792].〕
Compose a congratulatory memorial from the court officials on the completion of the grand military review ceremony.

Legal judgments 〔Five cases〕
Officials exceeding the time limit for reporting to their posts.
Supervisory officials and influential persons obtaining salt trading licenses.
Practitioners of divination making unfounded predictions of misfortune and good fortune.
Persons assigned official duties hiring substitutes or entrusting the work to others [?].
Soldiers and commoners arranging to bring lawsuits jointly.

Third Session
Policy questions 〔Five questions〕
Question: Emperors and kings stand above the myriad people, regarding Heaven as their father and themselves as its sons. Are reverence for Heaven and diligent care for the people not, then, matters of the utmost, utmost importance? In revering Heaven, nothing is greater than the suburban sacrifices; in diligently caring for the people, nothing is greater than the ceremonial ploughing of the imperial field. Leaving earlier times aside, …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
國初
二立分祀後廼合今又分
耕籍先享先農初上祀今中祀初有配今無
配此其義必有在可得而聞與
太祖高皇帝卽位之初
勅禮官曰聖帝明王嚴於祭祀內致誠敬外致
儀文他日
諭羣臣曰耕籍古禮也朕卽位以來恒舉行之
惟欲使民盡力於田畝以遂生養非事虛文
===
也則我
太祖之所以敬
天勤民殆有出於禮文之外者
聖子
神孫世守無失傳至
世宗肅皇帝
首正郊祀
躬耕籍田
欽天有頌
punctuated: 國初，二立分祀，後廼合，今又分。耕籍先享先農，初上祀，今中祀；初有配，今無配。此其義必有在，可得而聞與？太祖高皇帝卽位之初，勅禮官曰：「聖帝明王嚴於祭祀，內致誠敬，外致儀文。」他日，諭羣臣曰：「耕籍，古禮也。朕卽位以來，恒舉行之，惟欲使民盡力於田畝，以遂生養，非事虛文也。」則我太祖之所以敬天勤民，殆有出於禮文之外者。聖子神孫，世守無失，傳至世宗肅皇帝，首正郊祀，躬耕籍田，欽天有頌。
translation_en:
At the beginning of the dynasty, the two were established for separate worship [?]; later they were combined, and now they are separate again. Before ploughing the imperial ritual field, sacrifice is offered to the First Farmer. Initially this ranked as a major sacrifice; now it is a medium sacrifice. Initially there was an associated recipient of sacrifice; now there is none. There must be a rationale for these arrangements: may we hear it?

At the beginning of his reign, Emperor Gao of the Taizu temple name commanded the ritual officials: “The sage emperors and enlightened kings were exacting in their sacrifices: inwardly they manifested sincerity and reverence, and outwardly they perfected ceremonial forms.” On another occasion, he instructed his assembled ministers: “Ploughing the imperial ritual field is an ancient rite. Since ascending the throne, I have regularly performed it, wishing only to make the people devote their full efforts to their fields, so that they may sustain themselves and nurture their families. It is no exercise in empty ceremony.” Thus, the means by which our Taizu revered Heaven and diligently cared for the people surely extended beyond ceremonial forms.

His sagely sons and divine grandsons maintained this inheritance generation after generation without fail. It was transmitted down to Emperor Su of the Shizong temple name, who first rectified the suburban sacrifices and personally ploughed the imperial ritual field. There were hymns celebrating his reverence for Heaven …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
蠲民有詔蓋于
聖祖有光矣
皇上臨御肇祀
南郊而
天心降格星月呈輝
秉耒三推而民心鼓舞歡聲動地頃因畿輔
旱澇屢
勅羣臣省禱
軫河夫之艱京商之困
===
特賜議處蠲恤則我
皇上敬
天勤民之實殆不專於
郊祀籍耕之文已也誠與
太祖
世宗同一揆矣夫郊籍大典也惟
盛德之君能行焉乃諸士何幸身親見之可無
頌揚以彰
主德之盛
punctuated: 蠲民有詔，蓋于聖祖有光矣。皇上臨御，肇祀南郊，而天心降格，星月呈輝；秉耒三推，而民心鼓舞，歡聲動地。頃因畿輔旱澇，屢勅羣臣省禱，軫河夫之艱、京商之困，特賜議處蠲恤，則我皇上敬天勤民之實，殆不專於郊祀籍耕之文已也，誠與太祖、世宗同一揆矣。夫郊籍，大典也，惟盛德之君能行焉。乃諸士何幸，身親見之，可無頌揚以彰主德之盛？
translation_en: …and there were edicts remitting the people’s burdens, surely adding luster to the sagely founder. Upon ascending the throne, His Majesty first offered sacrifice at the southern suburban altar: Heaven graciously responded, and the stars and moon shone resplendently. He took up the plow and pushed it three times: the people’s hearts were uplifted, and their cheers shook the earth. Recently, because of droughts and floods in the capital region, he repeatedly commanded his ministers to examine their conduct and offer prayers. Concerned about the hardships of river laborers and the distress of merchants in the capital, he expressly ordered deliberations on measures for remission and relief. Thus, the substance of our emperor’s reverence for Heaven and diligent care for the people surely extends beyond the ceremonial forms of suburban sacrifice and plowing the imperial ritual field. He truly follows the same principles as Taizu and Shizong. Suburban sacrifice and ritual plowing are great ceremonies, which only a ruler of abundant virtue can perform. How fortunate you scholars are to have witnessed them in person! Can you refrain from offering praise to make manifest the fullness of your sovereign’s virtue?

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
問漢臣賈誼曰天下之命縣於太子太子
之善在於早諭敎與選左右其眞通達
國體者邪稽之往牒夏典商愆文謨武
烈諭敎嚴矣公少傅保道充弼丞左右
選矣萬世育儲法程昭然具在秦漢以
還如帝範戒子篇元良述承華要略果
皆垂裕之法言與有置六傅者有開博
望者有闢崇賢者有正四友者果皆極
一時之選與洪惟□
===
太祖高皇帝登極之初□□未遑首建
大本堂作
昭鑒錄其爲
儲嗣慮至深遠□
諭太子諭詹同諭□□□負敎誡之言日星
同麗可得而莊誦之歟中書不以設官
勳舊兼領
東宮職事又選國子生侍讀其人可悉指而
言歟逮我
punctuated:
問：漢臣賈誼曰：「天下之命縣於太子，太子之善在於早諭敎與選左右。」其眞通達國體者邪？稽之往牒，夏典、商愆、文謨、武烈，諭敎嚴矣；公少傅保，道充弼丞，左右選矣。萬世育儲法程，昭然具在。秦漢以還，如《帝範》《戒子篇》《元良述》《承華要略》，果皆垂裕之法言與？有置六傅者，有開博望者，有闢崇賢者，有正四友者，果皆極一時之選與？
洪惟□太祖高皇帝登極之初，□□未遑，首建大本堂，作《昭鑒錄》，其爲儲嗣慮至深遠□。諭太子、諭詹同、諭□□□負，敎誡之言，日星同麗，可得而莊誦之歟？中書不以設官，勳舊兼領東宮職事，又選國子生侍讀，其人可悉指而言歟？逮我
translation_en:
Question: Jia Yi, a minister of the Han, said: “The fate of the realm hangs upon the crown prince. The crown prince’s goodness depends upon instructing him early and selecting those around him.” Was he truly someone who understood the fundamental principles of government? Examining the records of the past—the statutes of Xia, the errors of Shang, the counsels of King Wen, and the achievements of King Wu—we find rigorous instruction. With the senior and junior preceptors, mentors, and guardians, and those who guided, supplemented, assisted, and supported him [?], those around the heir were carefully chosen. Models for educating the heir for all ages are plainly preserved. Since the Qin and Han, have such works as Rules for Emperors (Difan), Admonitions to a Son (Jiezi pian), Account of the Heir Apparent (Yuanliang shu), and Essential Outline for Supporting the Heir (Chenghua yaolüe) truly all contained exemplary teachings for securing the welfare of posterity? Some established six tutors; some opened the Bowang establishment; some founded the Chongxian establishment; some formally appointed the Four Companions. Did these appointments truly represent the finest selections of their times?
We reverently consider □ how, at the beginning of his reign, Emperor Taizu Gao, though he had not yet had leisure for □□, first established the Dabentang, the Hall of the Great Foundation, and compiled the Record of Illustrious Admonitions (Zhaojian lu). His concern for the heir was exceedingly profound and far-reaching □. In his instructions to the crown prince, to Zhan Tong, and to □□□負 [?], his words of instruction and admonition shone together with the sun and stars. Can you solemnly recite them? “The Central Secretariat did not thereby establish offices” [?]; longstanding meritorious servants concurrently performed duties in the Eastern Palace, and students of the Directorate of Education were also selected to attend the heir’s reading. Can you identify and discuss all these men? Coming down to our …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
成祖文皇帝集
文華寶鑑
宣宗章皇帝製
帝訓五十篇
憲宗純皇帝有
文華大訓四卷皆爲
聖子
神孫計也三書何所指與抑亦述
太祖之遺意否與當時輔導等官可得而詳與
===
今我
皇上茂育元良
諭誨有彝訓丞保有碩儒駕軼往代同符
祖宗天下臣民喁喁忻抃咸歌麟趾茲欲陳
獻以資講讀庶幾仰體
皇上早建豫教之盛心爾諸生懷芹曝忱有日
矣務悉心以對
問明王必延儒雋以宏化功賢士必崇儒
學以紹聖緒則儒之名實固不可不蚤
punctuated:
成祖文皇帝集《文華寶鑑》，宣宗章皇帝製《帝訓》五十篇，憲宗純皇帝有《文華大訓》四卷，皆爲聖子神孫計也。三書何所指與？抑亦述太祖之遺意否與？當時輔導等官可得而詳與？
今我皇上茂育元良，諭誨有彝訓，丞保有碩儒，駕軼往代，同符祖宗。天下臣民喁喁忻抃，咸歌麟趾。茲欲陳獻以資講讀，庶幾仰體皇上早建豫教之盛心。爾諸生懷芹曝忱有日矣，務悉心以對。
問：明王必延儒雋以宏化功，賢士必崇儒學以紹聖緒，則儒之名實固不可不蚤
translation_en:
…Emperor Wen, Chengzu, compiled the Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor; Emperor Zhang, Xuanzong, composed the fifty chapters of Imperial Instructions; and Emperor Chun, Xianzong, produced the four juan of the Great Instructions of Literary Splendor. All were plans for their sagely sons and divine grandsons. What do these three books address? Do they also transmit the intentions bequeathed by Taizu? Can you give a detailed account of the officials charged with assisting and guiding the heir at that time?
Our present Emperor assiduously nurtures the heir apparent. His admonitions follow enduring precepts, and eminent Confucian scholars serve as assistants and guardians. He surpasses former ages and accords with his imperial ancestors. Throughout the realm, officials and common people eagerly rejoice and clap their hands, all singing “The Qilin’s Hoof,” in praise of his virtuous offspring. We now wish to submit material to support lectures and readings, hoping thereby to accord with His Majesty’s noble intention to establish instruction early and provide education in advance. You students have long cherished the sincere wish to offer your humble contributions, like offerings of celery or the warmth of the sun. Apply yourselves wholeheartedly in answering.
Question: An enlightened king must recruit outstanding Confucian scholars to extend the work of moral transformation; worthy scholars must honor Confucian learning to carry forward the legacy of the sages. Thus, the name and substance of being a Confucian scholar must surely, at an early stage, …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
辨者也周官有九兩之法而儒居一焉
至與牧長主吏並稱儒何重與班氏有
九家之論而儒居一焉至與陰陽農雜
槩列又何隘與儒者之行宣父語魯君
備矣然謂遽數之不能終其物悉數之
乃留更僕其事何居真儒之功楊子述
法言似矣然謂一用而四海皇皇一用
而鄰國章章其人何指洙泗以還儒學
蓋失傳矣隱柴桑者嘗述八儒其所評
===
===
覈果精乎聖門高第儒術宜盡醇矣令
蘭陵者嘗賤三儒其所譏詆果當乎漢
史立儒林傳潜心大業者何以不與唐
史立儒學傳學本六經者何以見遺至
宋史則又於儒林之外別為道學一傳
豈儒自儒道自道與得中原文献之傳
謹屋漏夢寐之際亦一代碩儒也又不
獲與濂洛關閩諸賢為伍何與諸士產
多儒之邦且逢
punctuated: 辨者也。周官有九兩之法，而儒居一焉，至與牧、長、主、吏並稱，儒何重與？班氏有九家之論，而儒居一焉，至與陰陽、農、雜槩列，又何隘與？儒者之行，宣父語魯君備矣。然謂遽數之不能終其物，悉數之乃留更僕，其事何居？真儒之功，楊子述《法言》似矣。然謂一用而四海皇皇，一用而鄰國章章，其人何指？洙泗以還，儒學蓋失傳矣。隱柴桑者嘗述八儒，其所評覈果精乎？聖門高第，儒術宜盡醇矣。令蘭陵者嘗賤三儒，其所譏詆果當乎？漢史立《儒林傳》，潜心大業者何以不與？唐史立《儒學傳》，學本六經者何以見遺？至宋史，則又於儒林之外別為《道學》一傳，豈儒自儒，道自道與？得中原文献之傳，謹屋漏夢寐之際，亦一代碩儒也，又不獲與濂洛關閩諸賢為伍，何與？諸士產多儒之邦，且逢
translation_en:
…must be distinguished. The Offices of Zhou sets out nine means of binding the people together, and Confucian scholars constitute one of them. They are ranked alongside regional governors, local chiefs, heads of noble houses, and officials: why are Confucian scholars accorded such importance? Ban Gu discusses nine schools of thought, and the Confucians constitute one of them. Yet they are placed alongside the Yin-Yang, Agriculturalist, and Eclectic schools: why, in this case, are they assigned so restricted a standing?

As for the conduct of Confucian scholars, Confucius explained it fully to the ruler of Lu. Yet he said that a hurried enumeration could not exhaust its particulars, while a complete enumeration would require staying until the attendants had changed shifts. What did he mean by this? Master Yang’s account in Model Sayings (Fayan) seems to describe the achievements of true Confucians. Yet he says that when one was employed, all within the Four Seas shone in splendor, while when another was employed, the neighboring states displayed conspicuous order. To whom was he referring?

Since the days of teaching by the Zhu and Si rivers, the transmission of Confucian learning has presumably been lost. The recluse of Chaisang once described eight kinds of Confucians: were his assessments truly discerning? The leading disciples of the Sage’s school ought all to have possessed pure Confucian learning. Yet the man who served as Magistrate of Lanling once disparaged three kinds of Confucians: were his criticisms truly justified?

The History of the Han established a section entitled ‘Biographies of Confucian Scholars’: why was the man who devoted himself to the great undertaking not included? The History of the Tang established ‘Biographies of Confucian Learning’: why was the man whose learning was rooted in the Six Classics omitted? The History of the Song went further, establishing a separate section on ‘Learning of the Way’ in addition to ‘Confucian Scholars.’ Could Confucian learning and the Way really be separate things? A man who inherited the cultural and scholarly tradition of the Central Plain and remained vigilant over his conduct even in the privacy of his chamber and in his dreams was surely also an eminent Confucian of his age. Why, then, was he not permitted to rank with the worthies of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min?

You scholars were born in a land rich in Confucian scholars, and moreover have encountered…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
右儒之世其必稽古辨術思不詭于聖眞矣
願陳之無讓
問韓非子曰人臣循令而從事案法而治
官若然則法令也者臣子誠兢兢然持
守之罔有或越然後可以靖臣職而稱
治世乃猶有不盡然者姑舉一二言之
治晉陽者不繕城郭云脩其敎守鴈門
者縱虜入犯卒襲匈奴按梁國者輒焚
獄詞令晉城者擅用庫錢此皆非法令
===
所許也乃四子冒焉行之而人不以為
非何哉方
今律例森具紀法昭明二百餘年以來故無狂
譎之夫無干諄之衆何者恃有此三尺
耳而或有身犯姦臧逭於吏議罪麗罔
赦逃於邦刑豈亦於四子之意然與否
與至于慷慨激憤之士一或不當少有
詿誤輒不免焉何法詘於彼而顧伸於
此耶夫豪傑之士既不得越於法之外
punctuated:
右儒之世，其必稽古辨術，思不詭于聖眞矣。願陳之無讓。
問：韓非子曰：「人臣循令而從事，案法而治官。」若然，則法令也者，臣子誠兢兢然持守之，罔有或越，然後可以靖臣職而稱治世。乃猶有不盡然者，姑舉一二言之。治晉陽者不繕城郭，云脩其敎；守鴈門者縱虜入犯，卒襲匈奴；按梁國者輒焚獄詞；令晉城者擅用庫錢。此皆非法令所許也，乃四子冒焉行之，而人不以為非，何哉？方今律例森具，紀法昭明，二百餘年以來，故無狂譎之夫，無干諄之衆，何者？恃有此三尺耳。而或有身犯姦臧，逭於吏議，罪麗罔赦，逃於邦刑，豈亦於四子之意然與否與？至于慷慨激憤之士，一或不當，少有詿誤，輒不免焉。何法詘於彼，而顧伸於此耶？夫豪傑之士既不得越於法之外，
translation_en:
…an age that honors Confucian scholars, you surely will examine antiquity and distinguish among approaches to learning, taking care not to depart from the true teachings of the sages. Please set forth your views without reserve.
Question: Han Feizi said: “A minister follows commands in conducting affairs and acts according to law in administering his office.” If so, ministers must indeed uphold laws and commands with scrupulous care, never overstepping them; only then can they fulfill their official duties and bring about what may be called an age of good government. Yet there are cases in which this does not entirely hold true. Let us cite a few. The man who governed Jinyang did not repair its walls, saying that he was cultivating moral instruction. The man who defended Yanmen allowed enemy incursions and ultimately launched a surprise attack on the Xiongnu. The man who investigated the kingdom of Liang summarily burned the judicial depositions. The magistrate of Jincheng used treasury funds without authorization. None of these actions was permitted by the laws and commands. Yet these four men ventured to carry them out, and people did not regard them as wrong. Why?
Today, the statutes and substatutes are comprehensively arrayed, and the rules and laws are clear. For more than two hundred years, therefore, there have been no reckless, deceitful men and no crowds of offenders [?]. Why is this? Because we rely upon the law—these “three feet” of written statutes. Yet some personally commit illicit acts and corruption but evade official impeachment; their crimes admit of no pardon, yet they escape the state's punishments. Do their intentions, too, resemble those of the four men, or not? As for men of noble spirit and righteous indignation, if a single action is improper or they commit even a slight error, they invariably fail to escape punishment. Why does the law yield to the former, yet assert itself against the latter? Since men of outstanding ability may not overstep the bounds of the law…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
而姦罔之徒又或逃於法之中謂法之
無弊不可也夫法者國之所恃以爲治
者也而至於弊焉將何以理諸士窮經
致用其必究心於此矣願明言之以觀
治世之具
問閩方界在南服古稱鄒魯民不知兵素
樂土也往盜起海上引入島夷當事者
急爲蕩平之計乃募客兵以禦之夫寇
遄發而藉外募權也今數歲于茲矣昔
===
人謂兵無宗族不自重惜客兵似不可
久也然攘臂先登衝鋒陷敵其功可盡
泯歟建議者率持練土兵爲長計夫周
制入則爲比閭族黨出則爲伍兩軍師
其土兵之意與漢置材官騎士家人子
起田中從軍果周制與唐宋以來選土
兵者曰澤潞步兵曰雄邊子弟曰武定
軍曰保毅軍曰宣毅軍曰廣銳軍曰義
勇軍其詳可得聞與亦各有績效與或
punctuated:
而姦罔之徒又或逃於法之中，謂法之無弊，不可也。夫法者，國之所恃以爲治者也，而至於弊焉，將何以理？諸士窮經致用，其必究心於此矣。願明言之，以觀治世之具。
問：閩方界在南服，古稱鄒魯，民不知兵，素樂土也。往盜起海上，引入島夷，當事者急爲蕩平之計，乃募客兵以禦之。夫寇遄發而藉外募，權也。今數歲于茲矣。昔人謂兵無宗族，不自重惜，客兵似不可久也。然攘臂先登，衝鋒陷敵，其功可盡泯歟？建議者率持練土兵爲長計。夫周制，入則爲比閭族黨，出則爲伍兩軍師，其土兵之意與？漢置材官騎士，家人子起田中從軍，果周制與？唐宋以來，選土兵者曰澤潞步兵，曰雄邊子弟，曰武定軍，曰保毅軍，曰宣毅軍，曰廣銳軍，曰義勇軍，其詳可得聞與？亦各有績效與？或
translation_en:
…yet treacherous and deceitful men sometimes escape within the law itself. It cannot be said that the law is free of defects. The law is what the state relies upon to govern; when it becomes defective, how is order to be maintained? You gentlemen study the classics thoroughly to put them into practice, and surely must have devoted careful thought to this matter. Explain it clearly, so that we may see what means you possess for governing the age.
Question: Fujian lies in the southern region of the realm and has long been called a Zou and Lu, a homeland of Confucian learning. Its people knew nothing of warfare, and it had always been a land of contentment. Previously, bandits arose at sea and brought in island foreigners. Those responsible urgently sought a way to suppress them and restore peace, recruiting troops from outside the province to resist them. When raiders strike suddenly, relying on outside recruits is an expedient. Yet several years have now passed. The ancients said that soldiers without their clans about them do not value or cherish their own lives; it would thus seem that troops from elsewhere cannot be relied upon indefinitely. Nevertheless, they bared their arms and were first to scale the walls, charging forward and breaking through the enemy. Can their achievements be entirely effaced? Those submitting proposals generally advocate training local troops as a long-term plan. Under the Zhou system, men at home were organized into neighborhood groupings—bi, lü, zu, and dang—and on campaign into military units—wu, liang, jun, and shi. Was this the underlying principle of local troops? The Han established infantry and cavalry forces, with sons of ordinary households leaving the fields to join the army. Was this truly the Zhou system? From the Tang and Song onward, forces selected from local men included the Zelu Infantry, the Xiongbian Youths, the Wuding Army, the Baoyi Army, the Xuanyi Army, the Guangrui Army, and the Yiyong Army. May we hear the details of these? Did each also have achievements to its credit? Some…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
疑閩人脆不堪荷戈曩浙直有警閩子
弟連艘而上隷兵籍最稱蹻健乃今自
衞顧脆至借技於人何歟往歲莆陽之
變遂謂土兵驁不可用夫兵無統制雖
韓白不能用也罪果在兵與宋咸平中
詞臣建言福建等郡酌民戶衆寡竝許
置本城守捉軍士時論多之其說固在
也今可行與或謂練兵非難食足難枵
腹與人鬪雖烏獲負矣謂當給之閒田
===
付之寺租亦有見與頃仗
皇上威靈渠魁授首海氛稍稍告靖然桑土之
慮不可已也諸士生長海邦熟計久矣
宜悉心以對毋曰軍旅未學
punctuated: 疑閩人脆，不堪荷戈。曩浙直有警，閩子弟連艘而上，隷兵籍，最稱蹻健；乃今自衞，顧脆至借技於人，何歟？往歲莆陽之變，遂謂土兵驁不可用。夫兵無統制，雖韓白不能用也，罪果在兵與？宋咸平中，詞臣建言：福建等郡，酌民戶衆寡，竝許置本城守捉軍士。時論多之，其說固在也，今可行與？或謂練兵非難，食足難。枵腹與人鬪，雖烏獲負矣。謂當給之閒田，付之寺租，亦有見與？頃仗皇上威靈，渠魁授首，海氛稍稍告靖。然桑土之慮不可已也。諸士生長海邦，熟計久矣，宜悉心以對，毋曰軍旅未學。
translation_en:
…doubt whether the people of Fujian are too frail to bear arms. Formerly, when alarms arose in Zhejiang and the directly administered metropolitan region, young men of Fujian went there in fleets of boats and entered the military rolls, earning particular renown for their agility and strength. Yet now, when defending their own homes, they are supposedly so frail that they must rely on others’ prowess. Why is this? Following the disturbances at Puyang in past years, some declared that local troops were unruly and could not be employed. But without unified command and discipline, even Han Xin and Bai Qi could not employ troops. Does the fault really lie with the soldiers?

During the Xianping era of the Song, a literary court official proposed that Fujian and other jurisdictions be permitted to establish troops to guard their own cities, with numbers determined according to the size of their household populations. Contemporary opinion commended the proposal, and its argument remains on record. Could it be implemented today? Some say that training troops is not difficult; providing sufficient food is difficult. Fighting on an empty stomach, even Wu Huo would be defeated. They propose granting the troops idle land and assigning them rents from Buddhist monasteries. Does this, too, show insight?

Recently, through the Emperor’s awe-inspiring might, the ringleaders have been executed, and the coastal disturbances have gradually subsided. Yet we must not cease taking precautions against future danger. You gentlemen were born and raised in this coastal region and have long considered these matters carefully. Apply your minds fully in answering; do not say that you have never studied military affairs.

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君子學以致其道
林奇石
同考試官教諭趙批從心上發明君子致道之學一洗陳
言根極理要此時義不多得者
同考試官教授吳批諸作講學與致道殊多纏繞是篇
融會註意而於致道處歸重超卓之見也錄之
考試官教授夏批意邃而詞達佳士也
===
考試官教授帥批純正明確
賢者論君子純心以造乎道而已夫學所以純
此心也心純則道可馴致矣君子毋亦是務乎
子夏示人之意若曰天下之道足於心而已矣
君子之學求諸心而已矣居肆成事百工且知
所以用其心而况于君子乎何則燕僻而廢學
則其心放固無以為適道之基中道而自畫則
其心怠亦難以語大成之學惟君子也時敏以
遜志外物無所奪矣而繼之以不息之功篤行
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
君子學以致其道
林奇石

同考試官教諭趙批：從心上發明君子致道之學，一洗陳言，根極理要，此時義不多得者。

同考試官教授吳批：諸作講學與致道，殊多纏繞。是篇融會註意，而於致道處歸重，超卓之見也，錄之。

考試官教授夏批：意邃而詞達，佳士也。

考試官教授帥批：純正明確。

賢者論君子，純心以造乎道而已。夫學所以純此心也，心純則道可馴致矣。君子毋亦是務乎？子夏示人之意若曰：天下之道，足於心而已矣；君子之學，求諸心而已矣。居肆成事，百工且知所以用其心，而况于君子乎？何則？燕僻而廢學，則其心放，固無以為適道之基；中道而自畫，則其心怠，亦難以語大成之學。惟君子也，時敏以遜志，外物無所奪矣，而繼之以不息之功；篤行
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“The gentleman learns in order to attain his Way”
Lin Qishi

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: This elucidates, from the standpoint of the heart-mind, the learning by which the gentleman attains the Way. It sweeps away stale expressions and penetrates to the essential principles. Such an examination essay is rarely found.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Professor: Other compositions become considerably entangled in discussing learning and attaining the Way. This essay integrates the meaning of the commentary and places its chief emphasis on attaining the Way. Its insight is outstanding. Selected for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Xia, Professor: The ideas are profound and the language lucid. A fine scholar.

Comment by Examiner Shuai, Professor: Orthodox, clear, and precise.

When the worthy speaks of the gentleman, he means simply purifying the heart-mind in order to reach the Way. Learning is the means of purifying this heart-mind; once it is pure, the Way can gradually be attained. Should this not be the gentleman’s concern?

The intent of Zixia’s instruction might be expressed thus: The Way of all under Heaven is fully present in the heart-mind; the gentleman’s learning consists simply in seeking it there. Even the various artisans, dwelling in their workshops to accomplish their tasks, know how to apply their minds. How much more should the gentleman!

Why is this so? If one indulges in idleness and waywardness and neglects learning, the heart-mind runs loose, leaving no foundation for advancing toward the Way. If one draws a limit for oneself midway, the heart-mind grows indolent, and it is likewise difficult to speak of learning that achieves full fruition. Only the gentleman, diligently applying himself in due season to make his purpose humble and receptive, keeps external things from diverting him and follows this with unceasing effort; through earnest practice…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
以邁往他岐不能惑矣而貞之以有恒之守時
敎退息莫不有學非徒少有得而遽止也循序
以致精而所以窮神知化者由此焉敬業樂羣
莫不有學非徒以一善而自足也下學而上達
而所以盡性踐形者由此焉其始也以道爲標
的而所以期而至之望而趨之者必有事而勿
忘也而道其致於專精之後矣乎其終也以道
爲歸宿而所以知至至之知終終之者欲深造
而自得也而道其致於真積之久矣乎否則道
===
有未致是性分之有虧學未大成是能事之有
歉君子之心豈容已哉噫此子夏篤信聖道而
有得者也聖門自顏曾而下惟子夏以篤信稱
觀其謂盡倫爲已學因論詩而知學充其言可
以與聞性道而此以致道言之固其學之已至
者不然出入紛華靡麗之中烏能爲是言哉此
所以列于文學之科也
知遠之近知風之自知微之顯
楊佩訓
punctuated:
以邁往，他岐不能惑矣，而貞之以有恒之守。時敎退息，莫不有學，非徒少有得而遽止也；循序以致精，而所以窮神知化者由此焉。敬業樂羣，莫不有學，非徒以一善而自足也；下學而上達，而所以盡性踐形者由此焉。其始也，以道爲標的，而所以期而至之、望而趨之者，必有事而勿忘也，而道其致於專精之後矣乎？其終也，以道爲歸宿，而所以知至至之、知終終之者，欲深造而自得也，而道其致於真積之久矣乎？否則，道有未致，是性分之有虧；學未大成，是能事之有歉。君子之心豈容已哉！噫！此子夏篤信聖道而有得者也。聖門自顏曾而下，惟子夏以篤信稱。觀其謂盡倫爲已學，因論詩而知學，充其言，可以與聞性道；而此以致道言之，固其學之已至者。不然，出入紛華靡麗之中，烏能爲是言哉？此所以列于文學之科也。

知遠之近，知風之自，知微之顯。

楊佩訓
translation_en:
…to advance resolutely, so that other paths cannot lead him astray; he then makes this firm through steadfast adherence. Whether receiving instruction at the proper times or resting in retirement, he never ceases learning. He does not abruptly stop upon gaining some small insight. By proceeding in due order, he attains refinement; from this comes his ability to fathom the wondrous and understand transformation. Devoted to his studies and delighting in his companions, he never ceases learning. He does not rest content with a single good achievement. Through learning what is below, he reaches what is above; from this comes his ability fully to realize his nature and fulfill what his bodily form embodies.

At the outset, he takes the Way as his target. To reach what he aspires to and advance toward what he looks to, he must constantly apply himself and never forget his task. Will the Way, then, be attained after such concentrated refinement? At the culmination, he takes the Way as his final destination. To know where to arrive and arrive there, and to know where to finish and finish there, he seeks to advance deeply in learning and make it his own. Will the Way, then, be attained after a long accumulation of genuine effort? Otherwise, insofar as the Way remains unattained, what his nature endows him with remains unfulfilled; insofar as his learning falls short of full accomplishment, what he is capable of achieving remains incomplete. How could the gentleman’s heart allow him to stop?

Ah! These are the words of Zixia, who firmly believed in the sage’s Way and had gained an understanding of it. Among the sage’s disciples, after Yan Hui and Zeng Shen, Zixia alone was celebrated for steadfast belief. Consider his assertion that one who fully discharges human relationships has already learned, and how discussing the Odes brought him to understand learning. Extended to their full implications, his words would qualify him to hear teachings on human nature and the Way. Here, in speaking of attaining the Way, he surely speaks as one whose learning has already reached its goal. Otherwise, how could someone moving amid dazzling luxury and seductive splendor utter such words? This is why he was ranked in the category of literary learning.

“Know that the distant begins with the near; know whence influences arise; know how the subtle becomes manifest.”

Yang Peixun.

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭李批知幾之學人所難言子能於遠近
風自顯微處挑剔精透不費詞而理自足是務實勝者
同考試官學正黃批講三知處俱有心得自與尚浮者
迥異
考試官教授夏批闡君子審幾之意條晰
考試官教授帥批峻潔渾成
君子于幾之當謹者而皆有真知焉夫動必有
幾人之所易忽也而君子為能知之其學務實
勝者與且夫天下有不可忽之真幾吾心有不
===
容昧之實見君子心乎為巳而其知幾果何如
哉彼近而吾身遠而天下勢相懸矣君子以近
裏之心觀之則知遠之所見由于邇之所發而
近固遠之幾也蓋遠主其應近主其感天下固
未有應而不出于感者知此而君子之舉遠敢
忽于其近乎順動為風存主為自迹則殊矣君
子以自反之心觀之則知樹之風聲莫非原之
性術而自固風之幾也蓋風動于外理發諸內
天下固未有外之不本于內者知此而君子之
punctuated:
同考試官教諭李批：「知幾之學，人所難言。子能於遠近、風自、顯微處挑剔精透，不費詞而理自足，是務實勝者。」
同考試官學正黃批：「講三知處，俱有心得，自與尚浮者迥異。」
考試官教授夏批：「闡君子審幾之意，條晰。」
考試官教授帥批：「峻潔渾成。」
君子于幾之當謹者，而皆有真知焉。夫動必有幾，人之所易忽也，而君子為能知之，其學務實勝者與！且夫天下有不可忽之真幾，吾心有不容昧之實見。君子心乎為巳，而其知幾果何如哉？彼近而吾身，遠而天下，勢相懸矣。君子以近裏之心觀之，則知遠之所見，由于邇之所發，而近固遠之幾也。蓋遠主其應，近主其感，天下固未有應而不出于感者。知此，而君子之舉遠，敢忽于其近乎？順動為風，存主為自，迹則殊矣。君子以自反之心觀之，則知樹之風聲，莫非原之性術，而自固風之幾也。蓋風動于外，理發諸內，天下固未有外之不本于內者。知此，而君子之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Learning to recognize incipient tendencies is something people find difficult to explain. You distinguish and probe with precision and penetration the relations between the distant and the near, influence and its source, and the manifest and the subtle. Without expending many words, you fully convey the principles. This is work that strives for substantial excellence.”
Associate Examiner Huang, School Instructor, comments: “Your explanations of all three kinds of knowledge show personal insight. They are decidedly different from those that prize superficiality.”
Examiner Xia, Professor, comments: “Clearly and systematically elucidates the gentleman’s careful discernment of incipient tendencies.”
Examiner Shuai, Professor, comments: “Rigorous and pure, forming a seamless whole.”
The gentleman possesses true knowledge of every incipient tendency that calls for vigilance. Every movement necessarily has its incipient signs, which people readily overlook; yet the gentleman can recognize them. Surely his learning strives for substantial excellence! Now, in the world there are actual incipient tendencies that must not be disregarded, and in our minds there is solid insight that must not be obscured. The gentleman sets his mind on learning for his own cultivation [?]; what, then, is his knowledge of incipient tendencies really like?
What is near is one’s own person; what is distant is all under Heaven. Their respective scope differs enormously. Viewing them with a mind directed inward, the gentleman knows that what becomes apparent far away arises from what issues forth close at hand. The near is indeed the incipient source of the distant. For the distant concerns the response, and the near concerns the stimulus. In the world there has never been a response that did not arise from a stimulus. Knowing this, when the gentleman undertakes something with far-reaching effects, would he dare neglect what is near?
That which moves others to follow is influence; that which is inwardly held and governs is its source. Their outward manifestations differ. Viewing them with a mind turned toward self-examination, the gentleman knows that the influence and reputation one establishes all originate in one’s character and methods [?]. The source is indeed the incipient basis of influence. For influence moves outwardly, while principle issues from within. In the world there has never been anything outward that was not rooted in what is inward. Knowing this, the gentleman’s …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
觀風敢忘其所自乎以至幾微方動寂感初分
孰不以爲微矣而何與于顯也而君子之心蓋
通顯微而無間者則知存之于念慮者不終隱
見之于事爲者則甚著而昭然獨炳于幾先矣
蓋始于獨見獨聞終于共見共聞天下固未有
隱而不彰者知此而謹微以爲丕顯之地者又
烏容已哉吁此三知者天下之真知也由此謹
之於入德易易矣抑甞聞之虞書曰人心惟危
道心惟微語幾也又曰惟精惟一語知幾也易
===
===
曰知幾其神乎下學之事宜未及此然觀中庸
一書推極於中和位育而本之戒懼謹獨推極
於篤恭而天下平矣而始于爲已可知幾是知獨
即幾也是幾也約之愈精充之愈廣下學上達
一以貫之矣
孟子曰言近而指遠者善言也守約而施
博者善道也君子之言也不下帶而道
存焉君子之守脩其身而天下平
陳瑛
punctuated:
觀風敢忘其所自乎？以至幾微方動，寂感初分，孰不以爲微矣，而何與于顯也？而君子之心，蓋通顯微而無間者，則知存之于念慮者不終隱，見之于事爲者則甚著，而昭然獨炳于幾先矣。蓋始于獨見獨聞，終于共見共聞，天下固未有隱而不彰者。知此而謹微以爲丕顯之地者，又烏容已哉？吁！此三知者，天下之真知也。由此謹之，於入德易易矣。抑甞聞之，《虞書》曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微。」語幾也。又曰：「惟精惟一。」語知幾也。《易》曰：「知幾其神乎！」下學之事宜未及此，然觀《中庸》一書，推極於中和位育，而本之戒懼謹獨；推極於篤恭而天下平矣，而始于爲已。可知幾是知獨，即幾也是幾也[?]約之愈精，充之愈廣，下學上達，一以貫之矣。

孟子曰：「言近而指遠者，善言也；守約而施博者，善道也。君子之言也，不下帶而道存焉；君子之守，脩其身而天下平。」

陳瑛
translation_en:
…in observing the influence spreading abroad, dare he forget its source? Even when the first subtle stirrings have only just arisen, and stillness and response have only begun to divide, who would not regard them as minute and ask what connection they have with the manifest? Yet the gentleman’s mind comprehends the manifest and the subtle without any gap between them. He therefore knows that what resides in thoughts and reflections will not remain concealed, and that what appears in actions and affairs will be plainly evident. This shines clearly in his solitary awareness before those first stirrings unfold. What begins as something seen and heard by oneself alone ends as something seen and heard by all. In the world, nothing hidden fails eventually to become manifest. Knowing this, how could he cease attending carefully to the subtle, making it the foundation of what will become greatly manifest? Ah! These three kinds of knowing are true knowledge in the world. If one exercises care on this basis, entering into virtue becomes easy indeed.

Moreover, I have heard these words from the Book of Yu: “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle.” This speaks of incipient stirrings. It also says: “Be discerning; be single-minded.” This speaks of knowing those stirrings. The Book of Changes says: “To know incipient stirrings—is this not spirit-like?” Learning at the ordinary level might seem not yet to reach this. Yet consider the Doctrine of the Mean: it extends its account to the utmost attainment of equilibrium and harmony, whereby Heaven and Earth take their proper places and all things are nourished, but grounds this in vigilance, apprehension, and care in solitude. It extends its account to earnest reverence bringing peace to all under Heaven, but begins with cultivation for oneself [the transcription reads 爲已, probably for 爲己]. Thus, knowing incipient stirrings may be understood as knowing what is present in solitude; the following repeated wording concerning these stirrings is doubtful [?]. The more precisely one concentrates this understanding, the more refined it becomes; the more fully one extends it, the broader it becomes. Learning below and reaching understanding above are threaded together by a single principle.

Mencius said: “Words that are close at hand yet point far afield are good words. Holding to what is simple while applying it broadly is a good way. The gentleman’s words do not go below his sash, yet the Way is present in them. What the gentleman holds to is the cultivation of his own person, and all under Heaven is thereby brought to peace.”

Chen Ying 陳瑛

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正龍批題似易而實難場中多類大
融貫此篇體認眞切不爲支離影響語可以爲式矣
考試官教授夏批意新理到
考試官教授帥批詞氣宏雅
大賢卽言與道之善而歸諸君子焉夫近可遠
約可博此言道之爲善也非君子其孰能之孟
子之意蓋曰垂訓立教必資於言經世理物莫
先於道胡立言脩道者之不得其要也是故言
之近者而其指則易窮非善言也惟言之所及
===
者近而不遺而指之所涵者遠而莫禦則一言
盡天下之道而聖賢之格言在是矣不其善乎
守之約者而其施則易窒非善道也惟守之在
我者約而可循而施之在人者博而不匱則易
簡得天下之理而帝王之要道在是矣不其善
乎是言也惟君子爲能言之是道也惟君子爲
能道之爾彼其率淺易以敷詞其言之近若不
下於帶也然神化性命之精卽此而寓則其指
誠未可以易窺者又何遠也近而能遠而所謂
punctuated:
同考試官學正龍批：題似易而實難，場中多類大融貫，此篇體認眞切，不爲支離影響語，可以爲式矣。
考試官教授夏批：意新理到。
考試官教授帥批：詞氣宏雅。
大賢卽言與道之善而歸諸君子焉。夫近可遠，約可博，此言道之爲善也。非君子，其孰能之？孟子之意蓋曰：垂訓立教，必資於言；經世理物，莫先於道。胡立言脩道者之不得其要也？是故言之近者，而其指則易窮，非善言也。惟言之所及者近而不遺，而指之所涵者遠而莫禦，則一言盡天下之道，而聖賢之格言在是矣，不其善乎？守之約者，而其施則易窒，非善道也。惟守之在我者約而可循，而施之在人者博而不匱，則易簡得天下之理，而帝王之要道在是矣，不其善乎？是言也，惟君子爲能言之；是道也，惟君子爲能道之爾。彼其率淺易以敷詞，其言之近若不下於帶也。然神化性命之精卽此而寓，則其指誠未可以易窺者，又何遠也！近而能遠，而所謂
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Long, School Instructor, comments: The topic seems easy but is actually difficult. Many responses in the examination hall resemble a broad synthesis [?]. This essay shows genuine and precise understanding and avoids disjointed or vaguely derivative expressions. It can serve as a model.
Examiner Xia, Professor, comments: The conception is fresh, and the principles are fully grasped.
Examiner Shuai, Professor, comments: The diction and spirit are expansive and elegant.
The great worthy takes excellence in words and in the Way and attributes both to the gentleman. What is near can reach far; what is concise can extend broadly: herein lies the excellence of words and the Way. Who but the gentleman can achieve this? Mencius’s meaning is, in effect, as follows: To transmit instruction and establish teaching, one must rely on words; to order the world and regulate affairs, nothing takes precedence over the Way. Why, then, do those who formulate teachings and cultivate the Way fail to grasp their essentials? Thus, words that concern what is near, but whose implications are soon exhausted, are not excellent words. Only when words address what is near without omission, while their implications embrace what is far without restriction, can a single utterance encompass the Way of all under Heaven. Herein lie the exemplary sayings of sages and worthies. Is this not excellence? What one holds to may be concise, but if its application readily meets an obstruction, it is not an excellent Way. Only when what one holds to within oneself is concise and practicable, while its application to others is broad and inexhaustible, can ease and simplicity comprehend the principles of all under Heaven. Herein lies the essential Way of emperors and kings. Is this not excellence? Only the gentleman can utter such words; only the gentleman can put such a Way into practice. He uses plain and accessible language to express himself, and the nearness of what he speaks of seems not to extend below his belt. Yet the subtleties of spiritual transformation, human nature, and destiny reside precisely here. His meaning is therefore truly not something readily fathomed: how far-reaching it is! Near yet capable of reaching far, and what is called …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
善言者孰有尚於君子哉本愼脩以立極其守
之約僅不出于身爾然均平天下之化即此而
臻則其施誠非可以限量者又何博也約而能
博而所謂善道者孰有尚於君子哉吁知君子
之善言則立言者固當求諸道知君子之善道
則體道者又當求諸身矣彼世之枝葉其辭而
泛濫其學者無惑乎君子之道鮮也孟子知言
養氣得統于一貫其以是爲天下後世告也意
獨至矣以此爲訓猶有談虛而流於老莊之荒
===
唐守靜而宗夫佛氏之寂滅者
易
象曰天行健君子以自彊不息
楊佩訓
同考試官教諭許 批崔寔即自彊不息分為二義殊失易
傳本旨今以一理貫串而法天之意自明非苟作者
同考試官學正龍 批天運不已惟君子法之是即所謂
聖人之學也求其發揮精到者無踰此篇
考試官教授夏 批是善言物象之大者
punctuated:
善言者，孰有尚於君子哉？本愼脩以立極，其守之約，僅不出于身爾。然均平天下之化，即此而臻，則其施誠非可以限量者，又何博也！約而能博，而所謂善道者，孰有尚於君子哉？吁！知君子之善言，則立言者固當求諸道；知君子之善道，則體道者又當求諸身矣。彼世之枝葉其辭而泛濫其學者，無惑乎君子之道鮮也。孟子知言養氣，得統于一貫，其以是爲天下後世告也，意獨至矣。以此爲訓，猶有談虛而流於老莊之荒唐、守靜而宗夫佛氏之寂滅者。

易
象曰：「天行健，君子以自彊不息。」
楊佩訓

同考試官教諭許批：「崔寔即自彊不息分為二義，殊失易傳本旨。今以一理貫串，而法天之意自明，非苟作者。」

同考試官學正龍批：「天運不已，惟君子法之，是即所謂聖人之學也。求其發揮精到者，無踰此篇。」

考試官教授夏批：「是善言物象之大者。」
translation_en:
…among those who speak well, who surpasses the gentleman? He takes careful self-cultivation as the foundation for establishing the ultimate standard. What he maintains is so concentrated that it scarcely extends beyond his own person. Yet the transforming influence that brings equity and peace to all under Heaven is achieved through this very means. Its application truly cannot be bounded or measured: how far-reaching it is! Concentrated yet capable of far-reaching application—among those said to be skilled in the Way, who surpasses the gentleman? Ah! Knowing that the gentleman speaks well, those who establish teachings must surely seek their basis in the Way; knowing that the gentleman is skilled in the Way, those who embody the Way must in turn seek it in themselves. With people of this age elaborating their language into branches and leaves and letting their learning sprawl without restraint, it is no wonder that the gentleman’s Way is seldom found. Mengzi’s understanding of words and cultivation of vital energy were unified by a single connecting principle. His intention in proclaiming this to all under Heaven and to later generations was supremely profound. Yet even with this instruction, there are still those who discourse on emptiness and stray into the extravagances of Laozi and Zhuangzi, or preserve stillness and revere the Buddhists’ quiescent extinction.

Book of Changes
The Commentary on the Images says: “Heaven’s movement is vigorous; the gentleman accordingly strengthens himself without cease.”
Yang Peixun

Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “Cui Shi divided ‘strengthening oneself without cease’ into two meanings, seriously missing the original purport of the Commentary on the Changes. Here, a single principle runs throughout, and the meaning of taking Heaven as one’s model becomes clear of itself. This is no careless composition.”

Associate Examiner Long, School Instructor, comments: “Heaven moves without stopping; only the gentleman takes it as his model. This is precisely what is called the learning of the sages. For a penetrating and exact exposition of this, no essay surpasses this one.”

Examiner Xia, Professor, comments: “This is an excellent exposition of the grandeur of the images of things.”

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授帥批莊重可誦
象傳卽天運之不已而因著君子有法天之學
焉夫天惟至健故運而不已也君子法之亦不
已焉非其合德於天者哉夫子發乾之象欲人
法天以爲學也蓋謂夫聖人者與昊天而同道
者也乾健之德天以之而立命聖人以之而立
心其理一而已矣是故乾之象天也乾之德健
也上下皆乾陽之純而健之至則是維天之命
太極以宰其機而運行不已上帝之載於穆以
===
貞其運而混闢無窮蓋自有天地以來而未改
歷古今如斯而常運者也天之行健如此君子
法之則以吾心之德本與天而同體亦與天而
同運故果確以勝其私矣而物欲不撓則天理
流行而主靜以立極者成性以之而存存至大
至剛者充塞於天地之間也强毅以恒其德矣
而己私淨盡則德性常用而凡動之得宜者上
達以之而亹亹無貳無雜者常伸於萬物之表
也以之而進德脩業則緝熈於宥密者與帝載
punctuated:
考試官敎授帥批：莊重可誦。

象傳卽天運之不已，而因著君子有法天之學焉。夫天惟至健，故運而不已也。君子法之，亦不已焉，非其合德於天者哉？夫子發乾之象，欲人法天以爲學也。蓋謂夫聖人者，與昊天而同道者也。乾健之德，天以之而立命，聖人以之而立心，其理一而已矣。是故乾之象，天也；乾之德，健也。上下皆乾，陽之純而健之至，則是維天之命，太極以宰其機而運行不已；上帝之載，於穆以貞其運而混闢無窮。蓋自有天地以來而未改，歷古今如斯而常運者也。天之行健如此，君子法之，則以吾心之德本與天而同體，亦與天而同運。故果確以勝其私矣，而物欲不撓，則天理流行，而主靜以立極者，成性以之而存存，至大至剛者充塞於天地之間也。强毅以恒其德矣，而己私淨盡，則德性常用，而凡動之得宜者，上達以之而亹亹，無貳無雜者常伸於萬物之表也。以之而進德脩業，則緝熈於宥密者與帝載
translation_en:
Examiner Shuai 帥, Instructor, comments: “Dignified and worthy of recitation.”

The Commentary on the Images takes Heaven’s unceasing movement as its point of departure and thereby makes clear that the noble man pursues learning by modeling himself on Heaven. It is because Heaven possesses the utmost vigor that it moves without ceasing. The noble man models himself on it and likewise never ceases. Does he not thereby unite his virtue with Heaven’s? In expounding the image of Qian, the Master intended people to model themselves on Heaven in their learning. His meaning is that the sage shares the same Way as August Heaven. Through Qian’s vigorous virtue, Heaven establishes its mandate and the sage establishes his mind. The principle is one and the same.

Thus, Qian’s image is Heaven, and Qian’s virtue is vigor. With Qian both above and below, yang is pure and vigor reaches its utmost. This is Heaven’s mandate: the Supreme Ultimate governs its moving springs, and its movement never ceases. These are the workings of the Lord on High: their profound mystery keeps their movement constant, and the passage from undifferentiated unity to opening forth is inexhaustible. Since Heaven and Earth first existed, this has never changed; throughout antiquity and the present, it has continued to move in this same manner.

Such is the vigor of Heaven’s movement. The noble man models himself on it because the virtue of his own mind is fundamentally of one substance with Heaven and likewise shares its movement. Thus, through resolution and firmness he overcomes his selfishness. When material desires do not disturb him, Heaven’s principle flows freely. By taking stillness as his guiding principle, he establishes the ultimate standard; through this he fulfills his nature and continually preserves it, so that what is supremely great and supremely firm fills the space between Heaven and Earth. Through strength and perseverance he makes his virtue constant. When personal selfishness is entirely cleansed away, his moral nature functions constantly, and all his actions attain their proper measure. Through this he advances tirelessly toward higher understanding, and what is undivided and unmixed ever extends beyond the myriad things.

Through this he advances in virtue and cultivates his work; then that which shines continually in deep stillness, together with the workings of the Lord on High…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
而同其流行即盈虛消息而觀於天天不可變
則道亦不可變也以之而乗龍御天則維勅於
時幾者與乾元而相為悠久即常變久暫而求
諸理理不可易則心亦不可易也其自强不息
有如此至是則天以健而立德人以健而立心
聖人天道之極致不可觀其深乎大抵聖人全
體乎太極而有功於造化亦惟其至誠之無息
如天地之無不覆載而不自以為德也是故其
心蓋未肯以自暇自逸於變時雍者兢業於萬
===
幾光顯西土者翼翼以小心良以敬肆之間天
人之介王霸之幾也志於法天者其要只在慎
獨
夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業也知崇禮卑
崇效天卑法地
林應訓
同考試官教諭許批易為聖學之所資而是篇廣大
精密獨能形容之宜錄以式
同考試官學正龍批知禮崇卑體貼自有識見非泛
punctuated:
而同其流行。即盈虛消息而觀於天，天不可變，則道亦不可變也。以之而乗龍御天，則維勅於時幾者與乾元而相為悠久。即常變久暫而求諸理，理不可易，則心亦不可易也。其自强不息有如此。至是，則天以健而立德，人以健而立心。聖人天道之極致，不可觀其深乎？大抵聖人全體乎太極而有功於造化，亦惟其至誠之無息，如天地之無不覆載，而不自以為德也。是故其心蓋未肯以自暇自逸，於變時雍者兢業於萬幾，光顯西土者翼翼以小心。良以敬肆之間，天人之介，王霸之幾也。志於法天者，其要只在慎獨。
夫易，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。
林應訓
同考試官教諭許批：易為聖學之所資，而是篇廣大精密，獨能形容之，宜錄以式。
同考試官學正龍批：知禮崇卑，體貼自有識見，非泛
translation_en:
…and shares in its flowing operation. If we contemplate Heaven through fullness and emptiness, waning and waxing, Heaven cannot change, and so the Way likewise cannot change. By this, one rides the dragons and governs Heaven; vigilance concerning the incipient workings of each moment endures together with the primal power of Qian. If we seek principle amid constancy and change, duration and brevity, principle cannot be altered, and so the heart likewise cannot be altered. Such is ceaseless self-strengthening. At this point, Heaven establishes its virtue through vigor, and human beings establish their hearts through vigor. Can we not perceive the profundity of the sage’s supreme realization of Heaven’s Way? In general, the sage fully embodies the Supreme Ultimate and contributes to the work of creation and transformation solely through the ceaselessness of his utmost sincerity. Like Heaven and Earth, which cover and sustain everything, he does not regard this as his own virtue. Thus his heart is never willing to indulge in leisure or ease. He who brought about transformation and harmony remained apprehensively attentive to the myriad incipient affairs; he who made the western lands illustrious was reverent and cautious at heart. For the distinction between reverence and laxity marks the boundary between Heaven and the human, and the incipient divergence between kingly and hegemonic rule. For those intent on modeling themselves on Heaven, the essential point lies solely in vigilance when alone.
The Changes is that through which the sage exalts his virtue and broadens his undertakings. Knowledge is lofty; ritual practice is lowly. Loftiness emulates Heaven; lowliness models itself on Earth.
Lin Yingxun.
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “The Changes provides resources for sagely learning. Broad in scope yet precise and meticulous, this essay is uniquely able to portray this. It should be recorded as a model.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Long, Instructor: “In its close appreciation of knowledge and ritual practice, loftiness and lowliness, this essay shows independent discernment; it is no casual…”

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
學易者不能及此
考試官敎授夏批詞理雅健粹然出於正
考試官敎授帥批文有深思取之
大傳論聖學之資於易而必徵諸學之大者焉
夫聖人之德業而效法於天地則聖學之資於
易也大矣易之所以爲至也不其可見乎大傳
懼人以卜筮小易也其言若曰大哉易也聖人
因之以發其蘊而又資之以終其功是故理蘊
於心之爲德德至於聖人若無所資矣而齋戒
===
以神明則日新而不已者莫不求端於易也理
措諸事之謂業業至於聖人若無所資矣而變
通以趣時則富有而無窮者莫不默成於易也
而何以明其然也蓋易之爲道語高而極於神
化性命也語卑而顯於日用事物也聖人會易
理於心而爲智焉則達於昭曠有以發其獨覺
之明而其智崇矣聖人體易理於事而爲禮焉
則允蹈無愆有以見諸躬行之實而其禮卑矣
夫崇莫如天而聖人之智效諸天焉昭明有融
punctuated:
學易者不能及此。
考試官敎授夏批：詞理雅健，粹然出於正。
考試官敎授帥批：文有深思，取之。
大傳論聖學之資於易，而必徵諸學之大者焉。
夫聖人之德業而效法於天地，則聖學之資於易也大矣。易之所以爲至也，不其可見乎？大傳懼人以卜筮小易也，其言若曰：「大哉，易也！聖人因之以發其蘊，而又資之以終其功。是故理蘊於心之爲德，德至於聖人，若無所資矣，而齋戒以神明，則日新而不已者，莫不求端於易也。理措諸事之謂業，業至於聖人，若無所資矣，而變通以趣時，則富有而無窮者，莫不默成於易也。而何以明其然也？蓋易之爲道，語高而極於神化性命也，語卑而顯於日用事物也。聖人會易理於心而爲智焉，則達於昭曠，有以發其獨覺之明，而其智崇矣。聖人體易理於事而爲禮焉，則允蹈無愆，有以見諸躬行之實，而其禮卑矣。夫崇莫如天，而聖人之智效諸天焉，昭明有融
translation_en:
…students of the Changes cannot attain this.
Examiner Xia, Instructor, comments: “The language and reasoning are elegant and vigorous, issuing wholly from what is correct.”
Examiner Shuai, Instructor, comments: “The composition shows profound thought. Accept it.”
The Great Commentary discusses how the learning of the sages draws upon the Changes, necessarily substantiating this through the greatest aspects of learning.
When the virtue and achievements of the sages take Heaven and Earth as their models, great indeed is the aid that the learning of the sages derives from the Changes. Does this not reveal why the Changes is unsurpassed? The Great Commentary fears that people will belittle the Changes by regarding it merely as a book of divination. Its words amount to this: “Great indeed is the Changes! Through it the sages bring forth what lies within them, and they also draw upon it to complete their work. Thus, principle stored within the heart constitutes virtue. When virtue reaches the level of the sages, it would seem to need no further aid. Yet through purification and abstinence they attain spiritual illumination; their ceaseless daily renewal invariably finds its source in the Changes. Principle applied to affairs is called achievement. When achievement reaches the level of the sages, it would seem to need no further aid. Yet through transformation and adaptation they keep pace with the times; their inexhaustible abundance invariably comes to silent fulfillment through the Changes. How can we make clear that this is so? The Way of the Changes, spoken of in its loftiest aspects, reaches to spiritual transformation, human nature, and destiny; spoken of in its lowly aspects, it manifests itself in everyday affairs and things. The sages comprehend the principles of the Changes in their hearts, thereby attaining wisdom. They reach a state of luminous breadth, bringing forth the light of their singular insight, and thus their wisdom is exalted. The sages embody the principles of the Changes in affairs, thereby realizing ritual propriety. They tread faithfully without error, manifesting it in actual personal conduct, and thus their ritual propriety is lowly. Nothing is more exalted than Heaven, and the wisdom of the sages takes Heaven as its model. Its splendid radiance…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
者合其太虛之體旁燭無疆者擬其清通之象
而崇斯至矣德之達諸天者非以易而何卑莫
如地而聖人之禮法諸地焉踐履篤實者同其
厚載之機躬行懇到者應夫安貞之吉而卑斯
至矣業之配諸地者非以易而何夫德以易而
崇則聖人之德資於易以為德也業以易而廣
則聖人之業資於易以為業也易之為書其可
以卜筮小之哉大抵易理充塞乎天地而神明
於聖心善觀易者求之於吾心而不泥之於法
===
象則仰觀俯察稽驗不忒也陰陽散殊至理躍
如也信哉畫前原有易所謂效天法地者正以
見聖人之善用易也
書
帝曰夔命汝典樂教胄子直而溫寬而栗
剛而無虐簡而無傲詩言志歌永言聲
依永律和聲八音克諧無相奪倫神人
以和
陳瑛
punctuated:
者，合其太虛之體；旁燭無疆者，擬其清通之象，而崇斯至矣。德之達諸天者，非以易而何？卑莫如地，而聖人之禮法諸地焉。踐履篤實者，同其厚載之機；躬行懇到者，應夫安貞之吉，而卑斯至矣。業之配諸地者，非以易而何？夫德以易而崇，則聖人之德資於易以為德也；業以易而廣，則聖人之業資於易以為業也。易之為書，其可以卜筮小之哉？大抵易理充塞乎天地，而神明於聖心。善觀易者，求之於吾心，而不泥之於法象，則仰觀俯察，稽驗不忒也；陰陽散殊，至理躍如也。信哉，畫前原有易！所謂效天法地者，正以見聖人之善用易也。

書

帝曰：「夔，命汝典樂，教胄子，直而溫，寬而栗，剛而無虐，簡而無傲。詩言志，歌永言，聲依永，律和聲，八音克諧，無相奪倫，神人以和。」

陳瑛
translation_en:
…accords with the substance of Heaven’s Great Void; that which illuminates all around without limit resembles Heaven’s clarity and unimpeded operation. Thus sublimity reaches its utmost. Through what, if not the Changes, does virtue reach Heaven? Nothing is lower than Earth, and the sage’s ritual propriety takes Earth as its model. Steadfast and substantial practice shares in Earth’s capacity to bear all things generously; earnest and thorough personal conduct accords with the auspiciousness of peaceful steadfastness. Thus lowliness reaches its utmost. Through what, if not the Changes, do the sage’s undertakings match Earth? If virtue is exalted through the Changes, then the sage’s virtue draws upon the Changes to become virtue; if undertakings are broadened through the Changes, then the sage’s undertakings draw upon the Changes to become undertakings. Can the Changes, as a book, be diminished to a mere work of divination? Broadly speaking, the principles of the Changes fill Heaven and Earth and find spiritual illumination in the sage’s mind. Those who study the Changes well seek these principles within their own minds and do not become bound by its patterns and images. Looking upward and examining below, they verify them without error; amid the manifold differentiations of yin and yang, the ultimate principle stands vividly revealed. How true it is that the Changes originally existed before the hexagram lines were drawn! What is called taking Heaven as an exemplar and Earth as a model precisely demonstrates the sage’s skill in putting the Changes to use.

Book of Documents

The Emperor said: “Kui, I appoint you to direct music and instruct the sons of the nobility, so that they may be upright yet gentle, generous yet disciplined, firm without cruelty, and unassuming without arrogance. Poetry expresses intent; song prolongs the words; musical sounds follow that prolongation; the pitch standards harmonize the sounds. When the eight kinds of musical instruments sound in harmony, none disrupting the proper order of the others, spirits and human beings are thereby brought into harmony.”

Chen Ying

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭李批思致舂容而詞復清雅讀之洋洋然
其大䟦之音歟
考試官敎授夏批發虞廷育才之意殆盡
考試官敎授帥批詞理精切
聖君命大臣以樂爲敎因推樂之足以感焉甚
矣樂之所感者深也樂和而神人之和應之矣
何有于胄子之德哉帝舜因伯夷之讓而命夔
者如此若曰治以人才爲先而尤以敎化爲本
今此胄子行將有天下國家之責者也汝其爲
===
我典樂以敎之蓋人性不無氣稟之累而施敎
當有涵育之方要必本優柔之趣以養其中俾
直與寬者咸進于温栗而不至于偏焉可矣廣
易良之化以融其累俾剛與簡者弗失之傲虐
而不至于過焉可矣斯則有以成胄子中和之
德而樂之敎其庶矣乎然吾所以有取夫樂者
而豈徒哉亦以由人心生耳是故心有所之匪
詩莫宣也由是歌以永之而聲出焉聲有高下
匪律莫和也由是益之損之而樂成焉將見
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭李批：思致舂容，而詞復清雅，讀之洋洋然，其大䟦之音歟！
考試官敎授夏批：發虞廷育才之意殆盡。
考試官敎授帥批：詞理精切。
