聖君命大臣以樂爲敎，因推樂之足以感焉。甚矣，樂之所感者深也！樂和而神人之和應之矣，何有于胄子之德哉？帝舜因伯夷之讓而命夔者如此。若曰：「治以人才爲先，而尤以敎化爲本。今此胄子，行將有天下國家之責者也。汝其爲我典樂以敎之。蓋人性不無氣稟之累，而施敎當有涵育之方。要必本優柔之趣以養其中，俾直與寬者咸進于温栗，而不至于偏焉可矣；廣易良之化以融其累，俾剛與簡者弗失之傲虐，而不至于過焉可矣。斯則有以成胄子中和之德，而樂之敎其庶矣乎！然吾所以有取夫樂者，而豈徒哉？亦以由人心生耳。是故心有所之，匪詩莫宣也；由是歌以永之，而聲出焉。聲有高下，匪律莫和也；由是益之損之，而樂成焉。將見
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The conception is expansive and unhurried [?], and the language is also pure and elegant. Reading it, one feels its abundant flow. Is this the sound of the great ba [?]?”
Examiner Xia, Professor, comments: “It brings out almost fully the intention behind nurturing talent at Shun’s court.”
Examiner Shuai, Professor, comments: “The language and reasoning are refined and precise.”
The sage ruler commanded a great minister to use music in education, and then elaborated on music’s power to move its hearers. How profound is the influence of music! When music is harmonious, spirits and human beings respond in harmony. What difficulty, then, could there be in cultivating the virtue of the sons of the nobility? Such was Emperor Shun’s intention when, following Bo Yi’s yielding of the appointment, he commissioned Kui. It was as though he said:
“In government, talented men come first, and education and moral transformation are still more fundamental. These sons of the nobility will soon bear responsibility for the realm and its states and great households. Take charge of music for me, and use it to educate them. Human nature is not free from the encumbrances of one’s endowment of vital force, and education must have a means of nurturing it. One must draw upon music’s gentle and unhurried character to nourish their inner balance, enabling the straightforward and the generous alike to advance toward warmth and disciplined gravity, without becoming one-sided. One must extend its easy and kindly transforming influence to dissolve their encumbrances, enabling the firm and the simple to avoid falling into arrogance and cruelty, without going to excess. In this way the virtue of equilibrium and harmony can be perfected in the sons of the nobility, and education through music will come close to its aim!
“Yet surely my reason for valuing music is not without foundation? It is also because music arises from the human heart. Thus, when the heart tends toward something, only poetry can express it. Song then prolongs that expression, and musical sounds emerge. These sounds have their high and low pitches, and only the pitch standards can harmonize them. Through increasing and diminishing them, music is brought to completion. Then we shall see …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
音迭奏雍雍乎從律而不姦以薦郊廟一和氣
之所熏蒸也有時歆而罔時恫神且格之矣而
何有于胄子哉律呂相宣秩秩乎倫清而無僭
以奏朝廷一太和之所洋溢也羣后讓而庶尹
諧人且應之矣謂不足以敎胄子哉是蓋以其
生于人心者而感乎人心則其機易入而爲敎
易行也汝之章敎舍樂曷以哉雖然樂之足以
敎也固矣而德其本也重華之德既有以會聲
氣之元則九成之樂亦不過鳴其盛耳苟無平
===
中之德而徒事于聲器之末祗足爲導慾增悲
具也 此房中之奏開元之聲所以無裨於儲養
之敎
徽柔懿恭懷保小民惠鮮鰥寡自朝至于
日中昃不遑暇食用咸和萬民
許國誠
同考試官敎諭李 批 上下語意皆有淺深而發揮殆盡
其深於道者耶宜錄以式
考試官敎授夏 批 體認精切練士也
punctuated:
音迭奏，雍雍乎從律而不姦，以薦郊廟，一和氣之所熏蒸也。有時歆而罔時恫，神且格之矣，而何有于胄子哉？律呂相宣，秩秩乎倫清而無僭，以奏朝廷，一太和之所洋溢也。羣后讓而庶尹諧，人且應之矣，謂不足以敎胄子哉？是蓋以其生于人心者而感乎人心，則其機易入，而爲敎易行也。汝之章敎，舍樂曷以哉？雖然，樂之足以敎也固矣，而德其本也。重華之德既有以會聲氣之元，則九成之樂亦不過鳴其盛耳。苟無平中之德，而徒事于聲器之末，祗足爲導慾增悲具也。此房中之奏、開元之聲，所以無裨於儲養之敎。
徽柔懿恭，懷保小民，惠鮮鰥寡，自朝至于日中昃，不遑暇食，用咸和萬民。
許國誠
同考試官敎諭李批：上下語意皆有淺深，而發揮殆盡。其深於道者耶？宜錄以式。
考試官敎授夏批：體認精切，練士也。
translation_en:
…the tones sound in succession, harmoniously following the pitch standards without disorder. Offered at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, they are entirely suffused with harmonious vital energy. The spirits ever delight in them and are never distressed; if even the spirits respond, what difficulty could there be with the sons of the nobility? The yang and yin pitch standards complement one another, orderly and clearly distinguished, without encroachment. Performed at court, they overflow with supreme harmony. The assembled lords yield to one another, and the various officials act in concord. If people respond to them, can one say that they are insufficient to teach the sons of the nobility? This is because what arises from the human heart is used to move the human heart: its influence readily enters, and teaching through it is easily carried out. In making your teaching manifest, what could you employ if you abandoned music?
Nevertheless, although music is assuredly adequate for teaching, virtue is its foundation. Since the virtue of Chonghua [Shun] could unite the primal sources of sound and vital energy, the music in nine completed movements merely gave voice to his flourishing virtue. Without the virtue of balance and centrality, merely attending to the peripheral matters of sounds and instruments serves only to provide a means of inciting desires and increasing sorrow. This is why the performances of chamber music and the sounds of the Kaiyuan era contributed nothing to the education and nurture of the heir apparent.
“He was admirably gentle and beautifully reverent, cherishing and protecting the common people and showing kindness to the widowed and bereft. From morning until the sun had passed its zenith, he had no leisure to eat; thus he brought all the people into harmony.”
Xu Guocheng
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “The wording and meaning of both the upper and lower portions have shallower and deeper levels, and he has brought out nearly all of them. Is he not one who has penetrated deeply into the Way? This should be recorded as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Xia, Professor: “His understanding is refined and exact. He is a seasoned scholar.”

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授帥批雅暢不凡可取
觀聖王之本德以勤民而無逸之實見矣蓋聖
王仁民之心無窮也德以施之而勤以繼之其
無逸也為何如哉想周公告成王之意謂夫人
君以一身而居萬民之上則必以一心而切斯
民之憂固未嘗一日而忘于勤也我文王之無
逸豈特崇素儉已哉彼柔者容民之德也而徽
為難文王則至順所發不失于懦何徽柔焉恭
者臨民之德也而懿為難文王則至敬所形不
過乎禮何懿恭焉惟柔恭而有則故平易而近
民於小民則懷保之視之如傷而愛護以體其
情者何弗用也於鰥寡則惠鮮之哀其無告而
賙恤以厚其生者何弗至也文王以盛德而行
仁政如此而其心豈但已哉自朝至于日之中
自中至于日之昃退食有恒節矣而文王則有
所不暇焉惟以萬民廣矣其懷保之未及者何
限也汲汲焉覃仁以丕冒之俾咸囿于太和之
天斯已焉此其心固有惟日不足者而烏知時
punctuated:
考試官教授帥批：雅暢不凡，可取。

觀聖王之本德以勤民，而無逸之實見矣。蓋聖王仁民之心無窮也，德以施之，而勤以繼之，其無逸也為何如哉！想周公告成王之意，謂夫人君以一身而居萬民之上，則必以一心而切斯民之憂，固未嘗一日而忘于勤也。我文王之無逸，豈特崇素儉已哉！彼柔者，容民之德也，而徽為難。文王則至順所發，不失于懦，何徽柔焉！恭者，臨民之德也，而懿為難。文王則至敬所形，不過乎禮，何懿恭焉！惟柔恭而有則，故平易而近民。於小民則懷保之，視之如傷，而愛護以體其情者，何弗用也！於鰥寡則惠鮮之，哀其無告，而賙恤以厚其生者，何弗至也！文王以盛德而行仁政如此，而其心豈但已哉！自朝至于日之中，自中至于日之昃，退食有恒節矣，而文王則有所不暇焉。惟以萬民廣矣，其懷保之未及者何限也！汲汲焉覃仁以丕冒之，俾咸囿于太和之天斯已焉。此其心固有惟日不足者，而烏知時
translation_en:
Examiner Shuai, Professor, comments: Elegant, fluent, and outstanding; worthy of selection.

Observe how the sage king grounded himself in virtue and labored for the people: the reality of his freedom from ease becomes apparent. The sage king’s concern to treat the people humanely was inexhaustible. He put it into practice through virtue and sustained it through diligence. How complete was his refusal of ease! We may imagine the intention of the Duke of Zhou in admonishing King Cheng: a ruler, standing alone above the myriad people, must devote his whole heart to their troubles. Never for a single day could he forget diligent effort. Did our King Wen’s refusal of ease consist merely in esteeming simplicity and frugality?

Gentleness is the virtue by which one accommodates the people, but making it admirable is difficult. In King Wen, the expression of utmost mildness never lapsed into weakness. How admirable his gentleness! Reverence is the virtue by which one presides over the people, but making it excellent is difficult. In King Wen, the manifestation of utmost respect never exceeded ritual propriety. How excellent his reverence! Because his gentleness and reverence were governed by proper standards, he was approachable and close to the people. He cherished and protected the common people, regarding them as though they were injured. What means of loving and protecting them, with sympathetic understanding of their feelings, did he leave unused? He bestowed kindness upon widowers and widows and brought them relief, pitying them because they had no one to appeal to. To what lengths did he not go in aiding them and improving their livelihood?

Such was King Wen’s exercise of humane government through abundant virtue. Yet how could his heart rest content with this? From morning until noon, and from noon until the sun declined, there were fixed times to withdraw and eat; yet King Wen could find no leisure for it. He reflected that the people were so numerous: how many remained beyond the reach of his care and protection! He worked urgently to extend his benevolence and shelter them all, stopping only when all dwelt beneath a heaven of supreme harmony. His heart thus always felt that the day was insufficient; how could he be aware that the time …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
之當食哉萬民衆矣其有遺于惠鮮者何限也
汲汲焉布德以覆育之俾咸歸于和裕之域斯
已焉此其心固有一息匪懈者而遑食之計哉
夫文王之德已盛而心克勤心愈勤則其德益
盛此其所以紹抑畏之統而稱無逸之君今王
治文王之民寧不思法文王之勤歟論者謂無
逸一篇爲周家王業之本而八百之祚則自文
王啓之信矣然以成王基命宥密之主豈不知
勤政恤民者而周公拳拳以是告之無非慮其
===
幼冲而以其耳目所逮動之耳老成忠愛於此
可見
詩
鳳凰于飛翽翽其羽亦集爰止藹藹王多
吉士維君子使媚于天子鳳凰于飛翽
翽其羽亦傅于天藹藹王多吉人維君
子命媚于庶人鳳凰鳴矣于彼高岡梧
桐生矣于彼朝陽菶菶萋萋雝雝喈喈
林奇石
punctuated:
之當食哉！萬民衆矣，其有遺于惠鮮者何限也！汲汲焉布德以覆育之，俾咸歸于和裕之域斯已焉。此其心固有一息匪懈者，而遑食之計哉！夫文王之德已盛，而心克勤；心愈勤，則其德益盛。此其所以紹抑畏之統，而稱無逸之君。今王治文王之民，寧不思法文王之勤歟？論者謂《無逸》一篇爲周家王業之本，而八百之祚則自文王啓之，信矣！然以成王基命宥密之主，豈不知勤政恤民者？而周公拳拳以是告之，無非慮其幼冲，而以其耳目所逮動之耳。老成忠愛，於此可見。

詩

鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦集爰止。藹藹王多吉士，維君子使，媚于天子。鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦傅于天。藹藹王多吉人，維君子命，媚于庶人。鳳凰鳴矣，于彼高岡。梧桐生矣，于彼朝陽。菶菶萋萋，雝雝喈喈。

林奇石
translation_en:
…that it was time to eat? The myriad people were numerous: how many must still have been left without his kindness and relief! He urgently spread his beneficence to shelter and nurture them, resting only when all had entered a realm of harmony and abundance. His heart never slackened for even a single breath; how could he spare a thought for eating? King Wen’s virtue was already great, yet his heart remained diligent; the more diligent his heart, the greater his virtue became. This was how he carried on the tradition of restraint and reverence and earned the name of a ruler who took no ease. You, the present king, govern King Wen’s people: should you not think of emulating King Wen’s diligence? Those who discuss these matters call the chapter “Against Ease” the foundation of the Zhou royal enterprise and say that its eight hundred years of rule began with King Wen. Truly so! Yet King Cheng, a ruler who established the foundations of the mandate with magnanimity and quiet depth, surely understood diligence in government and solicitude for the people. The Duke of Zhou nevertheless earnestly admonished him on these matters, solely out of concern for his tender youth, seeking to move him through what he himself had heard and seen. Here we can discern an elder statesman’s loyalty and affection.

Book of Odes

The phoenixes fly,
their wings fluttering;
they gather and come to rest.
In great abundance, the king has many worthy officers;
the sovereign employs them,
and they are beloved of the Son of Heaven.
The phoenixes fly,
their wings fluttering;
they reach the heavens.
In great abundance, the king has many worthy men;
the sovereign commissions them,
and they are beloved of the common people.
The phoenixes call
upon that high ridge.
The wutong trees grow
on its sun-facing slope.
Luxuriant and flourishing,
harmonious and melodious.

Lin Qishi

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭趙批形容治世君臣之盛宛然在目
雅義之粹者也
考試官教授夏批發明召公寓諷之意殆盡
考試官教授帥批明暢工緻
詩人兩興賢才之嚮用而因喻明良之盛焉蓋
上不負君下不負民賢才嚮用之志則然也而
明良之際不因可觀其盛耶召康公戒成王之
意若謂聖君之於賢臣其義本相成而其遇甚
不偶也載觀王國夫豈乏人者哉彼鳳凰于飛
===
亦甞覽德輝而集爰止矣此藹藹王多吉士固
生此王國者也維君子有以使之則媚兹之懷
締焉而爲上爲德殆根於天性而不容已者矣
鳳凰于飛亦甞振羽儀而傅于天矣此藹藹王
多吉人固王國克生者也維君子有以命之則
綏懷之術顯焉而爲下爲民殆出於天衷而不
容遏者矣夫賢才願忠於王國如此則上下交
而理道隆者胥此矣其盛不有可言者哉彼鳳
凰之鳴非無所擇也希聲之發其惟千仞之表
punctuated:
同考試官教諭趙批：形容治世君臣之盛，宛然在目，雅義之粹者也。
考試官教授夏批：發明召公寓諷之意殆盡。
考試官教授帥批：明暢工緻。
詩人兩興賢才之嚮用，而因喻明良之盛焉。蓋上不負君，下不負民，賢才嚮用之志則然也，而明良之際，不因可觀其盛耶？召康公戒成王之意，若謂聖君之於賢臣，其義本相成，而其遇甚不偶也。載觀王國，夫豈乏人者哉？彼鳳凰于飛，亦甞覽德輝而集爰止矣。此藹藹王多吉士，固生此王國者也。維君子有以使之，則媚兹之懷締焉，而爲上爲德，殆根於天性而不容已者矣。鳳凰于飛，亦甞振羽儀而傅于天矣。此藹藹王多吉人，固王國克生者也。維君子有以命之，則綏懷之術顯焉，而爲下爲民，殆出於天衷而不容遏者矣。夫賢才願忠於王國如此，則上下交而理道隆者胥此矣。其盛不有可言者哉？彼鳳凰之鳴，非無所擇也。希聲之發，其惟千仞之表
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “The flourishing relations between ruler and ministers in an age of good government are depicted as vividly as if before our eyes. This captures the quintessence of the meaning of the Elegantiae.”
Comment by Examiner Xia, Professor: “It brings out almost fully the intent of the admonition that the Duke of Shao embedded in the poem.”
Comment by Examiner Shuai, Professor: “Lucid, fluent, skillful, and refined.”
The poet twice uses evocative imagery to express worthy men's desire to enter service, thereby illustrating the flourishing partnership of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers. For to fail neither their ruler above nor the people below is precisely the aspiration with which worthy men seek employment. Can we not thereby behold the flourishing relations between an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers? The intent with which Duke Kang of Shao admonished King Cheng seems to be this: a sage ruler and worthy ministers inherently complement one another in their duties, yet their encounter is far from a matter of chance. Looking upon the royal realm, could it possibly lack men of talent?
Those phoenixes in flight have indeed beheld the radiance of virtue and gathered there to rest. These abundant good officers of the king are men born in this very royal realm. If the lord has the means to employ them, their heartfelt attachment to him is secured; their service to their superior and to virtue [?] is rooted, it would seem, in their innate nature and cannot cease. The phoenixes in flight have also spread their splendid wings and reached the heavens. These abundant good men of the king are indeed men whom the royal realm has been able to produce. If the lord has the means to commission them, their methods of bringing peace and winning hearts become manifest; their service to those below, to the people, issues, it would seem, from their Heaven-endowed nature and cannot be restrained.
Such is the desire of worthy men to serve the royal realm loyally. Thus, the communion of those above and below and the flourishing of good government all derive from this. Is there not something to be said of such flourishing? Those phoenixes do not cry out without choosing their place. When their rare notes sound, must it be only beyond a height of a thousand ren…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
乎梧桐之生非無所自也靈根之托其惟明盛
之地乎惟生于朝陽也則蓁蓁焉萋萋焉本深
末茂足爲棲止之安如此乎嘉木之盛也而能
忘情於靈鳥耶惟鳴于高岡也則雝雝焉喈喈
焉氣和聲和足爲治世之音如此乎靈鳥之適
也而能自外於嘉木耶是知鳳凰梧桐物類之
相感也聖君賢臣理道之相成也然其機不在
鳳凰而在梧桐其具不在賢臣而在聖君吾王
可以深長思矣抑觀成王之時周召夾輔宇宙
===
太和萬世稱得人歌盛治者蔑以加矣而召公
何惓惓不置也蓋賢才難於布列老成宜於倚
毗倘人主親賢之念一或少忽則乘間抵隙比
暱交而德業隳矣此召公之所深憂也卷阿之
咏真善諷者與
有秩斯祜申錫無疆
林皆春
同考試官教諭趙批揄揚烈祖垂裕之遠根本功德
上來是善言頌義者
punctuated:
乎？梧桐之生，非無所自也，靈根之托，其惟明盛之地乎？惟生于朝陽也，則蓁蓁焉，萋萋焉，本深末茂，足爲棲止之安。如此乎嘉木之盛也，而能忘情於靈鳥耶？惟鳴于高岡也，則雝雝焉，喈喈焉，氣和聲和，足爲治世之音。如此乎靈鳥之適也，而能自外於嘉木耶？是知鳳凰梧桐，物類之相感也；聖君賢臣，理道之相成也。然其機不在鳳凰而在梧桐，其具不在賢臣而在聖君，吾王可以深長思矣。抑觀成王之時，周召夾輔，宇宙太和，萬世稱得人、歌盛治者，蔑以加矣。而召公何惓惓不置也？蓋賢才難於布列，老成宜於倚毗。倘人主親賢之念一或少忽，則乘間抵隙，比暱交而德業隳矣。此召公之所深憂也。《卷阿》之咏，真善諷者與！

有秩斯祜，申錫無疆。
林皆春
同考試官教諭趙批：揄揚烈祖垂裕之遠，根本功德上來，是善言頌義者。
translation_en:
…is it not? Nor does the parasol tree grow without a source: surely its wondrous roots take hold in a bright and flourishing place? Growing on a sun-facing slope, it is luxuriant and thick with foliage; its roots are deep and its branches flourish, offering a secure place to roost. Such is the flourishing of this splendid tree: could it remain indifferent to the numinous bird? Calling upon a high ridge, the bird sings harmoniously and melodiously; its vital spirit and its voice are in harmony, fit to provide the music of a well-governed age. Such is the contentment of the numinous bird: could it keep itself apart from the splendid tree? Thus we know that the phoenix and the parasol tree exemplify the mutual responsiveness of living things, while the sage ruler and worthy ministers exemplify mutual fulfillment in the way of good government. Yet the crucial impulse lies with the parasol tree, not the phoenix; the means lie with the sage ruler, not the worthy ministers. Our king should ponder this deeply.

Consider, moreover, the time of King Cheng: the Dukes of Zhou and Shao assisted him on either side, and supreme harmony prevailed throughout the world. In all subsequent ages, those praising the securing of worthy men and celebrating flourishing government have found nothing to surpass it. Why, then, did the Duke of Shao remain so tirelessly solicitous? Worthy men are difficult to establish throughout the offices, and seasoned elders deserve reliance and support. Should the ruler relax even slightly in his resolve to draw close to the worthy, others will seize an opening and exploit a weakness; cliques and favorites will join forces, and his moral achievements will fall into ruin. This was the Duke of Shao’s profound concern. The song “Winding Mound” (Juan A) truly exemplifies skillful indirect admonition!

“Enduring are these blessings, bestowed again without limit.”
Lin Jiechun
Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “He extols how far the illustrious ancestor’s abundant legacy extends, grounding his argument in meritorious deeds and virtue. This is a skillful exposition of the meaning of the hymn.”

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授夏批得詩人登歌之意
考試官敎授帥批簡古
詩人祀聖祖而頌其垂裕之遠焉蓋先王以裕
後爲福也功德如成湯而所被寧有窮耶此祀
成湯之樂也若曰帝王以萬世爲業則必以萬
世爲福而有不能者功德限之也我祖成湯佑
啓後人者豈其微哉是故聖敬日躋烈祖之德
與天同運者也是以天心克享畀之祜以光其
德者秩然宏遠之規模焉爰革夏正烈祖之功
===
永世無極者也是以帝命不易隆之祜以昭其
功者秩然恒久之氣象焉弘一統以開天受祉
旣多也而且孔厚也申錫之爲後人之令緒而
何有於終窮式九圍以基命發祥旣遠也而且
甚長也申錫之爲後人之保極而何有於限量
以延曆數之傳豈徒一世二世已乎近之而子
子而又子以似以續有常享焉百代之休光此
固爲之伊始矣以衍靈長之運豈但一傳再傳
已乎遠之而孫孫而又孫繼體承祧有常保焉
punctuated:
考試官敎授夏批：得詩人登歌之意。
考試官敎授帥批：簡古。
詩人祀聖祖而頌其垂裕之遠焉。蓋先王以裕後爲福也，功德如成湯，而所被寧有窮耶？此祀成湯之樂也。若曰：帝王以萬世爲業，則必以萬世爲福，而有不能者，功德限之也。我祖成湯，佑啓後人者，豈其微哉？是故聖敬日躋，烈祖之德，與天同運者也。是以天心克享，畀之祜以光其德者，秩然宏遠之規模焉。爰革夏正，烈祖之功，永世無極者也。是以帝命不易，隆之祜以昭其功者，秩然恒久之氣象焉。弘一統以開天，受祉旣多也，而且孔厚也；申錫之爲後人之令緒，而何有於終窮？式九圍以基命，發祥旣遠也，而且甚長也；申錫之爲後人之保極，而何有於限量？以延曆數之傳，豈徒一世二世已乎？近之而子，子而又子，以似以續，有常享焉。百代之休光，此固爲之伊始矣。以衍靈長之運，豈但一傳再傳已乎？遠之而孫，孫而又孫，繼體承祧，有常保焉。
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Xia, Instructor: “This captures the poet’s intention in the hymn sung at the sacrifice.”
Comment by Examiner Shuai, Instructor: “Concise and antique in style.”
The poet sacrifices to the sage ancestor and praises the enduring bounty he bequeathed. For the former kings regarded providing abundantly for their descendants as blessedness. With achievements and virtue such as Cheng Tang’s, could their beneficent reach ever end? This is the music for sacrificing to Cheng Tang. It speaks as if to say: emperors and kings take ten thousand generations as the scope of their undertaking, and must therefore also take ten thousand generations as the scope of their blessings. Where they fail to achieve this, the limits lie in their achievements and virtue. Could the protection and guidance our ancestor Cheng Tang afforded his descendants have been slight?
Thus, his sagely reverence rose daily: the illustrious ancestor’s virtue moved in concert with Heaven. Hence Heaven’s heart accepted his offerings, bestowing blessings to glorify his virtue in an ordered pattern, vast and far-reaching. He then changed the Xia calendar: the illustrious ancestor’s achievement would endure forever without limit. Hence the Supreme Lord’s mandate remained unchanged, heaping blessings upon him to manifest his achievement in an ordered prospect of enduring constancy.
He enlarged the unified realm and inaugurated a new heavenly dispensation. The blessings he received were already numerous, and moreover exceedingly abundant. Bestowed again and again, they became a splendid inheritance for his descendants—how could they ever be exhausted? He ordered the nine regions and established the mandate. The auspicious beginnings already reached far back, and moreover would endure far into the future. Bestowed again and again, they enabled his descendants to preserve the supreme standard—how could they be bounded or measured?
In prolonging the transmission of the allotted dynastic succession, could this have been merely for one generation or two? In the nearer line came sons, and sons after sons, following and continuing their forebears, perpetually enjoying these blessings. The glorious prosperity of a hundred generations assuredly had its beginning here. In extending the dynasty’s numinous and enduring fortune, could this have been merely for one transmission or two? In the more distant line came grandsons, and grandsons after grandsons, succeeding to the ancestral position and inheriting the ancestral temple, perpetually preserving these blessings.…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
萬年之景命此固為之肇端矣蓋豐功無窮則
休澤亦無窮駿德常在則福慶亦常在今日之
祭誠莫非烈祖之申錫者而敢忘所自哉抑聞
之先王法度不可廢德澤不可恃商之孫子豈
念不及此哉吾觀武丁孫子皆能恭默其心悠
久其德而祀事之脩則又孚之天人盡之志物
和之節奏以答先祖申錫之仁此所以必得其
福而庶幾於賢者之祭歟
春秋
===
春王正月公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯
許男曹伯侵蔡蔡潰遂伐楚次于陘〔僖公四年〕冬公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒
子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子
光伐鄭十有二月已亥同盟于戲〔襄公九年〕夏公會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷〔定公十年〕
周良寅
同考試官教諭朱 批 王霸服人德力自是不同茲作
punctuated:
萬年之景命，此固為之肇端矣。蓋豐功無窮，則休澤亦無窮；駿德常在，則福慶亦常在。今日之祭，誠莫非烈祖之申錫者，而敢忘所自哉？抑聞之：先王法度不可廢，德澤不可恃。商之孫子，豈念不及此哉？吾觀武丁孫子，皆能恭默其心，悠久其德；而祀事之脩，則又孚之天人，盡之志物，和之節奏，以答先祖申錫之仁。此所以必得其福，而庶幾於賢者之祭歟！

春秋

春，王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。〔僖公四年〕冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。十有二月，已亥，同盟于戲。〔襄公九年〕夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。〔定公十年〕

周良寅

同考試官教諭朱批：王霸服人，德力自是不同。茲作
translation_en:
…This indeed laid the foundation for the glorious mandate lasting ten thousand years. For when great achievements are inexhaustible, their beneficent blessings are likewise inexhaustible; when grand virtue endures, good fortune and felicity likewise endure. The sacrifices offered today truly all derive from the illustrious ancestor’s repeatedly bestowed gifts. How could one dare forget their source? Yet I have heard that the former kings’ laws and institutions must not be abandoned, and that one must not simply rely upon the blessings of their virtue. Could the descendants of Shang have failed to consider this? I observe that Wu Ding’s descendants could all keep their hearts reverent and still, and make their virtue enduring. In conducting sacrifices, moreover, they established trust with Heaven and humankind, fully expressed their intentions and furnished their offerings, and harmonized the musical rhythms, thereby requiting their ancestors’ benevolence in repeatedly bestowing gifts. Is this not why they were certain to receive blessings and came close to performing the sacrifices of the worthy?

Spring and Autumn Annals

In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao in invading Cai. Cai collapsed. They then attacked Chu and encamped at Xing. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi〕 In winter, the duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Xiao Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, in attacking Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the yihai day [?], they jointly concluded a covenant at Xi. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xiang〕 In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu. 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding〕

Zhou Liangyin

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “The kingly and hegemonic ways of securing people’s submission differ inherently in their use of virtue and force. This composition…”

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
於均善中而屬詞寓意甚得經㫖
同考試官敎授吳批善為國者惟執禮以化强是作
獨歸美聖績而詞㫖明切宜錄以式
考試官敎授夏批詞簡意足經義優長
考試官敎授帥批精健不繁得謹嚴體
春秋紀内外制敵之善所以昭王事也此桓悼
之善師善陣雖不逮孔子之不師乃君子猶有
取焉彼詐而捷也何為哉昔齊人伐魯魯也禦
之曹劌效謀長勺敗焉而春秋深以為魯罪者
===
何君子曰是不聞待敵有道乎彼為國不師上
矣此王事也其次有善師而不陣者又其次有
善陣而不戰者不觀之桓悼孔子乎以桓言之
方其伐楚也兵連八國潰首蔡師剪而食以逞
君心似無有難者乃桓則不然責問以包茅王
祭辱貺以徼好同心陘亭次而屈完惠來益顯
實征之績矣師旅雖勤行伍未列不其善師乎
然猶未免於師也以悼言之方其伐鄭也鄭疑
未同楚爭益競戰而捷以長諸侯似不可緩者
punctuated:
於均善中，而屬詞寓意甚得經㫖。
同考試官敎授吳批：善為國者，惟執禮以化强。是作獨歸美聖績，而詞㫖明切，宜錄以式。
考試官敎授夏批：詞簡意足，經義優長。
考試官敎授帥批：精健不繁，得謹嚴體。
春秋紀内外制敵之善，所以昭王事也。此桓、悼之善師善陣，雖不逮孔子之不師，乃君子猶有取焉。彼詐而捷也，何為哉？昔齊人伐魯，魯也禦之，曹劌效謀，長勺敗焉，而春秋深以為魯罪者何？君子曰：是不聞待敵有道乎？彼為國不師，上矣，此王事也。其次有善師而不陣者，又其次有善陣而不戰者。不觀之桓、悼、孔子乎？以桓言之，方其伐楚也，兵連八國，潰首蔡師，剪而食以逞君心，似無有難者。乃桓則不然，責問以包茅王祭，辱貺以徼好同心，陘亭次而屈完惠來，益顯實征之績矣。師旅雖勤，行伍未列，不其善師乎？然猶未免於師也。以悼言之，方其伐鄭也，鄭疑未同，楚爭益競，戰而捷以長諸侯，似不可緩者。
translation_en:
…among works that are all good, its phrasing and the meaning conveyed accord particularly well with the purport of the Classic.
Associate Examiner Wu, an Instructor, comments: Those skilled in governing a state hold fast to ritual propriety to transform the powerful. This composition gives particular praise to the achievements of the sage. Its language and meaning are clear and incisive; it should be recorded as a model.
Examiner Xia, an Instructor, comments: Concise in wording and full in meaning, it excels in interpreting the Classic.
Examiner Shuai, an Instructor, comments: Refined and vigorous without prolixity, it achieves a careful and disciplined style.
The Spring and Autumn Annals records successful ways of subduing enemies, both within and outside Lu, in order to make manifest the work of true kingship. Thus, although the skill of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Dao of Jin in deploying armies and arranging battle formations fell short of Confucius’s avoidance of military mobilization altogether, the gentleman still finds something worthy in them. What worth, then, is there in gaining victory through deception? Formerly, the men of Qi attacked Lu, and Lu resisted them. Cao Gui offered his counsel, and Qi was defeated at Changshao. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals lay such grave blame upon Lu?
The gentleman says: Have you not heard that there is a proper way to deal with an enemy? To govern a state without mobilizing an army is the highest achievement: this is the work of true kingship. Next come those who deploy armies well without drawing up battle formations; next again come those who arrange formations well without engaging in battle. Can we not observe these principles in Duke Huan, Duke Dao, and Confucius?
Consider Duke Huan. When he attacked Chu, he joined the forces of eight states and first routed the army of Cai. Cutting down and devouring the enemy to gratify his own desires as ruler would seemingly have presented no difficulty. Yet Duke Huan did otherwise. He demanded an explanation concerning the bundled mao grass required for the king’s sacrifices, and graciously bestowed favors to seek friendship and concord [?]. He encamped at Xingting, and Qu Wan graciously came to him, further demonstrating the achievements of a genuine punitive expedition. Though the troops had labored, their ranks had not been drawn up for battle. Was this not skillful deployment of an army? Yet it still did not dispense with military mobilization.
Consider Duke Dao. When he attacked Zheng, Zheng remained hesitant and had not joined the alliance, while Chu contended ever more fiercely. To fight and win, thereby securing leadership over the regional lords, seemed to brook no delay…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
乃悼則不然謀深於息民固本力全於分銳逆
來剽門次而子騑趨盟坐收三駕之功矣威武
雖揚兵刃未接不其善陣乎然猶未免于陣也
以孔子言之方夾谷之會也犁彌倡謀禍且不
測魯蓋岌岌矣幸而孔子以禮義相焉責之以
干盟偪好懼之以棄德不祥齊能無屈乎由是
敵國謝過而好會用成萊兵阻却而策勳飮至
戰陣固不足道師亦將焉用之不其善國耶夫
是之謂王者之事待敵之道斯其至矣彼二伯
===
者在桓猶爲近正在悼巳云德衰乃今詐而捷
如魯焉不獨孔子之罪人抑亦桓悼之罪人矣
此長勺之役必主魯以深責之歟抑桓悼之伯
仲筦之謀也二君能庸之尚足以取伯定威夫
子以綏來動和之聖有變齊變魯之機而卒以
女樂去焉固不待權臣竊命而巳知定之無能
爲也嗚呼歸三田墮三都孔子豈二臣所敢班
而定乃不桓悼若焉蓋君臣相遇之難抑世道
汙隆之運歟
punctuated: 乃悼則不然，謀深於息民固本，力全於分銳逆來。剽門次而子騑趨盟，坐收三駕之功矣。威武雖揚，兵刃未接，不其善陣乎？然猶未免于陣也。以孔子言之，方夾谷之會也，犁彌倡謀，禍且不測，魯蓋岌岌矣。幸而孔子以禮義相焉，責之以干盟偪好，懼之以棄德不祥，齊能無屈乎？由是敵國謝過，而好會用成；萊兵阻却，而策勳飮至。戰陣固不足道，師亦將焉用之？不其善國耶？夫是之謂王者之事，待敵之道斯其至矣。彼二伯者，在桓猶爲近正，在悼巳云德衰。乃今詐而捷如魯焉，不獨孔子之罪人，抑亦桓悼之罪人矣。此長勺之役必主魯以深責之歟？抑桓悼之伯，仲筦之謀也。二君能庸之，尚足以取伯定威。夫子以綏來動和之聖，有變齊變魯之機，而卒以女樂去焉。固不待權臣竊命，而巳知定之無能爲也。嗚呼！歸三田，墮三都，孔子豈二臣所敢班？而定乃不桓悼若焉。蓋君臣相遇之難，抑世道汙隆之運歟？
translation_en:
…Yet Duke Dao acted otherwise. His plans looked deeply to giving the people respite and securing the foundations of the state; he preserved his strength by dividing his elite troops to meet the approaching enemy. He encamped at Piaomen, and Zifei hastened to conclude a covenant: thus he secured the achievement of three successive campaigns. Although his military might was displayed, weapons had not crossed. Was he not skilled at deploying an army? Yet he still could not dispense with deployment.

As for Confucius, at the meeting at Jiagu, Li Mi proposed a plot whose disastrous consequences could not be foreseen, and Lu was indeed in grave danger. Fortunately, Confucius assisted his ruler through ritual propriety and righteousness. He reproached the men of Qi for violating the covenant and coercing a friendly state, and intimidated them by warning that abandoning virtue would bring misfortune. Could Qi fail to yield? Consequently, the rival state apologized for its wrongdoing, and the friendly meeting was successfully concluded. The troops of Lai were held back, and achievements were recorded and celebrated with the ceremonial banquet upon returning. Battle and deployment were scarcely worth discussing; what need was there even to mobilize an army? Was he not skilled at governing a state? This is what is meant by the work of a true king: the way of dealing with an enemy here reached its highest point.

Of those two hegemons, Duke Huan still came close to uprightness, while with Duke Dao virtue was already said to have declined. Now, to gain victory through deceit, as Lu did, was to stand condemned not only before Confucius, but even before Dukes Huan and Dao. Is this why the account of the battle of Changshao necessarily makes Lu the principal party, in order to censure it severely?

Moreover, the hegemonies of Huan and Dao rested on the plans of Zhong and Guan. Because the two rulers could employ them, they were still able to attain hegemony and establish their authority. The Master was a sage who could bring others to him by giving them peace and move them to harmony. He had the opportunity to transform Qi and Lu, yet in the end he departed because of the female musicians. Even without waiting for powerful ministers to usurp sovereign authority, one could already see that Duke Ding was incapable of accomplishing anything.

Alas! In securing the return of the three territories and dismantling the fortifications of the three cities, how could those two ministers presume to rank alongside Confucius? Yet Duke Ding did not measure up to Huan and Dao. Was this because it is so difficult for ruler and minister to find their proper counterparts, or was it the course of the age, with its alternations of decline and flourishing?

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
六月齊侯來獻戎捷莊公三十有一年
楊日采
同考試官教諭朱批霸者毎喜功尚誇聖門羞稱茲作
發明題旨透徹無餘錄之
同考試官教授吳批經抑桓之矜功由惡桓之略遠詞
極簡嚴意尤明確
考試官教授夏批意精式合取之
考試官教授帥批發勤兵矜功意最精
霸主矜略遠之功春秋所以抑之也甚矣功不
===
足矜也而况略遠之功乎此齊桓之獻戎捷春
秋卑辭以抑之與甞聞軍獲曰捷捷而致之於
君曰獻魯齊匹耳北戎病燕桓師往正而遺俘
于魯乃春秋書曰來獻宛然以下奉上之辭何
哉王者之道覲文德而匿武功崇退讓而恥誇
大故倖功勤遠者治之蠹飾虛凌人者德之慙
君子無取焉淺哉桓仲之于戎也伐而捷捷而
獻何爲哉忽内治而不脩動衆勤民旣以逞心
於漠北之虜棄禮讓而不顧恫疑恐喝更欲誇
punctuated:
六月，齊侯來獻戎捷。莊公三十有一年。
楊日采
同考試官教諭朱批：「霸者毎喜功尚誇，聖門羞稱。茲作發明題旨，透徹無餘，錄之。」
同考試官教授吳批：「經抑桓之矜功，由惡桓之略遠。詞極簡嚴，意尤明確。」
考試官教授夏批：「意精式合，取之。」
考試官教授帥批：「發勤兵矜功意最精。」
霸主矜略遠之功，春秋所以抑之也。甚矣，功不足矜也！而况略遠之功乎？此齊桓之獻戎捷，春秋卑辭以抑之與？甞聞軍獲曰捷，捷而致之於君曰獻。魯齊匹耳，北戎病燕，桓師往正，而遺俘于魯，乃春秋書曰「來獻」，宛然以下奉上之辭，何哉？王者之道，覲文德而匿武功，崇退讓而恥誇大。故倖功勤遠者，治之蠹；飾虛凌人者，德之慙。君子無取焉。淺哉，桓仲之于戎也！伐而捷，捷而獻，何爲哉？忽内治而不脩，動衆勤民，旣以逞心於漠北之虜；棄禮讓而不顧，恫疑恐喝，更欲誇
translation_en:
“In the sixth month, the Marquis of Qi came to present spoils captured from the Rong.” Thirty-first year of Duke Zhuang.
Yang Ricai.
Associate Examiner Zhu, an Instructor, comments: “Hegemons invariably delight in achievements and prize boasting, which the Confucian school is ashamed to commend. This composition elucidates the meaning of the topic thoroughly, leaving nothing unexplained. Include it.”
Associate Examiner Wu, a Professor, comments: “The Classic disparages Duke Huan’s boasting of his achievements because it condemns his campaigning in distant regions. The language is exceptionally concise and rigorous, and the meaning particularly clear.”
Examiner Xia, a Professor, comments: “The conception is refined and the form appropriate. Accept it.”
Examiner Shuai, a Professor, comments: “Its exposition of the ideas of exhausting troops and boasting of achievements is especially incisive.”
The hegemon boasted of his achievements in campaigning in distant regions: this is why the Spring and Autumn Annals disparages him. How utterly unworthy of boasting are achievements—even more so achievements in distant campaigns! Is this why, in recording Duke Huan of Qi’s presentation of spoils from the Rong, the Spring and Autumn Annals uses language that lowers his standing to disparage him? I have heard that what an army captures is called ‘spoils,’ and bringing those spoils to one’s ruler is called ‘presenting.’ Lu and Qi were merely peers. The Northern Rong troubled Yan; Duke Huan’s army went to chastise them and sent captives to Lu. Yet the Spring and Autumn Annals records this as ‘came to present,’ unmistakably using the language of an inferior offering something to a superior. Why?
The way of a true king is to display civil virtue and conceal military achievements, to honor modest deference and regard boasting as shameful. Thus those who seek achievements through luck and expend their strength on distant campaigns are a blight upon good government; those who embellish empty pretensions to overawe others bring shame upon virtue. The gentleman finds nothing in them to commend.
How shallow were Duke Huan and Guan Zhong in their dealings with the Rong! They attacked and took spoils; having taken spoils, they presented them. What were they seeking? Neglecting domestic government and failing to put it in order, they mobilized the multitude and wearied the people, already indulging their desires against the captives north of the desert. Casting aside ritual propriety and deference without a thought, intimidating through uncertainty and threats, they further wished to boast…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
示乎東蒙之君豈知地列要荒疆理所不及也
伐之已黷武矣乃復震而矜焉不已甚乎古人
以隕淵之心而居已成之功桓其識之耶寇非
門庭利禦所弗用也伐之已不祥矣乃復挾而
驕焉能無愧乎古人以不伐之心而消爭能之
妬桓其知之耶君子謂是舉也柔懷之道闕而
未聞侈耀之心蕩而莫制安得比於采芑之奏
功泮水之獻馘哉故齊魯非君臣也乃卑辭以
抑之而書來獻云此義行而勤兵遠略好大喜
功者戒矣抑此桓仲之謀也蓋楚近而山戎遠
楚難而山戎易也先其近而易者以折諸侯之
心則楚不待兵而服矣此其酌緩急識機宜以
雄起伯桓仲亦人傑也惜其王道未聞而持盈
之戒不講遂令戎捷之張為首伯累自是而濤
塗執九國叛威名亦少損矣噫玆桓仲之所以
止于桓仲與
禮記
詩云肅雝和鳴先祖是聽夫肅肅敬也雝
punctuated:
示乎東蒙之君。豈知地列要荒，疆理所不及也？伐之已黷武矣，乃復震而矜焉，不已甚乎？古人以隕淵之心而居已成之功，桓其識之耶？寇非門庭，利禦所弗用也。伐之已不祥矣，乃復挾而驕焉，能無愧乎？古人以不伐之心而消爭能之妬，桓其知之耶？君子謂是舉也，柔懷之道闕而未聞，侈耀之心蕩而莫制，安得比於《采芑》之奏功、《泮水》之獻馘哉？故齊魯非君臣也，乃卑辭以抑之，而書「來獻」云。此義行，而勤兵遠略、好大喜功者戒矣。抑此桓仲之謀也。蓋楚近而山戎遠，楚難而山戎易也。先其近而易者以折諸侯之心，則楚不待兵而服矣。此其酌緩急、識機宜以雄起伯，桓仲亦人傑也。惜其王道未聞，而持盈之戒不講，遂令戎捷之張為首伯累。自是而濤塗執，九國叛，威名亦少損矣。噫！玆桓仲之所以止于桓仲與！

禮記

《詩》云：「肅雝和鳴，先祖是聽。」夫肅肅，敬也；雝
translation_en:
…to make a display before the ruler of Dongmeng. How could he understand that these lands lay in the remote outer domains, beyond the reach of territorial administration? Attacking them was already an abuse of arms; then to overawe others and boast of it—was this not excessive? The ancients held their accomplished successes with the apprehension of falling into an abyss. Did Duke Huan understand this? The raiders were not at his gates, so the principle that it is advantageous to resist invaders did not apply. Attacking them was already inauspicious; then to use that victory as grounds for arrogance—could he be without shame? The ancients dispelled the jealousy arising from rivalry in ability by refraining from boasting. Did Duke Huan know this? The gentleman judges that in this undertaking the way of winning distant peoples over through kindness was absent and unheard of, while the impulse toward extravagant display ran unchecked. How could this compare with the achievement celebrated in “Gathering Millet” (Cai qi), or the presentation of severed enemy ears in “Waters of the Pan” (Pan shui)? Thus, although Qi and Lu were not ruler and subject, the Spring and Autumn Annals employed language of subordination to censure Qi, recording that it “came to present” the captives. When this principle is upheld, those who exhaust their armies in distant conquests and delight in grand undertakings and military achievements will take warning.

Yet this was the strategy of Duke Huan and Guan Zhong. Chu was near and the Shanrong far away; Chu was difficult to subdue and the Shanrong easy. By first dealing with those who were near and easy to subdue [?], they would break the resolve of the regional lords, and Chu would submit without the use of troops. In thus weighing urgency and timing, and recognizing opportunities to rise powerfully to hegemony, Duke Huan and Guan Zhong were indeed outstanding men. Regrettably, they had not learned the Way of the Kings or studied the admonition to preserve success by guarding against excess. Consequently, their flaunting of victory over the Rong became a blemish upon the foremost hegemon. Thereafter Taotu was seized and the nine states rebelled, somewhat diminishing their awe-inspiring reputation. Alas! Is this why Duke Huan and Guan Zhong advanced no further than they did?

Record of Rites (Li ji)

The Odes says: “Reverently and harmoniously they sing together; the ancestors hear them.” Now, “reverently” means respect; “harmoniously”…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
雝和也夫敬以和何事不行
余一愚
同考試官教諭王批和敬二字多泥樂音上說是作
獨推本大當大定處來最得肯綮錄之
同考試官學正黃批正樂感通之旨體認既真敷詞
自別當是作手
考試官教授夏批迥異諸作
考試官教授帥批雅健
賢者引言古樂之正而裕於用焉蓋萬事莫不
===
以和敬爲本也古樂兼之其裕於用也宜哉此
子夏釋詩以告文侯有曰先王作樂固將以致
用也而用之有弗宜者以音之不古若耳乃古
樂則何如耶夫聲音之感至微也鬼神之幽至
難格也詩曰肅雝和鳴先祖是聽是果何以致
之哉彼云肅肅者非無謂也言是樂也自紀綱
大定之時而中聲巳肇是故爲莊誠爲勁正其
極天下之至敬者耶曰雝雝者非無謂也言是
樂也自大化均調之日而元聲巳諧是故爲寬
punctuated:
雝，和也。夫敬以和，何事不行？
余一愚
同考試官教諭王批：和敬二字，多泥樂音上說。是作獨推本大當大定處來，最得肯綮，錄之。
同考試官學正黃批：正樂感通之旨，體認既真，敷詞自別，當是作手。
考試官教授夏批：迥異諸作。
考試官教授帥批：雅健。
賢者引言古樂之正，而裕於用焉。蓋萬事莫不以和敬爲本也，古樂兼之，其裕於用也宜哉！此子夏釋詩以告文侯有曰：先王作樂，固將以致用也，而用之有弗宜者，以音之不古若耳。乃古樂則何如耶？夫聲音之感至微也，鬼神之幽至難格也。詩曰：「肅雝和鳴，先祖是聽。」是果何以致之哉？彼云肅肅者，非無謂也。言是樂也，自紀綱大定之時，而中聲巳肇，是故爲莊誠，爲勁正，其極天下之至敬者耶？曰雝雝者，非無謂也。言是樂也，自大化均調之日，而元聲巳諧，是故爲寬
translation_en:
…“Yong” means harmony. With reverence joined to harmony, what undertaking will not succeed?

Yu Yiyu

Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “In discussing the two words ‘harmony’ and ‘reverence,’ most writers remain confined to musical sounds. This essay alone traces them back to the point at which the great order was firmly established [?]. It grasps the essential point most precisely. Include it.”

Associate Examiner Huang, School Director, comments: “The meaning of correct music’s power to move and communicate with spirits is truly understood; the expression is consequently distinctive. This must be an accomplished writer.”

Examiner Xia, Professor, comments: “Far different from the other compositions.”

Examiner Shuai, Professor, comments: “Elegant and vigorous.”

The worthy cites words concerning the correctness of ancient music and its ample efficacy in practice. All undertakings take harmony and reverence as their foundation. Ancient music combines both: how fitting that its efficacy should be so ample! Thus Zixia, explaining the Odes to Marquis Wen, says: The former kings created music precisely to put it to use. When its use proves unsuitable, this is merely because its sounds do not match those of antiquity. What, then, was ancient music like? The influence of sounds is exceedingly subtle, and ghosts and spirits, in their hidden realm, are exceedingly difficult to reach. The Odes says: “Solemn and harmonious, the sounds blend; the ancestors listen.” How indeed was this achieved? The words “solemn, solemn” are not without meaning. They mean that, in this music, balanced tones had already arisen from the time when the guiding principles of order were firmly established. Hence its solemn sincerity and firm rectitude: does it not embody the utmost reverence under Heaven? The words “harmonious, harmonious” are not without meaning. They mean that, in this music, the primal tones had already attained harmony from the day when the great transforming influence became evenly attuned. Hence its generous…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
裕焉順成其極天下之至和者耶夫匪敬則流
匪和則離事之所以不行也玆惟敬而且和則
整肅之中而有優游者在施之隨事而皆宜端
嚴之內而有和平者存措之無往而弗利以之
篤近而身可脩家可齊焉德音之發越殆不止
於一身之咸淑矣先祖聽之云乎哉以之舉遠
而天下可平焉正樂之感通殆不止於四國之
克順矣祭祀用之云乎哉夫曰敬而且和則感
之也爲有本曰何事不行則用之也爲無方德
===
音異於溺音信矣抑有疑焉惠王有世俗之慙
孟子告以今樂同於古文侯有鄭衞之聽子夏
告以古樂異於今何哉蓋言同者所以啓其偕
樂之情言異者所以抑其新聲之好也奈何雅
俗迭陳而正樂卒爲淫哇所勝文侯猶之惠王
焉則鍾聲左高之辨亦不過鏗鏘音韻之末耳
噫吾於是而知梁魏均不足以有爲而和樂之
興必有所待也
子曰君子不以辭盡人故天下有道則行
punctuated:
裕焉，順成，其極天下之至和者耶？夫匪敬則流，匪和則離，事之所以不行也。玆惟敬而且和，則整肅之中而有優游者在，施之隨事而皆宜；端嚴之內而有和平者存，措之無往而弗利。以之篤近，而身可脩、家可齊焉，德音之發越殆不止於一身之咸淑矣，先祖聽之云乎哉？以之舉遠，而天下可平焉，正樂之感通殆不止於四國之克順矣，祭祀用之云乎哉？夫曰敬而且和，則感之也爲有本；曰何事不行，則用之也爲無方。德音異於溺音，信矣！抑有疑焉：惠王有世俗之慙，孟子告以今樂同於古；文侯有鄭衞之聽，子夏告以古樂異於今，何哉？蓋言同者，所以啓其偕樂之情；言異者，所以抑其新聲之好也。奈何雅俗迭陳，而正樂卒爲淫哇所勝！文侯猶之惠王焉，則鍾聲左高之辨，亦不過鏗鏘音韻之末耳。噫！吾於是而知梁魏均不足以有爲，而和樂之興必有所待也。

子曰：「君子不以辭盡人。」故天下有道，則行
translation_en:
…expansive and bringing things harmoniously to completion: does it not embody the utmost harmony under Heaven? Without reverence, things lapse into excess; without harmony, they fall apart. This is why affairs fail to proceed. Here, however, reverence and harmony coexist: within order and solemnity there is ease, so that its application suits every affair; within dignity and gravity there is peaceful harmony, so that wherever it is employed, it brings benefit. Used to strengthen relationships close at hand, it enables one to cultivate oneself and regulate one’s family. The far-reaching resonance of virtuous music surely does more than make one’s own person wholly good. Can its effect be described merely as “the ancestors listen to it”? Used to reach those far away, it enables one to bring peace to all under Heaven. The power of proper music to move and communicate surely does more than bring the lands of the four quarters into obedience. Can its function be described merely as “it is used in sacrifices”? To say that it is reverent and harmonious means that its power to move has a foundation; to ask “What affair will not proceed?” means that its applications have no bounds. Virtuous music is indeed different from music that leads one astray!

Yet there is a doubt. King Hui was ashamed of his taste for popular music, and Mengzi told him that modern music was the same as ancient music. Marquis Wen listened to the music of Zheng and Wei, and Zixia told him that ancient music differed from modern music. Why? Speaking of their sameness was a means of awakening the king’s desire to share his enjoyment with others; speaking of their difference was a means of restraining the marquis’s fondness for new tunes. How was it, then, that refined and vulgar music were presented in turn, yet proper music was ultimately overcome by licentious, bawling sounds? Marquis Wen was just like King Hui. His discernment that the bells on the left were higher in pitch amounted to no more than attention to the trifles of ringing tones and musical sounds. Alas! From this I know that neither Liang nor Wei was capable of accomplishing anything, and that the flourishing of harmonious music would have to await its time.

The Master said: “The gentleman does not judge a person wholly by his words.” Thus, when the Way prevails under Heaven, conduct…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
有枝葉
莊履豐
同考試官教諭王批言不煩而意自足殆能芟去枝葉
者可式可式
同考試官學正黃批用意切實而文足以發之經義
之最佳者
考試官教授夏批講尚行處明淨
考試官教授帥批精到
惟觀人不盡於言此盛世必尚乎行也甚矣言
===
可以觀人而不可以盡人也故行為治世之所
尚有以哉想夫子之意豈不曰好尚有關乎氣
運言行視世為重輕使言而足以盡人謂其為
治世之所重可也而孰知有不然者何也言者
心之聲心未易測君子固嘗緣聲以探其微而
辭者德之華德鮮克舉君子未嘗因華而忘其
實以一言之庶幾而遽信其由衷焉此安知非
色莊者而君子弗盡與也以一時之議論而遂
槩其為人焉此安知能持久者而君子弗盡信
punctuated:
有枝葉。
莊履豐
同考試官教諭王批：言不煩而意自足，殆能芟去枝葉者，可式，可式。
同考試官學正黃批：用意切實，而文足以發之，經義之最佳者。
考試官教授夏批：講尚行處明淨。
考試官教授帥批：精到。
惟觀人不盡於言，此盛世必尚乎行也。甚矣，言可以觀人，而不可以盡人也！故行為治世之所尚，有以哉！想夫子之意，豈不曰：好尚有關乎氣運，言行視世為重輕。使言而足以盡人，謂其為治世之所重，可也。而孰知有不然者？何也？言者，心之聲，心未易測，君子固嘗緣聲以探其微；而辭者，德之華，德鮮克舉，君子未嘗因華而忘其實。以一言之庶幾，而遽信其由衷焉，此安知非色莊者？而君子弗盡與也。以一時之議論，而遂槩其為人焉，此安知能持久者？而君子弗盡信
translation_en:
…has branches and leaves.

Zhuang Lüfeng

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: His words are not prolix, yet their meaning is complete. He has indeed managed to prune away the branches and leaves. Worthy of imitation, worthy of imitation!

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, School Director: The conception is pertinent and substantial, and the writing adequately expresses it. Among the very best interpretations of the Classics.

Comment by Examiner Xia, Professor: The discussion of valuing conduct is clear and lucid.

Comment by Examiner Shuai, Professor: Precise and penetrating.

Since words cannot exhaust what one may discern about a person, a flourishing age must esteem conduct. How true it is that words allow one to assess a person, yet cannot reveal that person fully! There is good reason, then, for conduct to be esteemed in a well-governed age. If we imagine the Master's meaning, would it not be this: what people favor bears upon the fortunes of the age, and the relative weight accorded to words and conduct varies with the times. If words sufficed to reveal a person fully, one could rightly say that they should carry weight in a well-governed age. Yet who realizes that this is not so? Why is this? Words are the voice of the heart. Since the heart is not easily fathomed, the gentleman has indeed sought to trace that voice to its hidden subtleties. But expressions are the blossoms of virtue. Since virtue is seldom fully realized, the gentleman has never allowed its blossoms to make him forget its fruit. If a single utterance comes close to what is right, and one immediately trusts that it comes from the heart, how can one know that the speaker is not merely solemn in appearance? Thus the gentleman does not grant him unqualified approval. If, on the basis of a discussion on one occasion, one proceeds to judge his character as a whole, how can one know that he can sustain it over time? Thus the gentleman does not place complete trust…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
也夫辭之不可盡人如此詎以治世而復尚辭
耶故天下之有道也天子公卿躬行於上聿崇
實勝之風百官萬民敦行於下自妙默成之化
樹德之本植於中者既裕矣斯英華發於和順
而敷之經綸者奕奕焉蓋根本盛而枝葉自茂也
彼靜言庸違者其能復容於斯世哉敦化之基
涵於內者既厚矣斯輝光奮於篤實而發之事
業者亹亹焉蓋植本固而枝葉自敷也彼佞言
無當者尚能自容於斯時哉吁治世尚行如此
===
則言之不足盡人益可徵矣君子其慎諸雖然
言不可尚而亦不可廢也行所當崇而亦不可
偏也以辭盡人夫子既致警矣而子貢問君子
復以先行後從告之迺知浮靡之習固不可長
而訥言敏行尤君子大中之道也否則刻意尚
行將流於賢者之過豈盛世所宜有哉故他日
又曰君子言必慮其所終行必稽其所敝
第貳場
論
punctuated:
也。夫辭之不可盡人如此，詎以治世而復尚辭耶？故天下之有道也，天子公卿躬行於上，聿崇實勝之風；百官萬民敦行於下，自妙默成之化。樹德之本，植於中者既裕矣，斯英華發於和順，而敷之經綸者奕奕焉，蓋根本盛而枝葉自茂也。彼靜言庸違者，其能復容於斯世哉？敦化之基，涵於內者既厚矣，斯輝光奮於篤實，而發之事業者亹亹焉，蓋植本固而枝葉自敷也。彼佞言無當者，尚能自容於斯時哉？吁！治世尚行如此，則言之不足盡人益可徵矣。君子其慎諸！雖然，言不可尚，而亦不可廢也；行所當崇，而亦不可偏也。以辭盡人，夫子既致警矣，而子貢問君子，復以先行後從告之。迺知浮靡之習固不可長，而訥言敏行尤君子大中之道也。否則，刻意尚行，將流於賢者之過，豈盛世所宜有哉？故他日又曰：「君子言必慮其所終，行必稽其所敝。」

第貳場

論
translation_en:
…Words are thus incapable of fully revealing a person. Could one nevertheless esteem words in a well-governed age? Hence, when the Way prevails throughout the realm, the Son of Heaven, the dukes, and the ministers personally put it into practice above, promoting a prevailing regard for substance; the hundred officials and the myriad people earnestly practice it below, bringing about the subtle transformation that is accomplished without words. Once the roots of virtue planted within are abundant, their finest blossoms emerge in harmony and accord, and shine brilliantly when extended to ordering the world. When the roots flourish, the branches and leaves naturally thrive. Could those whose words are fine but whose deeds run counter to them still find acceptance in such an age? Once the foundation of profound transforming influence nurtured within is substantial, its radiance springs forth from sincerity and solidity, manifesting itself in tireless achievement. When the roots are firmly planted, the branches and leaves naturally spread. Could those whose glib words have no substance still find a place in such a time? Ah! Since a well-governed age esteems conduct in this way, it is all the more evident that words cannot fully reveal a person. Let the gentleman be cautious about this!

Nevertheless, although words must not be prized above all else, neither may they be discarded; although conduct should be honored, neither may it be pursued one-sidedly. The Master had already warned against judging a person entirely by his words; and when Zigong asked about the gentleman, he further told him to act first and let his words follow. Thus we know that habits of superficiality and extravagance must certainly not be encouraged, while being slow to speak and prompt to act is especially the gentleman’s way of the great mean. Otherwise, deliberately exalting conduct would lead to the excesses of the worthy. Could this be fitting in a flourishing age? Thus, on another occasion, he also said: “In speaking, the gentleman must consider the eventual outcome; in acting, he must examine the abuses to which his actions may lead.”

Second Session

Discourse

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖人一天人賛化育之道
林奇石
同考試官教諭李批律本處作者類多未達是
篇直指本原究極功用末復歸重上非平日潜心律吕
者不能到此
同考試官學正龍批格調髙古而迂迴曲折不失矩
矱可以式多士矣
考試官教授夏批有學識有力量
考試官教授帥批充贍不浮
===
作樂者其有所本乎得其本而功化神矣甚矣
樂之爲道難言也而其所可見者不能有外於
聲氣然聲者其迹也氣者其幾也不泥其迹不
滯其幾而直求夫聲氣之元者樂之本也本也
者吾心中和之理是也以吾心自然之理而寄
諸器數聲容之間則器數者樂也而莫非此心
之寓也聲容者樂也而莫非此心之顯也以吾
心之中而感中以吾心之和而召和則盈宇宙
間皆無有鬱而不通滯而不宣之情而位育之
punctuated:
聖人一天人賛化育之道
林奇石

同考試官教諭李批：律本處，作者類多未達。是篇直指本原，究極功用，末復歸重上，非平日潜心律吕者不能到此。
同考試官學正龍批：格調髙古，而迂迴曲折不失矩矱，可以式多士矣。
考試官教授夏批：有學識，有力量。
考試官教授帥批：充贍不浮。

作樂者，其有所本乎？得其本而功化神矣。甚矣，樂之爲道難言也！而其所可見者，不能有外於聲氣。然聲者，其迹也；氣者，其幾也。不泥其迹，不滯其幾，而直求夫聲氣之元者，樂之本也。本也者，吾心中和之理是也。以吾心自然之理，而寄諸器數聲容之間，則器數者，樂也，而莫非此心之寓也；聲容者，樂也，而莫非此心之顯也。以吾心之中而感中，以吾心之和而召和，則盈宇宙間，皆無有鬱而不通、滯而不宣之情，而位育之
translation_en:
The Way by Which the Sage Unites Heaven and Humanity and Assists Transformation and Nurture
By Lin Qishi

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Most writers have failed to grasp the point concerning the foundation of the pitch standards. This essay points directly to their fundamental source and thoroughly explores their efficacy, finally returning its emphasis to the ruler [?]. Only someone who has habitually devoted himself to studying the pitch standards could attain this level.

Comment by Associate Examiner Long, Assistant Instructor: Its style is lofty and antique. Through all its winding turns, it never departs from proper standards. It can serve as a model for the many candidates.

Comment by Examiner Xia, Professor: It possesses learning and discernment, as well as force.

Comment by Examiner Shuai, Professor: Full and ample, without superficiality.

Must those who create music have some foundation on which to base it? When they grasp that foundation, its efficacy in transforming becomes wondrous. How difficult it is indeed to speak of the Way of music! What can be perceived of it cannot extend beyond sound and vital force. Yet sound is its outward trace, and vital force its incipient impulse. To cling neither to its trace nor to its impulse, but to seek directly the source of sound and vital force: this is to seek the foundation of music. That foundation is the principle of equilibrium and harmony within our own minds. When we lodge the natural principle of our minds in instruments and numerical measures, sounds and ceremonial movements, the instruments and measures constitute music, and all are repositories of this mind; the sounds and movements constitute music, and all are manifestations of this mind. Through the equilibrium of our minds, we evoke equilibrium; through the harmony of our minds, we summon harmony. Then, throughout the universe, no feeling remains pent up without passage or obstructed without expression, and the transformation through which all things take their proper places and receive nurture…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
化在是矣其斯以爲一天人賛化育之道與請
因蔡氏之言而論之嘗觀之易曰大哉乾元萬
物資始至哉坤元萬物資生此天人化育之妙
也樂者器也而黃鍾者又樂之一也執一音而
曰可以一天人賛化育然則黃鍾與天地齊乎
君子曰以黃鍾言黃鍾器數焉耳安得與天地
齊耶然窮其元識其情達其順而究其極則黃
鍾之理一天地之理也何也天地當六陰極剥
之時一陽萌動於地雷之復自此而歷臨泰壯
===
夬至乾爲左行之陽歷姤遯否觀至坤爲右轉
之陰所以妙出入而神闔闢者復之一陽肇之
也其天地中和之心乎律始黃鍾作樂者蓋亦
以吾心之復準天地之復而制之中制之和者
也自此太簇至中吕爲下生之陽蕤賓至應鍾
爲上生之陰上生六而倍之下生六而損之其
律十二其調六十其實一黃鍾也蓋黃者中之
色也鍾種也陽氣潜萌於黃宫而萬物萌孽於
此也言中而和也故在律則稱母在象則稱君
punctuated:
化在是矣。其斯以爲一天人、賛化育之道與？請因蔡氏之言而論之。嘗觀之《易》曰：「大哉乾元，萬物資始！至哉坤元，萬物資生！」此天人化育之妙也。樂者，器也，而黃鍾者又樂之一也。執一音而曰可以一天人、賛化育，然則黃鍾與天地齊乎？君子曰：「以黃鍾言黃鍾，器數焉耳，安得與天地齊耶？然窮其元，識其情，達其順，而究其極，則黃鍾之理，一天地之理也。」

何也？天地當六陰極剥之時，一陽萌動於地雷之復，自此而歷臨、泰、壯、夬，至乾，爲左行之陽；歷姤、遯、否、觀，至坤，爲右轉之陰。所以妙出入而神闔闢者，復之一陽肇之也。其天地中和之心乎？律始黃鍾，作樂者蓋亦以吾心之復準天地之復，而制之中、制之和者也。自此太簇至中吕，爲下生之陽；蕤賓至應鍾，爲上生之陰。上生六而倍之，下生六而損之，其律十二，其調六十，其實一黃鍾也。蓋黃者，中之色也；鍾，種也。陽氣潜萌於黃宫，而萬物萌孽於此也。言中而和也，故在律則稱母，在象則稱君。
translation_en:
…the transforming work through which all things find their proper places and flourish lies herein. Might this be the way to unite Heaven and humanity and assist transformation and nurture? Allow me to discuss this on the basis of Master Cai’s words. I have read in the Book of Changes: “Great indeed is the primal power of Qian! All things depend upon it for their beginning. Consummate indeed is the primal power of Kun! All things depend upon it for their birth.” Here lies the wonder of transformation and nurture in Heaven and humanity. Music belongs to the realm of instruments, and Huangzhong—the Yellow Bell pitch—is but one constituent of music. If one takes a single note and says that it can unite Heaven and humanity and assist transformation and nurture, does this mean that Huangzhong stands equal to Heaven and Earth? The gentleman replies: “Considered merely as Huangzhong, it is nothing more than an instrument and its numerical measures. How could it stand equal to Heaven and Earth? Yet if we fathom its origin, comprehend its true nature, understand its orderly course, and investigate its ultimate reach, then the principle of Huangzhong is one with the principle of Heaven and Earth.”

Why is this so? When Heaven and Earth reach the stage at which the six yin lines have brought stripping-away to its utmost, a single yang begins to stir in Fu, Return, with Earth above Thunder. From this point, the sequence passes through Lin, Approach; Tai, Peace; Zhuang, Great Strength; and Guai, Breakthrough, reaching Qian, the Creative: this is yang proceeding to the left. It passes through Gou, Encounter; Dun, Withdrawal; Pi, Obstruction; and Guan, Contemplation, reaching Kun, the Receptive: this is yin turning to the right. The single yang of Return initiates the wondrous movement outward and inward and the numinous closing and opening. Is this not the heart of equilibrium and harmony in Heaven and Earth? The pitch standards begin with Huangzhong. Those who create music likewise take the return within our own hearts and align it with the return in Heaven and Earth, thereby establishing music in equilibrium and harmony. From here, Taicu through Zhonglü constitute the yang pitches generated downward; Ruibin through Yingzhong constitute the yin pitches generated upward. The six upward generations double the measure, while the six downward generations diminish it [?]. There are twelve pitch standards and sixty modes, yet in substance they are all the single Huangzhong. For yellow is the color of the center, and zhong, “bell,” means zhong, “seed.” Yang energy sprouts unseen in the Yellow Palace, and here the myriad things bud and shoot. This expresses equilibrium together with harmony. Thus, among the pitch standards it is called the mother; among the images, it is called the ruler.

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
一黃鍾定而樂之道無餘矣嗚呼天地養此微
陽以成化育之功人心養此微陽以成中和之
樂天地也吾心也黃鍾也通一而無二者也聖
人之心與天地陰陽相爲脗合而或順而喜或
拂而怒或觸而哀或感而樂莫非造化自然之
中而一毫無所乖戾焉則天人化育之理旣巳
涵蓄於聖人之心而聲氣之元自我而會其全
矣由是以之候氣而氣應焉以之調聲而聲和
焉紀之以三而天人化育之理洩於三也成之
===
以六而天人化育之理宣於六也統之以十二
分之以六十四而天人化育之理寄於律調也
驗之以二變輔之以半倍而天人化育之理有
以通其窮相其不及也不特此也由是奏諸廟
朝則天神降地祗出庶尹諧而莫非此心自然
之中和感之也由是孚乎民物則湮鬱宣淫慝
消民無札瘥物無疵癘而莫非此心自然之中
和育之也由是通乎天地則日月順軌雨暘若
時無霜雹之災無童涸之患休氣旁流於宇宙
punctuated: 一黃鍾定，而樂之道無餘矣。嗚呼！天地養此微陽，以成化育之功；人心養此微陽，以成中和之樂。天地也，吾心也，黃鍾也，通一而無二者也。聖人之心與天地陰陽相爲脗合，而或順而喜，或拂而怒，或觸而哀，或感而樂，莫非造化自然之中，而一毫無所乖戾焉。則天人化育之理旣巳涵蓄於聖人之心，而聲氣之元自我而會其全矣。由是，以之候氣而氣應焉，以之調聲而聲和焉。紀之以三，而天人化育之理洩於三也；成之以六，而天人化育之理宣於六也；統之以十二，分之以六十四，而天人化育之理寄於律調也；驗之以二變，輔之以半倍，而天人化育之理有以通其窮，相其不及也。不特此也。由是奏諸廟朝，則天神降，地祗出，庶尹諧，而莫非此心自然之中和感之也。由是孚乎民物，則湮鬱宣，淫慝消，民無札瘥，物無疵癘，而莫非此心自然之中和育之也。由是通乎天地，則日月順軌，雨暘若時，無霜雹之災，無童涸之患，休氣旁流於宇宙
translation_en:
Once Huangzhong, the Yellow Bell pitch, is established, nothing in the Way of music remains unaccounted for. Ah! Heaven and Earth nurture this faint yang to accomplish their work of transforming and nourishing; the human heart nurtures this faint yang to achieve the music of equilibrium and harmony. Heaven and Earth, my heart, and Huangzhong are united as one, without duality. The sage’s heart accords with the yin and yang of Heaven and Earth. Whether pleased by favorable circumstances, angered by opposition, saddened by what touches it, or gladdened by what moves it, it invariably observes the natural equilibrium of creation, without the slightest deviation. Thus the principles of transformation and nurture in Heaven and humanity are already contained within the sage’s heart, and the primal source of sound and vital energy attains its full unity within oneself. Hence, when this is used to ascertain the vital energy, that energy responds; when it is used to tune sounds, those sounds harmonize. Ordered by three, the principles of transformation and nurture in Heaven and humanity are revealed in three; completed by six, those principles are manifested in six. Unified in twelve and divided into sixty-four, those principles reside in the pitch standards and modes. Tested through the two altered notes and supplemented by halving and doubling, those principles provide a means to overcome impasses and make good deficiencies.

Nor is this all. When music is thus performed in ancestral temples and at court, the celestial spirits descend, the earthly spirits emerge, and the various officials act in harmony: all are moved by this heart’s natural equilibrium and harmony. When it thus reaches the people and other living things, what is pent up finds release and depravity disappears; the people suffer neither premature death nor sickness, and other living things suffer neither defects nor pestilence. All are nurtured by this heart’s natural equilibrium and harmony. When it thus communicates with Heaven and Earth, the sun and moon follow their proper courses, rain and sunshine arrive in season, there are no disasters of frost or hail, no afflictions of barren growth or dried-up waters, and auspicious vital energy flows throughout the cosmos…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
而亦莫非此心自然之中和順之也不特此也
推此而大章大韶以賛協和風動之化者其允
執厥中之心爲之而此心一中和也推此而大
夏大濩以賛平成允殖之化者其祗台日躋之
心爲之而此心一中和也推此而大武以賛四
海永清之化者其敬勝義勝之心爲之而此心
一中和也樂而至是則乾元之所不能始者有
以發其始坤元之所不能終者有以成其終熏
烝透徹莫非氣也欣喜歡暢莫非聲也渾渾乎
===
===
雝雝乎而昔之所謂率舞來儀者亦自此而致
之矣而聖人一天人賛化育者其孰有外於此
心哉抑于是而知以黍求尺以尺生律者之謬
也易曰雷出地奮豫先王以作樂崇德豫也者
言人心之悅也孔氏曰人而不仁如樂何仁也
者言吾心之正也此樂之原也若反之吾心而
正求之民心而悅而所謂鍾律秬黍之制雖循
器以求之可也舍器以求之亦可也否則雖使
后夔典音太師審樂斷竹飛灰尺寸矩度絲毫
punctuated: 而亦莫非此心自然之中和順之也。不特此也，推此而大章、大韶以賛協和風動之化者，其允執厥中之心爲之，而此心一中和也。推此而大夏、大濩以賛平成允殖之化者，其祗台日躋之心爲之，而此心一中和也。推此而大武以賛四海永清之化者，其敬勝義勝之心爲之，而此心一中和也。樂而至是，則乾元之所不能始者，有以發其始；坤元之所不能終者，有以成其終。熏烝透徹，莫非氣也；欣喜歡暢，莫非聲也。渾渾乎，雝雝乎，而昔之所謂率舞來儀者，亦自此而致之矣。而聖人一天人、賛化育者，其孰有外於此心哉？抑于是而知以黍求尺、以尺生律者之謬也。《易》曰：「雷出地奮，豫。先王以作樂崇德。」豫也者，言人心之悅也。孔氏曰：「人而不仁，如樂何？」仁也者，言吾心之正也。此樂之原也。若反之吾心而正，求之民心而悅，而所謂鍾律秬黍之制，雖循器以求之可也，舍器以求之亦可也。否則，雖使后夔典音，太師審樂，斷竹飛灰，尺寸矩度，絲毫
translation_en:
…and all this, too, is brought into accord by the natural equilibrium and harmony of this heart. Nor is this all. Extending this principle, the Great Manifestation (Dazhang) and Great Shao (Dashao) aided a transforming influence that brought concord and moved people as the wind moves things. This was accomplished by the heart that sincerely held fast to the Mean; and this heart was wholly equilibrium and harmony. Extending it further, the Great Xia (Daxia) and Great Hu (Dahu) aided a transforming influence that brought the land into order and enabled things to flourish. This was accomplished by the heart expressed in “I shall be reverent” and “daily ascent”; and this heart was wholly equilibrium and harmony. Extending it further, the Great Martial Dance (Dawu) aided a transforming influence that brought lasting peace within the Four Seas. This was accomplished by the heart in which reverence and righteousness prevailed; and this heart was wholly equilibrium and harmony.

When music reaches this point, it can initiate what the primal power of Heaven cannot initiate, and bring to completion what the primal power of Earth cannot complete. All that warms, permeates, and penetrates is vital energy; all that expresses joy, delight, and gladness is sound. Vast and flowing, harmonious and concordant! What the ancients called the beasts “all dancing” and the phoenixes “coming in stately bearing” is likewise brought about through this. When the sage unites Heaven and humanity and assists their transforming and nurturing work, what could lie outside this heart?

From this we also recognize the error of those who use millet grains to determine the foot measure and use that measure to generate the pitch standards. The Book of Changes says: “Thunder emerges from the earth and stirs: Enthusiasm. The former kings accordingly made music to exalt virtue.” Enthusiasm speaks of the human heart’s delight. Confucius said: “If a man lacks benevolence, what can he do with music?” Benevolence speaks of the rectitude of one’s own heart. This is the source of music. If we turn back to our own hearts and find rectitude, and look to the people’s hearts and find delight, then, as for the prescribed arrangements of bells, pitch standards, and black millet, it is permissible to seek them through the instruments, and also permissible to seek them apart from the instruments. Otherwise, even if Hou Kui were put in charge of musical tones and the Grand Music Master examined the music, with bamboo cut into pitch pipes and ashes flying from them, with every foot and inch, every rule and measure, to the slightest degree…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
不失古人之舊而曰吾能樂焉君子猶以爲德
之慙也彼妄意郊廟之音希心參摹之書者又
烏足以語此
表
擬
大閱禮成廷臣
賀表
周良寅
同考試官教諭趙批文非雕繪事極詳明宛然若
===
親扈
鑾輿而有得者是足以華
國矣錄之
同考試官教授吳批以駢麗之詞形容
張皇之典而能刋落浮華其工於四六者
考試官教授夏批詞語豐腴體裁端重
考試官教授帥批麗而典可誦
隆慶三年九月二十一日具官臣某等恭遇
皇上大閱禮成謹奉
punctuated:
不失古人之舊，而曰吾能樂焉，君子猶以爲德之慙也。彼妄意郊廟之音、希心參摹之書者，又烏足以語此？

表

擬大閱禮成廷臣賀表

周良寅

同考試官教諭趙批：文非雕繪，事極詳明，宛然若親扈鑾輿而有得者，是足以華國矣，錄之。

同考試官教授吳批：以駢麗之詞形容張皇之典，而能刋落浮華，其工於四六者。

考試官教授夏批：詞語豐腴，體裁端重。

考試官教授帥批：麗而典，可誦。

隆慶三年九月二十一日，具官臣某等恭遇皇上大閱禮成，謹奉
translation_en:
…without departing in the slightest from the ancient practices, and yet declare, “I understand music,” the gentleman would still regard this as a cause for shame concerning one’s virtue. As for those who entertain idle notions about the music of the suburban and ancestral-temple sacrifices and set their hopes on books of consultation and imitation [?], how could they be fit to discuss this?

Memorial

A hypothetical congratulatory memorial from the court officials upon completion of the Grand Military Review

Zhou Liangyin

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “The writing does not depend on ornamentation, and the matters are presented with the utmost detail and clarity. It is just as though the author had personally accompanied the imperial carriage and gained insight from the occasion. This is sufficient to bring distinction to the state. Include it in the record.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Professor: “He uses elegant parallel prose to portray a ceremony of imposing grandeur, yet manages to prune away superficial embellishment. He is skilled in prose of four- and six-character phrases.”

Comment by Examiner Xia, Professor: “The language is rich and full; the form is dignified and grave.”

Comment by Examiner Shuai, Professor: “Elegant and classically grounded; worthy of recitation.”

On the twenty-first day of the ninth month of the third year of Longqing [1569], your servants, so-and-so and others, holding their respective offices, respectfully mark the completion of Your Majesty’s Grand Military Review and reverently present…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
表稱
賀者伏以
哲王制治以保邦恒切無虞之儆
盛世經文而緯武式基有道之長
虎帳天開一代
皇靈丕振
龍輿雲擁百年
曠典維新
朝野歡騰華夷慶洽臣等誠欣誠抃稽首頓
===
首竊惟煦育震曜乾坤運二氣以迭施順
治威嚴帝王兼五材而竝用敷文而有苗
旣格尚嚴猾夏之防愼德而四夷咸賓猶
謹詰戎之戒逮伍兩軍師之制設兵政愈
詳暨蒐苗獮狩之禮行軍容益壯從醜載
歌吉日選徒則賦車攻自周而還此禮幾
墜勞軍營壘棘門之兒戲何裨習射殿廷
渭水之狼烽莫殄豈如
昭代聿創
punctuated:
表稱賀者，伏以：哲王制治以保邦，恒切無虞之儆；盛世經文而緯武，式基有道之長。虎帳天開，一代皇靈丕振；龍輿雲擁，百年曠典維新。朝野歡騰，華夷慶洽。臣等誠欣誠抃，稽首頓首。
竊惟煦育震曜，乾坤運二氣以迭施；順治威嚴，帝王兼五材而竝用。敷文而有苗旣格，尚嚴猾夏之防；愼德而四夷咸賓，猶謹詰戎之戒。逮伍兩軍師之制設，兵政愈詳；暨蒐苗獮狩之禮行，軍容益壯。從醜載歌《吉日》，選徒則賦《車攻》。自周而還，此禮幾墜。勞軍營壘，棘門之兒戲何裨；習射殿廷，渭水之狼烽莫殄。豈如昭代聿創
translation_en:
…present this memorial of congratulation, humbly reflecting that enlightened kings establish government to safeguard the realm, ever mindful of warnings even when no danger threatens; flourishing ages weave civil governance together with military preparedness, thereby laying the foundation for the enduring rule of the Way. The imperial military pavilion opens beneath Heaven, and the sovereign’s majesty is mightily displayed throughout this age; clouds cluster about the dragon carriage, and a grand ceremony seldom seen in a hundred years is renewed. Court and countryside rejoice; Chinese and foreign peoples alike share in the celebration. We, your servants, truly rejoice and clap our hands with delight, bowing our heads to the ground and kowtowing.
We humbly consider that, in nurturing warmth and awe-inspiring force, Heaven and Earth wield the two vital energies in alternation; in orderly governance and stern authority, emperors and kings employ the five materials together. Though the spread of civil virtue had brought the Youmiao into submission, precautions against those who would disturb the Chinese realm remained strict; though care for virtue had brought the peoples of the four quarters to pay homage, the injunction to maintain military preparedness was still scrupulously observed. Once the system of military units—wu, liang, jun, and shi—was established, military administration became increasingly detailed; when the seasonal hunting rites of sou, miao, xian, and shou were performed, military displays grew still more imposing. Pursuing herds of game was celebrated in “Auspicious Day”; selecting troops was commemorated in “Chariots Well Equipped.” Since the Zhou, this ceremony had all but fallen into disuse. What benefit came from visiting troops in their camps, when the camp at Jimen was mere child’s play? Archery practice in the palace courts failed to extinguish the beacon fires of invasion along the Wei River. How could these compare with our illustrious dynasty, which first established …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
弘規
制定五軍列貔貅七十二衞營名三大置將領
千八百員義略倣乎府兵法實沿於司馬
不獨安內而攘外實以居重而馭輕頃緣
昇平漸至怠弛事關
國計慮切
宸衷鑒於
祖憲以裁成斷自
廟謨而振舉茲蓋伏遇
===
皇帝陛下
聰明天縱
仁孝夙成
纘令緒以重光神人協應
凝洪圖而丕赫述作兼隆
郊祀同
廟饗時親式重明禋之典
常朝與
講筵日御務隆延訪之誠顧文治之既新念武
punctuated:
弘規，制定五軍，列貔貅七十二衞；營名三大，置將領千八百員。義略倣乎府兵，法實沿於司馬。不獨安內而攘外，實以居重而馭輕。頃緣昇平，漸至怠弛，事關國計，慮切宸衷。鑒於祖憲以裁成，斷自廟謨而振舉。
茲蓋伏遇皇帝陛下，聰明天縱，仁孝夙成。纘令緒以重光，神人協應；凝洪圖而丕赫，述作兼隆。郊祀同廟饗時親，式重明禋之典；常朝與講筵日御，務隆延訪之誠。顧文治之既新，念武
translation_en:
…a grand design: the system established the Five Armies, arraying tiger-like warriors in seventy-two guards; the camps were designated the Three Great Camps, with eighteen hundred commanders appointed. In conception, this broadly followed the garrison militia system (fubing); its regulations in fact derived from those of the Minister of War (Sima). It served not only to secure the interior and repel external threats, but also to concentrate strength at the center and thereby control the lesser forces elsewhere. Recently, prolonged peace had gradually brought laxity. Since this affected the affairs of state, it weighed deeply upon the imperial mind. Taking the ancestral institutions as a guide, Your Majesty fashioned appropriate measures; through decisions made in the imperial council, you restored their vigor.
Now we humbly find ourselves under Your Majesty the Emperor, endowed by Heaven with intelligence and discernment, and possessed from youth of benevolence and filial devotion. Continuing the glorious succession, you have renewed its radiance, with spirits and men responding in harmony; consolidating the grand imperial undertaking, you have made it splendid, flourishing alike in carrying on inherited institutions and creating new ones. You personally attend the suburban sacrifices and the offerings in the ancestral temple at their appointed seasons, thus honoring the rites of pure sacrifice. You preside daily at regular court audiences and the imperial lectures, earnestly seeking to consult and inquire. Seeing that civil governance has been renewed, you reflect upon military…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
功之當競廼因輔臣之
請肆脩
大閱之儀序屬金行時維農隙諏良辰以青
龍之吉闢正位于玄武之墟
葆蓋出天閽擁千官而雲連玉珮
翠華臨日觀望六師而氣吐金霓走風伯以
清塵先雨師而灑道千旗雲引牙前停
王者之屬車萬戟霜飛幕下止
聖人之清蹕鳴鐃擊鐸各備厥官太常大綏咸
===
若其制
令下而喧聲頓肅營營若海靜山空旗舉而猛
氣倍增人人似鷹揚鷙擊刁斗鳴而風煙
起節旄指而瘴霧開右虎左龍雜鵝鸛魚
麗而互變中權後勁錯龜蛇鳥隼以相生
捲甲歸營禮終八陣陳侯立的藝閱三軍
士卒則列署分掄競逐穿楊之步將帥乃
登臺親簡爭喧落鴈之聲戎行整而喜動
天顏
punctuated:
功之當競，廼因輔臣之請，肆脩大閱之儀。序屬金行，時維農隙，諏良辰以青龍之吉，闢正位于玄武之墟。葆蓋出天閽，擁千官而雲連玉珮；翠華臨日觀，望六師而氣吐金霓。走風伯以清塵，先雨師而灑道。千旗雲引，牙前停王者之屬車；萬戟霜飛，幕下止聖人之清蹕。鳴鐃擊鐸，各備厥官；太常大綏，咸若其制。
令下而喧聲頓肅，營營若海靜山空；旗舉而猛氣倍增，人人似鷹揚鷙擊。刁斗鳴而風煙起，節旄指而瘴霧開。右虎左龍，雜鵝鸛魚麗而互變；中權後勁，錯龜蛇鳥隼以相生。捲甲歸營，禮終八陣；陳侯立的，藝閱三軍。士卒則列署分掄，競逐穿楊之步；將帥乃登臺親簡，爭喧落鴈之聲。戎行整而喜動天顏。
translation_en:
…military achievements ought to be pursued with vigor. Thus, at the request of his assisting ministers, he performed the ceremonies of a grand military review. The season belonged to Metal, and it was a lull in agricultural work. An auspicious day was chosen under the favorable sign of the Azure Dragon, and the imperial station was established in the precinct of the Dark Warrior.
The imperial canopy emerged from Heaven’s gate, surrounded by a thousand officials whose jade pendants stretched like banks of clouds. The kingfisher-feather standard approached the sun-viewing height; overlooking the Six Armies, its majesty breathed forth a golden rainbow. The Wind Lord was dispatched to clear the dust, and the Rain Master sent ahead to sprinkle the road. A thousand banners led onward like clouds; before the commander’s standard halted the sovereign’s attendant carriages. Ten thousand halberds flashed like frost; beneath the command pavilion came to rest the sage ruler’s procession, its passage cleared by calls for silence. Gongs and bells sounded, each officer fulfilling his charge; the great imperial banner and grand streamers [?] all conformed to their prescribed forms.
An order descended, and the clamor fell instantly silent: camp after camp was like a tranquil sea or an empty mountain. Banners rose, and martial ardor redoubled: every man soared like an eagle and struck like a bird of prey. Watch kettles rang, and windblown smoke arose; yak-tail command standards pointed, and murky mists parted. Tiger on the right and dragon on the left intermingled with goose, crane, and fish-scale formations, changing into one another; the directing force at the center and the strong force in the rear interwove tortoise, snake, bird, and falcon formations, each giving rise to the next.
Armor was rolled up for the return to camp, and the ceremony of the Eight Formations concluded. Archery targets were set out and their marks positioned, and the skills of the Three Armies were reviewed. Soldiers were arrayed by unit and selected in groups, competing at the range to pierce a willow leaf. Commanders mounted the platform for selection by the emperor himself, vying amid the clamor of shots that could bring down wild geese. The martial ranks stood in perfect order, and joy stirred the imperial countenance…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
賞賚分而歡搖地軸
鴻典告成于玉壘兆示垂櫜
鑾輿遄返于
清都心非耀武陋漢主長楊校獵軌物奚存
邁成周洛水莅師家邦永保九關聲震龍
沙寢西北妖氛百粵威騰鯨海澄東南蜃
氣允矣
煕朝盛事誠哉
奕世彜章臣等學慙博古旣爼豆之無聞志
===
切籌邊恨韜鈐之未識幾年竭股肱之力
惟有赤心小技同腹背之毛何裨實用骨
非將種敢妄希投筆之封腹鮮甲兵徒留
意從戎之論經營重寄分心膂恐負躬逢
訓練強兵動鬼神何期目覩伏願
軫山濤外懼之慮
抱賈生全盛之虞思內憂方可外寧任老成
而補
廷中之衮念選兵不如選將簡謀勇而寄閫
punctuated:
賞賚分而歡搖地軸，鴻典告成于玉壘，兆示垂櫜；鑾輿遄返于清都，心非耀武。陋漢主長楊校獵，軌物奚存？邁成周洛水莅師，家邦永保。九關聲震龍沙，寢西北妖氛；百粵威騰鯨海，澄東南蜃氣。允矣，煕朝盛事！誠哉，奕世彜章！
臣等學慙博古，旣爼豆之無聞；志切籌邊，恨韜鈐之未識。幾年竭股肱之力，惟有赤心；小技同腹背之毛，何裨實用？骨非將種，敢妄希投筆之封？腹鮮甲兵，徒留意從戎之論。經營重寄，分心膂，恐負躬逢；訓練強兵，動鬼神，何期目覩！
伏願軫山濤外懼之慮，抱賈生全盛之虞。思內憂方可外寧，任老成而補廷中之衮；念選兵不如選將，簡謀勇而寄閫
translation_en:
…Rewards were distributed, and rejoicing shook the earth’s axis. The grand ceremony was completed at the jade ramparts, an auspicious sign that bows would be put away in their cases. The imperial carriage swiftly returned to the Pure Capital, for Your Majesty’s purpose was no display of martial might. How paltry the Han ruler’s hunting review at Changyang: what proper standards did it preserve? Surpassing even the Zhou king’s review of his forces by the Luo River, Your Majesty ensures the enduring security of the ruling house and realm. The renown of the Nine Passes resounds through Longsha, stilling the sinister vapors of the northwest; awe spreads through the Hundred Yue lands and across the whale-filled seas, dispelling the mirage vapors of the southeast. Truly, this is a splendid event of an illustrious reign! Indeed, it is an enduring model for successive generations!
We, your servants, are ashamed that our learning falls short of broad knowledge of antiquity: we have gained no reputation for understanding ritual vessels and observances. Our hearts are set on planning for the frontiers, yet we regret our ignorance of military strategy. For years we have exerted ourselves as your limbs, with nothing to offer but loyal hearts. Our meager skills are like hair on the belly or back: what practical use can they serve? Not born of the stock of generals, dare we vainly hope for the enfeoffment won by casting aside the writing brush? With little military knowledge within us, we merely give thought to discussions of taking up arms. Entrusted with weighty responsibilities for ordering affairs and sharing the burdens of your closest servants, we fear failing the opportunity we have personally been granted. That the training of strong troops should move even ghosts and spirits—how could we have expected to witness it ourselves!
We humbly wish that you would give heed to Shan Tao’s concern over threats from abroad and cherish Master Jia’s apprehensions amid complete prosperity. Consider that only by attending to troubles within can peace be secured without; employ mature and experienced men to mend the imperial robes at court—that is, to remedy shortcomings in government. Remember that selecting soldiers is less important than selecting generals; choose men of strategic ability and courage, and entrust them with command beyond…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
外之權
握金鏡於鸞門光遍五千之禹服
偃銅符於鶴仗風清百二之秦關臣等無任
瞻
天仰
聖懽忭踴躍之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
===
第叄塲
策五道
第一問
楊佩訓
同考試官敎諭趙批敷陳敬
天勤民取譬子之事父父之保子意甚明切至末歸重勤民爲敬
天之本尤見忠愛
同考試官敎諭王批我
皇上舉行曠典昭示臣民蓋尚實而非尚文也此作敷厲揄揚中恭
punctuated:
外之權。握金鏡於鸞門，光遍五千之禹服；偃銅符於鶴仗，風清百二之秦關。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、懽忭踴躍之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。

第叄塲
策五道
第一問
楊佩訓

同考試官敎諭趙批：敷陳敬天勤民，取譬子之事父、父之保子，意甚明切。至末歸重勤民爲敬天之本，尤見忠愛。

同考試官敎諭王批：我皇上舉行曠典，昭示臣民，蓋尚實而非尚文也。此作敷厲揄揚中恭
translation_en:
…authority beyond the court. Hold the golden mirror at the phoenix gates, its light reaching throughout Yu’s domains of five thousand li; lay aside the bronze military tallies amid the crane standards, bringing a tranquil breeze to Qin’s mountain passes, where two men can withstand a hundred. We, your servants, cannot contain our utmost joy and exultation as we gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sagely Majesty. We respectfully submit this memorial of congratulation for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question
Yang Peixun

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: The essay expounds reverence for Heaven and diligent care for the people, drawing analogies with a son’s service to his father and a father’s protection of his son. Its meaning is exceptionally clear and apt. At the end, it places particular emphasis on diligent care for the people as the foundation of reverence for Heaven, revealing still more clearly the author’s loyalty and loving concern.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: Our August Emperor has performed a ceremony of exceptional rarity, making it manifest to his subjects; surely he esteems substance rather than ornament. Amid its vigorous exposition and praise, this composition respectfully…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
獻誠悃其知探本之論異日必不負所學者耶
考試官敎授夏批條答婉盡
考試官敎授帥批敷對根據發揮典暢可取
帝王一身上爲天之元子是故有昭事之
道焉知事親則知所以事天矣下爲民之
父母是故有懷保之道焉知保子則知所
以保民矣人之於親非不實敦牟以羞之
撰席衽以隨之也而心則有出於是者承
其志而形聲耳目之不違體其意而膚髮
===
樹木之必愛夫豈僞爲於笑貌哉一實心
之形耳帝王事天何以異此人之於子非
不時戒諭以勸之躬勞瘁以率之也而心
則有出於是者圖其安而第宅絲粟之必
周防其疾而箴石湯爇之必庀夫豈僞爲
於笑貌哉一實心之形耳帝王保民何以
異此事天在敬保民在勤無其實有其文
是所以事親者不過敦牟之滑甘席衽之
趾向而已所以保子者不過戒諭之諄諄
punctuated:
獻誠悃，其知探本之論，異日必不負所學者耶！
考試官敎授夏批：條答婉盡。
考試官敎授帥批：敷對根據，發揮典暢，可取。
帝王一身，上爲天之元子，是故有昭事之道焉。知事親，則知所以事天矣。下爲民之父母，是故有懷保之道焉。知保子，則知所以保民矣。人之於親，非不實敦牟以羞之，撰席衽以隨之也，而心則有出於是者：承其志，而形聲耳目之不違；體其意，而膚髮樹木之必愛。夫豈僞爲於笑貌哉？一實心之形耳。帝王事天，何以異此？人之於子，非不時戒諭以勸之，躬勞瘁以率之也，而心則有出於是者：圖其安，而第宅絲粟之必周；防其疾，而箴石湯爇之必庀。夫豈僞爲於笑貌哉？一實心之形耳。帝王保民，何以異此？事天在敬，保民在勤。無其實，有其文，是所以事親者，不過敦牟之滑甘、席衽之趾向而已；所以保子者，不過戒諭之諄諄
translation_en:
…offers sincere devotion. His argument shows that he knows to investigate the fundamentals; surely in days to come he will not fail to live up to his learning!
Examiner Xia, an instructor, comments: “The answers to the individual points are tactful and thorough.”
Examiner Shuai, an instructor, comments: “The response is well grounded; its exposition is refined and fluent, and merits approval.”
The emperor, in his own person, is above the eldest son of Heaven, and therefore has a way of serving Heaven illustriously. Knowing how to serve one’s parents, one knows how to serve Heaven. Below, he is father and mother to the people, and therefore has a way of cherishing and protecting them. Knowing how to protect one’s children, one knows how to protect the people.
In attending to their parents, people certainly fill the ritual vessels with food to offer them and arrange their mats and bedding to suit them. Yet their hearts go beyond these things: they uphold their parents’ wishes, allowing nothing in their demeanor, speech, hearing, or sight to contravene them; they embody their parents’ intentions, taking loving care of their own skin and hair and of the trees their parents planted. How could this be a pretense put on through smiles and outward appearances? It is simply the manifestation of a sincere heart. How is the emperor’s service to Heaven any different?
In attending to their children, people certainly admonish and instruct them at suitable times to encourage them, and toil in person to lead them by example. Yet their hearts go beyond these things: they plan for their children’s security, ensuring that housing, clothing, and food are fully provided; they guard against their illnesses, ensuring that needles, medicinal stones, decoctions, and heat treatments [?] are ready. How could this be a pretense put on through smiles and outward appearances? It is simply the manifestation of a sincere heart. How is the emperor’s protection of the people any different?
Serving Heaven rests on reverence; protecting the people rests on diligence. If there is outward form without substance, then serving one’s parents amounts merely to sweet and savory food in ritual vessels and the proper orientation of their bedding [?]; protecting one’s children amounts merely to repeated admonitions…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
勞瘁之悁悁而已而曰我爲孝子我爲慈
父豈不妄哉知此則我
祖宗之所以
敬天勤民與我
皇上之所以承
休光
訓可得敷揚其實矣詩曰時邁其邦昊天其
子之則夫敬以事之子道宜爾而莫大於
郊祀記曰因名山升中於天因吉土饗帝
===
于郊蓋言敬也是故因丘掃地尚其質也
陶匏藁靿象其性也疏布素車尊其樸也
鎮圭繅藉重其事也五采五就繁其飾也
龍旂日月明其道也黃鍾大呂極其變也
大裘龍袞備其物也豈徒以文已乎書曰
元后作民父母則夫勤以保之父道宜爾
而莫大於耕籍記曰孟春之月乃擇元辰
親載耒耜帥公卿諸侯大夫躬耕於南郊
蓋言勤也是故覘土省脈以若利也占正
punctuated: 勞瘁之悁悁而已，而曰「我爲孝子，我爲慈父」，豈不妄哉？知此，則我祖宗之所以敬天勤民，與我皇上之所以承休光訓，可得敷揚其實矣。詩曰：「時邁其邦，昊天其子之。」則夫敬以事之，子道宜爾，而莫大於郊祀。記曰：「因名山升中於天，因吉土饗帝于郊。」蓋言敬也。是故因丘掃地，尚其質也；陶匏藁靿，象其性也；疏布素車，尊其樸也；鎮圭繅藉，重其事也；五采五就，繁其飾也；龍旂日月，明其道也；黃鍾大呂，極其變也；大裘龍袞，備其物也。豈徒以文已乎？書曰：「元后作民父母。」則夫勤以保之，父道宜爾，而莫大於耕籍。記曰：「孟春之月，乃擇元辰，親載耒耜，帥公卿諸侯大夫，躬耕於南郊。」蓋言勤也。是故覘土省脈，以若利也；占正
translation_en:
…and nothing more than anxious toil; yet to say, “I am a filial son; I am a loving father”—would this not be presumptuous? Understanding this, we can expound the true substance of how our imperial ancestors reverently served Heaven and diligently cared for the people, and how our present emperor carries on their glorious instructions [?]. The Book of Odes says: “He makes his timely progresses through his states; august Heaven treats him as its son.” Thus, serving Heaven with reverence is fitting conduct for a son, and nothing is greater in this regard than the suburban sacrifice. The Book of Rites says: “At famous mountains, he ascends to report his accomplishments to Heaven; on auspicious ground, he offers sacrifice to the Supreme Lord in the suburbs.” This speaks of reverence. Thus, using a hill and sweeping the ground honors simplicity; earthenware vessels, gourds, and straw footwear [?] embody natural qualities; coarse cloth and an unadorned carriage honor plainness; the guardian jade tablet and its patterned silk mat give weight to the ceremony; the five colors and fivefold ornamentation elaborate its adornments; dragon banners bearing the sun and moon illuminate its Way; the Huangzhong and Dalu musical pitches bring its variations to their fullest expression; and the great fur robe and dragon robe complete its ceremonial equipment. Could these be merely outward forms?
