罔之議，上之謬托干豪傑之名，所當審也。人主運遠照之明，察近似之迹，而以行至正至通之法，幾矣。姦罔易知也，而似非而是者難識也。是故，以繕城郭不爲尹鐸美矣，徐考之：城果高乎？池果深乎？兵卒盡城守乎？寇至不鳥獸遯乎？以禦寇賊不爲李牧美矣，徐考之：果能戰乎？不畫城自保，使自來去乎？不虔劉我赤子乎？不飾虛功以邀爵賞乎？以治獄訟不爲田叔美矣，徐考之：不朴擊賣請乎？不勢奪乎人？不故出入乎？不囊贖鍰爲已利乎？文不增損爲已便乎？以司府庫不爲明道美矣，徐考之：不狗盜乎？出納不輕重乎？不私竄抵乎？此四者，上之不能與豪傑同功，下之不得與姦罔同罪，既逃乎法，而反以令名終，罪浮於顯戮者也，所當審也。人主運遠照之明，察近似之迹，而以行至正至通之法，幾矣。

抑愚又有說焉：制令在君，行
translation_en:
…the charge of deception at the lower extreme, while at the higher they falsely claim the name of outstanding men. These are matters requiring scrutiny. If the ruler exercises far-seeing discernment, examines the traces of deceptive resemblance, and thereby applies laws of utmost rectitude and adaptability, he will come close to the ideal.

Wickedness and deception are easy to recognize; what appears wrong but is right is difficult to discern. Thus, if someone repairing city walls does not attain the excellence of Yin Duo, examine him carefully: Are the walls truly high? Are the moats truly deep? Do all the soldiers defend the walls? When raiders arrive, do they refrain from scattering like birds and beasts? If someone resisting raiders does not attain the excellence of Li Mu, examine him carefully: Can he actually fight? Does he refrain from marking off the city for his own protection and letting the enemy come and go at will? Does he refrain from slaughtering our innocent people? Does he refrain from embellishing fictitious achievements to seek rank and rewards? If someone adjudicating lawsuits does not attain the excellence of Tian Shu, examine him carefully: Does he refrain from beating people and selling his influence over their petitions [?]? Does he avoid being swayed by others’ power? Does he refrain from deliberately acquitting the guilty or condemning the innocent? Does he refrain from pocketing redemption fines for his own profit? Are documents neither augmented nor abridged for his own convenience? If someone administering treasuries and storehouses does not attain the excellence of Mingdao, examine him carefully: Does he refrain from petty theft? Does he avoid using unequal measures in disbursements and receipts? Does he refrain from secretly falsifying accounts or offsets [?]?

These four kinds of men cannot, at the higher extreme, share the achievements of outstanding men, yet at the lower they cannot be assigned the same guilt as the wicked and deceitful. Having escaped the law, they instead end their days with a fine reputation; their guilt exceeds that of those publicly executed. This requires scrutiny. If the ruler exercises far-seeing discernment, examines the traces of deceptive resemblance, and thereby applies laws of utmost rectitude and adaptability, he will come close to the ideal.

Yet I, in my ignorance, have another point to make: establishing commands rests with the ruler; carrying them out…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
令在臣議法在君守法在臣法令之弊豈
法令之不善哉用之者或失其道也用法
令之吏宜何如其平若衡其明若鑑其仁
恕若徐有功其剛正若包孝肅其罪也果
麗于法耶則雖弄臣豪奴不得以私愛奪
而又何姦罔者之幸脫也其罪也果不當
抵法耶則雖犯蹕盜環不得以私怒加而
何豪傑者之濫及也若是則嚴用之而不
以爲苛寬用之而不以爲縱正用之而豪
===
傑不束於深文通用之而姦罔莫逃於法
外縱橫闔闢無施不可而
祖宗之法雖萬世共守之可也又烏乎弊哉故
曰制而用之存乎法推而行之存乎人
第五問
余一愚
同考試官教諭朱批去冗兵練客兵不可驟遣此議
極中時宜至論簡練二法尤鑿鑿可裨實用非拘方之士也
同考試官教諭李批論時事者不激即泛是篇言
punctuated:
令在臣，議法在君，守法在臣。法令之弊，豈法令之不善哉？用之者或失其道也。用法令之吏宜何如？其平若衡，其明若鑑，其仁恕若徐有功，其剛正若包孝肅。其罪也果麗于法耶？則雖弄臣豪奴，不得以私愛奪，而又何姦罔者之幸脫也？其罪也果不當抵法耶？則雖犯蹕盜環，不得以私怒加，而何豪傑者之濫及也？若是，則嚴用之而不以爲苛，寬用之而不以爲縱，正用之而豪傑不束於深文，通用之而姦罔莫逃於法外，縱橫闔闢，無施不可，而祖宗之法雖萬世共守之可也，又烏乎弊哉？故曰：「制而用之存乎法，推而行之存乎人。」

第五問
余一愚

同考試官教諭朱批：去冗兵，練客兵，不可驟遣，此議極中時宜。至論簡練二法，尤鑿鑿可裨實用，非拘方之士也。

同考試官教諭李批：論時事者，不激即泛，是篇言
translation_en:
…carrying out commands rests with the ministers. Deliberating upon laws rests with the ruler; upholding them rests with the ministers. Do defects in laws and commands really arise from their being unsound? Those who apply them sometimes depart from the proper way. What should officials who apply laws and commands be like? As impartial as a balance, as discerning as a mirror, as humane and forgiving as Xu Yougong, and as firm and upright as Bao Xiaosu. If an offense truly falls under the law, then even for court favorites and powerful servants, private affection must not override it. How, then, could deceitful wrongdoers escape by good fortune? If an offense truly does not warrant the prescribed punishment, then even for someone who trespasses upon the imperial procession or steals a ring, private anger must not increase it. How, then, could outstanding men be indiscriminately implicated? In this way, strict application will not be considered harsh, and lenient application will not be considered indulgent. Applied uprightly, the law will not entangle outstanding men in strained interpretations; applied flexibly, it will leave deceitful wrongdoers no escape beyond its reach. Whether extending or restraining, closing or opening, every application will be appropriate. The laws of the imperial ancestors could thus be upheld by all for ten thousand generations. What defects could there then be? Hence the saying: “Regulation and application depend upon laws; their extension and implementation depend upon people.”

Fifth Policy Question
Yu Yiyu

He is no man bound by rigid formulas.

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
辭剴切經畫老成可式
考試官敎授夏批條答詳明
考試官敎授帥批此必熟知時務者
執事策諸生而終及練兵之計蓋欲攘寇
安民爲閩中遠慮甚盛心也顧豎儒非夙
諳武備其何以攄一得復明問試卽所聞
于故老者陳之夫八閩之地昔稱海濱鄒
魯以士人喜談詩書而不言兵也粵考形
勢則延建邵汀阻山依谷福興泉漳帶海
===
襟江故
國初都司衞所郡縣相錯竝設而於銅山浯
嶼南日小埕諸要害處水寨星列墩堠鱗
次非以外接島夷內聯峒箐故爲計特周
且悉耶承平旣久法度漸弛頃歲一二猾
寇弄兵潢池黠夷乘之擣虛深入甲腐而
不可張兵鈍而不足試束手待斃嗟乎戚
矣當事者慘目戒心權宜拯解策先募兵
此猶驟病之夫危在旦夕顧視其家乃無
punctuated:
辭剴切，經畫老成，可式。
考試官敎授夏批：條答詳明。
考試官敎授帥批：此必熟知時務者。

執事策諸生，而終及練兵之計，蓋欲攘寇安民，爲閩中遠慮，甚盛心也。顧豎儒非夙諳武備，其何以攄一得復明問？試卽所聞于故老者陳之。夫八閩之地，昔稱海濱鄒魯，以士人喜談詩書而不言兵也。粵考形勢，則延建邵汀阻山依谷，福興泉漳帶海襟江。故國初都司衞所郡縣相錯竝設，而於銅山、浯嶼、南日、小埕諸要害處，水寨星列，墩堠鱗次，非以外接島夷、內聯峒箐，故爲計特周且悉耶？承平旣久，法度漸弛。頃歲一二猾寇弄兵潢池，黠夷乘之，擣虛深入，甲腐而不可張，兵鈍而不足試，束手待斃。嗟乎，戚矣！當事者慘目戒心，權宜拯解，策先募兵。此猶驟病之夫，危在旦夕，顧視其家，乃無
translation_en:
… Its language is incisive and pertinent, its planning seasoned and mature: it can serve as a model.
Examiner Xia, Instructor, comments: The answers to the individual points are detailed and clear.
Examiner Shuai, Instructor, comments: This must be someone thoroughly acquainted with current affairs.

You, sir, have posed policy questions to the candidates and concluded by addressing plans for training troops. Your intention is surely to repel bandits and bring peace to the people, taking the long view for Fujian—a most generous concern. Yet I, a mere bookish scholar, have no longstanding familiarity with military preparations. How can I set forth even one useful insight in reply to your discerning question? Let me try to relate what I have heard from the elders. The land of the Eight Min was formerly called the Zou and Lu of the seacoast, because its scholars delighted in discussing the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, rather than military matters. Examining its terrain, we find that Yanping, Jianning, Shaowu, and Tingzhou are protected by mountains and nestled in valleys, while Fuzhou, Xinghua, Quanzhou, and Zhangzhou are girdled by the sea and skirted by rivers. Thus, at the founding of the dynasty, the Regional Military Commission, guards, and battalions were established alongside the prefectures and counties in an interlocking arrangement. At strategic places such as Tongshan, Wuyu, Nanri, and Xiaocheng, naval stockades were scattered like stars, and watchtowers stood in close succession like fish scales. Was this not because the region adjoined island peoples beyond its shores and connected with mountain caves and bamboo thickets inland, so that its defensive planning was exceptionally comprehensive and detailed?

After a long period of peace, laws and regulations gradually grew lax. In recent years, one or two crafty bandits took up arms, like rebels sporting weapons in a shallow pool. Cunning foreign raiders seized the opportunity, struck at undefended points, and penetrated deep inland. Armor had rotted and could no longer be put on; weapons were blunt and unfit for use. People could only await death with their hands tied. Alas, how grievous! Those responsible for affairs, appalled by what they saw and alarmed at heart, sought expedient means of relief, giving priority to recruiting troops. This was like a man suddenly stricken with illness, his life in imminent danger, who looked about his household only to find no …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
宿艾汲汲然裹糧求巳于秦越人計也是
時攘臂先登摧鋒陷敵東支西吾不至大
壞皆客兵力耳然購募必重犒賚必厚鎧
仗必給需求必煩驛遞必擾亦勢之不得
不然者昔李泌謂兵不土著又無宗族不
自顧惜客兵其可久哉而建議者遂持練
土兵之計以為募兵當在昔日練兵當在
今日夫病勢亟而利用召醫勢稍緩而利
在蓄艾亦計也然土兵非始于今日也自
===
成周時而此制已權輿矣成周之制居則
為比閭族黨州鄉之民行則為伍兩卒旅
軍師之衆夫其居也乃所以為農而其出
也即所以為兵是農亦兵而兵亦農也非
即土兵之意乎始壞於齊之内政家一人
繼壞於晉之州兵家五人而後兵農異途
耕戰殊業矣漢制材官騎士皆家人子起
田中者為之雖未必盡合於周官而亦用
農為兵之遺也漢世所以威行八埏鞭撻
punctuated:
宿艾，汲汲然裹糧求巳于秦越人，計也。是時攘臂先登，摧鋒陷敵，東支西吾，不至大壞，皆客兵力耳。然購募必重，犒賚必厚，鎧仗必給，需求必煩，驛遞必擾，亦勢之不得不然者。昔李泌謂兵不土著，又無宗族，不自顧惜。客兵其可久哉？而建議者遂持練土兵之計，以為募兵當在昔日，練兵當在今日。夫病勢亟而利用召醫，勢稍緩而利在蓄艾，亦計也。然土兵非始于今日也，自成周時而此制已權輿矣。
成周之制，居則為比閭族黨州鄉之民，行則為伍兩卒旅軍師之衆。夫其居也，乃所以為農；而其出也，即所以為兵。是農亦兵，而兵亦農也，非即土兵之意乎？始壞於齊之内政家一人，繼壞於晉之州兵家五人，而後兵農異途，耕戰殊業矣。漢制材官騎士，皆家人子起田中者為之，雖未必盡合於周官，而亦用農為兵之遺也。漢世所以威行八埏，鞭撻
translation_en:
…aged mugwort, and so hastily packs provisions and seeks a cure [?] from Qin Yueren: this, too, is a strategy. At that time, those who bared their arms and led the advance, broke the enemy’s spearhead and penetrated its ranks, sustaining resistance in the east and holding firm in the west [?], were all troops recruited from elsewhere. It was their strength alone that prevented a great collapse. Yet recruiting them necessarily entailed substantial payments, rewarding them required generous gifts, armor and weapons had to be supplied, their demands inevitably became burdensome, and the postal relay service was inevitably disrupted. These, too, were unavoidable consequences of the circumstances. Li Mi once said that soldiers who were not locally rooted and had no clans there would take no care to preserve themselves. Could reliance on troops from elsewhere endure? Those offering proposals therefore advocated training local troops, arguing that recruiting troops had been appropriate earlier, whereas training them was appropriate now. When an illness is acute, it is advantageous to summon a physician; when its severity has somewhat abated, the advantage lies in storing mugwort. This, too, is a strategy. Yet local troops are no innovation of the present day: this institution had already begun in the Zhou era.
Under the Zhou system, at home the people belonged to the residential units called bi, lü, zu, dang, zhou, and xiang; on campaign they formed the military units called wu, liang, zu, lü, jun, and shi. At home they worked as farmers; when they went out, they served as soldiers. Thus farmers were also soldiers, and soldiers were also farmers. Is this not precisely the principle of local troops? The system first deteriorated under Qi’s domestic organization, which supplied one man per household; it deteriorated further under Jin’s regional troop system, which supplied five men per household. Thereafter, soldiers and farmers followed separate paths, and cultivation and warfare became distinct occupations. Under the Han system, the selected infantry and cavalry were all sons of ordinary households called up from the fields. Although this may not have accorded in every respect with the Offices of Zhou, it nevertheless preserved the practice of employing farmers as soldiers. This was how, under the Han, awe-inspiring power extended to the eight limits of the earth, scourging…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
四夷與唐李抱眞守懷州三丁籍一蠲其
徭役給以弓矢官無廩餼各精技射名曰
澤潞步兵而勇敢爲諸道最李德裕守西
川率戶二百取一緩則農急則戰名曰雄
邊子弟而南詔不敢犯塞悉怛謀降他若
晉齊王之武定軍宋慶曆之保毅軍宣毅
軍景德之廣銳軍治平之義勇軍此皆兵
之出於民而隸之州縣者也非土兵績効
章章耶夫土兵所以勝於客兵者非謂其
===
智勇獨先而技藝獨精也亦非謂其轉餉
較易而鈔掠較省也以其有父兄室家之
念祖宗丘隴之思其心固較客兵異也凡
用兵者用其心耳驅土人以禦寇是俾之
自衛家室自樊丘隴心固戀戀向也夫昏
夜貯物於衢以他人守卽股枕臥矣守以
主者則盻盻然中宵張睫焉何者心之繫
與否也此非土客二兵大辨耶土兵之在
今日有三曰保甲曰弓兵曰機兵保甲之
punctuated:
四夷，與唐李抱眞守懷州，三丁籍一，蠲其徭役，給以弓矢，官無廩餼，各精技射，名曰澤潞步兵，而勇敢爲諸道最。李德裕守西川，率戶二百取一，緩則農，急則戰，名曰雄邊子弟，而南詔不敢犯塞，悉怛謀降。他若晉齊王之武定軍，宋慶曆之保毅軍、宣毅軍，景德之廣銳軍，治平之義勇軍，此皆兵之出於民而隸之州縣者也，非土兵績効章章耶？
夫土兵所以勝於客兵者，非謂其智勇獨先而技藝獨精也，亦非謂其轉餉較易而鈔掠較省也。以其有父兄室家之念、祖宗丘隴之思，其心固較客兵異也。凡用兵者，用其心耳。驅土人以禦寇，是俾之自衛家室，自樊丘隴，心固戀戀向也。夫昏夜貯物於衢，以他人守，卽股枕臥矣；守以主者，則盻盻然中宵張睫焉。何者？心之繫與否也。此非土客二兵大辨耶？
土兵之在今日有三：曰保甲，曰弓兵，曰機兵。保甲之
translation_en:
…the peoples of the four quarters. And under the Tang, when Li Baozhen governed Huaizhou, he enrolled one man out of every three adult males, exempted them from labor service, and supplied them with bows and arrows. The government provided no grain allowances; each became proficient in archery. They were called the Zelu Infantry, and their courage ranked foremost among the forces of all the circuits. When Li Deyu governed Xichuan, he selected one man for every two hundred households. In quiet times they farmed; in emergencies they fought. They were called the Frontier Heroes. Nanzhao dared not violate the frontier, and Xi Damou surrendered. Other examples include the Martial Pacification Army of the Prince of Qi of Jin; the Resolute Defense Army and the Proclaimed Valor Army of the Song’s Qingli era; the Broad Valor Army of the Jingde era; and the Righteous Valor Army of the Zhiping era. All these were troops drawn from the common people and placed under prefectural and county authority. Are these not conspicuous proofs of the achievements of local troops?
Local troops surpass troops brought in from elsewhere, not because their intelligence and courage are uniquely superior or their skills uniquely refined, nor because supplying them is easier or their plundering less extensive. Rather, they think of their fathers, elder brothers, wives, and families, and care for their ancestors’ graves. Their disposition is thus inherently different from that of troops from elsewhere. Whoever employs troops employs their hearts, and nothing more. To mobilize local people against raiders is to have them defend their own households and protect their own ancestral graves. Their hearts are naturally bound to these things. Suppose goods are deposited in a thoroughfare after dark. Set someone else to guard them, and he will lie down with his head pillowed on his thigh; set their owner to guard them, and he will keep his eyes wide open, watching intently through the night. Why? It depends on whether his heart is engaged. Is this not the great distinction between local troops and troops brought in from elsewhere?
There are three kinds of local troops today: the baojia household militia, the archers, and the mobile troops. As for the baojia’s…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
法歲檄有司編什伍置尺籍脩鉏挺止矣
保甲其可恃乎弓兵額數既單近復裁減
供追呼走鄉聚逐鷄豚止矣弓兵其可使
乎機兵時有調發常自負爲公家出力守
令閱視則擐甲而趨持干而倚羣呼迭鬨
若將爲戲止矣緩急其可賴乎若此者皆
羸夫弱子朽甲斷戟聰明不足赴旗鼓強
銳不足犯死傷見敵即望風走當事者以
爲脆弱宜也然往歲寇在吳閩人既爲兵
===
於吳已而寇在越閩人又爲兵於越繼寇
在閩則閩人不自兵而吳越人反爲兵於
閩豈閩人強於吳越而獨弱於桑梓里哉
無以練之故也夫土兵未練而遽曰客兵
可去一旦寇起倉卒何以應之所謂見兔
而顧犬吾竊懼其晚也故爲今之計莫若
預練土兵而練之之法有三一曰定經制
二曰嚴教習三曰明賞罰此皆今日之不
可不講者夫兵制不定則眾寡不均兵籍
punctuated:
法，歲檄有司編什伍，置尺籍，脩鉏挺止矣。保甲其可恃乎？弓兵額數既單，近復裁減，供追呼，走鄉聚，逐鷄豚止矣。弓兵其可使乎？機兵時有調發，常自負爲公家出力，守令閱視，則擐甲而趨，持干而倚，羣呼迭鬨，若將爲戲止矣。緩急其可賴乎？若此者，皆羸夫弱子，朽甲斷戟，聰明不足赴旗鼓，強銳不足犯死傷，見敵即望風走。當事者以爲脆弱，宜也。然往歲寇在吳，閩人既爲兵於吳；已而寇在越，閩人又爲兵於越；繼寇在閩，則閩人不自兵，而吳越人反爲兵於閩。豈閩人強於吳越，而獨弱於桑梓里哉？無以練之故也。
夫土兵未練，而遽曰客兵可去，一旦寇起倉卒，何以應之？所謂見兔而顧犬，吾竊懼其晚也。故爲今之計，莫若預練土兵。而練之之法有三：一曰定經制，二曰嚴教習，三曰明賞罰。此皆今日之不可不講者。夫兵制不定，則眾寡不均；兵籍
translation_en:
…the system amounts to no more than issuing annual orders to the responsible officials to organize households into groups of ten and five, establish military registers, and put hoes and clubs in order. Can the baojia household militia be relied upon? The quota of archer constables was already small and has recently been reduced further. They merely serve to pursue and summon people, run about the villages, and chase chickens and pigs. Can these archer constables be put to use? The local militia troops are occasionally mobilized and always pride themselves on exerting themselves for the government. When prefects and magistrates inspect them, they hurry forward clad in armor, lean upon their shields, and shout together in successive uproars, as though merely putting on a show. Can they be counted on in an emergency? Such men are all feeble fellows and weak youths, with rotten armor and broken halberds. Their sight and hearing are insufficient to respond to flags and drums; their strength and spirit are insufficient to brave death and injury. At the sight of the enemy, they flee at the first alarm. It is understandable that those in charge should consider them frail and weak. Yet in past years, when raiders were in Wu, men from Min served as soldiers in Wu; subsequently, when raiders were in Yue, men from Min again served as soldiers in Yue. When the raiders then came to Min, however, the men of Min did not themselves take up arms, and men from Wu and Yue instead served as soldiers in Min. Could men from Min be strong in Wu and Yue, yet weak only in their native villages? The reason is that no means have been provided to train them.
If local troops remain untrained, yet we hastily declare that troops from elsewhere may be dismissed, how shall we respond if raiders suddenly rise up? This is what is meant by looking around for the hound only after seeing the hare: I fear it will be too late. Thus, the best course now is to train local troops in advance. There are three methods for training them: first, establish a regular military organization; second, enforce rigorous instruction and practice; third, make rewards and punishments clear. All these are matters that must be addressed today. If military organization is not settled, troop numbers will be uneven; if the military registers…

text:

必稽占役必禁逋逃必復部墜必全版築
迎送勿以干預文吏詰查不得漁擾規畫
周而後練習可加故曰經制之不可不定
者此也兵家之法超忽變化目駭耳廻苟
===
非素閑臨敵必亂今宜於戈矛之用礮石
之制决拾之方營陣之規具有成法者購
募良師以一教十以十教百其執技也長
短步騎靡用弗適其成列也縱橫首尾隨
變輒應技藝既精膽氣自壯聞敵而躍然
思赴見敵而羣然爭前矣故曰教習之不
可不嚴者此也夫鋒鏑注目而士弗却矢
鏃貫顱而兵不動者賞罰素明耳練習之
時號令不明賞不信罰不必則驅之臨陣
punctuated:
不覈，則强弱不分，操練之術安從施耶？今宜倣新題事例，查照弘治年間舊規，大縣該兵幾何，中縣該兵幾何，悉復前額，嚴加挑選：老者遣之，弱者汰之，虛者補之，冒者正之。影射必稽，占役必禁，逋逃必復，部墜必全。版築迎送，勿以干預；文吏詰查，不得漁擾。規畫周而後練習可加，故曰經制之不可不定者，此也。

兵家之法，超忽變化，目駭耳廻。苟非素閑，臨敵必亂。今宜於戈矛之用、礮石之制、决拾之方、營陣之規，具有成法者，購募良師，以一教十，以十教百。其執技也，長短步騎，靡用弗適；其成列也，縱橫首尾，隨變輒應。技藝既精，膽氣自壯，聞敵而躍然思赴，見敵而羣然爭前矣。故曰教習之不可不嚴者，此也。

夫鋒鏑注目而士弗却，矢鏃貫顱而兵不動者，賞罰素明耳。練習之時，號令不明，賞不信，罰不必，則驅之臨陣
translation_en:
…if the military registers are not verified, the strong cannot be distinguished from the weak. How, then, can methods of military drill be applied? We should now follow the precedents newly submitted to the throne and consult the old regulations of the Hongzhi reign: how many troops a large county should provide, and how many a medium-sized county should provide. The former quotas should all be restored, and selection should be rigorous: discharge the old, weed out the weak, fill vacancies, and correct fraudulent registrations. Concealed affiliations used to evade obligations must be investigated; the appropriation of soldiers for private service must be prohibited; deserters must be brought back; depleted units must be restored to full strength [?]. Construction work and duties of welcoming and seeing off officials must not interfere with training. Civil clerks conducting investigations must not exploit or harass the troops. Only when arrangements are comprehensive can training be undertaken. This is why, as I have said, the military establishment must be firmly regulated.

The methods of warfare change with bewildering speed, startling the eyes and confounding the ears. Unless soldiers are thoroughly familiar with them beforehand, they will inevitably fall into confusion when facing the enemy. We should now recruit skilled instructors in established methods for using dagger-axes and spears, handling artillery and stone projectiles, employing archery thumb rings and arm guards, and organizing camps and battle formations. Let one teach ten, and ten teach a hundred. In exercising their skills, whether with long or short weapons, on foot or on horseback, they should be adept in every application. In forming ranks, whether lengthwise or crosswise, at the front or rear, they should respond immediately to every change. Once their skills are refined, their courage will naturally grow. On hearing of the enemy, they will eagerly wish to rush into action; on seeing the enemy, they will vie with one another to advance. This is why, as I have said, instruction and training must be rigorous.

When blades and arrowheads are aimed at their eyes yet the soldiers do not recoil, and when arrowheads pierce skulls yet the troops remain unshaken, it is simply because rewards and punishments have long been clearly established. If, during training, commands are unclear, rewards unreliable, and punishments uncertain, then, when the troops are driven into battle…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
必不前矣此孫武所以加刑於莊賈也今
宜重之以將領之職假之以便宜之權愆
期後至必刑踰行越伍必刑旌旗金鼓不
如敎必刑坐作進退不如法必刑其若于
訓者什伯之長以次遞進且有厚賚由是
而率以赴敵則人知進有殊賞退有嚴誅
孰不捐軀以自効哉故曰賞罰之不可不
明者此也三者旣舉而又責成於有司守
令以此爲盡職臺臣以此爲殿最則袂鼎
===
===
超距之人出𤽤蛟射鵰之技進而人咸奮
武隊咸稱強矣夫一人敎成然後客兵可
去一人也一隊敎成然後客兵可去一隊
也旋敎旋去不二三年而客兵可以盡遣
客兵之餉可以盡蠲蓋以機兵而代客兵
以軍餉而爲工食正相乘矣况所省又不
訾乎不然艾不素蓄遠方之醫終不可謝
卽使儲金若丘積粟如山江河之大其能
當漏卮哉故議兵者率以是爲憂於是有
punctuated: 必不前矣。此孫武所以加刑於莊賈也。今宜重之以將領之職，假之以便宜之權。愆期後至必刑，踰行越伍必刑，旌旗金鼓不如敎必刑，坐作進退不如法必刑。其若于訓者，什伯之長以次遞進，且有厚賚。由是而率以赴敵，則人知進有殊賞，退有嚴誅，孰不捐軀以自効哉？故曰賞罰之不可不明者此也。三者旣舉，而又責成於有司，守令以此爲盡職，臺臣以此爲殿最，則袂鼎超距之人出，𤽤蛟射鵰之技進，而人咸奮武，隊咸稱強矣。夫一人敎成，然後客兵可去一人也；一隊敎成，然後客兵可去一隊也。旋敎旋去，不二三年，而客兵可以盡遣，客兵之餉可以盡蠲。蓋以機兵而代客兵，以軍餉而爲工食，正相乘矣。况所省又不訾乎？不然，艾不素蓄，遠方之醫終不可謝。卽使儲金若丘，積粟如山，江河之大，其能當漏卮哉？故議兵者率以是爲憂，於是有
translation_en:
…they will certainly not advance. This is why Sun Wu inflicted punishment upon Zhuang Jia [?; the text appears to conflate Sun Wu with Sima Rangju]. We should now invest commanders with the weight of their office and grant them authority to act as circumstances require. Those who miss the appointed time and arrive late must be punished; those who stray beyond their ranks and files must be punished; those who fail to follow instructions concerning banners, gongs, and drums must be punished; and those whose sitting, rising, advancing, and withdrawing do not conform to regulations must be punished. As for those who obey instructions, leaders of tens and hundreds should be promoted successively through the ranks and also receive generous rewards. If troops are then led against the enemy, everyone will know that advancing brings exceptional rewards and retreating brings severe punishment. Who would not sacrifice his life in service? This is why rewards and punishments must be clearly established.

Once these three measures have been implemented, responsibility for their success should also be assigned to the officials concerned. Prefects and magistrates should regard this as the fulfillment of their duties, and censorial officials should use it to assess their performance as inferior or superior. Then men capable of lifting cauldrons [?] and leaping great distances will emerge, skills in grappling with dragons [?] and shooting eagles will develop, every man will display martial vigor, and every unit will be renowned for its strength. Once one man has completed his training, one soldier brought in from elsewhere can be dismissed; once one unit has completed its training, one unit brought in from elsewhere can be dismissed. As training proceeds, dismissals can follow. Within two or three years, all the troops brought in from elsewhere can be sent away, and the levies for their pay and provisions can be entirely remitted. Replacing these outside troops with local militia troops (jibing), and converting military funding into wages and subsistence allowances, would make the two arrangements support each other. Moreover, would not the savings be incalculable?

Otherwise, if moxa has not been stored in advance, the physician from afar can never be sent away. Even if money is amassed in heaps like hills and grain piled up like mountains, could resources as vast as rivers ever keep pace with a leaking cup? Thus those who discuss military affairs generally regard this as a cause for concern, and consequently there have arisen…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
閒田之論寺租之說夫今閩升斗之地盡
入版圖無復閒田可供召募而寺租雖多
悉充軍餉又安有奇贏給土兵哉二說蓋
不可行也宋咸平中王元之言於朝曰福
建等郡酌民户衆寡城池大小並許置本
城守捉軍士習弓劔葺城壘夫抽取于民
非土兵邪元之欲行之於宋顧不可行之
於今邪抑有說焉曩者寇犯閩境其爲嚮
導而來者多土人也蓋遊手之徒囂然好
===
逞中有魁黠者起而倡之往往相率從亂
大抵寇盜最可慮者其中有魁黠也魁黠
在中未易卒制周亞夫征吳楚急索劇孟
誠慮之也乃今用土兵則草萊之魁黠具
可籠取束縛之而銷亡外寇之術固寓焉
此又練兵之一益也雖然謀國之要不在
立法而在得人守懷州者得一抱真焉則
澤潞孱丁皆爲勇敢矣守西川者得一德
裕焉則劔南子弟可以雄邊矣故愚之所
punctuated:
閒田之論、寺租之說。夫今閩升斗之地盡入版圖，無復閒田可供召募，而寺租雖多，悉充軍餉，又安有奇贏給土兵哉？二說蓋不可行也。宋咸平中，王元之言於朝曰：「福建等郡，酌民户衆寡、城池大小，並許置本城守捉軍士，習弓劔，葺城壘。」夫抽取于民，非土兵邪？元之欲行之於宋，顧不可行之於今邪？抑有說焉：曩者寇犯閩境，其爲嚮導而來者多土人也。蓋遊手之徒，囂然好逞，中有魁黠者起而倡之，往往相率從亂。大抵寇盜最可慮者，其中有魁黠也。魁黠在中，未易卒制。周亞夫征吳楚，急索劇孟，誠慮之也。乃今用土兵，則草萊之魁黠具可籠取，束縛之，而銷亡外寇之術固寓焉。此又練兵之一益也。

雖然，謀國之要不在立法，而在得人。守懷州者，得一抱真焉，則澤潞孱丁皆爲勇敢矣；守西川者，得一德裕焉，則劔南子弟可以雄邊矣。故愚之所
translation_en:
…discussions of idle land and proposals concerning monastery rents. Yet in Fujian today, every scrap of land is already entered in the territorial registers; no idle land remains to support recruitment. Although monastery rents are considerable, they are all devoted to military pay and provisions. Where, then, could there be any surplus to support local troops? Neither proposal is practicable. During the Xianping reign of the Song, Wang Yuanzhi told the court: “In Fujian and other prefectures, permission should be granted to establish soldiers to guard each prefectural city, taking account of the number of civilian households and the size of the city and its walls. They should practice archery and swordsmanship and repair the walls and fortifications.” Men drawn from the civilian population—are these not local troops? If Yuanzhi wished to implement this in the Song, could it really not be implemented today? There is another consideration. When raiders formerly invaded Fujian, many of those who came as their guides were local people. Idle fellows are boisterous and eager to assert themselves; when a cunning ringleader arises among them and takes the lead, they often follow one another into rebellion. Generally, what is most worrying about bandits is the presence of cunning ringleaders among them. With such men in their midst, they cannot easily be subdued at short notice. When Zhou Yafu campaigned against Wu and Chu, he urgently sought out Ju Meng precisely because he feared this. If local troops are now employed, the cunning ringleaders among the common people can all be drawn in and brought under restraint. A means of eliminating outside raiders is thus inherent in the scheme. This is another benefit of training troops.

Even so, the essential point in planning for the state lies in obtaining the right men rather than establishing regulations. With a Baozhen to defend Huaizhou, even the weak men of Ze and Lu became brave fighters; with a Deyu to defend Xichuan, the young men of Jiannan could make the frontier formidable. Thus, what I, in my humble judgment, …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
陳者皆自其救偏補弊者言之而究其本
則固存乎其人耳子朱子有言曰聖王制
禦夷狄之道其具不在兵食而在綱紀愚
則曰今日整飭八閩之方其具不在兵食
而在守令執事以爲何如
punctuated: 陳者，皆自其救偏補弊者言之，而究其本，則固存乎其人耳。子朱子有言曰：「聖王制禦夷狄之道，其具不在兵食，而在綱紀。」愚則曰：「今日整飭八閩之方，其具不在兵食，而在守令。」執事以爲何如？
translation_en: …what I have set forth has all been concerned with correcting imbalances and remedying abuses; yet, tracing the matter to its root, it surely rests with the right people. Master Zhu Xi once said: “In the sage kings’ way of controlling the barbarians, the means lay not in troops and provisions, but in the guiding principles and discipline of government.” I, for my part, would say: “In setting the Eight Min regions of Fujian in order today, the means lie not in troops and provisions, but in prefects and county magistrates.” What is your judgment on this, honored examiners?

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄後序
隆慶庚午秋福建當賓興御
史蒙詔申飭規條視昔益虔
益密事竣大勳不佞從諸執
事後例得敘諸末簡竊謂賢
哲之生受才於天鍾氣於地
而應用於
===
君天運會則昌地形靈則傑而
君道盛則得以竟其所施此古今
大較也八閩古揚州域吻海
派江孤峯危嶽秀美甲天下
逸氣所鍾豈獨鹽鐵金沙素
馨長竹已哉其間洪猷偉器
後先繼鳴或慷慨憂時孤直
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄後序

隆慶庚午秋，福建當賓興，御史蒙詔申飭規條，視昔益虔益密。事竣，大勳不佞，從諸執事後，例得敘諸末簡。竊謂賢哲之生，受才於天，鍾氣於地，而應用於君。天運會則昌，地形靈則傑，而君道盛則得以竟其所施，此古今大較也。八閩古揚州域，吻海派江，孤峯危嶽，秀美甲天下。逸氣所鍾，豈獨鹽鐵金沙、素馨長竹已哉？其間洪猷偉器，後先繼鳴，或慷慨憂時，孤直
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the gengwu year of Longqing [1570], Fujian was due to select and honor worthy candidates. The Censor received an imperial edict reiterating and enforcing the regulations, observing them with still greater reverence and care than before. When the proceedings were complete, I, Daxun, untalented though I am, having followed behind the officials conducting them, was permitted by precedent to append a postface to the final pages. I humbly believe that worthy and wise men, at birth, receive their talents from Heaven and the concentrated vital energies of the earth, and put these to use in serving their ruler. When Heaven’s cycles converge, they flourish; where the land’s configuration possesses numinous potency, outstanding men arise; and when the ruler’s Way flourishes, they can fully realize their abilities. This is the general pattern throughout antiquity and the present.

The Eight Min [Fujian] lay within the territory of ancient Yangzhou. Bordering the sea and threaded with branching rivers [?], its isolated peaks and lofty mountains possess a beauty unsurpassed under Heaven. Could the exceptional energies concentrated here produce only salt, iron, golden sands, jasmine, and tall bamboo? Among its people, men of grand designs and extraordinary capacity have won renown in succession, some passionately concerned for their times, solitary in their uprightness …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
自遂或深沉莊重明習故常
或耿介絕羣清標離俗或委
身經略力成朝廷或繼堯舜
周孔之傳或衍春秋皇極之
學求之唐宋間已褒然顯矣
明興人文益賁濟濟彬彬未易屈
指數今
===
皇上嗣位百度咸貞納言官儒臣
之
請開
恩選增科額
夢寐英賢如饑如渴非君子嚮
用日耶矧序當薦期歲屬庚
午陰陽之運尤為不偶何者
punctuated:
自遂，或深沉莊重，明習故常；或耿介絕羣，清標離俗；或委身經略，力成朝廷；或繼堯舜周孔之傳；或衍春秋皇極之學。求之唐宋間，已褒然顯矣。明興，人文益賁，濟濟彬彬，未易屈指數。
今皇上嗣位，百度咸貞，納言官儒臣之請，開恩選，增科額，夢寐英賢，如饑如渴，非君子嚮用日耶？矧序當薦期，歲屬庚午，陰陽之運尤為不偶。何者？
translation_en:
…fulfilled their own aspirations; some were profound and dignified, thoroughly versed in established precedents; some were upright and stood above the crowd, their pure distinction setting them apart from worldly ways; some devoted themselves to affairs of state, exerting themselves to strengthen the court; some continued the tradition of Yao, Shun, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius; and some developed the learning of the Spring and Autumn Annals and the August Ultimate. Such men were already conspicuous in their distinction during the Tang and Song. With the rise of the Ming, cultural accomplishment became still more resplendent. So numerous were these cultivated men that they could scarcely be counted on one’s fingers.
Now that His Majesty has succeeded to the throne, all institutions have been set right. Accepting the petitions of remonstrance officials and scholar-officials, he has authorized selection by imperial grace and increased the examination quota. He dreams of outstanding and worthy men, hungering and thirsting for them. Is this not the day when gentlemen are welcomed into service? Moreover, the season has come for recommending candidates, and the year is gengwu: the workings of yin and yang are especially extraordinary. Why is this so? …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
天地生生之數實在庚午元
之氣盛在午故庚於五行爲
金有從革之義焉蓋說文以
庚爲更也意者其人文丕變
之時乎午於月令爲火有離
明之象焉蓋律吕以午爲蕤
賓也意者其利用賓王之會
===
乎夫槩封疆之全可以徵地
靈察歲德之隆可以占
昌運惟玆多士豈無洪猷偉器
如古者以應
大君側席之求哉上續臯陶之歌
下述王褒之頌士生斯世而
得遇
punctuated:
天地生生之數，實在庚午，元之氣盛在午，故庚於五行爲金，有從革之義焉。蓋《說文》以庚爲更也，意者其人文丕變之時乎？午於月令爲火，有離明之象焉。蓋律吕以午爲蕤賓也，意者其利用賓王之會乎？
夫槩封疆之全，可以徵地靈；察歲德之隆，可以占昌運。惟玆多士，豈無洪猷偉器如古者，以應大君側席之求哉？上續臯陶之歌，下述王褒之頌。士生斯世，而得遇
translation_en:
The numerical cycle through which Heaven and Earth continually generate life rests indeed in gengwu. The primal vital force flourishes at wu; thus geng corresponds to metal among the Five Phases and carries the meaning of yielding to transformation. The Explanation of Graphs and Analysis of Characters (Shuowen) explains geng as “renewal.” Might this, then, be a time of great transformation in cultural accomplishment? Wu corresponds to fire in the Monthly Ordinances and possesses the image of brightness associated with the trigram Li. In the system of pitch standards, wu corresponds to Ruibin. Might this, then, be the occasion when “it is favorable to be a guest of the king”?
Surveying the entire territory, one can discern the spiritual potency of the land; observing the fullness of the year's auspicious virtue, one can foretell a flourishing age. Among these many scholars, surely there are men of grand designs and outstanding capacity, like those of antiquity, who can answer the great ruler's eager search for worthy men, for whom he leaves a place beside him? They may carry on the song of Gao Yao from remote antiquity and perpetuate the eulogies of Wang Bao from a later age. For scholars to be born into this age and have the opportunity to encounter…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
明天子幸矣顧諸士亦知所以自
靖乎耕人織婦以業爲供販
夫賈子以貨爲稅乃稻黍枲
絲嬪珠金錯丹漆玄黃之屬
姑無論卽微如齒毛羽革有
一不登
天府待財用耶而士獨以聲律
===
比耦之技
獻罔當世用視農賈不其有餘
赧哉夫人臣懷以人事
君之忠而僅惟手空文以求士士
人抱適用之學而僅亦以空
文售知於人乃今多士以文
進矣其自許云何夫處則綜
punctuated: 明天子，幸矣！顧諸士亦知所以自靖乎？耕人織婦以業爲供，販夫賈子以貨爲稅，乃稻黍枲絲、嬪珠金錯、丹漆玄黃之屬，姑無論；卽微如齒毛羽革，有一不登天府待財用耶？而士獨以聲律比耦之技獻，罔當世用，視農賈，不其有餘赧哉？夫人臣懷以人事君之忠，而僅惟手空文以求士；士人抱適用之學，而僅亦以空文售知於人。乃今多士以文進矣，其自許云何？夫處則綜
translation_en: …an enlightened Son of Heaven—how fortunate! Yet do you gentlemen also understand how to discharge your own responsibilities? Ploughmen and weaving women provide contributions through their occupations; peddlers and merchants pay taxes on their goods. Let us leave aside such things as rice and millet, hemp and silk, pearls and inlaid gold [?], cinnabar and lacquer, and black and yellow pigments. Even among such humble things as teeth, hair, feathers, and hides, is there anything that does not enter the imperial treasury to meet financial and material needs? Yet scholars alone offer their skill in tonal patterns and parallel phrasing, with nothing useful to the present age. Compared with farmers and merchants, should they not feel deeply ashamed? An official cherishes the loyalty that seeks to serve his ruler by finding worthy men, yet merely takes empty compositions in hand to recruit scholars; a scholar possesses learning suited to practical use, yet likewise seeks recognition from others merely through empty compositions. Now you gentlemen have advanced through literary composition: what do you pledge yourselves to accomplish? When living in retirement, you should comprehensively study…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
圖校史嚅嚌聖真出則抱功
脩職澤加品庶皆吾分內事
詎謂以文進遂以文用耶且
昔之所謂洪猷偉器者始進
孰不以文厥後功懋當時聲
施來葉無復以空文病之今
其人遠矣其事識在長老諸
===
士盍往諮之反之身心假令
今歲隨計吏來歲試春官授
以中外政其抉膽獻圖能如
鄭俠乎剖赤條畫能如曾公
亮乎抗顏停草能如楊億乎
智周經濟忠切時艱能如李
綱乎距詖放淫閑先開後能
punctuated: 圖校史，嚅嚌聖真；出則抱功脩職，澤加品庶，皆吾分內事。詎謂以文進，遂以文用耶？且昔之所謂洪猷偉器者，始進孰不以文？厥後功懋當時，聲施來葉，無復以空文病之。今其人遠矣，其事識在長老，諸士盍往諮之，反之身心？假令今歲隨計吏，來歲試春官，授以中外政，其抉膽獻圖，能如鄭俠乎？剖赤條畫，能如曾公亮乎？抗顏停草，能如楊億乎？智周經濟，忠切時艱，能如李綱乎？距詖放淫，閑先開後，能
translation_en:
…charts and collate histories, savoring the true teachings of the sages; upon entering office, undertake meritorious work [?] and discharge your duties, extending benefits to the common people—all these are within our allotted responsibilities. Could it be that, because one advances through literary accomplishment, one is therefore employed solely for it? Moreover, among those of former times celebrated for grand designs and outstanding abilities, who did not first advance through literary accomplishment? Later, their achievements distinguished their own age and their fame spread to succeeding generations; no one any longer reproached them for empty writing. Those men are now distant from us, but knowledge of their deeds remains among the elders. Why do you gentlemen not go and consult them, then turn what you learn back upon your own minds and conduct?

Suppose that this year you accompany the tribute delegation to the capital, next year sit the examination at the Ministry of Rites, and then receive administrative responsibilities in the capital or the provinces. In laying bare your deepest convictions and presenting an illustrated remonstrance, could you equal Zheng Xia? In revealing your sincere heart and setting out detailed plans, could you equal Zeng Gongliang? In maintaining an unyielding countenance and refusing to continue drafting, could you equal Yang Yi? In wisdom encompassing the ordering of the realm, and loyalty urgently addressing the difficulties of the times, could you equal Li Gang? In resisting biased doctrines and banishing extravagant teachings, safeguarding the legacy of earlier sages and opening the way for those to come, could you…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
如楊如羅如李如朱如胡氏
兄弟蔡氏父子乎方爾淹迹
草茅屏居自計謂天下事輒
有言之未可行之無由而掩
卷咨嗟思以身代之而莫得
其便者行將事事矣可弗訪
前脩圖厥終耶夫溺利易趨
===
者庸棄其平生和俗取容者
間變其初志釣名沽譽者終
不厭於眾情守寂空談者多
無得於實際而砥礪過激者
尚或歉於中行於此有一焉
豈惟若人羞之諺曰腐蠧不
提一筐盡染彼二三子者能
punctuated: 如楊、如羅、如李、如朱、如胡氏兄弟、蔡氏父子乎？方爾淹迹草茅，屏居自計，謂天下事輒有言之未可、行之無由，而掩卷咨嗟，思以身代之而莫得其便者，行將事事矣，可弗訪前脩、圖厥終耶？夫溺利易趨者，庸棄其平生；和俗取容者，間變其初志；釣名沽譽者，終不厭於眾情；守寂空談者，多無得於實際；而砥礪過激者，尚或歉於中行。於此有一焉，豈惟若人羞之？諺曰：「腐蠧不提，一筐盡染。」彼二三子者能
translation_en:
…like Yang, Luo, Li, Zhu, the Hu brothers, or the Cai father and son?

While you remained obscure among the common people, living in retirement and reflecting privately, you considered the affairs of the realm and repeatedly found matters about which you could not yet speak and had no means to act. You closed your books and sighed, wishing to take the place of those responsible but finding no opportunity. Now you will soon be handling affairs yourselves. Can you fail to inquire into the worthy men of earlier times and plan how to carry your purpose through to the end?

Those who become engrossed in profit and shift their allegiances readily abandon their lifelong principles; those who conform to prevailing customs to win acceptance sometimes change their original resolve; those who angle for fame and purchase praise ultimately fail to satisfy public sentiment; those who cling to quietude and empty talk generally accomplish nothing in practical affairs; and even those who discipline themselves with excessive severity may fall short of balanced conduct. If any one of these failings is present, would the shame belong only to the person concerned? As the proverb says: “If what is rotten and worm-eaten is not removed, the whole basket becomes infected.” Can those gentlemen …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
無緣一不檢者而槩目爲敗
羣哉爾其矢志宣猷交相勸
勉毋沿今習毋謝昔軌脩之
帷席措之巖廊勿使背而馳
若兩人焉果爾則仰足以當
天運俯足以應地靈上之不負
天子下之不誤蒼生即八閩山川
===
且有華色而大勳等以人事
君之忠庶幾可慰藉萬一矣諸士
其重念之哉
直隸松江府儒學敎授夏大
勳謹序
punctuated:
無緣一不檢者而槩目爲敗羣哉？爾其矢志宣猷，交相勸勉，毋沿今習，毋謝昔軌。脩之帷席，措之巖廊，勿使背而馳，若兩人焉。果爾，則仰足以當天運，俯足以應地靈，上之不負天子，下之不誤蒼生，即八閩山川且有華色，而大勳等以人事君之忠，庶幾可慰藉萬一矣。諸士其重念之哉！
直隸松江府儒學敎授夏大勳謹序。
translation_en:
… avoid being indiscriminately branded as corrupting the company on account of a single person’s misconduct? You should resolve to advance sound governance and encourage one another. Do not follow present-day habits or abandon the standards of the past. Cultivate yourselves in your private chambers and put that cultivation into practice at court; do not let the two run in opposite directions, as though you were two different people. If you do this, you will be worthy of Heaven’s course above and responsive to the earth’s spiritual potency below. You will neither fail the Son of Heaven above nor lead the common people astray below. Even the mountains and rivers of the Eight Min regions will gain lustre, and our loyal efforts—those of myself, Daxun, and my colleagues—to serve our ruler by providing worthy men may thereby find some small measure of consolation. Gentlemen, ponder this deeply!
Preface respectfully written by Xia Daxun, Instructor in the Confucian School of Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region.

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄序
庚午秋八月天下當復貢士
于鄉今
皇上龍飛之第二科也方
建元初屬大比期
皇上冀得真才任使首
詔下有司釐正文體諸不應經義
===
浮蔓者黜之天下士蒸蒸嚮
風至是復從禮官議申飭約
束而限之言法視昔加密矣
維時御史蒙詔奉
上命來按閩部祗承
德意惟惓惟虔乃博訪四方文學
之臣以禮聘機暨教授夏大
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄序

庚午秋八月，天下當復貢士于鄉，今皇上龍飛之第二科也。方建元初，屬大比期，皇上冀得真才任使，首詔下有司，釐正文體，諸不應經義、浮蔓者黜之。天下士蒸蒸嚮風。至是，復從禮官議，申飭約束，而限之言法，視昔加密矣。維時御史蒙詔奉上命來按閩部，祗承德意，惟惓惟虔，乃博訪四方文學之臣，以禮聘機暨教授夏大
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the gengwu year [1570], the time had come once again for the provinces throughout the realm to present candidates through their Provincial Examinations. This was the second examination cycle since His Majesty ascended the throne. At the beginning of his reign, a triennial examination fell due. His Majesty, hoping to obtain men of genuine ability to employ in office, first issued an edict to the responsible authorities to rectify the style of examination writing: any essays that failed to accord with the meaning of the Classics or were superficial and prolix were to be rejected. Scholars throughout the realm increasingly responded to this guidance. Now, following a further recommendation from the ritual officials, he reiterated the regulations and imposed rules governing expression, making them more exacting than before.

At this time, Censor Meng Zhao, acting on imperial command, came to inspect Fujian. Reverently receiving His Majesty’s benevolent intentions, he applied himself with devotion and reverence. He therefore made extensive inquiries for officials of literary learning from all quarters and, with due ceremony, invited me, Ji, together with the Confucian School Professor Xia Da…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
勳爲考試官敎授吳希旦學
正黃自任龍養性敎諭李明
通王汝振朱繼魯趙友仁許
嘉榮爲同考試官各以其經
至届期以左布政使陳典右
布政使周賢宣司提調按察
使陳一松僉事王圻司監試
===
其餘百執事咸愼遴以充而
御史寔監臨焉御史率諸大
夫文學集于庭揚觶矢言曰
上臣事君以人舉非其人惟
爾不任如人臣之義何諸大
夫文學罔不懍懍改色惕慮
而後卽事於是進提學副使
punctuated:
勳爲考試官，敎授吳希旦、學正黃自任、龍養性、敎諭李明通、王汝振、朱繼魯、趙友仁、許嘉榮爲同考試官，各以其經至。届期，以左布政使陳典、右布政使周賢宣司提調，按察使陳一松、僉事王圻司監試。其餘百執事，咸愼遴以充，而御史寔監臨焉。
御史率諸大夫文學集于庭，揚觶矢言曰：「上臣事君以人，舉非其人，惟爾不任，如人臣之義何？」諸大夫文學罔不懍懍改色惕慮，而後卽事。於是進提學副使
translation_en:
…Xia Daxun to serve as Examiner; Professor Wu Xidan, Instructors Huang Ziren and Long Yangxing, and Instructors Li Mingtong, Wang Ruzhen, Zhu Jilu, Zhao Youren, and Xu Jiarong to serve as Associate Examiners. Each arrived to examine in his respective Classic. When the appointed time came, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Dian and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhou Xianxuan were assigned to serve as Proctors; Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Chen Yisong and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Wang Qi were assigned to oversee the examination. All the remaining functionaries were carefully selected to fill their posts, while the Censor himself served as Supervising Official.
The Censor led the officials and scholars in assembling in the courtyard. Raising a ritual wine cup, he solemnly declared: “A high minister [?] serves his ruler by finding worthy men. If you recommend someone unfit, you have failed in your charge. How would that accord with a minister’s duty?” Every official and scholar grew solemn, his expression changing as he considered his responsibilities with apprehension; only then did they begin their work. Thereupon, they brought forward the Education Intendant and Deputy Surveillance Commissioner’s…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
周弘祖所選士二千七百有
奇三試之登其雋者九十人
弁梓其文以
獻
制也機以職事當僭言于首簡機
聞之易曰君子藏器於身待
時而動夫士伏處嵓巖之下
冥搜墳典誦法孔孟席珍以
待聘孰不思表見所志徼尺
寸之功於當世哉然而出潛
遘會有時存焉時不可强也
是故君子恥懷寶以傲世而
亦不能違時以就功尺蠖附
於飛龍蒼蠅致乎千里時也
punctuated: 周弘祖所選士二千七百有奇，三試之，登其雋者九十人，弁梓其文以獻，制也。機以職事，當僭言于首簡。機聞之，《易》曰：「君子藏器於身，待時而動。」夫士伏處嵓巖之下，冥搜墳典，誦法孔孟，席珍以待聘，孰不思表見所志，徼尺寸之功於當世哉？然而出潛遘會，有時存焉，時不可强也。是故君子恥懷寶以傲世，而亦不能違時以就功。尺蠖附於飛龍，蒼蠅致乎千里，時也。
translation_en:
…the more than 2,700 candidates selected by Zhou Hongzu. They were examined in three sessions, and ninety of the most outstanding were selected. Their essays were provided with a preface and printed for presentation to the throne, as prescribed. By virtue of my official duties, I, Ji, must presume to offer some words on the opening pages.

I have heard these words from the Book of Changes: “The gentleman stores his capabilities within himself and awaits the proper time to act.” Scholars dwell in seclusion beneath rocky cliffs, delve deeply into the ancient canonical writings, recite and take as their models Confucius and Mencius, and preserve their precious learning while awaiting a summons to service. Who among them does not wish to manifest his aspirations and seek even a modest accomplishment in the world of his day? Yet emerging from seclusion and encountering an opportunity depend upon the proper time, and that time cannot be forced. Thus the gentleman considers it shameful to hoard his treasures and disdain the world, yet neither can he go against the times to achieve success. That an inchworm may cling to a flying dragon, or a bluebottle fly reach a thousand li away, is a matter of timely opportunity.

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
我
皇上聖神天縱
嗣登寶曆
總乾綱
親儒碩
從言速於轉圜
求賢徵於夢賚野無佚才
===
朝無素飽
仁恩所被薄海內外罔不磅礴四
塞
文明熈洽之運誠千載而一時也
夫時者士之所遭所以利見
展錯以顯洩其平生之藏者
也諸士際斯時應賢科之選
punctuated:
我皇上聖神天縱，嗣登寶曆，總乾綱，親儒碩，從言速於轉圜，求賢徵於夢賚，野無佚才，朝無素飽。仁恩所被，薄海內外，罔不磅礴四塞。文明熈洽之運，誠千載而一時也。
夫時者，士之所遭，所以利見展錯，以顯洩其平生之藏者也。諸士際斯時，應賢科之選，
translation_en:
Our Emperor, endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom and divine insight, has succeeded to the imperial throne. He holds supreme authority, draws eminent Confucian scholars close, and accepts counsel more swiftly than a sphere turns. His search for worthy men finds its portent in a dream of receiving a Heaven-sent assistant. No talent remains overlooked in the countryside, and no one at court draws sustenance without rendering service. His benevolence extends throughout the realm and beyond, reaching everywhere and filling all quarters. This age of flourishing culture and harmonious prosperity is truly an opportunity encountered only once in a thousand years.
For scholars, the times they encounter provide the opportunity to appear before their sovereign and put their abilities into practice, revealing what they have stored up throughout their lives. You scholars, living at this moment and answering the call to selection through the examination for worthy men, …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
策名
天府揚于王路其所遭甚偉乃
其所素具先資以成信者則
何以哉機謬從諸文學後縱
觀閩士所爲文其指遠其詞
達其言必稱先王其揆事曲
而中其上下今古博雅而裁
===
蔚乎華國之昌言一陶鎔
聖化而軌于正者也機亟讀亟收
之以告御史使偕計吏誠器
之矣而諸士其何以器于世
乎夫天球河圖寶刀大弓商
彝周鼎薦清廟侈國寶天下
之珍器也上也其次若簠簋
punctuated:
策名天府，揚于王路，其所遭甚偉。乃其所素具先資以成信者，則何以哉？機謬從諸文學後，縱觀閩士所爲文，其指遠，其詞達，其言必稱先王，其揆事曲而中，其上下今古，博雅而裁。蔚乎華國之昌言，一陶鎔聖化而軌于正者也。機亟讀亟收之，以告御史，使偕計吏，誠器之矣。而諸士其何以器于世乎？
夫天球、河圖、寶刀、大弓、商彝、周鼎，薦清廟，侈國寶，天下之珍器也，上也。其次若簠簋
translation_en:
…to have their names inscribed in the celestial repository and win distinction on the royal path: magnificent indeed is the opportunity they have encountered. Yet what are the qualities they have long possessed, their prior endowments by which they establish their worth [?]? I, Ji 機, have undeservedly followed in the ranks of men of learning. Surveying the writings of Fujian’s scholars, I find their meanings far-reaching and their language expressive. Their statements invariably invoke the former kings; their assessments of affairs are detailed and apt; and their excursions through past and present display broad learning, refinement, and discernment. These splendid pronouncements bring lustre to the realm: all have been moulded by the sage ruler’s transforming influence and guided onto the proper course. I, Ji, eagerly read and selected them, reporting to the Censor so that these scholars might travel with the officials presenting the provincial accounts. Truly, I esteemed their talents. But how will these scholars prove themselves useful instruments in the world?
Now the celestial jade sphere, the River Chart, the precious sword, the great bow, the ritual vessels of Shang, and the tripods of Zhou are presented in the pure ancestral temple, enhancing the splendour of the state’s treasures. These are the world’s precious objects, of the highest rank. Next come such vessels as the fu and gui …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
卮匜筐筥鬵鍑爲品不同皆
可以適世用而敝帚鉛刀則
視之爲贅物矣夫士之器亦
有類乎是者是不可以不辨
也機之執策進諸士也始而
喜已而大懼何也機鉛槧士
也幸而與於校士之役又幸
===
而祗役於閩閩才藪也羣千
百士之秀焉拔其尤茲人文
之極選也藉是可以報
天子矣故喜抑機之所以進諸士
也文也文可以信諸士乎否
也今天下之士習偽矣緣飾
詩書以游言譁衆者其詞理
punctuated: 卮、匜、筐、筥、鬵、鍑，爲品不同，皆可以適世用，而敝帚、鉛刀則視之爲贅物矣。夫士之器亦有類乎是者，是不可以不辨也。機之執策進諸士也，始而喜，已而大懼，何也？機，鉛槧士也，幸而與於校士之役，又幸而祗役於閩。閩，才藪也，羣千百士之秀焉，拔其尤，茲人文之極選也。藉是可以報天子矣，故喜。抑機之所以進諸士也，文也。文可以信諸士乎？否也。今天下之士習偽矣，緣飾《詩》《書》以游言譁衆者，其詞理，
translation_en:
… drinking cups, pouring vessels, square and round baskets, and cooking pots and cauldrons: although their kinds differ, all can serve practical needs. Worn-out brooms and leaden knives, however, are regarded as useless encumbrances. Scholars’ capacities likewise fall into comparable categories; these distinctions must be discerned.

When I, Ji, took up the examination essays to advance these scholars, I was at first delighted, but then became deeply apprehensive. Why? I am merely a scholar of pencil and writing tablet, fortunate enough to participate in the work of examining scholars, and fortunate, moreover, to perform this duty in Min. Min is a gathering place of talent. To assemble the finest among its hundreds and thousands of scholars and select the most outstanding is to make the highest selection of literary talent. Through this I could repay the Son of Heaven; hence my delight.

Yet what I used to advance these scholars was their writing. Can their writing establish that these scholars are trustworthy? No. Scholars throughout the realm today have become practiced in deception. Those who embellish their words with the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, using empty talk to impress the crowd—their language is well ordered …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
綴緝纖華以詭世巧售者其
詞澤剽竊異端以隱義誑俗
者其詞奥若是者皆足以炫
有司之目而或未之辨焉機
所以鰓鰓焉懼也嗟乎三代
而下取士代更自科目之制
起俶儻魁壘之佐鮮不羔鴈
===
於文藝文之貴乎世也久矣
自夫士以偽售於是庸之而
違試之罔功則雖雕龍吐鳳
燁然照世無裨實用君子弗
尚也諸士既襃然以文舉矣
由是而砥節礪躬亮工楨
國于以樹俶儻魁壘之烈光助
punctuated: 綴緝纖華以詭世巧售者，其詞澤；剽竊異端以隱義誑俗者，其詞奥。若是者，皆足以炫有司之目，而或未之辨焉，機所以鰓鰓焉懼也。嗟乎！三代而下，取士代更。自科目之制起，俶儻魁壘之佐，鮮不羔鴈於文藝。文之貴乎世也久矣！自夫士以偽售，於是庸之而違，試之罔功，則雖雕龍吐鳳，燁然照世，無裨實用，君子弗尚也。諸士既襃然以文舉矣，由是而砥節礪躬，亮工楨國，于以樹俶儻魁壘之烈，光助
translation_en:
… Those who stitch together delicate embellishments to deceive the world and artfully win acceptance have polished diction; those who plagiarize heterodox teachings to obscure right principles and delude ordinary people have abstruse diction. All such writers can dazzle the officials’ eyes, and their deception may go undetected. This is why I, Ji, am so anxiously afraid.

Alas! Since the Three Dynasties, methods of selecting officials have changed from age to age. Since the examination system arose, scarcely any outstanding and extraordinary ministers have received the gifts of recruitment except through literary accomplishment. Literature has long been esteemed in the world! Yet when scholars gain acceptance through deception, they prove wanting when employed and achieve nothing when put to the test. Even if their writing carves dragons and pours forth phoenixes, shining brilliantly upon the world, it contributes nothing to practical service; the gentleman does not esteem it.

You scholars have now been honorably selected for your writing. From this point, temper your integrity and discipline yourselves, faithfully discharge your duties and serve as pillars of the state, thereby establishing extraordinary and outstanding achievements and lending lustre and support to …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
太平施令聞無窮不亦偉乎是
又安可讓也夫閩奠在南服
山海之奧區也靈氣鬱發人
文昭宣爰稽往牒才哲項背
相望而龜山延平考亭數先
生者又以身任濂洛道統之
傳析微闡晦六經於是大明
===
今之緝藻橫塾褒衣膠序者
孰不嚌其菁華而窺其堂奧
其淵源蓋與海內學士異矣
夫求珠赤水𦋇玉崑崙市駿
大宛他郡國非無是三者而
必於赤水崑崙大宛乎稱焉
則其產良也道南一脈比跡
punctuated:
太平，施令聞無窮，不亦偉乎？是又安可讓也？夫閩奠在南服，山海之奧區也。靈氣鬱發，人文昭宣。爰稽往牒，才哲項背相望，而龜山、延平、考亭數先生者，又以身任濂洛道統之傳，析微闡晦，六經於是大明。
今之緝藻橫塾、褒衣膠序者，孰不嚌其菁華而窺其堂奧？其淵源蓋與海內學士異矣。夫求珠赤水，𦋇玉崑崙，市駿大宛，他郡國非無是三者，而必於赤水、崑崙、大宛乎稱焉，則其產良也。道南一脈，比跡
translation_en:
…great peace, and spread an honorable reputation without end: would this not be magnificent? How, then, could one yield this responsibility to others? Min lies firmly within the southern domains, a secluded region of mountains and sea. Its spiritual energies issue forth abundantly, and its cultural achievements shine resplendently. Examining past records, we find talented and wise men following closely upon one another. The masters Guishan, Yanping, and Kaoting moreover personally assumed responsibility for transmitting the orthodox succession of the Way from Lian and Luo. They elucidated subtleties and brought obscurities to light, so that the Six Classics became fully clear.
Among those who now compose ornate writings in the schools [?] and wear ample scholarly robes in the academies, who has not tasted their finest essence and glimpsed the inner chambers of their learning? Their intellectual sources and lineage surely distinguish them from scholars elsewhere in the realm. One seeks pearls in Chishui, gathers jade [?] in Kunlun, and buys fine horses in Dayuan. Other regions are not without these three things; yet whenever they are praised, Chishui, Kunlun, and Dayuan must be named, because their products are excellent. The single lineage of the Way transmitted southward, matching the achievements of…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
鄒魯非閩產邪諸士挾所產
之良以售于有司有司採而
進之以應
聖世之求譬之沒赤水之淵陟崑
崙之巔涉大宛之澤百珍千
騎畢陳於前殫精竭智惟瓌
瑋奇麗是收而其贋且似者
===
棄之若土苴勿顧也於乎盛
矣諸士出而珪璋治世驅騁
千里使天下後世指以為隋
珠卞璧龍媒然而終免於贋
且似焉之誚有司藉以休榮
渥甚機之懼可少釋也已唐
陸贄有言上不負天子下不
punctuated: 鄒魯，非閩產邪？諸士挾所產之良，以售于有司；有司採而進之，以應聖世之求。譬之沒赤水之淵，陟崑崙之巔，涉大宛之澤，百珍千騎畢陳於前，殫精竭智，惟瓌瑋奇麗是收，而其贋且似者，棄之若土苴，勿顧也。於乎盛矣！諸士出而珪璋治世，驅騁千里，使天下後世指以為隋珠、卞璧、龍媒，然而終免於贋且似焉之誚，有司藉以休榮渥甚，機之懼可少釋也已。唐陸贄有言：「上不負天子，下不
translation_en:
…Zou and Lu—is this not a product of Fujian? The candidates bring the excellence native to their region to offer to the responsible officials, who select and advance them to answer the demand of this sagely age. It is like plunging into the depths of the Chishui, ascending the peaks of Kunlun, or traversing the marshes of Dayuan: a hundred treasures and a thousand steeds are all displayed before one. Exhausting every resource of discernment, one takes only what is extraordinary, magnificent, rare, and beautiful; counterfeits and mere look-alikes are discarded like dirt and weeds, without another glance. Ah, how splendid!

When these candidates enter public service, serving as precious ritual jades in the governance of the age and galloping a thousand li, may they lead all under Heaven and later generations to point to them as the pearl of Sui, the jade of Bian, and dragon steeds, and thus escape forever the reproach of being counterfeits or mere look-alikes. The responsible officials would thereby gain honor in great abundance, and my apprehension—Ji’s—might somewhat abate. Lu Zhi of the Tang once said: “Above, one must not fail the Son of Heaven; below, one must not…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
負所學斯言古今韙之爾諸
士淑艾儒先兢兢於當世之
務則既學之素矣當
文明熈洽之朝抱其器以出行列
明廷交戟之下
聖天子將器其才而使之諸士其
厚自重惜以仰答
===
當宁以懋揚其素所蘊蓄者乎詩
曰藹藹王多吉士維君子使
媚于天子媚于天子而後可
以稱不負矣諸士勗諸是役
也提督巡撫右僉都御史何
寛輯寧疆宇文教弘敷前提
督南贛今巡撫湖廣右僉都
punctuated:
負所學。斯言古今韙之。爾諸士淑艾儒先，兢兢於當世之務，則既學之素矣。當文明熈洽之朝，抱其器以出，行列明廷交戟之下，聖天子將器其才而使之。諸士其厚自重惜，以仰答當宁，以懋揚其素所蘊蓄者乎！詩曰：「藹藹王多吉士，維君子使，媚于天子。」媚于天子，而後可以稱不負矣。諸士勗諸！
是役也，提督巡撫右僉都御史何寛，輯寧疆宇，文教弘敷；前提督南贛、今巡撫湖廣右僉都
translation_en:
…not fail what one has learned. This saying has been approved throughout the ages. You scholars have cultivated yourselves through the teachings of earlier Confucian masters and have diligently attended to the affairs of the present age: these are already the foundations of your learning. In this reign of enlightened culture and harmonious prosperity, you will come forth bearing your abilities and take your places beneath the crossed halberds of the illustrious court. The sagely Son of Heaven will employ you according to your talents. You scholars should deeply cherish and respect yourselves, thereby repaying the reigning sovereign and bringing fully to light what you have long cultivated within! The Book of Odes says: “In great numbers, the king has many worthy men; the lord employs them, and they win the Son of Heaven’s favor.” Only after winning the Son of Heaven’s favor can you be said not to have failed. Exert yourselves, scholars!
For this examination, He Kuan, Superintendent, Grand Coordinator, and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, has brought peace to the territory and widely extended cultural instruction; the former Superintendent of Nangan, now Grand Coordinator of Huguang and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
御史張翀風教丕宣章縫仰
止今提督南贛右僉都御史
殷從儉憲令初頒士心聿勸
鎮守總兵官署都督同知李
錫揚威茂績雅意尚文左參
政熊琦右參政顧𠄢副使陳
紹登黃宸參議劉志伊李紀
===
僉事蘇愚徐作王錫命顧養
謙副總兵官仍管參將事張
元勳遊擊將軍金科署都指
揮僉事狄從夏朱珏王克振
白瀚紀田義咸賛襄于外弼
成
盛典副使柴淶則以遷秩行亦始
punctuated: 御史張翀，風教丕宣，章縫仰止。今提督南贛右僉都御史殷從儉，憲令初頒，士心聿勸。鎮守總兵官署都督同知李錫，揚威茂績，雅意尚文。左參政熊琦、右參政顧𠄢、副使陳紹登、黃宸、參議劉志伊、李紀、僉事蘇愚、徐作、王錫命、顧養謙、副總兵官仍管參將事張元勳、遊擊將軍金科、署都指揮僉事狄從夏、朱珏、王克振、白瀚、紀田義，咸賛襄于外，弼成盛典。副使柴淶，則以遷秩行，亦始
translation_en:
…Censor-in-Chief Zhang Chong broadly disseminated moral instruction, and the scholars looked up to him. Yin Congjian, the current Supreme Commander of Nan-Gan and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, had only just promulgated his directives, yet already the scholars were encouraged. Li Xi, the Regional Commander stationed here and acting Vice Commissioner-in-Chief, displayed military prowess and achieved outstanding results, while esteeming literary learning.

Xiong Qi, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; Gu [?] 顧𠄢, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; Chen Shaodeng and Huang Chen, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Liu Zhiyi and Li Ji, Administration Assistant Commissioners; Su Yu, Xu Zuo, Wang Ximing, and Gu Yangqian, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; Zhang Yuanxun, Vice Regional Commander, still concurrently serving as Assistant Regional Commander; Jin Ke, Mobile Corps Commander; and Di Congxia, Zhu Jue, Wang Kezhen, Bai Han, and Ji Tianyi, acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners, all provided assistance outside the examination compound and helped bring this grand ceremony to completion. Surveillance Vice Commissioner Chai Lai departed upon promotion, but also, at the outset…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君子學以致其道
知遠之近知風之自知微之顯
孟子曰言近而指遠者善言也守約而施
博者善道也君子之言也不下帶而道
存焉君子之守脩其身而天下平
易
象曰天行健君子以自彊不息
===
惠我德大得志也
夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業也知崇禮卑
崇效天卑法地
天地之大德曰生聖人之大寶曰位
書
帝曰夔命汝典樂敎胄子直而溫寬而栗
剛而無虐簡而無傲詩言志歌永言聲
依永律和聲八音克諧無相奪倫神人
以和
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

君子學以致其道。

知遠之近，知風之自，知微之顯。

孟子曰：「言近而指遠者，善言也；守約而施博者，善道也。君子之言也，不下帶而道存焉；君子之守，脩其身而天下平。」

易

象曰：「天行健，君子以自彊不息。」

惠我德，大得志也。

夫易，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。

天地之大德曰生，聖人之大寶曰位。

書

帝曰：「夔！命汝典樂，敎胄子：直而溫，寬而栗，剛而無虐，簡而無傲。詩言志，歌永言，聲依永，律和聲。八音克諧，無相奪倫，神人以和。」
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The gentleman learns in order to realize his Way.

Know how what is distant lies in what is near, know whence the wind comes, and know how what is subtle becomes manifest.

Mencius said: “Words that are simple yet point far beyond themselves are good words; holding to what is essential yet applying it broadly is the good Way. The gentleman’s words do not go below his sash—that is, they concern what lies close at hand—yet the Way resides in them. What the gentleman holds to is cultivating his own person, and thereby all under Heaven is brought to peace.”

Book of Changes

The Commentary on the Images says: “Heaven moves with vigor; the gentleman accordingly strengthens himself without ceasing.”

“They show kindness toward my virtue”: this means fully attaining one’s purpose.

The Changes is that by which the sages exalt their virtue and extend their undertakings. Understanding is lofty; ritual propriety is humble. The lofty emulates Heaven; the humble models itself on Earth.

The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called life-giving; the great treasure of the sage is called his position.

Book of Documents

The Emperor said: “Kui! I command you to take charge of music and instruct the sons of the nobility: let them be upright yet gentle, tolerant yet firm, strong without cruelty, and straightforward without arrogance. Poetry expresses intent; song prolongs the words; musical tones follow that prolongation, and the pitch standards harmonize the tones. When the eight kinds of instruments sound in harmony, none disrupting the order of the others, spirits and humans are thereby brought into harmony.”

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
沿于江海達于淮泗
俾萬姓咸曰大哉王言又曰一哉王心
徽柔懿恭懷保小民惠鮮鰥寡自朝至于
日中昃不遑暇食用咸和萬民
詩
七月在野八月在宇九月在戶
駕彼四牡四牡奕奕赤芾金舄會同有繹
鳳凰于飛翽翽其羽亦集爰止藹藹王多
吉士維君子使媚于天子鳳凰于飛翽
===
翽其羽亦傅于天藹藹王多吉人維君
子命媚于庶人鳳凰鳴矣于彼高岡梧
桐生矣于彼朝陽菶菶萋萋雝雝喈喈
有秩斯祜申錫無疆
春秋
春王正月公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯
許男曹伯侵蔡蔡潰遂伐楚次于陘〔僖
公四年〕冬公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒
子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子
punctuated:
沿于江海，達于淮泗。
俾萬姓咸曰：「大哉王言！」又曰：「一哉王心！」
徽柔懿恭，懷保小民，惠鮮鰥寡，自朝至于日中昃，不遑暇食，用咸和萬民。

詩
七月在野，八月在宇，九月在戶。
駕彼四牡，四牡奕奕。赤芾金舄，會同有繹。
鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦集爰止。藹藹王多吉士，維君子使，媚于天子。鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦傅于天。藹藹王多吉人，維君子命，媚于庶人。鳳凰鳴矣，于彼高岡。梧桐生矣，于彼朝陽。菶菶萋萋，雝雝喈喈。
有秩斯祜，申錫無疆。

春秋
春，王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡。蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。〔僖公四年〕冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子
translation_en:
They followed the Jiang and the sea, reaching the Huai and Si rivers.
Let all the people say, “How great are the king’s words!” and also, “How single in purpose is the king’s heart!”
Admirable in gentleness and exemplary in reverence, he cherished and protected the common people and graciously relieved widowers and widows. From morning until the sun had passed its zenith, he had no leisure to eat; thus he brought all the people into harmony.

Book of Odes
In the seventh month, they are in the fields; in the eighth month, beneath the eaves; in the ninth month, at the doors.
They harness those four stallions, those four splendid stallions. In red knee-coverings and gold-adorned shoes, they attend assemblies and audiences in an unbroken succession.
The phoenixes fly, their wings rustling; they gather here and alight. In abundant array, the king has many worthy officers. Employed by the lord, they are beloved by the Son of Heaven. The phoenixes fly, their wings rustling; they reach up to heaven. In abundant array, the king has many worthy men. Appointed by the lord, they are beloved by the common people. The phoenixes call upon that lofty ridge. The wutong trees grow there on its sun-facing slope, lush and luxuriant; harmonious and melodious are the birds’ calls.
Abundant are these blessings, bestowed repeatedly without end.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao in invading Cai. Cai collapsed. They then attacked Chu and encamped at Xing. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕 In winter, the duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Xiaozhu, and the heir apparent of Qi …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
光伐鄭十有二月巳亥同盟于戲〔襄公〕
〔九年〕夏公會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷
〔定公十年〕
六月齊侯來獻戎捷〔莊公三十有一年〕
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕夏曹公孫會
自鄭出奔宋〔昭公二十年〕
五月公及諸侯盟于皐鼬〔定公四年〕
禮記
本仁以聚之播樂以安之
===
詩云肅雝和鳴先祖是聽夫肅肅敬也雝
雝和也夫敬以和何事不行
子曰君子不以辭盡人故天下有道則行
有枝葉
孚尹旁達信也
第貳塲
論
聖人一天人贊化育之道
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
punctuated:
光伐鄭，十有二月巳亥，同盟于戲〔襄公〕〔九年〕。夏，公會齊侯于夾谷，公至自夾谷〔定公十年〕。
六月，齊侯來獻戎捷〔莊公三十有一年〕。
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕。夏，曹公孫會自鄭出奔宋〔昭公二十年〕。
五月，公及諸侯盟于皐鼬〔定公四年〕。
禮記
本仁以聚之，播樂以安之。
詩云：「肅雝和鳴，先祖是聽。」夫肅肅，敬也；雝雝，和也。夫敬以和，何事不行？
子曰：「君子不以辭盡人，故天下有道，則行有枝葉。」
孚尹旁達，信也。
第貳塲
論
聖人一天人，贊化育之道。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
translation_en:
…Guang attacked Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the sihai day [?], they jointly swore a covenant at Xi. 〔Duke Xiang〕〔Ninth year〕 In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu. 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding〕
In the sixth month, the Marquis of Qi came to present spoils of victory over the Rong. 〔Thirty-first year of Duke Zhuang〕
Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng. 〔Sixth year of Duke Cheng〕 In summer, Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Zheng to Song. 〔Twentieth year of Duke Zhao〕
In the fifth month, the duke and the feudal lords swore a covenant at Gaoyou. 〔Fourth year of Duke Ding〕
Record of Rites
Take benevolence as the foundation for bringing the people together, and spread music to bring them peace.
The Book of Odes says: “Solemn and harmonious, their voices blend; the ancestors listen.” Solemnity means reverence; harmony means concord. With reverence and concord, what undertaking will not succeed?
The Master said: “The gentleman does not judge a person entirely by his words. Thus, when the Way prevails in the world, conduct has branches and leaves.”
The lustre of jade shines forth on every side: this represents trustworthiness.
Second Session
Discourse
The way in which the sage unites Heaven and humanity and assists the transforming and nurturing processes of the cosmos.
Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One topic to be set from among these [?]〕

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔〔建元〕
〔元年〕
擬唐以陸贄爲中書侍郎同平章事誥〔貞〕
〔元八年〕
擬
大閱禮成廷臣
賀表
判語〔五條〕
官員赴任過限
===
監臨勢要中鹽
術士妄言禍福
承差轉雇寄人
軍民約會詞訟
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問帝王居萬民之上父天而爲之子則敬
天勤民豈非至重至重者哉敬天莫大
郊祀勤民莫大籍田往無論已
punctuated:
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔〔建元〕〔元年〕。
擬唐以陸贄爲中書侍郎同平章事誥〔貞〕〔元八年〕。
