判語〔五條〕：官員赴任過限；監臨勢要中鹽；術士妄言禍福；承差轉雇寄人；軍民約會詞訟。
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問：帝王居萬民之上，父天而爲之子，則敬天勤民，豈非至重至重者哉？敬天莫大郊祀，勤民莫大籍田。往無論已。
translation_en:
Compose, in the manner of the Han, an edict calling for the recommendation of men who are worthy and good, upright and correct, and who speak frankly and remonstrate with utmost candor. 〔First year of Jianyuan.〕

Compose, in the manner of the Tang, a proclamation appointing Lu Zhi as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Joint Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery. 〔Eighth year of Zhenyuan.〕

Compose a congratulatory memorial from the court officials upon the completion of the Grand Military Review ceremonies.

Legal judgments 〔five items〕:
An official exceeds the time limit for taking up his post.
Supervisory officials and powerful persons obtain salt allotments under the salt monopoly.
A practitioner of occult arts makes unfounded predictions of misfortune and good fortune.
A person assigned official duties hires another to perform them or entrusts them to someone else [?].
Military personnel and civilians arrange to bring litigation jointly.

Third Session
Policy essays 〔five questions〕
Question: Emperors and kings stand above the myriad people, treating Heaven as their father and serving as its sons. Are reverence for Heaven and diligent care for the people, then, not matters of the utmost, utmost importance? In revering Heaven, nothing is greater than the suburban sacrifices; in diligently caring for the people, nothing is greater than the ceremonial cultivation of the imperial field. Leaving aside the distant past…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
國初
二丘分祀後廼合今又分
耕籍先享先農初上祀今中祀初有配今無
配此其義必有在可得而聞與
太祖高皇帝卽位之初
勅禮官曰聖帝明王嚴於祭祀內致誠敬外致
儀文他日
諭羣臣曰耕籍古禮也朕卽位以來恒舉行之
惟欲使民盡力於田畝以遂生養非事虛文
===
也則我
太祖之所以敬
天勤民殆有出於禮文之外者
聖子
神孫世守無失傳至
世宗肅皇帝
首正郊祀
躬耕籍田
欽天有頌
punctuated:
國初，二丘分祀，後廼合，今又分。耕籍先享先農，初上祀，今中祀；初有配，今無配。此其義必有在，可得而聞與？
太祖高皇帝卽位之初，勅禮官曰：「聖帝明王嚴於祭祀，內致誠敬，外致儀文。」他日，諭羣臣曰：「耕籍，古禮也。朕卽位以來恒舉行之，惟欲使民盡力於田畝，以遂生養，非事虛文也。」則我太祖之所以敬天勤民，殆有出於禮文之外者。聖子神孫，世守無失，傳至世宗肅皇帝，首正郊祀，躬耕籍田，欽天有頌。
translation_en:
… At the founding of the dynasty, sacrifices at the two altars were performed separately; later they were combined, and now they are again separate. Before plowing the imperial ritual field, an offering is made to the First Farmer. Originally this was a major sacrifice; now it is a medium sacrifice. Originally there was an associated recipient of sacrifice; now there is none. There must be reasons underlying these arrangements. May we hear them explained?
At the beginning of his reign, Taizu, Emperor Gao, instructed the ritual officials: “Sage emperors and enlightened kings are exacting in their sacrifices: inwardly they bring sincerity and reverence to the utmost; outwardly they perfect ceremonial forms.” On another occasion, he instructed his assembled ministers: “Plowing the imperial ritual field is an ancient rite. Since ascending the throne, I have regularly performed it, wishing only to make the people devote their utmost efforts to their fields so that they may sustain themselves and nurture their families. It is not an exercise in empty ceremony.” Thus, the means by which our Taizu revered Heaven and diligently cared for the people surely extended beyond ritual forms. His sagely sons and divine grandsons upheld these practices generation after generation without fail. They were transmitted down to Shizong, Emperor Su, who first rectified the suburban sacrifices and personally plowed the imperial ritual field. There was an ode on revering Heaven …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
蠲民有詔蓋于
聖祖有光矣
皇上臨御肇祀
南郊而
天心降格星月呈輝
秉耒三推而民心鼓舞歡聲動地頃因畿輔
旱澇屢
勅羣臣省禱
軫河夫之艱京商之困
===
特賜議處蠲恤則我
皇上敬
天勤民之實殆不專於
郊祀籍耕之文已也誠與
太祖
世宗同一揆矣夫郊籍大典也惟
盛德之君能行焉乃諸士何幸身親見之可無
頌揚以彰
主德之盛
punctuated: 蠲民有詔，蓋于聖祖有光矣。皇上臨御，肇祀南郊，而天心降格，星月呈輝；秉耒三推，而民心鼓舞，歡聲動地。頃因畿輔旱澇，屢勅羣臣省禱，軫河夫之艱、京商之困，特賜議處蠲恤。則我皇上敬天勤民之實，殆不專於郊祀籍耕之文已也，誠與太祖、世宗同一揆矣。夫郊籍，大典也，惟盛德之君能行焉。乃諸士何幸身親見之，可無頌揚以彰主德之盛？
translation_en: …and issued edicts granting the people tax remissions, thereby bringing lustre to the sagely founder. Upon ascending the throne, His Majesty first offered sacrifice at the southern suburban altar; Heaven responded and descended, and the stars and moon shone brilliantly. He took up the plough and pushed it three times; the people’s hearts were uplifted, and their cheers shook the earth. Recently, because of droughts and floods in the capital region, he repeatedly commanded his ministers to examine themselves and offer prayers. Concerned for the hardships of river labourers and the distress of merchants in the capital, he specially ordered deliberation on measures for tax remission and relief. Thus, the substance of our Emperor’s reverence for Heaven and diligent care for the people surely extends beyond the ceremonial forms of suburban sacrifice and ploughing the imperial field. He truly follows the same principles as Taizu and Shizong. The suburban sacrifices and ceremonial ploughing are grand rites, which only a ruler of abundant virtue can perform. How fortunate you scholars are to have witnessed them in person! Can you refrain from offering praise to make manifest the fullness of your sovereign’s virtue?

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
問漢臣賈誼曰天下之命縣於太子太子
之善在於早諭教與選左右其真通達
國體者邪稽之往牒夏典商愆文謨武
烈諭教嚴矣公少傳保道充弼丞左右
選矣萬世育儲法程昭然具在秦漢以
還如帝範戒子篇元良述承華要略果
皆垂裕之法言與有置六傅者有開博
望者有闢崇賢者有延四友者果皆極
一時之選與洪惟
===
太祖高皇帝登極之初他務未遑首建
大本堂作
昭鑒錄其為
儲嗣慮至深遠矣
諭太子諭詹同諭諸儒與賢教誡之言日星
同麗可得而莊誦之歟中書不以設官
勳舊兼領
東宮職事又選國子生侍讀其人可悉指而
言歟逮我
punctuated: 問：漢臣賈誼曰：「天下之命縣於太子，太子之善在於早諭教與選左右。」其真通達國體者邪？稽之往牒，夏典、商愆、文謨、武烈，諭教嚴矣；公少傳保，道充弼丞，左右選矣。萬世育儲法程，昭然具在。秦漢以還，如《帝範》《戒子篇》《元良述》《承華要略》，果皆垂裕之法言與？有置六傅者，有開博望者，有闢崇賢者，有延四友者，果皆極一時之選與？洪惟太祖高皇帝登極之初，他務未遑，首建大本堂，作《昭鑒錄》，其為儲嗣慮至深遠矣。諭太子、諭詹同、諭諸儒與賢，教誡之言，日星同麗，可得而莊誦之歟？中書不以設官，勳舊兼領東宮職事，又選國子生侍讀，其人可悉指而言歟？逮我
translation_en:
Question: Jia Yi, a minister of the Han, said: “The fate of All under Heaven hangs upon the heir apparent. The heir apparent’s goodness depends upon instructing him early and selecting those who attend him.” Was he truly one who thoroughly understood the principles of governing the state? Examining the records of the past, we find the canons of Xia, the errors of Shang, the counsels of King Wen, and the achievements of King Wu: instruction was rigorous indeed. With the senior and junior tutors and guardians, and those who guided, supplemented, assisted, and supported him [?], his attendants were carefully chosen. Models and rules for educating the heir apparent throughout all ages stand clearly before us. From the Qin and Han onward, were such works as Model for Emperors (Di fan), Admonitions to a Son (Jie zi pian), Account of the Heir Apparent (Yuanliang shu), and Essential Outline for the Heir Apparent (Chenghua yaolüe) all truly exemplary teachings that would bequeath blessings to posterity? Some rulers appointed six tutors; some opened Bowang; some established Chongxian; some invited the Four Friends. Did all these appointments truly represent the finest selection of their age?

We reverently reflect that, at the beginning of his reign, before he had leisure for other affairs, Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, first established the Daben Hall and compiled the Record of Illustrious Examples (Zhaojian lu). His concern for the imperial heir was profoundly far-reaching. In his instructions to the heir apparent, to Zhan Tong, and to the scholars and worthies [?], his words of instruction and admonition shone together with the sun and stars. Can you solemnly recite them? The Central Secretariat did not establish official posts on this basis [?]; longstanding meritorious officials concurrently held offices in the Eastern Palace, and students of the Directorate of Education were also selected to attend the heir apparent in his reading. Can you identify and discuss all these men? Coming down to our …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
成祖文皇帝集
文華寶鑑
宣宗章皇帝製
帝訓五十篇
憲宗純皇帝有
文華大訓四卷皆爲
聖子
神孫計也三書何所指與抑亦述
太祖之遺意否與當時輔導等官可得而詳與
===
今我
皇上茂育元良
諭誨有彝訓丞保有碩儒駕軼往代同符
祖宗天下臣民喁喁忻忭咸歌麟趾玆欲陳
獻以資講讀庶幾仰體
皇上早建豫教之盛心爾諸生懷芹曝忱有日
矣務悉心以對
問明王必延儒雋以宏化功賢士必崇儒
學以紹聖緒則儒之名實固不可不蚤
punctuated:
成祖文皇帝集《文華寶鑑》，宣宗章皇帝製《帝訓》五十篇，憲宗純皇帝有《文華大訓》四卷，皆爲聖子神孫計也。三書何所指與？抑亦述太祖之遺意否與？當時輔導等官，可得而詳與？
今我皇上茂育元良，諭誨有彝訓，丞保有碩儒，駕軼往代，同符祖宗。天下臣民喁喁忻忭，咸歌麟趾。玆欲陳獻以資講讀，庶幾仰體皇上早建豫教之盛心。爾諸生懷芹曝忱有日矣，務悉心以對。
問：明王必延儒雋以宏化功，賢士必崇儒學以紹聖緒，則儒之名實固不可不蚤
translation_en:
…Emperor Wen, Chengzu, compiled the Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor (Wenhua baojian); Emperor Zhang, Xuanzong, composed the fifty chapters of Imperial Instructions (Dixun); and Emperor Chun, Xianzong, produced the four juan of the Great Instructions of Literary Splendor (Wenhua daxun). All were plans for their sagely sons and divine grandsons. What were the guiding purposes of these three books? Did they also carry forward Taizu’s intentions? Can you give a detailed account of the officials responsible for assisting and guiding the heir at that time?
Now our Emperor assiduously nurtures the heir apparent. His admonitions follow enduring precepts, and eminent Confucian scholars serve as the heir’s assistants and guardians. He surpasses earlier ages and accords with his imperial ancestors. Officials and common people throughout the realm look up with eager joy, all singing “The Qilin’s Hoof” in celebration of his offspring. We now wish to present material to assist lectures and readings, hoping thereby to honor His Majesty’s lofty intention to establish the heir’s preparatory education early. You students have long cherished the sincere desire to offer your humble contributions, like celery or the warmth of the sun. Apply your minds fully in answering.
Question: An enlightened king must invite outstanding Confucian scholars to extend the work of moral transformation; a worthy scholar must esteem Confucian learning to carry on the succession of the sages. Thus, the name and substance of being a Confucian must surely, at an early stage…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
辨者也周官有九兩之法而儒居一焉
至與牧長主吏竝稱儒何重與班氏有
九家之論而儒居一焉至與陰陽農雜
槩列又何隘與儒者之行宣父語魯君
備矣然謂遽數之不能終其物悉數之
乃留更僕其事何居眞儒之功楊子述
法言似矣然謂一用而四海皇皇一用
而鄰國章章其人何指洙泗以還儒學
蓋失傳矣隱柴桑者甞述八儒其所評
===
覈果精乎聖門高第儒術宜盡醇矣令
蘭陵者甞賤三儒其所譏詆果當乎漢
史立儒林傳潛心大業者何以不與唐
史立儒學傳學本六經者何以見遺至
宋史則又於儒林之外别爲道學一傳
豈儒自儒道自道與得中原文獻之傳
謹屋漏夢寐之際亦一代碩儒也又不
獲與濂洛關閩諸賢爲伍何與諸士産
多儒之邦且逢
punctuated: 辨者也。《周官》有九兩之法，而儒居一焉，至與牧、長、主、吏竝稱，儒何重與？班氏有九家之論，而儒居一焉，至與陰陽、農、雜槩列，又何隘與？儒者之行，宣父語魯君備矣。然謂遽數之不能終其物，悉數之乃留更僕，其事何居？眞儒之功，楊子述《法言》似矣。然謂一用而四海皇皇，一用而鄰國章章，其人何指？洙泗以還，儒學蓋失傳矣。隱柴桑者甞述八儒，其所評覈果精乎？聖門高第，儒術宜盡醇矣。令蘭陵者甞賤三儒，其所譏詆果當乎？漢史立《儒林傳》，潛心大業者何以不與？唐史立《儒學傳》，學本六經者何以見遺？至宋史，則又於儒林之外别爲《道學》一傳，豈儒自儒，道自道與？得中原文獻之傳，謹屋漏夢寐之際，亦一代碩儒也，又不獲與濂洛關閩諸賢爲伍，何與？諸士産多儒之邦，且逢
translation_en:
…must be distinguished. The Offices of Zhou sets forth nine bonds, with Confucian scholars constituting one of them; indeed, they are named alongside regional governors, local chiefs, heads of hereditary houses, and officials. Why are Confucian scholars accorded such importance? Master Ban discusses nine schools, with the Confucians constituting one of them; yet they are listed indiscriminately alongside the Yin-Yang, Agriculturalist, and Miscellaneous schools. Why, here, are they treated so narrowly? Father Xuan—Confucius—gave the lord of Lu a full account of the conduct of Confucian scholars. Yet he said that a hurried enumeration could not exhaust its categories, while a complete enumeration would require staying long enough for the attendants to take turns. What did he mean by this? Master Yang’s account in Model Sayings seems to describe the achievements of true Confucian scholars. Yet he speaks of one whose employment made all within the four seas radiant, and another whose employment made neighboring states illustrious. To whom was he referring? Since the days of teaching beside the Zhu and Si rivers, the transmission of Confucian learning has, it seems, been lost. The recluse of Chaisang once described eight kinds of Confucians: were his assessments truly discerning? The outstanding disciples of the Sage’s school ought all to have possessed wholly pure Confucian learning. Yet the man who served as Magistrate of Lanling once disparaged three kinds of Confucians: were his criticisms and denunciations truly justified?

The History of the Han established a section of Biographies of Confucian Scholars. Why was the man who devoted his mind to the great undertaking not included? The History of the Tang established a section of Biographies of Confucian Learning. Why was the man whose learning was rooted in the Six Classics omitted? The History of the Song went further, establishing a separate section of Biographies of Learning of the Way in addition to its Biographies of Confucian Scholars. Can it be that Confucian learning and the Way are separate things? A man who received the transmission of the textual and scholarly heritage of the Central Plain, and maintained vigilance over himself even in the privacy of his chamber and in his dreams, was surely a great Confucian scholar of his age. Why, then, was he not allowed to stand alongside the worthies of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min? You scholars were born in a land rich in Confucian scholars, and moreover have encountered…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
右儒之世其必稽古辨術思不詭于聖眞矣
願陳之無讓
問韓非子曰人臣循令而從事案法而治
官若然則法令也者臣子誠兢兢然持
守之罔有或越然後可以靖臣職而稱
治世乃猶有不盡然者姑舉一二言之
治晉陽者不繕城郭云脩其教守鴈門
者縱虜入犯卒讋匈奴按梁國者輒焚
獄詞令晉城者擅用庫錢此皆非法令
===
所許也乃四子冒焉行之而人不以為
非何哉方
今律例森具紀法昭明二百餘年以來故無枉
矯之夫無干諄之衆何者恃有此三尺
耳而或有身犯姦臧逭於吏議罪麗罔
赦逃於邦刑豈亦於四子之意然與否
與至于慷慨激憤之士一或不當少有
詿誤輒不免焉何法詘於彼而顧伸於
此耶夫豪傑之士既不得越於法之外
punctuated:
右儒之世，其必稽古辨術，思不詭于聖眞矣。願陳之無讓。

問：韓非子曰：「人臣循令而從事，案法而治官。」若然，則法令也者，臣子誠兢兢然持守之，罔有或越，然後可以靖臣職而稱治世。乃猶有不盡然者，姑舉一二言之。治晉陽者不繕城郭，云脩其教；守鴈門者縱虜入犯，卒讋匈奴；按梁國者輒焚獄詞；令晉城者擅用庫錢。此皆非法令所許也，乃四子冒焉行之，而人不以為非，何哉？方今律例森具，紀法昭明，二百餘年以來，故無枉矯之夫，無干諄之衆。何者？恃有此三尺耳。而或有身犯姦臧，逭於吏議；罪麗罔赦，逃於邦刑。豈亦於四子之意然與否與？至于慷慨激憤之士，一或不當，少有詿誤，輒不免焉。何法詘於彼，而顧伸於此耶？夫豪傑之士既不得越於法之外
translation_en:
…an age that honors Confucian scholars, you must surely examine antiquity and distinguish among doctrines, taking care not to depart from the truth of the sages. Please set forth your views without reserve.

Question: Han Feizi said: “A minister follows orders in conducting affairs and acts according to the law in administering his office.” If so, ministers must indeed uphold laws and ordinances with scrupulous care, never overstepping them; only then can they discharge their duties and bring about an age of good government. Yet there are cases in which this does not entirely hold true. Let us mention a few. The administrator of Jinyang did not repair its walls, saying that he was cultivating moral instruction; the defender of Yanmen allowed enemy incursions, yet ultimately cowed the Xiongnu; the official investigating the kingdom of Liang summarily burned the judicial depositions; and the magistrate of Jincheng used treasury funds without authorization. None of these actions was permitted by law or ordinance. Yet these four men ventured to act thus, and people did not regard them as wrong. Why?

Today, the statutes and substatutes are comprehensive and rigorous, and legal discipline is clearly established. Thus, for more than two hundred years, there have been no men who pervert or falsify authority [?], nor crowds causing trouble [?]. Why is this? Simply because we have these “three-foot tablets” of law to rely upon. Yet some personally commit wrongdoing and corruption and evade official prosecution; their crimes admit of no pardon, yet they escape the punishments of the state. Does this, too, accord with the intentions of those four men, or does it not? As for men of ardent spirit, stirred by indignation, whenever they act even slightly amiss or fall into some minor error, they invariably fail to escape punishment. Why does the law bend for the former, yet assert its force against the latter? Since men of outstanding ability are not permitted to step beyond the bounds of the law…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
而姦罔之徒又或逃於法之中謂法之
無弊不可也夫法者國之所恃以爲治
者也而至於弊焉將何以理諸士窮經
致用其必究心於此矣願明言之以觀
治世之具
問閩方畧在南服古稱鄒魯民不知兵素
樂土也往盜起海上引入島夷當事者
急爲蕩平之計乃募客兵以禦之夫寇
遄發而藉外募權也今數歲于茲矣昔
===
人謂兵無宗族不自重惜客兵似不可
久也然攘臂先登衝鋒陷敵其功可盡
泯歟建議者率持練土兵爲長計夫周
制入則爲比閭族黨出則爲伍兩軍師
其土兵之意與漢置材官騎士家人子
起田中從軍果周制與唐宋以來選土
兵者曰澤潞步兵曰雄邊子弟曰武定
軍曰保毅軍曰宣毅軍曰廣銳軍曰義
勇軍其詳可得聞與亦各有績效與或
punctuated:
而姦罔之徒又或逃於法之中，謂法之無弊，不可也。夫法者，國之所恃以爲治者也，而至於弊焉，將何以理？諸士窮經致用，其必究心於此矣。願明言之，以觀治世之具。
問：閩方畧在南服，古稱鄒魯，民不知兵，素樂土也。往盜起海上，引入島夷，當事者急爲蕩平之計，乃募客兵以禦之。夫寇遄發而藉外募，權也。今數歲于茲矣。昔人謂兵無宗族，不自重惜，客兵似不可久也。然攘臂先登，衝鋒陷敵，其功可盡泯歟？建議者率持練土兵爲長計。夫周制，入則爲比閭族黨，出則爲伍兩軍師，其土兵之意與？漢置材官騎士，家人子起田中從軍，果周制與？唐宋以來，選土兵者，曰澤潞步兵，曰雄邊子弟，曰武定軍，曰保毅軍，曰宣毅軍，曰廣銳軍，曰義勇軍，其詳可得聞與？亦各有績效與？或
translation_en:
…yet deceitful lawbreakers may still escape within the law itself. It is impossible to say that the law has no defects. Law is what the state relies upon to maintain order; when it becomes defective, how is order to be maintained? You candidates study the classics exhaustively in order to put them into practice, and surely must have examined this matter closely. Please explain it clearly, so that we may see your resources for governing the world.
Question: The territory of Fujian [?] lies in the southern domain. Since antiquity it has been called a land of Zou and Lu; its people knew nothing of warfare, and it was always a happy land. Formerly, bandits arose at sea and brought in island barbarians. Those responsible urgently devised plans to suppress them, recruiting troops from outside the province to repel them. When raiders strike suddenly, relying on outside recruits is an expedient. But several years have now passed. People of old said that soldiers without their lineage and kin nearby do not value or preserve their own lives; it would seem that troops from elsewhere cannot be relied upon indefinitely. Yet they bared their arms, led the assaults, charged forward, and broke through the enemy. Can their achievements be entirely effaced? Those offering proposals generally maintain that training local troops is the long-term solution. Under the Zhou system, at home the people were organized into neighborhood groups—bi, lü, zu, and dang—and on campaign into squads, platoons, armies, and divisions. Was this the principle behind local troops? The Han established infantry and cavalry forces, with sons of ordinary households leaving the fields to join the army. Was this truly the Zhou system? Among the locally recruited forces selected from the Tang and Song onward were the Zelu Infantry, the Frontier-Valiant Sons, the Military Pacification Army, the Resolute Protection Army, the Manifest Resolution Army, the Expansive Vigor Army, and the Righteous Valor Army. May we hear their details? Did each also achieve results? Some…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
疑閩人脆不堪荷戈曩浙直有警閩子
弟連艘而上隷兵籍最稱驕健乃今自
衞顧脆至借技於人何歟往歲莆陽之
變遂謂土兵驁不可用夫兵無統制雖
韓白不能用也罪果在兵與宋咸平中
詞臣建言福建等郡酌民戶衆寡並許
置本城守捉軍士時論多之其說固在
也今可行與或謂練兵非難食足難枵
腹與人鬭雖烏獲負矣謂當給之閒田
===
付之寺租亦有見與頃仗
皇上威靈渠魁授首海氛稍稍告靖然桑土之
慮不可已也諸士生長海邦熟計久矣
宜悉心以對毋曰軍旅未學
punctuated: 疑閩人脆，不堪荷戈。曩浙直有警，閩子弟連艘而上，隷兵籍，最稱驕健；乃今自衞，顧脆至借技於人，何歟？往歲莆陽之變，遂謂土兵驁不可用。夫兵無統制，雖韓白不能用也，罪果在兵與？宋咸平中，詞臣建言，福建等郡酌民戶衆寡，並許置本城守捉軍士，時論多之，其說固在也，今可行與？或謂練兵非難，食足難；枵腹與人鬭，雖烏獲負矣。謂當給之閒田，付之寺租，亦有見與？頃仗皇上威靈，渠魁授首，海氛稍稍告靖。然桑土之慮不可已也。諸士生長海邦，熟計久矣，宜悉心以對，毋曰軍旅未學。
translation_en:
…suspect that the people of Fujian are weak and unfit to bear arms. Formerly, when alarms arose in Zhejiang and the directly administered metropolitan region, the young men of Fujian went up in successive boatloads and enrolled in the military registers, earning particular renown for their fierceness and vigor. Yet now, when defending their own homes, they are supposedly so weak that they must borrow the skills of others. Why is this? Following the disturbance at Puyang in past years, people declared that local troops were unruly and could not be employed. But without unified command and discipline, even Han Xin and Bai Qi could not employ troops. Does the fault really lie with the soldiers?

During the Xianping reign of the Song, a literary official proposed that Fujian and other prefectures be permitted to establish soldiers to guard and hold their own cities, with numbers proportioned to the number of civilian households. Contemporary opinion praised this proposal, and its argument remains on record. Could it be put into practice today? Some say that training soldiers is not difficult; providing sufficient food is difficult. Fighting others on an empty stomach, even Wu Huo would be defeated. They suggest granting the soldiers unused fields and assigning them rents from monastery lands. Does this, too, show insight?

Recently, through the Emperor’s awe-inspiring power, the chief bandits have been beheaded, and the troubles at sea have gradually subsided. Yet we must not cease taking precautions, like the bird that binds its nest with mulberry roots before the storm. You gentlemen were born and raised in this coastal land and have long considered these matters carefully. Apply yourselves wholeheartedly in your answers; do not say that you have never studied military affairs.

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君子學以致其道
林竒石
同考試官教諭趙批從心上發明君子致道之學一洗陳
言根極理要此時義不多得者
同考試官教授吳批諸作講學與致道殊多纏繞是篇
融會註意而於致道處歸重超卓之見也録之
考試官教授夏批意邃而詞達佳士也
===
考試官教授帥批純正明確
賢者論君子純心以造乎道而已夫學所以純
此心也心純則道可馴致矣君子毋亦是務乎
子夏示人之意若曰天下之道足於心而已矣
君子之學求諸心而已矣居肆成事百工且知
所以用其心而况于君子乎何則燕僻而廢學
則其心放固無以爲適道之基中道而自畫則
其心怠亦難以語大成之學惟君子也時敏以
遜志外物無所奪矣而繼之以不息之功篤行
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「君子學以致其道」
林竒石

同考試官教諭趙批：從心上發明君子致道之學，一洗陳言，根極理要，此時義不多得者。

同考試官教授吳批：諸作講學與致道，殊多纏繞。是篇融會註意，而於致道處歸重，超卓之見也，録之。

考試官教授夏批：意邃而詞達，佳士也。

考試官教授帥批：純正明確。

賢者論君子，純心以造乎道而已。夫學所以純此心也，心純則道可馴致矣，君子毋亦是務乎？

子夏示人之意若曰：天下之道，足於心而已矣；君子之學，求諸心而已矣。居肆成事，百工且知所以用其心，而况于君子乎？何則？燕僻而廢學，則其心放，固無以爲適道之基；中道而自畫，則其心怠，亦難以語大成之學。惟君子也，時敏以遜志，外物無所奪矣，而繼之以不息之功；篤行
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“The gentleman studies in order to attain his Way.”
Lin Qishi

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: By elucidating from the standpoint of the mind the learning through which the gentleman attains the Way, this essay sweeps away conventional expressions and probes to the root of essential principles. Such an examination essay is rarely found.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Professor: The other compositions become considerably entangled in discussing learning and attaining the Way. This essay thoroughly integrates the meaning of the commentary and places its chief emphasis on attaining the Way. Its insight is outstanding; I select it for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Xia, Professor: His thought is profound and his expression lucid. He is an excellent scholar.

Comment by Examiner Shuai, Professor: Orthodox, correct, clear, and precise.

In discussing the gentleman, the worthy speaks simply of purifying the mind so as to reach the Way. Learning is the means of purifying this mind. Once the mind is pure, the Way can gradually be attained. Should this not be the gentleman’s concern?

The intent of Zixia’s instruction may be expressed thus: The Way of all under Heaven is fully present in the mind; the gentleman’s learning consists simply in seeking it within the mind. Even the various craftsmen, working in their shops to complete their tasks, know how to apply their minds. How much more should the gentleman! Why is this so? If one idles in seclusion and abandons learning, the mind becomes unrestrained, and there is certainly no foundation for advancing toward the Way. If one sets limits upon oneself halfway along the road, the mind grows indolent, and one can scarcely speak of learning that reaches full accomplishment. The gentleman alone applies himself diligently at all times to render his will receptive, so that external things cannot divert him, and follows this with unceasing effort; he practices earnestly…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
以邁往他岐不能惑矣而貞之以有恒之守時
敎退息莫不有學非徒少有得而遽止也循序
以致精而所以窮神知化者由此焉敬業樂羣
莫不有學非徒以一善而自足也下學而上達
而所以盡性踐形者由此焉其始也以道爲標
的而所以期而至之望而趨之者必有事而勿
忘也而道其致於專精之後矣乎其終也以道
爲歸宿而所以知至至之知終終之者欲深造
而自得也而道其致於眞積之久矣乎否則道
===
有未致是性分之有虧學未大成是能事之有
歉君子之心豈容巳哉噫此子夏篤信聖道而
有得者也聖門自顏曾而下惟子夏以篤信稱
觀其謂盡倫爲巳學因論詩而知學充其言可
以與聞性道而此以致道言之固其學之巳至
者不然出入紛華靡麗之中烏能爲是言哉此
所以列于文學之科也
知遠之近知風之自知微之顯
楊佩訓
punctuated:
以邁往，他岐不能惑矣，而貞之以有恒之守。時敎退息，莫不有學，非徒少有得而遽止也；循序以致精，而所以窮神知化者由此焉。敬業樂羣，莫不有學，非徒以一善而自足也；下學而上達，而所以盡性踐形者由此焉。其始也，以道爲標的，而所以期而至之、望而趨之者，必有事而勿忘也，而道其致於專精之後矣乎？其終也，以道爲歸宿，而所以知至至之、知終終之者，欲深造而自得也，而道其致於眞積之久矣乎？否則，道有未致，是性分之有虧；學未大成，是能事之有歉。君子之心豈容巳哉？噫！此子夏篤信聖道而有得者也。聖門自顏曾而下，惟子夏以篤信稱。觀其謂盡倫爲巳學，因論詩而知學，充其言，可以與聞性道。而此以致道言之，固其學之巳至者。不然，出入紛華靡麗之中，烏能爲是言哉？此所以列于文學之科也。

知遠之近，知風之自，知微之顯。
楊佩訓
translation_en:
…to press forward, so that divergent paths cannot lead him astray, and he makes this steadfast through constant adherence. During formal instruction and during rest from study, he never ceases to learn; he does not abruptly stop upon gaining some small understanding. By proceeding in due order, he attains refinement: this is how he fathoms the numinous and understands transformation. In attending earnestly to his studies and delighting in the company of fellow students, he never ceases to learn; he does not rest content with a single good attainment. Through learning what is below, he reaches an understanding of what is above: this is how he fully realizes his nature and fulfills what his bodily form embodies.

At the outset, he takes the Way as his target. To reach what he has set his sights upon and advance toward what he beholds, he must continually apply himself and never forget his task. Will the Way then not be attained after such concentrated effort? In the end, he takes the Way as his final resting place. To know where to arrive and arrive there, and to know where to finish and finish there, he seeks to advance deeply in learning and grasp it for himself. Will the Way then not be attained through the long accumulation of genuine effort? Otherwise, if the Way remains unattained, there is a deficiency in the realization of his allotted nature; if his learning has not reached full accomplishment, there is something wanting in the work he is capable of doing. How could the gentleman allow himself to stop?

Ah! Here is Zixia, who firmly believed in the Way of the sages and gained an understanding of it. Among the disciples of the Sage, after Yan Hui and Zeng Shen, Zixia alone was renowned for steadfast belief. Consider his statement that someone who fully discharges human relationships has already learned, and how, through discussing the Odes, he came to understand learning. Extend the implications of his words, and one may participate in hearing of human nature and the Way. Here, in speaking of attaining the Way, he surely reveals that his own learning had already reached that point. Otherwise, how could someone moving amid the bustle of splendor and extravagance have uttered these words? This is why he was ranked in the category of literary learning.

“Know how what is distant lies in what is near; know whence the wind comes; know how what is subtle becomes manifest.”

Yang Peixun.

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭李批知幾之學人所難言子能於遠近
風自顯微處挑剔精透不費詞而理自足是務實勝者
同考試官學正黄批講三知處俱有心得自與尚浮者
逈異
考試官敎授夏批闡君子審幾之意條晰
考試官敎授帥批峻潔渾成
君子于幾之當謹者而皆有真知焉夫動必有
幾人之所易忽也而君子爲能知之其學務實
勝者與且夫天下有不可忽之眞幾吾心有不
===
容昧之實見君子心乎爲己而其知幾果何如
哉彼近而吾身遠而天下勢相懸矣君子以近
裏之心觀之則知遠之所見由于邇之所發而
近固遠之幾也蓋遠主其應近主其感天下固
未有應而不出于感者知此而君子之舉遠敢
忽于其近乎順動爲風存主爲自迹則殊矣君
子以自反之心觀之則知樹之風聲莫非原之
性術而自固風之幾也蓋風動于外理發諸內
天下固未有外之不本于內者知此而君子之
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭李批：知幾之學，人所難言。子能於遠近、風自、顯微處挑剔精透，不費詞而理自足，是務實勝者。
同考試官學正黄批：講三知處，俱有心得，自與尚浮者逈異。
考試官敎授夏批：闡君子審幾之意，條晰。
考試官敎授帥批：峻潔渾成。
君子于幾之當謹者，而皆有真知焉。夫動必有幾，人之所易忽也，而君子爲能知之，其學務實勝者與！且夫天下有不可忽之眞幾，吾心有不容昧之實見。君子心乎爲己，而其知幾果何如哉？彼近而吾身，遠而天下，勢相懸矣。君子以近裏之心觀之，則知遠之所見，由于邇之所發，而近固遠之幾也。蓋遠主其應，近主其感，天下固未有應而不出于感者。知此，而君子之舉遠，敢忽于其近乎？順動爲風，存主爲自，迹則殊矣。君子以自反之心觀之，則知樹之風聲，莫非原之性術，而自固風之幾也。蓋風動于外，理發諸內，天下固未有外之不本于內者。知此，而君子之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Learning to discern incipient tendencies is difficult to articulate. Yet you probe the distant and the near, influence and its source, and the manifest and the subtle with precision and penetration. Without wasting words, you fully convey the principles. This is work that seeks excellence in substance.”

Associate Examiner Huang, School Instructor, comments: “Your treatment of all three kinds of knowledge shows personal insight and is markedly different from work that prizes superficiality.”

Examiner Xia, Professor, comments: “The noble man’s attentive discernment of incipient tendencies is elucidated clearly and systematically.”

Examiner Shuai, Professor, comments: “Rigorous and pure, forming an integrated whole.”

The noble man possesses true knowledge of every incipient tendency that calls for vigilance. Every movement necessarily has its incipient signs, which people readily overlook; the noble man alone can discern them. Surely his learning seeks excellence in substance! Now, in the world there are genuine incipient tendencies that must not be neglected, and within our minds there is substantive insight that must not be obscured. The noble man sets his heart on cultivating himself: what, then, is his knowledge of incipient tendencies actually like?

What is near is one’s own person; what is distant is the world. Their respective situations are far apart. Yet when the noble man examines them with a mind directed inward, he knows that what becomes manifest at a distance proceeds from what issues forth nearby. The near is thus the incipient source of the distant. For the distant concerns the response, and the near concerns the stimulus: nowhere in the world is there a response that does not arise from a stimulus. Knowing this, when the noble man undertakes something reaching far afield, would he dare neglect what is near?

The movement that follows is influence; what is maintained as the inner directing principle is its source. Their outward traces differ. Yet when the noble man examines them with a mind turned back upon himself, he knows that the influence and reputation established outwardly invariably originate in one’s nature and methods [?]. The source is thus the incipient basis of influence. For influence moves outwardly, while principle issues from within: nowhere in the world is there anything outward that is not rooted in the inward. Knowing this, the noble man’s …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
觀風敢忘其所自乎以至幾微方動寂感初分
孰不以爲微矣而何與于顯也而君子之心蓋
通顯微而無間者則知存之于念慮者不終隱
見之于事爲者則甚著而昭然獨炳于幾先矣
蓋始于獨見獨聞終于共見共聞天下固未有
隱而不彰者知此而謹微以爲丕顯之地者又
烏容已哉吁此三知者天下之眞知也由此謹
之於入德易易矣抑嘗聞之虞書曰人心惟危
道心惟微語幾也又曰惟精惟一語知幾也易
===
曰知幾其神乎下學之事宜未及此然觀中庸
一書推極於中和位育而本之戒懼謹獨推極
於篤恭而天下平矣而始于爲已知幾是知獨
卽幾也是幾也約之愈精充之愈廣下學上達
一以貫之矣
孟子曰言近而指遠者善言也守約而施
博者善道也君子之言也不下帶而道
存焉君子之守脩其身而天下平
陳瑛
punctuated:
觀風，敢忘其所自乎？以至幾微方動，寂感初分，孰不以爲微矣，而何與于顯也？而君子之心，蓋通顯微而無間者，則知存之于念慮者不終隱，見之于事爲者則甚著，而昭然獨炳于幾先矣。蓋始于獨見獨聞，終于共見共聞，天下固未有隱而不彰者。知此，而謹微以爲丕顯之地者，又烏容已哉！吁！此三知者，天下之眞知也。由此謹之，於入德易易矣。抑嘗聞之，《虞書》曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微。」語幾也。又曰：「惟精惟一。」語知幾也。《易》曰：「知幾其神乎！」下學之事，宜未及此。然觀《中庸》一書，推極於中和位育，而本之戒懼謹獨；推極於篤恭而天下平矣，而始于爲已知幾。是知獨卽幾也。是幾也，約之愈精，充之愈廣，下學上達，一以貫之矣。
孟子曰：「言近而指遠者，善言也；守約而施博者，善道也。君子之言也，不下帶而道存焉；君子之守，脩其身而天下平。」
陳瑛
translation_en:
…when observing an influence, dare he forget its source? When incipient stirrings first arise and stillness and response first become distinct, who would not consider them subtle and ask what connection they have with the manifest? Yet the gentleman’s mind comprehends the manifest and the subtle without any gap between them. He thus knows that what is harbored in thoughts will not remain hidden forever, and that when it appears in deeds it becomes conspicuous. This shines clearly in his solitary awareness even before the first stirrings. What begins as something seen and heard by oneself alone ends as something seen and heard by all. Nothing under Heaven is hidden without eventually becoming manifest. Knowing this, how could one cease attending carefully to the subtle, making it the foundation of what will become greatly manifest? Ah! These three kinds of knowing are true knowledge under Heaven. Through exercising care on this basis, entering into virtue becomes very easy. Now, I have heard these words from the Book of Yu: “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle.” This speaks of incipient stirrings. It also says: “Be discerning; be single-minded.” This speaks of knowing those stirrings. The Book of Changes says: “To know incipient stirrings—is this not divine?” The work of learning below would seem not yet to reach this level. Yet consider the Doctrine of the Mean: it extends its argument to the utmost achievement of equilibrium and harmony, whereby Heaven and Earth take their proper places and the myriad things are nurtured, while grounding this in vigilance, apprehension, and care in solitude. It extends its argument to the utmost achievement of profound reverence bringing peace to all under Heaven, while beginning with learning for oneself [?] and knowing incipient stirrings. Thus we know that what is known to oneself alone is precisely the incipient stirring. The more closely one concentrates on these stirrings, the finer one’s discernment becomes; the further one extends this understanding, the broader its scope becomes. Learning below and attaining understanding above are threaded together by a single principle.
Mencius said: “Words that concern what is near yet point to what is far are good words. Holding to what is succinct yet applying it broadly is a good way. The gentleman’s words do not reach below his sash, yet the Way resides in them. What the gentleman holds to is cultivating his own person, and all under Heaven is brought to peace.”
Chen Ying 陳瑛.

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正龍批題似易而實難塲中士子類欠
融貫此篇體認真切不為支離影響語可以為式矣
考試官教授夏批意新理到
考試官教授帥批詞氣宏雅
大賢即言與道之善而歸諸君子焉夫近可遠
約可博此言道之為善也非君子其孰能之孟
子之意蓋曰垂訓立教必資於言經世理物莫
先於道胡立言脩道者之不得其要也是故言
之近者而其指則易窮非善言也惟言之所及
===
者近而不遺而指之所涵者遠而莫禦則一言
盡天下之道而聖賢之格言在是矣不其善乎
守之約者而其施則易窒非善道也惟守之在
我者約而可循而施之在人者博而不匱則易
簡得天下之理而帝王之要道在是矣不其善
乎是言也惟君子為能言之是道也惟君子為
能道之爾彼其率淺易以敷詞其言之近若不
下於帶也然神化性命之精即此而寓則其指
誠未可以易窺者又何遠也近而能遠而所謂
punctuated:
同考試官學正龍批：題似易而實難，塲中士子類欠融貫。此篇體認真切，不為支離影響語，可以為式矣。
考試官教授夏批：意新理到。
考試官教授帥批：詞氣宏雅。
大賢即言與道之善而歸諸君子焉。夫近可遠，約可博，此言道之為善也。非君子，其孰能之？孟子之意蓋曰：垂訓立教，必資於言；經世理物，莫先於道。胡立言脩道者之不得其要也？是故言之近者，而其指則易窮，非善言也。惟言之所及者近而不遺，而指之所涵者遠而莫禦，則一言盡天下之道，而聖賢之格言在是矣，不其善乎？守之約者，而其施則易窒，非善道也。惟守之在我者約而可循，而施之在人者博而不匱，則易簡得天下之理，而帝王之要道在是矣，不其善乎？是言也，惟君子為能言之；是道也，惟君子為能道之爾。彼其率淺易以敷詞，其言之近若不下於帶也，然神化性命之精即此而寓，則其指誠未可以易窺者，又何遠也！近而能遠，而所謂
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Long, School Instructor, comments: The topic seems easy but is actually difficult. Candidates in the examination hall generally fall short of a comprehensive, integrated understanding. This essay shows a genuine and penetrating grasp; it avoids disconnected statements and vague echoes of others’ words. It may serve as a model.
Examiner Xia, Prefectural School Professor, comments: The conception is fresh, and the reasoning fully developed.
Examiner Shuai, Prefectural School Professor, comments: The diction and tenor are elevated and refined.
The great worthy identifies excellence in speech and in the Way and attributes both to the gentleman. What is near can reach far; what is concentrated can extend broadly: herein lies the excellence of speech and the Way. Who but the gentleman could achieve this? Mencius’s meaning is, broadly, as follows: To transmit instruction and establish teachings, one must rely on speech; to order the world and regulate affairs, nothing takes precedence over the Way. Why, then, do those who formulate teachings and cultivate the Way fail to grasp their essentials? Thus, speech that concerns what is near, but whose import is readily exhausted, is not excellent speech. Only when what speech addresses is near and leaves nothing out, while what its import embraces reaches far without restriction, can a single utterance encompass the Way of all under Heaven. Herein lie the exemplary sayings of sages and worthies. Is this not excellence? A principle held to that is concentrated, but whose application is readily obstructed, is not an excellent way. Only when what I hold to within myself is concentrated and practicable, while its application to others is broad and inexhaustible, can ease and simplicity comprehend the principles of all under Heaven. Herein lies the essential Way of emperors and kings. Is this not excellence? Such speech only the gentleman can utter; such a Way only the gentleman can put into practice. He sets forth his words in plain and accessible terms. The immediacy of his speech is such that it seems not to reach below his belt. Yet the subtleties of wondrous transformation, human nature, and Heaven’s mandate are lodged within these very words. Their import truly cannot readily be fathomed—how far it reaches! Near yet capable of reaching far, and what is called…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
善言者孰有尚於君子哉本愼脩以立極其守
之約僅不出于身爾然均平天下之化即此而
臻則其施誠非可以限量者又何博也約而能
博而所謂善道者孰有尚於君子哉吁知君子
之善言則立言者固當求諸道知君子之善道
則體道者又當求諸身矣彼世之枝葉其辭而
泛濫其學者無惑乎君子之道鮮也孟子知言
養氣得統于一貫其以是爲天下後世告也意
獨至矣以此爲訓猶有談虛而流於老莊之荒
===
唐守靜而宗夫佛氏之寂滅者
易
象曰天行健君子以自彊不息
楊佩訓
同考試官教諭許 批〔𦍑𦍑即自彊不息分爲二義殊失易傳本旨今以運貫串而法天之意自明非苟作者〕
同考試官學正龍 批〔天運不已惟君子法之是即所謂聖人之學也求其發揮精到者無踰此篇〕
考試官教授夏 批〔□□□□□□〕
punctuated:
善言者，孰有尚於君子哉？本愼脩以立極，其守之約僅不出于身爾；然均平天下之化即此而臻，則其施誠非可以限量者，又何博也！約而能博，而所謂善道者，孰有尚於君子哉？吁！知君子之善言，則立言者固當求諸道；知君子之善道，則體道者又當求諸身矣。彼世之枝葉其辭而泛濫其學者，無惑乎君子之道鮮也！孟子知言養氣，得統于一貫，其以是爲天下後世告也，意獨至矣。以此爲訓，猶有談虛而流於老莊之荒唐、守靜而宗夫佛氏之寂滅者。

易
象曰：「天行健，君子以自彊不息。」
楊佩訓
同考試官教諭許批〔𦍑𦍑即自彊不息分爲二義，殊失易傳本旨。今以運貫串，而法天之意自明，非苟作者。〕
同考試官學正龍批〔天運不已，惟君子法之，是即所謂聖人之學也。求其發揮精到者，無踰此篇。〕
考試官教授夏批〔□□□□□□〕
translation_en:
…among those skilled in speaking, who could surpass the gentleman? He takes careful self-cultivation as his foundation and thereby establishes the highest standard. What he holds to is so concise that it scarcely extends beyond his own person; yet from this comes the transforming influence that brings equity and peace throughout the world. Its application truly cannot be measured or bounded: how broad it is! Concise yet capable of breadth—among those said to excel in the Way, who could surpass the gentleman? Ah! To understand the gentleman’s excellence in speaking is to recognize that those who establish teachings must seek their foundation in the Way; to understand his excellence in the Way is to recognize that those who embody the Way must seek it in themselves. When people in this world embroider their language with branches and leaves and let their learning range without restraint, it is no wonder that the gentleman’s Way is rarely found! Mencius understood words and nourished his vital force, unifying these through a single guiding thread. His intention in proclaiming this to the world and to later generations was supremely profound. Even with this instruction, there are still those who discourse on emptiness and drift into the extravagances of Laozi and Zhuangzi, or preserve stillness and take the Buddhist doctrine of quiescent extinction as their guiding principle.

Book of Changes
The Image Commentary says: “Heaven’s movement is vigorous; the gentleman accordingly strengthens himself without cease.”
By Yang Peixun.
Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: 〔[Opening characters unclear: 𦍑𦍑.] To divide “strengthens himself without cease” into two distinct meanings seriously misses the original purport of the Commentary on the Changes. Here, movement is used as the connecting thread, and the meaning of taking Heaven as one’s model becomes clear of itself. This is no carelessly composed work.〕
Associate Examiner Long, School Instructor, comments: 〔Heaven moves unceasingly, and the gentleman alone takes it as his model. This is precisely what is called the learning of the sages. For a penetrating and precise exposition of it, no essay surpasses this one.〕
Examiner Xia, Professor, comments: 〔Six illegible characters.〕

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授帥批莊重可誦
象傳卽天運之不已而因著君子有法天之學
焉夫天惟至健故運而不已也君子法之亦不
已焉非其合德於天者哉夫子發乾之象欲人
法天以為學也蓋謂夫聖人者與昊天而同道
者也乾健之德天以之而立命聖人以之而立
心其理一而已矣是故乾之象天也乾之德健
也上下皆乾陽之純而健之至則是維天之命
太極以宰其機而運行不已上帝之載於穆以
===
貞其運而混闢無窮蓋自有天地以來而未改
歷古今如斯而常運者也天之行健如此君子
法之則以吾心之德本與天而同體亦與天而
同運故果確以勝其私矣而物欲不撓則天理
流行而主靜以立極者成性以之而存存至大
至剛者充塞於天地之間也强毅以恒其德矣
而已私淨盡則德性常用而凡動之得宜者上
達以之而亹亹無貳無雜者常伸於萬物之表
也以之而進德脩業則緝熈於宥密者與帝載
punctuated:
考試官敎授帥批：莊重可誦。

象傳卽天運之不已，而因著君子有法天之學焉。夫天惟至健，故運而不已也。君子法之，亦不已焉，非其合德於天者哉？夫子發乾之象，欲人法天以為學也。蓋謂夫聖人者，與昊天而同道者也。乾健之德，天以之而立命，聖人以之而立心，其理一而已矣。是故乾之象，天也；乾之德，健也。上下皆乾，陽之純而健之至，則是維天之命，太極以宰其機而運行不已；上帝之載，於穆以貞其運而混闢無窮。蓋自有天地以來而未改，歷古今如斯而常運者也。天之行健如此，君子法之，則以吾心之德本與天而同體，亦與天而同運。故果確以勝其私矣，而物欲不撓，則天理流行，而主靜以立極者，成性以之而存存，至大至剛者充塞於天地之間也。强毅以恒其德矣，而已私淨盡，則德性常用，而凡動之得宜者，上達以之而亹亹，無貳無雜者常伸於萬物之表也。以之而進德脩業，則緝熈於宥密者與帝載
translation_en:
Examiner Shuai, Professor, comments: Solemn and dignified, worthy of recitation.

The Commentary on the Images takes Heaven’s unceasing movement as its starting point and thereby makes clear that the gentleman has a learning that models itself on Heaven. Heaven moves without ceasing precisely because it is supremely vigorous. The gentleman models himself on it and likewise never ceases. Is this not how he brings his virtue into accord with Heaven? In expounding the image of Qian, the Master wished people to model their learning on Heaven. His meaning was that the sage shares the same Way as August Heaven. Through the virtue of Qian’s vigor, Heaven establishes its mandate, and the sage establishes his heart. Their principle is one and the same.

Thus the image of Qian is Heaven, and the virtue of Qian is vigor. With Qian both above and below, yang is pure and vigor reaches its utmost. This is the mandate of Heaven: the Supreme Ultimate governs its workings, and its movement never ceases. This is the working of the Lord on High: its profound mystery keeps its movement constant, and its cycles of undifferentiation and opening unfold without end. Since Heaven and Earth first existed, this has never changed; through antiquity and the present, it has moved continually in this way.

Such is the vigor of Heaven’s movement. The gentleman models himself on it because the virtue of his own heart originally shares Heaven’s substance and likewise shares its movement. Thus he overcomes his selfishness through resolution and firmness. When material desires no longer disturb him, heavenly principle flows freely. By giving primacy to stillness and establishing the ultimate standard, he continually preserves his perfected nature; what is supremely great and supremely firm fills the space between Heaven and Earth. Through strength and perseverance he makes his virtue constant. When selfishness [?] has been entirely purged, his moral nature is constantly active. In all appropriately directed action, he advances tirelessly toward higher understanding; what is undivided and unmixed constantly extends beyond the myriad things. Through this he advances in virtue and cultivates his undertakings; then that which shines ever more brightly in profound stillness, together with the workings of the Lord on High …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
而同其流行即盈虛消息而觀於天天不可變
則道亦不可變也以之而乗龍御天則維勅於
時幾者與乾元而相為悠久即常變久暫而求
諸理理不可易則心亦不可易也其自強不息
有如此至是則天以健而立德人以健而立心
聖人天道之極致不可觀其深乎大抵聖人全
體乎太極而有功於造化亦惟其至誠之無息
如天地之無不覆載而不自以為德也是故其
心蓋未肯以自暇自逸於變時雍者兢業於萬
===
幾光顯西土者翼翼以小心良以敬肆之間天
人之介王霸之幾也志於法天者其要只在慎
獨
夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業也知崇禮卑
崇效天卑法地
林應訓
同考試官教諭許批易為聖學之所資而是篇廣大
精密獨能形容之宜錄以式
同考試官學正龍批知禮崇卑體貼自有識見非泛泛者
punctuated:
而同其流行。即盈虛消息而觀於天，天不可變，則道亦不可變也。以之而乗龍御天，則維勅於時幾者，與乾元而相為悠久。即常變久暫而求諸理，理不可易，則心亦不可易也。其自強不息有如此。至是，則天以健而立德，人以健而立心。聖人天道之極致，不可觀其深乎？大抵聖人全體乎太極，而有功於造化，亦惟其至誠之無息，如天地之無不覆載，而不自以為德也。是故其心蓋未肯以自暇自逸。於變時雍者，兢業於萬幾；光顯西土者，翼翼以小心。良以敬肆之間，天人之介，王霸之幾也。志於法天者，其要只在慎獨。
夫易，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。
林應訓
同考試官教諭許批：易為聖學之所資，而是篇廣大精密，獨能形容之，宜錄以式。
同考試官學正龍批：知禮崇卑，體貼自有識見，非泛泛者
translation_en:
…and shares in its flowing operation. If we contemplate Heaven through its fullness and emptiness, waning and waxing, Heaven cannot change, and thus the Way likewise cannot change. By this means one rides the dragons and governs Heaven; attentiveness to the incipient workings of the time endures together with the primal power of Qian. If we seek principle through constancy and change, duration and transience, principle cannot alter, and thus the heart likewise cannot alter. Such is unceasing self-strengthening. At this point, Heaven establishes its virtue through vigor, and human beings establish their hearts through vigor. Can we not perceive the depth of the sage’s supreme realization of Heaven’s Way? In general, the sage fully embodies the Supreme Ultimate and contributes to the work of creation and transformation solely through the ceaselessness of his utmost sincerity. Like Heaven and Earth, which leave nothing uncovered or unsupported, he does not count this as his own virtue. Thus his heart is never willing to indulge in leisure or ease. He under whom all were transformed and brought into harmony remained vigilant amid the myriad affairs of government; he who made the western lands illustrious remained reverent and cautious at heart. For between reverence and laxity lies the boundary between Heaven and human desire, and the subtle turning point between true kingship and hegemony. For those intent on modeling themselves on Heaven, the essential requirement lies solely in vigilance when alone.
“The Changes is that by which the sage exalts his virtue and broadens his undertakings. Knowledge is exalted; ritual is humble. The exalted emulates Heaven; the humble models itself on Earth.”
Lin Yingxun.
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “The Changes supplies the resources for the learning of sages. This essay, expansive yet precise, is uniquely able to give expression to this. It should be recorded as a model.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Long, Instructor: “In his close apprehension of knowledge and ritual, exaltation and humility, he displays discernment of his own; he is no commonplace writer…”

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
學易者不能及此
考試官教授夏批詞理雅健粹然出於正
考試官教授帥批文有深思取之
大傳論聖學之資於易而必徵諸學之大者焉
夫聖人之德業而效法於天地則聖學之資於
易也大矣易之所以爲至也不其可見乎大傳
懼人以卜筮小易也其言若曰大哉易也聖人
因之以發其蘊而又資之以終其功是故理蘊
於心之爲德德至於聖人若無所資矣而齋戒
===
以神明則日新而不已者莫不求端於易也理
措諸事之謂業業至於聖人若無所資矣而變
通以趣時則富有而無窮者莫不默成於易也
而何以明其然也蓋易之爲道語高而極於神
化性命也語卑而顯於日用事物也聖人會易
理於心而爲智焉則達於昭曠有以發其獨覺
之明而其智崇矣聖人體易理於事而爲禮焉
則允蹈無愆有以見諸躬行之實而其禮卑矣
夫崇莫如天而聖人之智效諸天焉昭明有融
punctuated:
學易者不能及此。
考試官教授夏批：詞理雅健，粹然出於正。
考試官教授帥批：文有深思，取之。
大傳論聖學之資於易，而必徵諸學之大者焉。
夫聖人之德業而效法於天地，則聖學之資於易也大矣。易之所以爲至也，不其可見乎？大傳懼人以卜筮小易也，其言若曰：大哉，易也！聖人因之以發其蘊，而又資之以終其功。是故理蘊於心之爲德，德至於聖人，若無所資矣；而齋戒以神明，則日新而不已者，莫不求端於易也。理措諸事之謂業，業至於聖人，若無所資矣；而變通以趣時，則富有而無窮者，莫不默成於易也。而何以明其然也？蓋易之爲道，語高而極於神化性命也，語卑而顯於日用事物也。聖人會易理於心而爲智焉，則達於昭曠，有以發其獨覺之明，而其智崇矣。聖人體易理於事而爲禮焉，則允蹈無愆，有以見諸躬行之實，而其禮卑矣。夫崇莫如天，而聖人之智效諸天焉，昭明有融
translation_en:
…students of the Changes cannot attain this.
Examiner Xia, an Instructor, comments: “The language and reasoning are elegant and vigorous, issuing wholly from what is correct.”
Examiner Shuai, an Instructor, comments: “The essay shows deep reflection. Accept it.”
The Great Commentary discusses how sagely learning draws upon the Changes, and necessarily substantiates this through the greatest aspects of learning.
When the sage’s virtue and achievements take Heaven and Earth as their models, great indeed is the aid that sagely learning receives from the Changes. Does this not reveal why the Changes is supreme? The Great Commentary fears that people will belittle the Changes by treating it merely as divination. Its words are as if to say: Great indeed is the Changes! The sage relies on it to unfold what lies within him and draws upon it to bring his work to completion. Thus, principle held within the heart constitutes virtue. When virtue reaches the level of the sage, it seems to need no further aid. Yet through purification and abstinence he attains spiritual illumination; his ceaseless daily renewal invariably finds its source in the Changes. Principle applied to affairs is called achievement. When achievement reaches the level of the sage, it seems to need no further aid. Yet through adapting and responding to changing circumstances, he keeps pace with the times; his inexhaustible abundance is invariably brought silently to fulfillment through the Changes.
How can we make clear that this is so? As for the Way of the Changes, at its highest it extends to spiritual transformation, human nature, and destiny; at its lowest it manifests itself in everyday affairs and things. The sage comprehends the principles of the Changes within his heart, making them wisdom. He thereby attains luminous breadth and brings forth the illumination of his unique insight: thus his wisdom is exalted. The sage embodies the principles of the Changes in affairs, making them ritual propriety. He thereby treads faithfully without error and manifests them in actual personal conduct: thus his ritual propriety is lowly. Nothing is more exalted than Heaven, and the sage’s wisdom takes Heaven as its model. Its radiant and pervasive illumination…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
者合其太虛之體旁燭無疆者擬其清通之象
而崇斯至矣德之達諸天者非以易而何卑莫
如地而聖人之禮法諸地焉踐履篤實者同其
厚載之機躬行懇到者應夫安貞之吉而卑斯
至矣業之配諸地者非以易而何夫德以易而
崇則聖人之德資於易以爲德也業以易而廣
則聖人之業資於易以爲業也易之爲書其可
以卜筮小之哉大抵易理充塞乎天地而神明
於聖心善觀易者求之於吾心而不泥之於法
===
象則仰觀俯察稽驗不忒也陰陽散殊至理躍
如也信哉畫前原有易所謂效天法地者正以
見聖人之善用易也
書
帝曰夔命汝典樂教冑子直而溫寬而栗
剛而無虐簡而無傲詩言志歌永言聲
依永律和聲八音克諧無相奪倫神人
以和
陳瑛
punctuated:
者合其太虛之體，旁燭無疆者擬其清通之象，而崇斯至矣。德之達諸天者，非以易而何？卑莫如地，而聖人之禮法諸地焉。踐履篤實者同其厚載之機，躬行懇到者應夫安貞之吉，而卑斯至矣。業之配諸地者，非以易而何？夫德以易而崇，則聖人之德資於易以爲德也；業以易而廣，則聖人之業資於易以爲業也。易之爲書，其可以卜筮小之哉？大抵易理充塞乎天地，而神明於聖心。善觀易者求之於吾心，而不泥之於法象，則仰觀俯察，稽驗不忒也；陰陽散殊，至理躍如也。信哉，畫前原有易！所謂效天法地者，正以見聖人之善用易也。
書
帝曰：「夔，命汝典樂，教冑子：直而溫，寬而栗，剛而無虐，簡而無傲。詩言志，歌永言，聲依永，律和聲。八音克諧，無相奪倫，神人以和。」
陳瑛
translation_en:
…that accords with Heaven’s substance as the Great Void; its boundless illumination on every side mirrors Heaven’s clarity and all-pervading openness. Thus sublimity reaches its utmost. Through what, if not the Changes, does the sage’s virtue reach Heaven? Nothing is lowlier than Earth, and the sage’s ritual propriety takes Earth as its model. His steadfast and earnest practice shares in Earth’s capacity to bear all things generously; his sincere and thorough personal conduct accords with the auspiciousness of peaceful constancy. Thus lowliness reaches its utmost. Through what, if not the Changes, do his accomplishments match Earth?
Since virtue becomes sublime through the Changes, the sage’s virtue draws upon the Changes to become virtue; since accomplishments become extensive through the Changes, the sage’s accomplishments draw upon the Changes to become accomplishments. Can the Changes, as a book, be belittled as merely a work of divination by tortoise shell and milfoil? In general, the principles of the Changes fill Heaven and Earth and become wondrously illuminated within the sage’s heart. Those who understand how to study the Changes seek them within their own hearts, without becoming fixated upon models and images. Then, whether looking upward or examining what lies below, their investigations and verifications do not err. Amid the manifold differentiation of yin and yang, the ultimate principles stand vividly revealed. True indeed: the Changes existed before the lines of the hexagrams were drawn! What is called emulating Heaven and modeling oneself on Earth precisely demonstrates the sage’s skill in applying the Changes.
Book of Documents
The Emperor said: “Kui, I command you to take charge of music and instruct the sons of the nobility to be upright yet gentle, tolerant yet circumspect, firm without being harsh, and unassuming without being arrogant. Poetry expresses intent; song prolongs its words. Musical notes follow that prolongation, and the pitch standards harmonize the notes. When the eight classes of musical instruments are brought into harmony, without encroaching upon one another’s proper order, spirits and human beings are thereby brought into harmony.”
Chen Ying 陳瑛

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭李批思致春容而詞復清雅讀之洋洋然
此大繇之音與
考試官敎授夏批發虞廷育才之意殆盡
考試官敎授帥批詞理精切
聖君命大臣以樂爲敎因推樂之足以感焉甚
矣樂之所感者深也樂和而神人之和應之矣
何有于胄子之德哉帝舜因伯夷之讓而命夔
者如此若曰治以人才爲先而尤以敎化爲本
今此胄子行將有天下國家之責者也汝其爲
===
我典樂以敎之蓋人性不無氣稟之累而施敎
當有涵育之方要必本優柔之趣以養其中俾
直與寬者咸進于温栗而不至于偏焉可矣廣
易良之化以融其累俾剛與簡者弗失之傲虐
而不至于過焉可矣斯則有以成胄子中和之
德而樂之敎其庶矣乎然吾所以有取夫樂者
而豈徒哉亦以由人心生耳是故心有所之匪
詩莫宣也由是歌以永之而聲出焉聲有高下
匪律莫和也由是益之損之而樂成焉將見
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭李批：思致春容，而詞復清雅，讀之洋洋然，此大繇之音與？
考試官敎授夏批：發虞廷育才之意殆盡。
考試官敎授帥批：詞理精切。
聖君命大臣以樂爲敎，因推樂之足以感焉。甚矣，樂之所感者深也！樂和，而神人之和應之矣，何有于胄子之德哉？帝舜因伯夷之讓而命夔者如此。若曰：「治以人才爲先，而尤以敎化爲本。今此胄子，行將有天下國家之責者也。汝其爲我典樂以敎之。蓋人性不無氣稟之累，而施敎當有涵育之方。要必本優柔之趣以養其中，俾直與寬者咸進于温栗，而不至于偏焉，可矣；廣易良之化以融其累，俾剛與簡者弗失之傲虐，而不至于過焉，可矣。斯則有以成胄子中和之德，而樂之敎其庶矣乎！然吾所以有取夫樂者，而豈徒哉？亦以由人心生耳。是故心有所之，匪詩莫宣也，由是歌以永之，而聲出焉；聲有高下，匪律莫和也，由是益之損之，而樂成焉。將見
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The conception has a springlike expansiveness, and the language is also pure and elegant. Reading it, one feels its abundant flow. Are these the strains of the Da You [?]?”
Examiner Xia, Professor, comments: “It brings out almost fully the intent behind the nurturing of talent at Shun’s court.”
Examiner Shuai, Professor, comments: “The language and reasoning are refined and exact.”
The sage ruler commanded a high minister to teach through music, and proceeded to elaborate upon music’s power to move. Profound indeed is the influence of music! When music is harmonious, spirits and human beings respond in harmony. What difficulty, then, could there be in cultivating virtue in the sons of the nobility? Such was Emperor Shun’s intent when, following Bo Yi’s yielding of the appointment, he appointed Kui. It was as though he said:
“Government gives priority to talented men, and rests still more fundamentally upon teaching and moral transformation. These sons of the nobility will soon bear responsibility for all under Heaven, for the states and their ruling houses. Take charge of music for me and instruct them through it. Human nature is not free of the encumbrances of one’s endowment of vital energy, and instruction must provide a means of nurturing it. One must draw upon music’s gentle, accommodating character to nourish their inner balance, so that the straightforward and the tolerant alike advance toward warmth and disciplined gravity, without becoming one-sided. That will suffice. Extend its power to transform through ease and goodness, dissolving their encumbrances, so that the firm and the unceremonious do not lapse into arrogance or harshness, and do not go to excess. That will suffice. Thus there will be a means of perfecting the virtues of equilibrium and harmony in the sons of the nobility: will the teaching afforded by music not then be close to its fulfillment?
“Yet is my reason for choosing music without further foundation? It is also because music arises from the human heart. Thus, when the heart inclines toward something, only poetry can express it. Singing then prolongs that expression, and musical sounds emerge. Sounds have their high and low pitches, and only the pitch standards can harmonize them. Accordingly, one augments and diminishes them, and music takes shape. We shall then see…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
音迭奏雍雍乎從律而不姦以薦郊廟一和氣
之所熏蒸也有時歆而罔時恫神且格之矣而
何有于胄子哉律呂相宣秩秩乎倫清而無僭
以奏朝廷一太和之所洋溢也羣后讓而庶尹
諧人且應之矣謂不足以敎胄子哉是蓋以其
生于人心者而感乎人心則其機易入而爲敎
易行也汝之章敎舍樂曷以哉雖然樂之足以
敎也固矣而德其本也重華之德既有以會聲
氣之元則九成之樂亦不過鳴其盛耳苟無平
===
中之德而徒事于聲器之末祗足爲導慾增悲
具也此房中之奏開元之聲所以無裨於儲養
之敎
徽柔懿恭懷保小民惠鮮鰥寡自朝至于
日中昃不遑暇食用咸和萬民
許國誠
同考試官敎諭李批上下語意自有淺深而發揮殆盡
其深造者耶宜錄以式
考試官敎授夏批體認精切傑士也
punctuated:
音迭奏，雍雍乎從律而不姦，以薦郊廟，一和氣之所熏蒸也。有時歆而罔時恫，神且格之矣，而何有于胄子哉？律呂相宣，秩秩乎倫清而無僭，以奏朝廷，一太和之所洋溢也。羣后讓而庶尹諧，人且應之矣，謂不足以敎胄子哉？是蓋以其生于人心者而感乎人心，則其機易入而爲敎易行也。汝之章敎，舍樂曷以哉？雖然，樂之足以敎也固矣，而德其本也。重華之德既有以會聲氣之元，則九成之樂亦不過鳴其盛耳。苟無平中之德，而徒事于聲器之末，祗足爲導慾增悲具也。此房中之奏、開元之聲所以無裨於儲養之敎。

徽柔懿恭，懷保小民，惠鮮鰥寡，自朝至于日中昃，不遑暇食，用咸和萬民。

許國誠

同考試官敎諭李批：上下語意自有淺深，而發揮殆盡，其深造者耶？宜錄以式。

考試官敎授夏批：體認精切，傑士也。
translation_en:
…tones sound in succession, harmoniously following the pitch standards without disorder. Offered at the suburban sacrifices and in the ancestral temples, they are wholly permeated by harmonious vital energy. The spirits are pleased and never distressed; even they come to receive the offerings. What difficulty, then, could there be in teaching the sons of the nobility? The yin and yang pitch standards give expression to one another, orderly, with their relations clear and no encroachment. Performed at court, they overflow with supreme harmony. The assembled lords yield to one another, and the various officials are in concord. People respond to this music: could one say that it is insufficient to teach the sons of the nobility? Since what arises from the human heart is used to move the human heart, its influence readily enters, and teaching through it is readily put into practice. In making your teaching manifest, what could you employ if you abandoned music? Nevertheless, although music is certainly sufficient for teaching, virtue is its foundation. Once the virtue of Chonghua [Shun] had brought together the primal source of sound and vital energy, the nine completed movements of his music merely gave voice to its abundance. Without the virtue of balance and centrality, attending only to the secondary matters of sounds and instruments merely provides a means to arouse desires and deepen sorrow. This is why the performances within the palace chambers and the music of the Kaiyuan era did nothing to assist the education and nurture of the heir apparent.

“Admirably gentle and splendidly reverent, he cherished and protected the common people and bestowed kindness and relief upon widowers and widows. From morning until the sun had passed its zenith, he had no leisure to eat, thereby bringing all the people into harmony.”

Xu Guocheng.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “The meanings of the earlier and later phrases differ in depth, yet he has expounded them almost completely. Is he not one who has attained profound understanding? This should be recorded as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Xia, Professor: “His understanding is precise and penetrating. An outstanding scholar.”

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授帥批雅暢不凡可取
觀聖王之本德以勤民而無逸之實見矣蓋聖
王仁民之心無窮也德以施之而勤以繼之其
無逸也爲何如哉想周公告成王之意謂夫人
君以一身而居萬民之上則必以一心而切斯
民之憂固未嘗一日而忘于勤也我文王之無
逸豈特崇素儉已哉彼柔者容民之德也而徽
爲難文王則至順所發不失于懦何徽柔焉恭
者臨民之德也而懿爲難文王則至敬所形不
===
過乎禮何懿恭焉惟柔恭而有則故平易而近
民於小民則懷保之視之如傷而愛護以體其
情者何弗用也於鰥寡則惠鮮之哀其無告而
賙恤以厚其生者何弗至也文王以盛德而行
仁政如此而其心豈但已哉自朝至于日之中
自中至于日之昃退食有恒節矣而文王則有
所不暇焉惟以萬民廣矣其懷保之未及者何
限也汲汲焉覃仁以丕冒之俾咸囿于太和之
天斯已焉此其心固有惟日不足者而烏知時
punctuated:
考試官敎授帥批：雅暢不凡，可取。

觀聖王之本德以勤民，而無逸之實見矣。蓋聖王仁民之心無窮也，德以施之，而勤以繼之，其無逸也爲何如哉！想周公告成王之意，謂夫人君以一身而居萬民之上，則必以一心而切斯民之憂，固未嘗一日而忘于勤也。我文王之無逸，豈特崇素儉已哉！彼柔者，容民之德也，而徽爲難。文王則至順所發，不失于懦，何徽柔焉！恭者，臨民之德也，而懿爲難。文王則至敬所形，不過乎禮，何懿恭焉！惟柔恭而有則，故平易而近民。於小民則懷保之，視之如傷，而愛護以體其情者，何弗用也！於鰥寡則惠鮮之，哀其無告，而賙恤以厚其生者，何弗至也！文王以盛德而行仁政如此，而其心豈但已哉！自朝至于日之中，自中至于日之昃，退食有恒節矣，而文王則有所不暇焉。惟以萬民廣矣，其懷保之未及者何限也！汲汲焉覃仁以丕冒之，俾咸囿于太和之天，斯已焉。此其心固有惟日不足者，而烏知時
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Shuai, Professor: Elegant and fluent, out of the ordinary; worthy of selection.

Observe how the sage king grounded himself in virtue and labored for the people: the substance of his freedom from ease becomes apparent. The sage king’s concern to treat the people humanely was inexhaustible. He put it into practice through virtue and sustained it through diligence. How remarkable was his refusal of ease! We may imagine the Duke of Zhou’s intention in admonishing King Cheng as follows: a ruler stands, in his single person, above the myriad people; he must therefore devote his whole heart to their troubles. Indeed, he must never let a single day pass in forgetfulness of his duty to exert himself. Was our King Wen’s refusal of ease merely a matter of esteeming simplicity and frugality? Gentleness is the virtue by which one embraces the people, but making it admirable is difficult. In King Wen, the expression of perfect mildness never lapsed into weakness: how admirable his gentleness! Reverence is the virtue by which one presides over the people, but making it fine is difficult. In King Wen, the manifestation of perfect respect never exceeded ritual propriety: how fine his reverence! Because his gentleness and reverence were governed by proper standards, he was accessible and close to the people. He cherished and protected the common people, regarding them as though they were injured: what means of loving and protecting them, with sympathetic understanding of their circumstances, did he fail to employ? He bestowed kindness upon widowers and widows, pitying them because they had no one to whom they could appeal: to what lengths did he not go in relieving their distress and enriching their livelihood? Such was King Wen’s practice of humane government through abundant virtue; yet how could his heart rest content there? From morning until noon, and from noon until the sun declined, there were fixed times for withdrawing to eat. Yet King Wen found himself without leisure for this. He reflected that the myriad people were so numerous: how countless were those whom his care and protection had yet to reach! He urgently extended his benevolence to encompass them all, stopping only when all were sheltered beneath a heaven of supreme harmony. His heart truly felt that even the whole day was insufficient; how could he be mindful of the time…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
之當食哉萬民衆矣其有遺于惠鮮者何限也
汲汲焉布德以覆育之俾咸歸于和裕之域斯
已焉此其心固有一息匪懈者而遑食之計哉
夫文王之德已盛而心克勤心愈勤則其德益
盛此其所以紹抑畏之統而稱無逸之君今王
治文王之民寧不思法文王之勤歟論者謂無
逸一篇爲周家王業之本而八百之祚則自文
王啓之信矣然以成王基命宥密之主豈不知
勤政恤民者而周公拳拳以是告之無非慮其
===
幼冲而以其耳目所逮動之耳老成忠愛於此
可見
詩
鳳凰于飛翽翽其羽亦集爰止藹藹王多
吉士維君子使媚于天子鳳凰于飛翽
翽其羽亦傅于天藹藹王多吉人維君
子命媚于庶人鳳凰鳴矣于彼高岡梧
桐生矣于彼朝陽菶菶萋萋雝雝喈喈
林奇石
punctuated:
之當食哉？萬民衆矣，其有遺于惠鮮者何限也！汲汲焉布德以覆育之，俾咸歸于和裕之域斯已焉。此其心固有一息匪懈者，而遑食之計哉？夫文王之德已盛而心克勤，心愈勤則其德益盛，此其所以紹抑畏之統而稱無逸之君。今王治文王之民，寧不思法文王之勤歟？論者謂《無逸》一篇爲周家王業之本，而八百之祚則自文王啓之，信矣！然以成王基命宥密之主，豈不知勤政恤民者？而周公拳拳以是告之，無非慮其幼冲而以其耳目所逮動之耳。老成忠愛，於此可見。
詩
鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦集爰止。藹藹王多吉士，維君子使，媚于天子。鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦傅于天。藹藹王多吉人，維君子命，媚于庶人。鳳凰鳴矣，于彼高岡。梧桐生矣，于彼朝陽。菶菶萋萋，雝雝喈喈。
林奇石
translation_en:
…that it was time to eat? The myriad people were so numerous: how many still lay beyond his kindness and relief! He urgently spread his beneficence to shelter and nurture them, stopping only when all had entered a realm of harmony and abundance. His heart never slackened for a single breath; how could he spare a thought for eating? King Wen’s virtue was already abundant, yet his heart remained diligent; the more diligent his heart, the more abundant his virtue became. Thus he carried on the tradition of reverent caution and was acclaimed as a ruler who took no ease. Now that Your Majesty governs King Wen’s people, should you not think to emulate King Wen’s diligence? Commentators say that the chapter “Against Ease” was the foundation of the Zhou royal enterprise, and that its eight hundred years of sovereignty began with King Wen. True indeed! Yet King Cheng was a ruler who established the Mandate in profound tranquility: how could he have been unaware of the need to attend diligently to government and care for the people? The Duke of Zhou’s earnest admonition on this matter arose solely from concern for his tender youth; he sought to move him through what he himself had heard and seen. Here we can discern the loyalty and loving concern of an experienced elder.
Book of Odes
The phoenixes fly, their wings rustling; they gather and come to rest. In throngs, the king’s many worthy officers are employed by the noble lord and win the affection of the Son of Heaven. The phoenixes fly, their wings rustling; they rise to heaven. In throngs, the king’s many worthy men receive the noble lord’s commands and win the affection of the common people. The phoenixes call upon that high ridge. The wutong trees grow upon its sun-facing slope. Luxuriant and lush are the trees; harmonious and sweet are the calls.
Lin Qishi.

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭趙批形容治世君臣之盛宛然在目
雅義之粹者也
考試官教授夏批發明召公寓諷之意殆盡
考試官教授帥批明暢工緻
詩人兩興賢才之嚮用而因喻明良之盛焉蓋
上不負君下不負民賢才嚮用之志則然也而
明良之際不因可觀其盛耶召康公戒成王之
意若謂聖君之於賢臣其義本相成而其遇甚
不偶也載觀王國夫豈乏人者哉彼鳳凰于飛
===
亦翽覽德輝而集爰止矣此藹藹王多吉士固
生此王國者也維君子有以使之則媚茲之懷
締焉而為上為德殆根於天性而不容已者矣
鳳凰于飛亦翽振羽儀而傅于天矣此藹藹王
多吉人固王國克生者也維君子有以命之則
綏懷之術顯焉而為下為民殆出於天衷而不
容遏者矣夫賢才願忠於王國如此則上下交
而理道隆者胥此矣其盛不有可言者哉彼鳳
凰之鳴非無所擇也希聲之發其惟千仞之表
punctuated:
同考試官教諭趙批：形容治世君臣之盛，宛然在目，雅義之粹者也。
考試官教授夏批：發明召公寓諷之意殆盡。
考試官教授帥批：明暢工緻。
詩人兩興賢才之嚮用，而因喻明良之盛焉。蓋上不負君，下不負民，賢才嚮用之志則然也。而明良之際，不因可觀其盛耶？召康公戒成王之意，若謂聖君之於賢臣，其義本相成，而其遇甚不偶也。載觀王國，夫豈乏人者哉？彼鳳凰于飛，亦翽，覽德輝而集爰止矣。此藹藹王多吉士，固生此王國者也。維君子有以使之，則媚茲之懷締焉，而為上為德，殆根於天性而不容已者矣。鳳凰于飛，亦翽，振羽儀而傅于天矣。此藹藹王多吉人，固王國克生者也。維君子有以命之，則綏懷之術顯焉，而為下為民，殆出於天衷而不容遏者矣。夫賢才願忠於王國如此，則上下交而理道隆者胥此矣。其盛不有可言者哉？彼鳳凰之鳴，非無所擇也。希聲之發，其惟千仞之表
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “The flourishing relations between ruler and ministers in a well-governed age are depicted so vividly that they seem before our eyes. This captures the pure essence of the meaning of the Elegantiae.”
Examiner Xia, Professor, comments: “This brings out almost fully the Duke of Shao’s intention to convey an indirect admonition.”
Examiner Shuai, Professor, comments: “Clear, fluent, skillful, and polished.”
The poet twice uses evocative imagery to convey worthy men’s aspiration to serve, thereby illustrating the flourishing partnership of an enlightened ruler and good ministers. For above, to fail neither their ruler, nor below, the people: such is the aspiration of worthy men who seek employment. Can we not thereby behold the flourishing relations between an enlightened ruler and good ministers? The intention of Duke Kang of Shao in admonishing King Cheng was seemingly to say that a sage ruler and worthy ministers are, in principle, mutually complementary, yet their coming together is far from a mere chance encounter. Looking upon the royal realm, could it possibly lack such men? Those phoenixes fly, their wings rustling; beholding the radiance of virtue, they gather and alight there. These numerous good officers of the king were indeed born within this royal realm. If only the ruler has the means to employ them, their affection for him takes firm root; their service to their sovereign and to virtue is surely rooted in their natural endowment and cannot cease. The phoenixes fly, their wings rustling; displaying their splendid plumage, they ascend to heaven. These numerous good men of the king are indeed men whom the royal realm has been able to produce. If only the ruler has the means to commission them, their arts of bringing peace and winning hearts become manifest; their service to those below and to the people surely springs from their Heaven-given nature and cannot be restrained. Since worthy men so desire to be loyal to the royal realm, it is entirely through this that those above and below are brought into communion and the Way of good government flourishes. Is there not something to be said of such abundance? When the phoenix calls, it does not do so without choosing its place. The utterance of its rare note must surely come from beyond a height of a thousand ren…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
乎梧桐之生非無所自也靈根之托其惟明盛
之地乎惟生于朝陽也則蓁蓁焉萋萋焉本深
末茂足為棲止之安如此乎嘉木之盛也而能
忘情於靈鳥耶惟鳴于高岡也則雝雝焉喈喈
焉氣和聲和足為治世之音如此乎靈鳥之適
也而能自外於嘉木耶是知鳳凰梧桐物類之
相感也聖君賢臣理道之相成也然其機不在
鳳凰而在梧桐其具不在賢臣而在聖君吾王
可以深長思矣抑觀成王之時周召夾輔宇宙
===
太和萬世稱得人歌盛治者蔑以加矣而召公
何惓惓不置也蓋賢才難於布列老成宜於倚
毗倘人主親賢之念一或少忽則乗間抵隙比
暱交而德業隳矣此召公之所深憂也卷阿之
咏真善諷者與
有秩斯祜申錫無疆
林皆春
同考試官教諭趙批揄揚烈祖垂裕之遠根本功德
上來是善言頌義者
punctuated:
乎？梧桐之生，非無所自也，靈根之托，其惟明盛之地乎？惟生于朝陽也，則蓁蓁焉，萋萋焉，本深末茂，足為棲止之安，如此乎嘉木之盛也，而能忘情於靈鳥耶？惟鳴于高岡也，則雝雝焉，喈喈焉，氣和聲和，足為治世之音，如此乎靈鳥之適也，而能自外於嘉木耶？是知鳳凰梧桐，物類之相感也；聖君賢臣，理道之相成也。然其機不在鳳凰而在梧桐，其具不在賢臣而在聖君，吾王可以深長思矣。抑觀成王之時，周召夾輔，宇宙太和，萬世稱得人、歌盛治者，蔑以加矣，而召公何惓惓不置也？蓋賢才難於布列，老成宜於倚毗。倘人主親賢之念一或少忽，則乗間抵隙，比暱交而德業隳矣。此召公之所深憂也。《卷阿》之咏，真善諷者與！
有秩斯祜，申錫無疆。
林皆春
同考試官教諭趙批：「揄揚烈祖垂裕之遠，根本功德上來，是善言頌義者。」
translation_en:
…is it not? Nor does the wutong tree grow without a fitting place: surely its numinous roots take hold only in a land of enlightened flourishing? Growing on a sun-facing slope, it is luxuriant and abundant, its roots deep and its branches flourishing, affording a secure place to perch. Such is the flourishing of this fine tree: could it be indifferent to the numinous bird? Calling upon the high ridge, the bird sings harmoniously and melodiously, its vital spirit and its voice alike in harmony, worthy to be the music of a well-governed age. Such is the contentment of the numinous bird: could it keep itself apart from the fine tree? Thus we know that the phoenix and the wutong respond to one another as kinds of living things, while the sage ruler and worthy ministers bring the Way of good government to fulfillment together. Yet the determining impulse lies not with the phoenix but with the wutong; the means lie not with worthy ministers but with the sage ruler. Our king should ponder this deeply and at length.
Consider, moreover, the time of King Cheng, when the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao assisted him on either side, and all under heaven enjoyed great harmony. Through the ages, those praising the employment of worthy men and celebrating flourishing government have found nothing to surpass it. Why, then, did the Duke of Shao persist so earnestly without ceasing? Because worthy talent is difficult to array in office, and seasoned elders deserve to be relied upon. Should the ruler become even slightly negligent in his resolve to associate closely with the worthy, those who seize opportunities and exploit openings will gather in partisan intimacy, and his virtue and achievements will fall into ruin. This was the Duke of Shao’s profound concern. The song Winding Mound (Juan A) is truly masterful in indirect admonition!
“Great indeed is this blessing, bestowed anew without limit.”
Lin Jiechun
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “It extols how far the illustrious ancestor’s abundant legacy extends, grounding this in his achievements and virtue. This is an excellent exposition of the meaning of the hymn.”

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授夏批得詩人登歌之意
考試官敎授帥批簡古
詩人祀聖祖而頌其垂裕之遠焉蓋先王以裕
後爲福也功德如成湯而所被寧有窮耶此祀
成湯之樂也若曰帝王以萬世爲業則必以萬
世爲福而有不能者功德限之也我祖成湯佑
啓後人者豈其微哉是故聖敬日躋烈祖之德
與天同運者也是以天心克享畀之祜以光其
德者秩然宏遠之規模焉爰革夏正烈祖之功
===
永世無極者也是以帝命不易隆之祜以昭其
功者秩然恒久之氣象焉弘一統以開天受祉
旣多也而且孔厚也申錫之爲後人之令緒而
何有於終窮式九圍以基命發祥旣遠也而且
甚長也申錫之爲後人之保極而何有於限量
以延曆數之傳豈徒一世二世已乎近之而子
子而又子以似以續有常享焉百代之休光此
固爲之伊始矣以衍靈長之運豈但一傳再傳
已乎遠之而孫孫而又孫繼體承祧有常保焉
punctuated:
考試官敎授夏批：得詩人登歌之意。
考試官敎授帥批：簡古。
詩人祀聖祖而頌其垂裕之遠焉。蓋先王以裕後爲福也，功德如成湯，而所被寧有窮耶？此祀成湯之樂也。若曰：帝王以萬世爲業，則必以萬世爲福，而有不能者，功德限之也。我祖成湯佑啓後人者，豈其微哉？是故聖敬日躋，烈祖之德與天同運者也，是以天心克享，畀之祜以光其德者，秩然宏遠之規模焉。爰革夏正，烈祖之功永世無極者也，是以帝命不易，隆之祜以昭其功者，秩然恒久之氣象焉。弘一統以開天，受祉旣多也，而且孔厚也；申錫之爲後人之令緒，而何有於終窮？式九圍以基命，發祥旣遠也，而且甚長也；申錫之爲後人之保極，而何有於限量？以延曆數之傳，豈徒一世二世已乎？近之而子，子而又子，以似以續，有常享焉。百代之休光，此固爲之伊始矣。以衍靈長之運，豈但一傳再傳已乎？遠之而孫，孫而又孫，繼體承祧，有常保焉。
translation_en:
Examiner Xia, Instructor, comments: “Captures the poet’s intention in the hymn sung in the hall.”
Examiner Shuai, Instructor, comments: “Concise and antique in style.”
The poet sacrifices to the sage ancestor and praises the far-reaching bounty he bequeathed. For the former kings regarded providing abundantly for their descendants as a blessing. With achievements and virtue such as those of Cheng Tang, could there be any limit to the reach of his beneficence? This is music for the sacrifice to Cheng Tang. It is as though the poet were saying: Emperors and kings take ten thousand generations as the span of their undertaking, and must therefore take ten thousand generations as the span of their blessings. If some cannot accomplish this, it is because their achievements and virtue impose a limit. Could the aid and guidance that our ancestor Cheng Tang bestowed upon his descendants have been slight?
Thus, his sagely reverence advanced daily: the illustrious ancestor’s virtue moved in harmony with Heaven. Hence Heaven’s heart accepted his offerings and bestowed blessings to make his virtue shine—a well-ordered design, vast and far-reaching. He then changed the Xia calendar: the illustrious ancestor’s achievements would endure forever without limit. Hence the Lord on High’s mandate remained unchanged, and the abundant blessings that made his achievements manifest displayed a well-ordered prospect of lasting endurance.
He enlarged the unified realm and inaugurated a new dispensation under Heaven. The blessings he received were already many, and exceedingly generous besides. Bestowed repeatedly, they became a splendid inheritance for his descendants: how could they ever come to an end? He brought order to the nine regions and established the foundation of the mandate. The auspicious beginnings already reached far back, and their continuance was exceedingly long. Bestowed repeatedly, these blessings enabled his descendants to preserve the supreme standard: how could they have any limit?
In prolonging the transmission of the dynastic mandate, could this have been merely a matter of one generation or two? In the nearer generations came sons, and sons after sons, following and continuing their predecessor, with blessings to enjoy perpetually. Here indeed began the glorious good fortune of a hundred generations. In extending the dynasty’s enduring, numinous destiny, could this have been merely a matter of one succession or two? In the distant generations came grandsons, and grandsons after grandsons, succeeding to the sovereign’s position and inheriting the ancestral shrines, with blessings to preserve perpetually. …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
萬年之景命此固爲之肇端矣蓋豐功無窮則
休澤亦無窮駿德常在則福慶亦常在今日之
祭誠莫非烈祖之申錫者而敢忘所自哉抑聞
之先王法度不可廢德澤不可恃商之孫子豈
念不及此哉吾觀武丁孫子皆能恭默其心悠
久其德而祀事之脩則又孚之天人盡之志物
和之節奏以答先祖申錫之仁此所以必得其
福而庶幾於賢者之祭歟
春秋
===
春王正月公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯
許男曹伯侵蔡蔡潰遂伐楚次于陘〔僖公四年〕冬公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒
子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子
光伐鄭十有二月巳亥同盟于戲〔襄公九年〕夏公會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷〔定公十年〕
周良寅
同考試官教諭朱 批 王霸服人德力自是不同兹作
punctuated:
萬年之景命，此固爲之肇端矣。蓋豐功無窮，則休澤亦無窮；駿德常在，則福慶亦常在。今日之祭，誠莫非烈祖之申錫者，而敢忘所自哉？抑聞之，先王法度不可廢，德澤不可恃。商之孫子，豈念不及此哉？吾觀武丁孫子，皆能恭默其心，悠久其德，而祀事之脩，則又孚之天人，盡之志物，和之節奏，以答先祖申錫之仁。此所以必得其福，而庶幾於賢者之祭歟？

春秋

春，王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。〔僖公四年〕冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。十有二月，巳亥，同盟于戲。〔襄公九年〕夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。〔定公十年〕

周良寅

同考試官教諭朱批：王霸服人，德力自是不同。兹作
translation_en:
…the glorious mandate lasting ten thousand years: this indeed marked its beginning. For when great achievements are inexhaustible, their beneficent blessings are likewise inexhaustible; when sublime virtue endures, good fortune and felicity likewise endure. The sacrifice offered today truly derives entirely from the illustrious ancestors’ repeated bestowals. How could one dare forget its source? Yet I have heard that the former kings’ laws and institutions must not be abandoned, nor may one simply rely upon their virtuous beneficence. Could the descendants of Shang have failed to consider this? I observe that Wu Ding’s descendants were all able to keep their hearts reverent and composed and make their virtue endure. In conducting sacrifices, moreover, they inspired the trust of Heaven and men, gave full expression to their intentions and made complete material offerings, and harmonized the musical measures and rhythms, thereby reciprocating their ancestors’ benevolence in repeatedly bestowing blessings. Is this not why they were certain to receive those blessings and approached the sacrificial practice of the worthy?

Spring and Autumn Annals

In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the Duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao in invading Cai. Cai collapsed. They then attacked Chu and encamped at Xing. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi〕 In winter, the Duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Xiao Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, in attacking Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the day recorded as sihai [?], they jointly covenanted at Xi. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xiang〕 In summer, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The Duke returned from Jiagu. 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding〕

Zhou Liangyin

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “In securing people’s submission, the true king and the hegemon differ inherently in their use of virtue and force. This composition …”

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
於均善中而屬詞寓意甚得經㫖
同考試官教授吳批善為國者惟執禮以化强是作
獨歸美聖績而詞㫖明切宜錄以式
考試官教授夏批詞簡意足經義優長
考試官教授帥批精健不繁得謹嚴體
春秋紀内外制敵之善所以昭王事也此桓悼
之善師善陣雖不逮孔子之不師乃君子猶有
取焉彼詐而捷也何爲哉昔齊人伐魯魯也禦
之曹劌效謀長勺敗焉而春秋深以爲魯罪者
===
何君子曰是不聞待敵有道乎彼爲國不師上
矣此王事也其次有善師而不陣者又其次有
善陣而不戰者不觀之桓悼孔子乎以桓言之
方其伐楚也兵連八國潰首蔡師剪而食以逞
君心似無有難者乃桓則不然責問以包茅王
祭辱貺以徼好同心陘亭次而屈完惠來益顯
實征之績矣師旅雖勤行伍未列不其善師乎
然猶未免於師也以悼言之方其伐鄭也鄭疑
未同楚爭益競戰而捷以長諸侯似不可緩者
punctuated:
於均善中，而屬詞寓意甚得經㫖。
同考試官教授吳批：善為國者，惟執禮以化强。是作獨歸美聖績，而詞㫖明切，宜錄以式。
考試官教授夏批：詞簡意足，經義優長。
考試官教授帥批：精健不繁，得謹嚴體。
春秋紀内外制敵之善，所以昭王事也。此桓、悼之善師善陣，雖不逮孔子之不師，乃君子猶有取焉。彼詐而捷也，何爲哉？昔齊人伐魯，魯也禦之，曹劌效謀，長勺敗焉，而春秋深以爲魯罪者，何？君子曰：是不聞待敵有道乎？彼爲國不師，上矣，此王事也。其次有善師而不陣者，又其次有善陣而不戰者。不觀之桓、悼、孔子乎？以桓言之，方其伐楚也，兵連八國，潰首蔡師，剪而食以逞君心，似無有難者。乃桓則不然，責問以包茅王祭，辱貺以徼好同心，陘亭次而屈完惠來，益顯實征之績矣。師旅雖勤，行伍未列，不其善師乎？然猶未免於師也。以悼言之，方其伐鄭也，鄭疑未同，楚爭益競，戰而捷以長諸侯，似不可緩者。
translation_en:
…among works that are all good, its phrasing and underlying meaning accord particularly well with the purport of the Classic.
Associate Examiner Wu, an Instructor, comments: Those who govern a state well rely solely on ritual propriety to transform the powerful. This composition reserves its highest praise for the sage’s achievement; its language and meaning are clear and incisive. It should be recorded as a model.
Examiner Xia, an Instructor, comments: Concise in wording and ample in meaning, it excels in interpreting the Classic.
Examiner Shuai, an Instructor, comments: Refined and vigorous without prolixity, it achieves a careful and disciplined style.
The Spring and Autumn Annals records excellence in dealing with enemies, both within Lu and beyond its borders, in order to illuminate the work of true kingship. Thus, although Duke Huan’s skill in deploying armies and Duke Dao’s skill in drawing up formations did not equal Confucius’s achievement in dispensing with an army altogether, the gentleman still finds something to commend in them. What worth, then, is there in winning through deception? Formerly, the men of Qi attacked Lu, and Lu resisted them. Cao Gui offered a plan, and Qi was defeated at Changshao. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals lay such grave blame upon Lu?
The gentleman says: Have you not heard that there is a proper way to deal with an enemy? To govern a state without deploying an army is the highest achievement: this is the work of true kingship. Next comes skill in deploying an army without drawing it up for battle; next again comes skill in drawing up formations without fighting. Can this not be seen in Duke Huan, Duke Dao, and Confucius?
Consider Duke Huan. When he attacked Chu, he joined the forces of eight states and first routed the army of Cai. To destroy and devour the enemy in order to gratify his ruler’s desires seemed to present no difficulty. Yet Duke Huan did otherwise. He demanded an accounting for the bundled mao grass owed for the royal sacrifices, and graciously conferred favor to seek friendship and concord [?]. He encamped at Xingting, and Qu Wan kindly came to him, further displaying the achievement of a truly corrective expedition. Although the troops had been put to work, their ranks had not been drawn up for battle. Was this not skill in deploying an army? Nevertheless, he had still not dispensed with an army.
Consider Duke Dao. When he attacked Zheng, Zheng remained hesitant and had not joined the alliance, while Chu’s rivalry grew ever more intense. To fight and win, thereby establishing leadership over the feudal lords, seemed something that could brook no delay…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
乃悼則不然謀深於息民固本力全於分銳逆
來𢧐門次而子駰趨盟坐收三駕之功矣威武
雖揚兵刄未接不其善陣乎然猶未免于陣也
以孔子言之方夾谷之會也犁彌倡謀禍且不
測魯蓋岌岌矣幸而孔子以禮義相焉責之以
干盟偪好懼之以棄德不祥齊能無屈乎由是
敵國謝過而好會用成萊兵阻却而策勳飮至
戰陣固不足道師亦將焉用之不其善國耶夫
是之謂王者之事待敵之道斯其至矣彼二伯
===
者在桓猶爲近正匜悼巳云德衰乃今詐而捷
如魯焉不獨孔子之罪人抑亦桓悼之罪人矣
此長勺之役必主魯以深責之歟抑桓悼之伯
仲罃之謀也二君能庸之尚足以取伯定威夫
子以綏來動和之聖有變齊變魯之機而卒以
女樂去焉固不待權臣竊命而巳知定之無能
爲也嗚呼歸三田墮三都孔子豈二臣所敢班
而定乃不桓悼若焉蓋君臣相遇之難抑世道
汙隆之運歟
punctuated: 乃悼則不然，謀深於息民固本，力全於分銳逆來，𢧐門次而子駰趨盟，坐收三駕之功矣。威武雖揚，兵刄未接，不其善陣乎？然猶未免于陣也。以孔子言之，方夾谷之會也，犁彌倡謀，禍且不測，魯蓋岌岌矣。幸而孔子以禮義相焉，責之以干盟偪好，懼之以棄德不祥，齊能無屈乎？由是敵國謝過，而好會用成；萊兵阻却，而策勳飮至。戰陣固不足道，師亦將焉用之？不其善國耶？夫是之謂王者之事，待敵之道斯其至矣！彼二伯者，在桓猶爲近正匜，悼巳云德衰。乃今詐而捷如魯焉，不獨孔子之罪人，抑亦桓悼之罪人矣。此長勺之役，必主魯以深責之歟？抑桓悼之伯，仲罃之謀也。二君能庸之，尚足以取伯定威。夫子以綏來動和之聖，有變齊變魯之機，而卒以女樂去焉，固不待權臣竊命，而巳知定之無能爲也。嗚呼！歸三田，墮三都，孔子豈二臣所敢班？而定乃不桓悼若焉。蓋君臣相遇之難，抑世道汙隆之運歟？
translation_en:
…Yet Duke Dao acted otherwise. His plans were deeply concerned with giving the people respite and securing the foundations of the state; he concentrated his efforts on dividing his picked troops and meeting the enemy’s advance [?]. He encamped at the battle gate [?], and Ziyin hastened to conclude a covenant: thus he secured the achievements of three campaigns without further exertion. Although he displayed martial might, weapons had not crossed. Was he not skilled in deploying armies? Yet he still could not dispense with deployment.

As for Confucius, at the meeting at Jiagu, Li Mi proposed a plot whose disastrous consequences could not be foreseen, and Lu was in grave peril. Fortunately, Confucius assisted his ruler through ritual propriety and righteousness. He reproached the other side for violating the covenant and coercing a friendly state, and made them fear the ill consequences of abandoning virtue. How could Qi fail to yield? Thus the rival state apologized for its offense, and the friendly meeting was successfully concluded. The troops of Lai were held back, and achievements were recorded and celebrated with the ceremonial drink upon returning. Battle and deployment were scarcely worth mentioning; what need was there even for an army? Was he not skilled in governing a state? This is what is meant by the work of a true king. Here the way of dealing with an enemy reaches its highest point!
