Of those two hegemons, Duke Huan could still be considered close to rectitude [?], whereas by Duke Dao’s time virtue was already said to have declined. Now, to gain victory through deception, as Lu did, makes one an offender not only against Confucius but also against Dukes Huan and Dao. Is this why the account of the battle at Changshao necessarily makes Lu the principal actor, in order to censure it severely?

Moreover, the hegemonies of Huan and Dao depended on the plans of Guan Zhong and Xun Ying. The two rulers could employ these men, and this was sufficient to attain hegemony and establish their authority. The Master was a sage who brought people to him by pacifying them and brought harmony through his actions; he had the opportunity to transform Qi and Lu. Yet in the end he departed because of the female musicians. Even before powerful ministers usurped the authority to issue commands, one could already tell that Duke Ding was incapable of accomplishing anything.

Alas! In securing the return of the three territories and demolishing the fortifications of the three cities, how could those two ministers have dared place themselves alongside Confucius? Yet Duke Ding did not measure up to Huan and Dao. Was this because a ruler and minister so rarely find their proper counterparts, or because of the turns by which the moral order of the age declines and flourishes?

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
六月齊侯來獻戎捷莊公三十有一年
楊日采
同考試官教諭朱批霸者每喜功尚誇聖門羞稱茲作
發明題旨透徹無餘錄之
同考試官教授吳批經抑桓之矜功由惡桓之略遠詞
極簡嚴意尤明確
考試官教授夏批意精式合取之
考試官教授帥批發勤兵矜功意最精
霸主矜略遠之功春秋所以抑之也甚矣功不
===
足矜也而况略遠之功乎此齊桓之獻戎捷春
秋卑辭以抑之與甞聞軍獲曰捷捷而致之於
君曰獻魯齊匹耳北戎病燕桓師往正而遺俘
于魯乃春秋書曰來獻宛然以下奉上之辭何
哉王者之道覲文德而匿武功崇退讓而恥誇
大故倖功勤遠者治之蠹飾虛凌人者德之慙
君子無取焉淺哉桓仲之于戎也伐而捷捷而
獻何為哉忽內治而不脩動眾勤民既以逞心
於漠北之虜棄禮讓而不顧恫疑恐喝更欲誇
punctuated:
「六月，齊侯來獻戎捷。」莊公三十有一年。
楊日采。
同考試官教諭朱批：「霸者每喜功尚誇，聖門羞稱。茲作發明題旨，透徹無餘，錄之。」
同考試官教授吳批：「經抑桓之矜功，由惡桓之略遠。詞極簡嚴，意尤明確。」
考試官教授夏批：「意精式合，取之。」
考試官教授帥批：「發勤兵矜功意最精。」
霸主矜略遠之功，春秋所以抑之也。甚矣，功不足矜也，而况略遠之功乎！此齊桓之獻戎捷，春秋卑辭以抑之與？甞聞軍獲曰捷，捷而致之於君曰獻。魯齊匹耳，北戎病燕，桓師往正，而遺俘于魯。乃春秋書曰「來獻」，宛然以下奉上之辭，何哉？王者之道，覲文德而匿武功，崇退讓而恥誇大。故倖功勤遠者，治之蠹；飾虛凌人者，德之慙。君子無取焉。淺哉，桓仲之于戎也！伐而捷，捷而獻，何為哉？忽內治而不脩，動眾勤民，既以逞心於漠北之虜；棄禮讓而不顧，恫疑恐喝，更欲誇
translation_en:
“In the sixth month, the Marquis of Qi came to present spoils taken from the Rong.” Thirty-first year of Duke Zhuang.
Yang Ricai.
Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor of a county Confucian school, comments: “Hegemons invariably delight in achievements and prize boasting; the school of the Sage disdains to speak of them. This composition elucidates the meaning of the topic thoroughly, leaving nothing unexplained. Record it.”
Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor of a prefectural Confucian school, comments: “The Classic censures Huan’s pride in his achievements because it condemns his incursions into distant lands. The wording is exceptionally concise and rigorous, and the meaning especially clear.”
Examiner Xia, Instructor of a prefectural Confucian school, comments: “The conception is refined and the form appropriate. Accept it.”
Examiner Shuai, Instructor of a prefectural Confucian school, comments: “Its exposition of the ideas of exhausting troops and vaunting achievements is most penetrating.”
The hegemon vaunted his achievement in campaigning far afield: this is why the Spring and Autumn Annals censures him. How utterly unworthy of boasting are military achievements—and how much more so achievements won by invading distant lands! When Huan of Qi presented spoils taken from the Rong, did the Spring and Autumn Annals not employ language that lowered his standing in order to censure him? I have heard that captures made in war are called ‘spoils,’ and that delivering these spoils to one’s ruler is called ‘presenting.’ Lu and Qi were merely peers. The Northern Rong afflicted Yan, and Huan’s army went to chastise them, afterward sending captives to Lu. Yet the Spring and Autumn Annals records this as ‘came to present,’ unmistakably using the language of an inferior offering something to a superior. Why?
The way of a true king is to display civil virtue [?] and conceal martial achievements, to honor deference and yielding, and to regard boasting as shameful. Thus those who seek achievements through mere good fortune and expend their strength on distant campaigns are a blight upon good government; those who embellish empty claims and overawe others bring shame upon virtue. The gentleman finds nothing to commend in them. How shallow was the conduct of Huan and Guan Zhong toward the Rong! They attacked and took spoils; having taken spoils, they presented them. To what purpose? Neglecting domestic government and failing to put it in order, they mobilized the multitude and exhausted the people, already indulging their desires against the barbarians north of the desert. Discarding ritual propriety and deference without a thought, employing intimidation and threats, they further wished to flaunt…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
示乎東蒙之君豈知地列要荒疆理所不及也
伐之已黷武矣乃復震而矜焉不已甚乎古人
以隕淵之心而居已成之功桓其識之耶寇非
門庭利禦所弗用也伐之已不祥矣乃復挾而
驕焉能無愧乎古人以不伐之心而消爭能之
妬桓其知之耶君子謂是舉也柔懷之道闕而
未聞侈耀之心蕩而莫制安得比於采芑之奏
功泮水之獻馘哉故齊魯非君臣也乃卑辭以
抑之而書來獻云此義行而勤兵遠略好大喜
===
功者戒矣抑此桓仲之謀也蓋楚近而山戎遠
楚難而山戎易也先其近而易者以折諸侯之
心則楚不待兵而服矣此其酌緩急識機宜以
雄起伯桓仲亦人傑也惜其王道未聞而持盈
之戒不講遂令戎捷之張為首伯累自是而濤
塗執九國叛威名亦少損矣噫玆桓仲之所以
止于桓仲與
禮記
詩云肅雝和鳴先祖是聽夫肅肅敬也雝
punctuated:
示乎東蒙之君，豈知地列要荒，疆理所不及也？伐之已黷武矣，乃復震而矜焉，不已甚乎？古人以隕淵之心而居已成之功，桓其識之耶？寇非門庭，利禦所弗用也。伐之已不祥矣，乃復挾而驕焉，能無愧乎？古人以不伐之心而消爭能之妬，桓其知之耶？君子謂是舉也，柔懷之道闕而未聞，侈耀之心蕩而莫制，安得比於《采芑》之奏功、《泮水》之獻馘哉？故齊魯非君臣也，乃卑辭以抑之，而書「來獻」云。此義行，而勤兵遠略、好大喜功者戒矣。抑此桓仲之謀也，蓋楚近而山戎遠，楚難而山戎易也。先其近而易者，以折諸侯之心，則楚不待兵而服矣。此其酌緩急、識機宜，以雄起伯，桓仲亦人傑也。惜其王道未聞，而持盈之戒不講，遂令戎捷之張為首伯累。自是而濤塗執，九國叛，威名亦少損矣。噫！玆桓仲之所以止于桓仲與？

禮記

《詩》云：「肅雝和鳴，先祖是聽。」夫肅肅，敬也；雝
translation_en:
…to display their might before the ruler of Dongmeng! How could they understand that these lands lay in the remote outer zones, beyond the reach of territorial administration? To attack them was already to abuse military force; then to overawe others and boast of it—was this not going too far? The ancients rested upon accomplished achievements with the apprehension of someone about to fall into an abyss. Did Duke Huan understand this? When invaders are not at one’s gates, the principle that it is advantageous to resist them does not apply. To attack them was already inauspicious; then to use that achievement as grounds for arrogance—could they be without shame? The ancients dispelled the jealousy arising from rivalry in ability by refusing to boast of themselves. Did Duke Huan know this? The gentleman would say that in this undertaking the way of winning people over through gentle treatment was absent and unheard of, while the desire for ostentatious display ran unchecked. How could it compare with the accomplishment celebrated in “Gathering Millet” (Cai qi), or the presentation of severed enemy ears in “The Waters of the Pan” (Pan shui)? Thus, although Qi and Lu did not stand in the relation of ruler and subject, the text employs a self-abasing expression to restrain Qi, recording that it “came to present” the captives. When this principle prevails, those who exhaust their armies on distant conquests and delight in grand undertakings and military achievements will take warning.

Yet this was a strategy devised by Duke Huan and Guan Zhong. Chu was near, whereas the Shanrong were far away; Chu was difficult to subdue, whereas the Shanrong were easy. By first dealing with the nearby and easy opponent [?], they would break the resolve of the regional lords, and Chu would submit without the need for warfare. In weighing what required immediate attention and what could wait, and recognizing timely opportunities, they rose powerfully to hegemony: Duke Huan and Guan Zhong were indeed outstanding men. Regrettably, they had not learned the kingly Way or studied the warning to remain cautious at the height of success. Thus their vaunting of the victory over the Rong became a blemish upon the foremost hegemon. Thereafter, Taotu was seized and the nine states rebelled, somewhat diminishing Duke Huan’s prestige. Alas! Is this why Duke Huan and Guan Zhong advanced no further than they did?

Record of Rites (Li ji)

The Book of Poetry says: “Solemn and harmonious, they sing in concord; the ancestors listen.” Solemnity means reverence; harmony…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
雝和也夫敬以和何事不行
余一愚
同考試官教諭王批和敬二字多泥樂音上說是作
獨推本太富大定處來最得肯綮錄之
同考試官學正黃批正樂感通之旨體認既直截詞
自別當是作手
考試官教授夏批迥異諸作
考試官教授帥批雄健
賢者引言古樂之正而裕於用焉蓋萬事莫不
===
以和敬爲本也古樂兼之其裕於用也宜哉此
子夏釋詩以告文侯有曰先王作樂固將以致
用也而用之有弗宜者以音之不古若耳乃古
樂則何如耶夫聲音之感至微也鬼神之幽至
難格也詩曰肅雝和鳴先祖是聽是果何以致
之哉彼云肅肅者非無謂也言是樂也自紀綱
大定之時而中聲巳肇是故爲莊誠爲勁正其
極天下之至敬者耶曰雝雝者非無謂也言是
樂也自大化均調之日而元聲巳諧是故爲寬
punctuated:
雝，和也。夫敬以和，何事不行？
余一愚
同考試官教諭王批：和敬二字，多泥樂音上說。是作獨推本太富大定處來，最得肯綮，錄之。
同考試官學正黃批：正樂感通之旨，體認既直截，詞自別，當是作手。
考試官教授夏批：迥異諸作。
考試官教授帥批：雄健。
賢者引言古樂之正，而裕於用焉。蓋萬事莫不以和敬爲本也，古樂兼之，其裕於用也宜哉！此子夏釋詩以告文侯，有曰：先王作樂，固將以致用也，而用之有弗宜者，以音之不古若耳。乃古樂則何如耶？夫聲音之感至微也，鬼神之幽至難格也。詩曰：「肅雝和鳴，先祖是聽。」是果何以致之哉？彼云肅肅者，非無謂也。言是樂也，自紀綱大定之時，而中聲巳肇，是故爲莊誠，爲勁正，其極天下之至敬者耶？曰雝雝者，非無謂也。言是樂也，自大化均調之日，而元聲巳諧，是故爲寬
translation_en:
…“yong” means harmony. With reverence joined to harmony, what undertaking could fail?

Yu Yiyu

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: Discussions of the two words “harmony” and “reverence” mostly confine themselves to musical sounds. This essay alone traces them back to “great abundance” [?] and the firm establishment of order. It gets to the heart of the matter most effectively. Include it.

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, School Director: Its grasp of how correct music evokes a response and establishes communion is direct and clear, and its language is distinctive. The author must be an accomplished writer.

Comment by Examiner Xia, Professor: Far different from the other essays.

Comment by Examiner Shuai, Professor: Vigorous and forceful.

The worthy cites words explaining the correctness of ancient music and the ample scope of its application. All undertakings have harmony and reverence as their foundation; ancient music combines both. How fitting that its application should be so ample! Thus Zixia, explaining the Odes to Marquis Wen, said: The former kings created music precisely to put it to use. Where its application proves unsuitable, this is simply because its sounds do not measure up to those of antiquity. What, then, was ancient music like? The influence of sound is exceedingly subtle, while spirits, hidden from view, are exceedingly difficult to reach. The Odes says: “Solemn and harmonious, the sounds blend; the ancestors listen.” How indeed was this achieved? The words “solemn, solemn” are not without meaning. They mean that in this music, from the time the guiding principles of order were firmly established, the balanced tones had already arisen. Hence its solemn sincerity and firm uprightness: does it not embody the utmost reverence in the world? The words “harmonious, harmonious” are not without meaning. They mean that in this music, from the day the great transforming process attained even balance, the fundamental tones were already in accord. Hence its breadth…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
裕焉順成其極天下之至和者耶夫匪敬則流
匪和則離事之所以不行也玆惟敬而且和則
整肅之中而有優游者在施之隨事而皆宜端
嚴之內而有和平者存措之無往而弗利以之
篤近而身可脩家可齊焉德音之發越殆不止
於一身之咸淑矣先祖聽之云乎哉以之舉遠
而天下可平焉正樂之感通殆不止於四國之
克順矣祭祀用之云乎哉夫曰敬而且和則感
之也爲有本曰何事不行則用之也爲無方德
===
音異於溺音信矣抑有疑焉惠王有世俗之慙
孟子告以今樂同於古文侯有鄭衛之聽子夏
告以古樂異於今何哉蓋言同者所以啓其偕
樂之情言異者所以抑其新聲之好也奈何雅
俗迭陳而正樂卒爲淫哇所勝文侯猶之惠王
焉則鍾聲左高之辨亦不過鏗鏘音韻之末耳
噫吾於是而知梁魏均不足以有爲而和樂之
興必有所待也
子曰君子不以辭盡人故天下有道則行
punctuated:
裕焉、順成，其極天下之至和者耶？夫匪敬則流，匪和則離，事之所以不行也。玆惟敬而且和，則整肅之中而有優游者在，施之隨事而皆宜；端嚴之內而有和平者存，措之無往而弗利。以之篤近，而身可脩、家可齊焉，德音之發越殆不止於一身之咸淑矣，先祖聽之云乎哉？以之舉遠，而天下可平焉，正樂之感通殆不止於四國之克順矣，祭祀用之云乎哉？夫曰敬而且和，則感之也爲有本；曰何事不行，則用之也爲無方。德音異於溺音，信矣！抑有疑焉：惠王有世俗之慙，孟子告以今樂同於古；文侯有鄭衛之聽，子夏告以古樂異於今，何哉？蓋言同者，所以啓其偕樂之情；言異者，所以抑其新聲之好也。奈何雅俗迭陳，而正樂卒爲淫哇所勝！文侯猶之惠王焉，則鍾聲左高之辨，亦不過鏗鏘音韻之末耳。噫！吾於是而知梁魏均不足以有爲，而和樂之興必有所待也。

子曰：「君子不以辭盡人，故天下有道，則行
translation_en:
…ample and conducive to fulfillment: does it not bring the utmost harmony under Heaven to its highest expression? Without reverence, there is dissipation; without harmony, estrangement. These are why affairs fail to proceed. Here, however, reverence and harmony are both present. Within order and solemnity there is ease, so that its application is fitting in every affair; within dignity and gravity there is peace, so that wherever it is employed, it brings benefit. Through it, one strengthens bonds with those nearby, and the person can be cultivated and the family regulated. The influence of virtuous music surely extends beyond making a single person wholly good. Can this mean merely that the ancestors listen to it? Through it, one reaches those far away, and all under Heaven can be brought to peace. The sympathetic influence of correct music surely extends beyond bringing the four quarters into willing accord. Can this mean merely that it is used in sacrifices? To say that it is reverent and harmonious is to say that its power to move has a foundation; to ask what affair would not proceed successfully is to say that its uses have no bounds. That virtuous music differs from debasing music is indeed true!

Yet there is a doubt. King Hui felt ashamed of his taste for popular music, and Mengzi told him that the music of the present was the same as that of antiquity. Marquis Wen listened to the music of Zheng and Wei, and Zixia told him that ancient music differed from modern music. Why? Speaking of their sameness was a means of awakening the king’s desire to share his enjoyment with others; speaking of their difference was a means of restraining the marquis’s fondness for novel sounds. How was it, then, that refined and vulgar music were performed in turn, yet correct music was ultimately overcome by licentious and lascivious sounds? Marquis Wen was just like King Hui. His discernment that the bells on the left were higher in pitch amounted to no more than the trifling details of clangor and tonal patterns. Alas! From this I know that neither Liang nor Wei was capable of accomplishing anything, and that the flourishing of harmonious music must await something further.

The Master said: “The gentleman does not judge a person wholly by his words. Thus, when the Way prevails under Heaven, conduct …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
有枝葉
莊履豐
同考試官教諭王批言不煩而意自足殆能芟去枝葉
者可式可式
同考試官學正黃批用意切實而文足以發之經義
之最佳者
考試官教授夏批講尚行處明淨
考試官教授帥批精到
惟觀人不盡於言此盛世必尚乎行也甚矣言
===
可以觀人而不可以盡人也故行為治世之所
尚有以哉想夫子之意豈不曰好尚有關乎氣
運言行視世為重輕使言而足以盡人謂其為
治世之所重可也而孰知有不然者何也言者
心之聲心未易測君子固嘗緣聲以探其微而
辭者德之華德鮮克舉君子未嘗因華而忘其
實以一言之庶幾而遽信其由衷焉此安知非
色莊者而君子弗盡與也以一時之議論而遂
槩其為人焉此安知能持久者而君子弗盡信
punctuated:
有枝葉。
莊履豐
同考試官教諭王批：言不煩而意自足，殆能芟去枝葉者，可式，可式。
同考試官學正黃批：用意切實，而文足以發之，經義之最佳者。
考試官教授夏批：講尚行處明淨。
考試官教授帥批：精到。
惟觀人不盡於言，此盛世必尚乎行也。甚矣，言可以觀人而不可以盡人也！故行為治世之所尚，有以哉！想夫子之意，豈不曰：好尚有關乎氣運，言行視世為重輕。使言而足以盡人，謂其為治世之所重，可也。而孰知有不然者？何也？言者，心之聲，心未易測，君子固嘗緣聲以探其微；而辭者，德之華，德鮮克舉，君子未嘗因華而忘其實。以一言之庶幾而遽信其由衷焉，此安知非色莊者，而君子弗盡與也；以一時之議論而遂槩其為人焉，此安知能持久者，而君子弗盡信
translation_en:
…has branches and leaves.

Zhuang Lüfeng 莊履豐

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: His words are few, yet his meaning is complete. He seems capable of pruning away extraneous branches and leaves. Worthy of emulation, worthy of emulation!

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: The conception is sound and practical, and the writing fully expresses it. Among the finest interpretations of the Classics.

Comment by Examiner Xia, Professor: The discussion of giving precedence to conduct is clear and uncluttered.

Comment by Examiner Shuai, Professor: Precise and penetrating.

Since assessing a person cannot rest entirely on words, a flourishing age must give precedence to conduct. How true it is that words may afford insight into a person but cannot reveal that person fully! There is good reason, then, that conduct is esteemed in an age of good government. Considering the Master's meaning, might he not be saying this: prevailing preferences bear upon the fortunes of the age, and the relative weight assigned to words and conduct varies with the times. If words sufficed to reveal a person fully, one could indeed say that they should be esteemed in an age of good government. Yet who recognizes that this is not so? Why is this? Words are the voice of the heart, and the heart is not easily fathomed; the gentleman has certainly sought to probe its subtleties by following its voice. But verbal expression is the flowering of virtue, and virtue is seldom fully realized; the gentleman has never allowed its flowers to make him forget its fruit. To hear a single utterance that approaches the ideal and immediately believe that it comes from the heart—how can one know that this is not someone whose solemnity is merely outward? Thus the gentleman does not grant him unqualified approval. To hear someone's discussion on one occasion and thereupon judge his entire character—how can one know that he can remain constant? Thus the gentleman does not trust him completely…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
也夫辭之不可盡人如此詎以治世而復尚辭
耶故天下之有道也天子公卿躬行於上聿崇
實勝之風百官萬民敦行於下自妙默成之化
樹德之本植於中者既裕矣斯英華發於和順
而敷之經綸者奕奕焉蓋根本盛而枝葉自茂也
彼靜言庸違者其能復容於斯世哉敦化之基
涵於內者既厚矣斯輝光奮於篤實而發之事
業者亹亹焉蓋植本固而枝葉自敷也彼侈言
無當者尚能自途於斯時哉吁治世尚行如此
===
則言之不足盡人益可徵矣君子其慎諸雖然
言不可尚而亦不可廢也行所當崇而亦不可
偏也以辭盡人夫子既致警矣而子貢問君子
復以先行後從告之迺知浮靡之習固不可長
而訥言敏行尤君子大中之道也否則刻意尚
行將流於賢者之過豈盛世所宜有哉故他日
又曰君子言必慮其所終行必稽其所敝
第貳場
論
punctuated:
也。夫辭之不可盡人如此，詎以治世而復尚辭耶？故天下之有道也，天子公卿躬行於上，聿崇實勝之風；百官萬民敦行於下，自妙默成之化。樹德之本，植於中者既裕矣，斯英華發於和順，而敷之經綸者奕奕焉，蓋根本盛而枝葉自茂也。彼靜言庸違者，其能復容於斯世哉？敦化之基，涵於內者既厚矣，斯輝光奮於篤實，而發之事業者亹亹焉，蓋植本固而枝葉自敷也。彼侈言無當者，尚能自途於斯時哉？吁！治世尚行如此，則言之不足盡人益可徵矣，君子其慎諸！雖然，言不可尚，而亦不可廢也；行所當崇，而亦不可偏也。以辭盡人，夫子既致警矣，而子貢問君子，復以先行後從告之。迺知浮靡之習固不可長，而訥言敏行，尤君子大中之道也。否則刻意尚行，將流於賢者之過，豈盛世所宜有哉？故他日又曰：「君子言必慮其所終，行必稽其所敝。」

第貳場

論
translation_en:
…so it is. Since words cannot fully reveal a person, how could an age of good government still give precedence to words? Thus, when the Way prevails throughout the realm, the Son of Heaven, the dukes, and the high ministers personally put it into practice above, promoting a climate in which substance predominates. Below, the officials and the people earnestly practice it, bringing about the subtle work of transformation accomplished without words. When the roots of virtue planted within are already abundant, their finest flowering emerges in harmony and concord, and their application to ordering affairs shines brilliantly. This is because, when the roots flourish, the branches and leaves naturally grow luxuriant. How could those whose agreeable words are belied by their conduct still find acceptance in such an age? When the foundation of profound moral transformation nurtured within is already deep, its radiance springs from earnest sincerity, and its expression in undertakings advances unceasingly. This is because, when the roots are firmly planted, the branches and leaves naturally spread. Could those whose extravagant words have no substance still make their way [?] in such a time?

Ah! When an age of good government prizes conduct in this way, the inadequacy of words for fully judging a person becomes all the more evident. Let the gentleman be cautious about this! Nevertheless, although words should not be given precedence, neither may they be discarded; although conduct ought to be honored, neither should it be stressed to the exclusion of everything else. The Master had already warned against judging a person entirely by his words. Yet when Zigong asked about the gentleman, he also told him to act first and let his words follow. Thus we know that habits of superficiality and extravagance must certainly not be encouraged, while being restrained in speech and diligent in action is above all the gentleman’s way of perfect balance. Otherwise, a determined insistence on conduct would tend toward the excesses of the worthy. How could this be fitting in a flourishing age? Hence, on another occasion he also said: “In speaking, the gentleman must consider the eventual outcome of his words; in acting, he must examine the abuses to which his conduct may lead.”

Second Session

Discourse

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖人一天人賛化育之道
林奇石
同考試官教諭李批律本處作者類多未達是
篇直指本原究極功用末復歸重心上非平日潜心律吕
者不能到此
同考試官學正龍批格調尚古而迂廻曲折不失矩
矱可以式多士矣
考試官教授夏批有學識有力量
考試官教授帥批充贍不浮
===
作樂者其有所本乎得其本而功化神矣甚矣
樂之爲道難言也而其所可見者不能有外於
聲氣然聲者其迹也氣者其幾也不泥其迹不
滯其幾而直求夫聲氣之元者樂之本也本也
者吾心中和之理是也以吾心自然之理而寄
諸器數聲容之間則器數者樂也而莫非此心
之寓也聲容者樂也而莫非此心之顯也以吾
心之中而感中以吾心之和而召和則盈宇宙
間皆無有鬱而不通滯而不宣之情而位育之
punctuated:
聖人一天人賛化育之道
林奇石

同考試官教諭李批：律本處，作者類多未達。是篇直指本原，究極功用，末復歸重心上，非平日潜心律吕者不能到此。
同考試官學正龍批：格調尚古，而迂廻曲折不失矩矱，可以式多士矣。
考試官教授夏批：有學識，有力量。
考試官教授帥批：充贍不浮。

作樂者，其有所本乎？得其本而功化神矣！甚矣，樂之爲道難言也！而其所可見者，不能有外於聲氣。然聲者，其迹也；氣者，其幾也。不泥其迹，不滯其幾，而直求夫聲氣之元者，樂之本也。本也者，吾心中和之理是也。以吾心自然之理，而寄諸器數聲容之間，則器數者，樂也，而莫非此心之寓也；聲容者，樂也，而莫非此心之顯也。以吾心之中而感中，以吾心之和而召和，則盈宇宙間，皆無有鬱而不通、滯而不宣之情，而位育之
translation_en:
The Way by Which the Sage Unites Heaven and Humanity and Assists Their Transforming and Nurturing Work
By Lin Qishi

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, School Instructor: Most writers fail to grasp the foundation of the pitch standards. This essay points directly to their source and explores their functions and effects to the utmost, finally returning to place primary emphasis on the mind. Only someone who habitually devotes himself to studying the pitch standards could attain this understanding.
Comment by Associate Examiner Long, School Instructor: Its style esteems antiquity; through all its winding turns, it remains within the proper standards. It can serve as a model for the many candidates.
Comment by Examiner Xia, Professor: It has learning and discernment, strength and force.
Comment by Examiner Shuai, Professor: Full and ample, without superficiality.

Must those who create music have a foundation on which to rely? Once they grasp that foundation, its achievements and transforming influence become numinous! How very difficult it is to speak of the Way of music! What can be perceived of it cannot lie outside sound and vital energy. Yet sound is its outward trace, and vital energy its incipient impulse. Without becoming bound to its traces or arrested at its incipient impulses, to seek directly the source of sound and vital energy is to seek the foundation of music. This foundation is the principle of equilibrium and harmony within my own mind. When I lodge my mind’s inherent principle among instruments, numerical measures, sounds, and ceremonial movements, instruments and numerical measures constitute music, and all embody this mind; sounds and ceremonial movements constitute music, and all manifest this mind. With the equilibrium of my mind I evoke equilibrium; with the harmony of my mind I summon harmony. Then, throughout the universe, no disposition remains pent up without communication, or obstructed without expression, and the transformation through which all things take their proper places and are nurtured …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
化在是矣其斯以爲一天人賛化育之道與請
因蔡氏之言而論之嘗觀之易曰大哉乾元萬
物資始至哉坤元萬物資生此天人化育之妙
也樂者器也而黃鍾者又樂之一也執一音而
曰可以一天人賛化育然則黃鍾與天地齊乎
君子曰以黃鍾言黃鍾器數焉耳安得與天地
齊耶然窮其元識其情達其順而究其極則黃
鍾之理一天地之理也何也天地當六陰極剥
之時一陽萌動於地雷之復自此而歷臨泰壯
===
夬至乾爲左行之陽歷姤遯否觀至坤爲右轉
之陰所以妙出入而神闔闢者復之一陽肇之
也其天地中和之心乎律始黃鍾作樂者蓋亦
以吾心之復準天地之復而制之中制之和者
也自此太簇至中吕爲下生之陽蕤賓至應鍾
爲上生之陰上生六而倍之下生六而損之其
律十二其調六十其實一黃鍾也蓋黃者中之
色也鍾種也陽氣潜萌於黃宮而萬物萌孽於
此也言中而和也故在律則稱母在象則稱君
punctuated: 化在是矣。其斯以爲一天人、賛化育之道與？請因蔡氏之言而論之。嘗觀之《易》曰：「大哉乾元，萬物資始！至哉坤元，萬物資生！」此天人化育之妙也。樂者器也，而黃鍾者又樂之一也。執一音而曰可以一天人、賛化育，然則黃鍾與天地齊乎？君子曰：「以黃鍾言黃鍾，器數焉耳，安得與天地齊耶？然窮其元，識其情，達其順，而究其極，則黃鍾之理，一天地之理也。何也？天地當六陰極剥之時，一陽萌動於地雷之復，自此而歷臨、泰、壯、夬，至乾，爲左行之陽；歷姤、遯、否、觀，至坤，爲右轉之陰。所以妙出入而神闔闢者，復之一陽肇之也。其天地中和之心乎？律始黃鍾，作樂者蓋亦以吾心之復，準天地之復，而制之中、制之和者也。自此太簇至中吕，爲下生之陽；蕤賓至應鍾，爲上生之陰。上生六而倍之，下生六而損之，其律十二，其調六十，其實一黃鍾也。蓋黃者，中之色也；鍾，種也。陽氣潜萌於黃宮，而萬物萌孽於此也。言中而和也，故在律則稱母，在象則稱君。
translation_en:
…the transforming work by which things find their proper places and flourish lies here. Is this, then, the way to unite Heaven and humanity and assist their transforming and nourishing work? Allow me to discuss this on the basis of Master Cai’s words. I have read in the Book of Changes: “Great indeed is the primal power of Qian! All things depend upon it for their beginning. Utmost indeed is the primal power of Kun! All things depend upon it for their birth.” Here lies the subtle working of transformation and nurture in Heaven and humanity. Music is an instrument, and Huangzhong is but one pitch within music. If one takes a single tone and says that it can unite Heaven and humanity and assist transformation and nurture, does this mean that Huangzhong stands equal to Heaven and Earth?

The gentleman says: “If we speak of Huangzhong merely as Huangzhong, it is only an affair of instruments and numerical measures. How could it stand equal to Heaven and Earth? Yet if we exhaustively investigate its source, understand its nature, comprehend its orderly course, and pursue it to its ultimate extent, then the principle of Huangzhong is one with the principle of Heaven and Earth. Why is this? When Heaven and Earth reach the stage at which the six yin lines have brought stripping away to its extreme, a single yang line begins to stir in Fu, Return, with Earth above Thunder. From this it passes through Lin, Tai, Zhuang, and Guai to Qian: this is yang proceeding to the left. It passes through Gou, Dun, Pi, and Guan to Kun: this is yin turning to the right. The wondrous coming forth and entering, the marvelous closing and opening, all originate in the single yang line of Fu. Is this not the heart of Heaven and Earth in equilibrium and harmony?

“The pitch standards begin with Huangzhong. Those who create music likewise take the return within their own hearts, model it on the return of Heaven and Earth, and fashion music in equilibrium and harmony. From here, Taicu through Zhonglü constitute the yang pitches generated downward; Ruibin through Yingzhong constitute the yin pitches generated upward. The six generated upward are doubled, and the six generated downward are diminished. There are twelve pitch standards and sixty modes, yet in substance they are all the single Huangzhong. For huang, yellow, is the color of the center; zhong means ‘seed.’ Yang energy secretly begins to sprout in the Yellow Palace, and here the myriad things put forth shoots. To speak of equilibrium is also to speak of harmony. Thus, among the pitch standards it is called the mother; among the images it is called the ruler. …”

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
一黃鍾定而樂之道無餘矣嗚呼天地養此微
陽以成化育之功人心養此微陽以成中和之
樂天地也吾心也黃鍾也通一而無二者也聖
人之心與天地陰陽相為脗合而或順而喜或
拂而怒或觸而哀或感而樂莫非造化自然之
中而一毫無所乖戾焉則天人化育之理既已
涵蓄於聖人之心而聲氣之元自我而會其全
矣由是以之候氣而氣應焉以之調聲而聲和
焉紀之以三而天人化育之理洩於三也成之
===
以六而天人化育之理宣於六也統之以十二
分之以六十四而天人化育之理寄於律調也
驗之以二變輔之以半倍而天人化育之理有
以通其窮相其不及也不特此也由是奏諸廟
朝則天神降地祇出庶尹諧而莫非此心自然
之中和感之也由是孚乎民物則湮鬱宣淫慝
消民無札瘥物無疵癘而莫非此心自然之中
和育之也由是通乎天地則日月順軌雨暘若
時無霜雹之災無童涸之患休氣旁流於宇宙
punctuated:
一黃鍾定，而樂之道無餘矣。嗚呼！天地養此微陽，以成化育之功；人心養此微陽，以成中和之樂。天地也，吾心也，黃鍾也，通一而無二者也。聖人之心與天地陰陽相為脗合，而或順而喜，或拂而怒，或觸而哀，或感而樂，莫非造化自然之中，而一毫無所乖戾焉。則天人化育之理既已涵蓄於聖人之心，而聲氣之元自我而會其全矣。由是，以之候氣而氣應焉，以之調聲而聲和焉。紀之以三，而天人化育之理洩於三也；成之以六，而天人化育之理宣於六也；統之以十二，分之以六十四，而天人化育之理寄於律調也；驗之以二變，輔之以半倍，而天人化育之理有以通其窮，相其不及也。
不特此也。由是奏諸廟朝，則天神降，地祇出，庶尹諧，而莫非此心自然之中和感之也。由是孚乎民物，則湮鬱宣，淫慝消，民無札瘥，物無疵癘，而莫非此心自然之中和育之也。由是通乎天地，則日月順軌，雨暘若時，無霜雹之災，無童涸之患，休氣旁流於宇宙
translation_en:
Once the single pitch Huangzhong (Yellow Bell) is established, nothing in the Way of music remains unaccounted for. Ah! Heaven and Earth nurture this faint yang to accomplish their work of transformation and nourishment; the human heart nurtures this faint yang to achieve the music of centrality and harmony. Heaven and Earth, my own heart, and Huangzhong are united as one, without duality. The sage’s heart accords with the yin and yang of Heaven and Earth: whether pleased by favorable circumstances, angered by opposition, moved to sorrow by what it encounters, or stirred to joy, it invariably embodies the natural centrality of the creative process, without the slightest deviation. Thus the principles of transformation and nourishment in Heaven and humanity are already contained within the sage’s heart, and the source of sound and vital qi finds its full unity within the self. Hence, when this is used to observe the seasonal qi, the qi responds; when it is used to tune sounds, the sounds harmonize. Ordered by three, the principles of transformation and nourishment in Heaven and humanity find expression in three; completed by six, these principles are manifested in six. Organized into twelve and divided into sixty-four [?], these principles reside in the pitches and modes. Tested through the two altered notes and assisted by halving and doubling, these principles provide the means to overcome impasses and make good deficiencies.
Nor is this all. When this music is performed in the ancestral temple and at court, the spirits of Heaven descend, the spirits of Earth emerge, and the many officials act in harmony: all are moved by this heart’s natural centrality and harmony. When its influence reaches the people and other living things, what is stifled is released and depravity and evil disappear; the people suffer no pestilence or sickness, and other creatures no affliction or blight: all are nourished by this heart’s natural centrality and harmony. When it communicates with Heaven and Earth, the sun and moon follow their proper courses, rain and sunshine arrive in season, there are no disasters of frost or hail and no scourges of barrenness or dried-up waters, and auspicious qi spreads throughout the universe…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
而亦莫非此心自然之中和順之也不特此也
推此而大章大韶以賛協和風動之化者其允
執厥中之心爲之而此心一中和也推此而大
夏大濩以賛平成允殖之化者其祗台日躋之
心爲之而此心一中和也推此而大武以賛四
海永清之化者其敬勝義勝之心爲之而此心
一中和也樂而至是則乾元之所不能始者有
以發其始坤元之所不能終者有以成其終熏
烝透徹莫非氣也欣喜歡暢莫非聲也渾渾乎
===
雝雝乎而昔之所謂率舞來儀者亦自此而致
之矣而聖人一天人賛化育者其孰有外於此
心哉抑于是而知以黍求尺以尺生律者之謬
也易曰雷出地奮豫先王以作樂崇德豫也者
言人心之悅也孔氏曰人而不仁如樂何仁也
者言吾心之正也此樂之原也若反之吾心而
正求之民心而悅而所謂鍾律秬黍之制雖循
器以求之可也舍器以求之亦可也否則雖使
后夔典音太師審樂斷竹飛灰尺寸矩度絲毫
punctuated:
而亦莫非此心自然之中和順之也。不特此也，推此而大章、大韶以賛協和風動之化者，其允執厥中之心爲之，而此心一中和也。推此而大夏、大濩以賛平成允殖之化者，其祗台日躋之心爲之，而此心一中和也。推此而大武以賛四海永清之化者，其敬勝義勝之心爲之，而此心一中和也。樂而至是，則乾元之所不能始者，有以發其始；坤元之所不能終者，有以成其終。熏烝透徹，莫非氣也；欣喜歡暢，莫非聲也。渾渾乎，雝雝乎，而昔之所謂率舞來儀者，亦自此而致之矣。而聖人一天人、賛化育者，其孰有外於此心哉？

抑于是而知以黍求尺、以尺生律者之謬也。《易》曰：「雷出地奮，豫。先王以作樂崇德。」豫也者，言人心之悅也。孔氏曰：「人而不仁，如樂何？」仁也者，言吾心之正也。此樂之原也。若反之吾心而正，求之民心而悅，而所謂鍾律秬黍之制，雖循器以求之可也，舍器以求之亦可也。否則，雖使后夔典音，太師審樂，斷竹飛灰，尺寸矩度，絲毫
translation_en:
…and all this, too, is brought into accord by the natural equilibrium and harmony of this heart. Nor is this all. Extending this principle, the Dazhang and Dashao music assisted a transforming influence that brought concord and moved the people as the wind moves things. This was accomplished by the heart that sincerely held fast to the Mean; this heart embodied the same equilibrium and harmony. Extending this principle, the Daxia and Dahu music assisted a transforming influence that brought the land into order and secured the growth of its produce. This was accomplished by the heart expressed in “reverence for oneself” and “daily advancement”; this heart embodied the same equilibrium and harmony. Extending this principle, the Dawu music assisted a transforming influence that brought lasting peace within the Four Seas. This was accomplished by the heart in which reverence and righteousness prevailed; this heart embodied the same equilibrium and harmony. When music reaches this point, it can initiate what the originating power of Heaven cannot itself begin, and complete what the originating power of Earth cannot itself bring to completion. All that suffuses and penetrates is vital energy; all that rejoices and delights is sound. How full and flowing! How harmonious! What the ancients called “dancing in unison” and “coming to display their grace”—the beasts and phoenixes—was likewise brought about through this. In uniting Heaven and humanity and assisting transformation and nurture, what could the sage accomplish outside this heart?

From this we also recognize the error of seeking to establish the foot measure through millet grains, and deriving the pitch standards from that measure. The Book of Changes says: “Thunder emerges from the earth and stirs: Enthusiasm. The former kings accordingly made music to exalt virtue.” “Enthusiasm” speaks of the delight of the human heart. Confucius said: “If a person lacks benevolence, what can he do with music?” “Benevolence” speaks of the rectitude of one's own heart. This is the source of music. If we turn back to our own hearts and find rectitude, and seek in the people's hearts and find delight, then, as for the prescribed systems of bells, pitch standards, and black millet measures, we may seek them by following the instruments, or we may seek them apart from the instruments. Otherwise, even if Hou Kui were put in charge of tones and the Music Master examined the music, with bamboo cut for pitch pipes and ashes flying from them, with measures in feet and inches and rules of proportion, down to the slightest fraction…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
不失古人之舊而曰吾能樂焉君子猶以爲慙
之慙也彼妄意郊廟之音希心參摹之書者又
烏足以語此
表
擬
大閱禮成廷臣
賀表
周良寅
同考試官教諭趙批文非雕繪事極詳明宛然如若
===
親扈
鑾輿而有得者是足以華
國矣錄之
同考試官教授吳批以駢麗之詞形容
張皇之典而能刋落浮華其工於四六者
考試官教授夏批詞語豐腴體裁端重
考試官教授帥批麗而典可誦
隆慶三年九月二十一日具官臣某等恭遇
皇上大閱禮成謹奉
punctuated:
不失古人之舊，而曰吾能樂焉，君子猶以爲慙之慙也。彼妄意郊廟之音、希心參摹之書者，又烏足以語此？

表
擬大閱禮成廷臣賀表
周良寅

同考試官教諭趙批：文非雕繪，事極詳明，宛然如若親扈鑾輿而有得者，是足以華國矣，錄之。
同考試官教授吳批：以駢麗之詞形容張皇之典，而能刋落浮華，其工於四六者。
考試官教授夏批：詞語豐腴，體裁端重。
考試官教授帥批：麗而典，可誦。

隆慶三年九月二十一日，具官臣某等恭遇皇上大閱禮成，謹奉
translation_en:
…without departing at all from ancient practice, and declare, “I understand music,” a gentleman would still regard this as shame upon shame. How, then, could those who presumptuously aspire to the music of the suburban altars and ancestral temples, and set their hopes on books of comparison and imitation [?], be qualified to discuss this?

Memorial
A proposed congratulatory memorial from the court officials upon the completion of the Grand Military Review
By Zhou Liangyin

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “The writing does not depend on ornamentation; its treatment of events is exceptionally detailed and clear. It reads just as though the author had personally accompanied the imperial carriage and gained insight from the experience. This is sufficient to bring lustre to the state. Include it in the record.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Professor: “He uses elegant parallel phrases to portray a magnificent ceremony, yet manages to cut away superficial embellishment. He is skilled in four-and-six prose.”

Comment by Examiner Xia, Professor: “The language is rich and full; the composition is dignified and solemn.”

Comment by Examiner Shuai, Professor: “Elegant and classically grounded; worthy of recitation.”

On the twenty-first day of the ninth month of the third year of Longqing [1569], your servants, so-and-so and others, holding the designated offices, respectfully mark Your Majesty’s completion of the Grand Military Review and reverently submit…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
表稱
賀者伏以
哲王制治以保邦恒切無虞之儆
盛世經文而緯武式基有道之長
虎帳天開一代
皇靈丕振
龍輿雲擁百年
曠典維新
朝野歡騰華夷慶洽臣等誠欣誠忭稽首頓
===
首竊惟煦育震曜乾坤運二氣以迭施順
治威嚴帝王兼五材而並用敷文而有苗
旣格尚嚴猾夏之防愼德而四夷咸賓猶
謹詰戎之戒逮伍兩軍師之制設兵政愈
詳曁蒐苗獮狩之禮行軍容益壯從醜載
歌吉日選徒則賦車攻自周而還此禮幾
墜勞軍營壘棘門之兒戲何裨習射殿廷
渭水之狼烽莫殄豈如
昭代聿創
punctuated:
表稱賀者。伏以哲王制治以保邦，恒切無虞之儆；盛世經文而緯武，式基有道之長。虎帳天開，一代皇靈丕振；龍輿雲擁，百年曠典維新。朝野歡騰，華夷慶洽。臣等誠欣誠忭，稽首頓首。
竊惟煦育震曜，乾坤運二氣以迭施；順治威嚴，帝王兼五材而並用。敷文而有苗旣格，尚嚴猾夏之防；愼德而四夷咸賓，猶謹詰戎之戒。逮伍兩軍師之制設，兵政愈詳；曁蒐苗獮狩之禮行，軍容益壯。從醜載歌《吉日》，選徒則賦《車攻》。自周而還，此禮幾墜。勞軍營壘，棘門之兒戲何裨？習射殿廷，渭水之狼烽莫殄。豈如昭代聿創
translation_en:
…a memorial offering congratulations. We humbly reflect that wise kings establish good government to preserve the realm, ever mindful of the warning against complacency in times of security; a flourishing age takes civil accomplishments as its warp and military prowess as its weft, thereby laying the foundation for the enduring rule of the Way. The tiger-decorated command tent opens beneath Heaven, and the imperial majesty of our dynasty is mightily displayed; clouds gather about the imperial carriage, and a grand ceremony seldom seen in a hundred years is renewed. Court and countryside rejoice; Chinese and non-Chinese alike share in the celebration. We, your servants, are truly delighted and truly joyful; we bow low and knock our heads upon the ground.
We venture to reflect that Heaven and Earth circulate the two vital forces, alternately bestowing nurturing warmth and awe-inspiring thunder; emperors and kings employ the five materials together, combining harmonious governance with stern authority. Though the dissemination of civil virtue had brought the Youmiao into submission, vigilance against those who disturbed the Chinese realm remained strict; though careful cultivation of virtue had brought the peoples of the four quarters to court, the injunction to maintain military preparedness was still scrupulously observed. Once the system of squads, companies, armies, and brigades was established, military administration became ever more detailed; once the rites of the spring, summer, autumn, and winter hunts were practiced, the military array became ever more imposing. Following the multitude [?], they sang “Auspicious Day” (Jiri); selecting the foot soldiers, they composed “Our Chariots Are Stout” (Che gong). Since the Zhou, these rites have almost fallen into disuse. What benefit came from visiting troops in their encampments when the camp at Jimen was mere child’s play? Archery was practiced in the palace courts, yet the beacon fires warning of invasion along the Wei River could not be extinguished. How could these compare with our illustrious dynasty, which first established …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
弘規
制定五軍列貔貅七十二衛營名三大置將領
千八百員義略倣乎府兵法實沿於司馬
不獨安內而攘外實以居重而馭輕頃緣
昇平漸至怠弛事關
國計慮切
宸衷鑒於
祖憲以裁成斷自
廟謨而振舉茲蓋伏遇
===
皇帝陛下
聰明天縱
仁孝夙成
纘令緒以重光神人協應
凝洪圖而丕赫述作兼隆
郊祀同
廟饗時親式重明禋之典
常朝與
講筵日御務隆延訪之誠顧文治之既新念武
punctuated: 弘規，制定五軍，列貔貅七十二衛；營名三大，置將領千八百員。義略倣乎府兵，法實沿於司馬。不獨安內而攘外，實以居重而馭輕。頃緣昇平，漸至怠弛。事關國計，慮切宸衷。鑒於祖憲以裁成，斷自廟謨而振舉。茲蓋伏遇皇帝陛下，聰明天縱，仁孝夙成，纘令緒以重光，神人協應；凝洪圖而丕赫，述作兼隆。郊祀同廟饗，時親，式重明禋之典；常朝與講筵，日御，務隆延訪之誠。顧文治之既新，念武
translation_en:
…grand institutions, establishing the five armies and arraying their fierce warriors in seventy-two guards. The camps were designated the Three Great Camps, with eighteen hundred commanders appointed. In principle, the arrangement broadly imitated the fubing militia system; its regulations actually followed those of the Minister of War (Sima). It served not only to secure the realm internally and repel external threats, but also to concentrate strength at the center and thereby control the less powerful periphery. Recently, prolonged peace gradually brought laxity. As the matter concerned the affairs of state, it weighed deeply upon the imperial heart. Drawing upon the ancestral regulations, the Emperor fashioned appropriate arrangements; through decisions made in the imperial councils, he restored their vigor.
We have indeed the good fortune to live under Your Majesty the Emperor, whose intelligence is Heaven-endowed and whose benevolence and filial devotion matured early. You carry forward the illustrious succession, renewing its radiance, with spirits and men responding in harmony; you consolidate the grand design in splendid majesty, equally eminent in carrying on established institutions and creating new ones. You personally attend the suburban sacrifices and ancestral temple offerings at their appointed times, thus honoring the rites of pure sacrifice. You preside daily over regular court audiences and the imperial lectures, earnestly fostering the sincere seeking of counsel. Seeing that civil governance has already been renewed, you consider military…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
功之當競廼因輔臣之
請聿脩
大閱之儀序屬金行時維農隙諏良辰以青
龍之吉闢正位于玄武之墟
葆蓋出天閽擁千官而雲連玉珮
翠華臨日觀望六師而氣吐金霓走風伯以
清塵先雨師而灑道千旗雲引牙前停
王者之屬車萬戟霜飛幕下止
聖人之清蹕鳴鐃擊鐸各備厥官太常大綏咸
===
若其制
令下而喧聲頓肅營營若海靜山空旗舉而猛
氣倍增人人似鷹揚鷙擊刁斗鳴而風煙
起節旄指而瘴霧開右虎左龍雜鵝鸛魚
麗而互變中權後勁錯龜蛇鳥隼以相生
捲甲歸營禮終八陣陳侯立的藝閱三軍
士卒則列署分掄競逐穿楊之步將帥乃
登臺親簡爭喧落鴈之聲戎行整而喜動
天顏
punctuated: 功之當競，廼因輔臣之請，聿脩大閱之儀。序屬金行，時維農隙，諏良辰以青龍之吉，闢正位于玄武之墟。葆蓋出天閽，擁千官而雲連玉珮；翠華臨日觀，望六師而氣吐金霓。走風伯以清塵，先雨師而灑道。千旗雲引，牙前停王者之屬車；萬戟霜飛，幕下止聖人之清蹕。鳴鐃擊鐸，各備厥官；太常大綏，咸若其制。令下而喧聲頓肅，營營若海靜山空；旗舉而猛氣倍增，人人似鷹揚鷙擊。刁斗鳴而風煙起，節旄指而瘴霧開。右虎左龍，雜鵝鸛魚麗而互變；中權後勁，錯龜蛇鳥隼以相生。捲甲歸營，禮終八陣；陳侯立的，藝閱三軍。士卒則列署分掄，競逐穿楊之步；將帥乃登臺親簡，爭喧落鴈之聲。戎行整而喜動天顏。
translation_en:
…that military achievement should be pursued. Thus, at the request of his grand secretaries, he conducted the ceremony of the Grand Military Review. The season belonged to Metal, a time of respite from farming. An auspicious day was chosen under the favorable sign of the Azure Dragon, and the imperial station was prepared on the ground of the Dark Warrior.

The feathered canopy emerged from the gates of Heaven; a thousand officials crowded around, their jade pendants linked like clouds. The kingfisher-feather standard approached the sun-viewing terrace; surveying the Six Armies, it exhaled a martial aura like a golden rainbow. The Wind Lord was sent racing to clear away the dust, and the Rain Master went ahead to sprinkle the road. A thousand banners led onward like clouds; before the command standard, the sovereign’s attendant carriages halted. Ten thousand halberds flashed like frost; beneath the command pavilion, the sage ruler’s procession, its passage cleared by calls for silence, came to rest. Gongs and bells sounded, each officer fulfilling his duty; the great imperial banners and tasselled standards [?] all conformed to prescribed forms.

At the issuing of an order, the clamor abruptly ceased: every camp was like a still sea or an empty mountain. At the raising of a flag, martial ardor redoubled: every man seemed an eagle soaring or a bird of prey striking. As the watch kettles rang, wind and smoke arose; wherever the command pennons pointed, pestilential mist dispersed. Tiger formations on the right and dragon formations on the left intermingled with goose, stork, and fish-scale formations, changing into one another. The center maneuvered and the rear supplied strength; tortoise, snake, bird, and falcon formations interlaced, each giving rise to the next.

Armor was rolled up and the troops returned to camp, bringing the ceremony of the Eight Formations to a close. Archery targets were arrayed and their marks set up, and the skills of the Three Armies were reviewed. Soldiers were arranged by unit and selected in groups, vying to perform the feat of piercing a willow leaf. The commanders then mounted the terrace to be selected by the emperor in person; they competed amid clamorous acclaim for shots that could bring down wild geese. The military ranks stood in perfect order, and joy stirred upon the imperial countenance.

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
賞賚分而歡搖地軸
鴻典告成于玉壘兆示垂櫜
鑾輿遄返于
清都心非耀武陋漢主長楊校獵軌物奚存
邁成周洛水莅師家邦永保九關聲震龍
沙寢西北妖氛百粤威騰鯨海澄東南蜃
氣允矣
熈朝盛事誠哉
奕世彜章臣等學慙博古旣俎豆之無聞志
===
切籌邊恨韜鈐之未識幾年竭股肱之力
惟有赤心小技同腹背之毛何裨實用骨
非將種敢妄希投筆之封腹鮮甲兵徒留
意徙戎之論經營重寄分心膂恐負躬逢
訓練強兵動鬼神何期目覩伏願
軫山濤外懼之慮
抱賈生全盛之虞思內憂方可外寧任老成
而補
廷中之衮念選兵不如選將簡謀勇而寄閫
punctuated:
賞賚分而歡搖地軸。鴻典告成于玉壘，兆示垂櫜；鑾輿遄返于清都，心非耀武。陋漢主長楊校獵，軌物奚存？邁成周洛水莅師，家邦永保。九關聲震龍沙，寢西北妖氛；百粤威騰鯨海，澄東南蜃氣。允矣，熈朝盛事！誠哉，奕世彜章！
臣等學慙博古，旣俎豆之無聞；志切籌邊，恨韜鈐之未識。幾年竭股肱之力，惟有赤心；小技同腹背之毛，何裨實用？骨非將種，敢妄希投筆之封？腹鮮甲兵，徒留意徙戎之論。經營重寄分心膂，恐負躬逢；訓練強兵動鬼神，何期目覩！伏願軫山濤外懼之慮，抱賈生全盛之虞。思內憂方可外寧，任老成而補廷中之衮；念選兵不如選將，簡謀勇而寄閫
translation_en:
…Rewards were distributed, and rejoicing shook the earth’s axis. The grand ceremony was completed at the magnificent ramparts, offering an auspicious sign that bows would be put away in their cases. The imperial carriage swiftly returned to the Pure Capital: Your Majesty’s intention was not to flaunt military might. How paltry was the Han ruler’s hunting review at Changyang—what proper standards did it preserve? Surpassing even the Zhou king’s review of the army by the Luo River, this ensures the lasting security of the dynasty and realm. The might of the nine gates resounds through the Longsha desert, stilling the sinister vapors of the northwest; imperial power rises across the whale-filled seas of the many Yue lands, clearing the mirage vapors of the southeast. Truly, this is a splendid event of our flourishing dynasty! Indeed, it is a constant standard for successive generations!
We, your servants, are ashamed that our learning falls short of broad knowledge of antiquity: we have gained no distinction in matters of ritual vessels and observances. Our aspirations are earnestly directed toward planning the frontier’s defense, yet we regret our ignorance of military strategy. For years we have exhausted our strength as Your Majesty’s limbs, possessing only loyal hearts. Our meager skills resemble the hair on belly and back—what practical use can they serve? We are not born of a line of generals: how could we presumptuously hope to cast aside the writing brush and win enfeoffment? With little military knowledge within us, we merely give thought to the discourse on relocating the Rong peoples. Entrusted with weighty responsibilities for managing affairs and sharing Your Majesty’s burdens as trusted aides, we fear failing the opportunity we have personally encountered. That we should witness troops trained to such strength as to move ghosts and spirits—how could we have expected it!
We humbly pray that Your Majesty take to heart Shan Tao’s concern about external dangers and cherish Master Jia’s apprehensions even at the height of prosperity. Reflect that only by attending to internal troubles can peace abroad be secured; employ mature and experienced men to mend the imperial robe at court. Remember that selecting soldiers is less important than selecting generals; choose men of strategic wisdom and courage, and entrust them with command beyond the military gate…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
外之權
握金鏡於鸞門光遍五千之禹服
偃銅符於鶴仗風清百二之秦關臣等無任
瞻
天仰
聖懽忭踴躍之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
===
第叄塲
策五道
第一問
楊佩訓
同考試官敎諭趙批敷陳敬
天勤民取譬子之事父父之保子意甚明切至末歸重勤民爲敬
天之本尤見忠愛
同考試官敎諭王批我
皇上舉行曠典昭示臣民蓋尚實而非尚文也此作敷厲揄揚中恭
punctuated:
外之權。握金鏡於鸞門，光遍五千之禹服；偃銅符於鶴仗，風清百二之秦關。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、懽忭踴躍之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。

第叄塲
策五道
第一問
楊佩訓

同考試官敎諭趙批：敷陳敬天勤民，取譬子之事父、父之保子，意甚明切。至末歸重勤民爲敬天之本，尤見忠愛。

同考試官敎諭王批：我皇上舉行曠典，昭示臣民，蓋尚實而非尚文也。此作敷厲揄揚中恭
translation_en:
…authority beyond the court. Hold the golden mirror at the phoenix gate, its radiance extending throughout the five-thousand-li domains ordered by Yu; lay the bronze military tallies to rest amid the crane-bannered imperial guard, bringing tranquil breezes to the passes of Qin, where two can withstand a hundred. We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sagely Majesty with boundless joy and exultation. We respectfully submit this memorial of congratulation for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question
Yang Peixun

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: The exposition of reverence for Heaven and diligent care for the people uses the analogies of a son serving his father and a father protecting his son. Its meaning is very clear and pertinent. At the end, it places particular weight on diligent care for the people as the foundation of reverence for Heaven, showing especially clearly the author’s loyalty and loving concern.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: Our Emperor has performed an exceptional ceremony and made it manifest to his officials and people: surely he prizes substance rather than ornament. Amid its expansive exposition and praise, this composition respectfully…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
獻誠悃其知探本之論異日必不負所學者耶
考試官敎授夏批條答婉盡
考試官敎授帥批敷對根據發揮典暢可取
帝王一身上爲天之元子是故有昭事之
道焉知事親則知所以事天矣下爲民之
父母是故有懷保之道焉知保子則知所
以保民矣人之於親非不實敦牟以羞之
撰席衽以隨之也而心則有出於是者承
其志而形聲耳目之不違體其意而膚髮
===
樹木之必愛夫豈僞爲於笑貌哉一實心
之形耳帝王事天何以異此人之於子非
不時戒諭以勸之躬勞瘁以率之也而心
則有出於是者圖其安而第宅絲粟之必
周防其疾而箴石湯爇之必庀夫豈僞爲
於笑貌哉一實心之形耳帝王保民何以
異此事天在敬保民在勤無其實有其文
是所以事親者不過敦牟之滑甘席衽之
趾向而已所以保子者不過戒諭之諄諄
punctuated:
獻誠悃，其知探本之論，異日必不負所學者耶！

考試官敎授夏批：條答婉盡。

考試官敎授帥批：敷對根據，發揮典暢，可取。

帝王一身，上爲天之元子，是故有昭事之道焉，知事親則知所以事天矣；下爲民之父母，是故有懷保之道焉，知保子則知所以保民矣。人之於親，非不實敦牟以羞之、撰席衽以隨之也，而心則有出於是者：承其志，而形聲耳目之不違；體其意，而膚髮樹木之必愛。夫豈僞爲於笑貌哉？一實心之形耳。帝王事天，何以異此？人之於子，非不時戒諭以勸之、躬勞瘁以率之也，而心則有出於是者：圖其安，而第宅絲粟之必周；防其疾，而箴石湯爇之必庀。夫豈僞爲於笑貌哉？一實心之形耳。帝王保民，何以異此？事天在敬，保民在勤。無其實，有其文，是所以事親者不過敦牟之滑甘、席衽之趾向而已；所以保子者不過戒諭之諄諄
translation_en:
…offers sincere devotion. In his argument he knows how to seek out the root; surely in days to come he will not betray what he has learned!

Examiner Xia, an Instructor, comments: “The answers to the individual points are tactful and thorough.”

Examiner Shuai, an Instructor, comments: “The response is well grounded, and its exposition is dignified and fluent. It merits acceptance.”

In his own person, the emperor is, above, Heaven’s eldest son; hence there is a way of serving Heaven with manifest reverence. Knowing how to serve one’s parents, one knows how to serve Heaven. Below, he is father and mother to the people; hence there is a way of cherishing and protecting them. Knowing how to protect one’s children, one knows how to protect the people.

In serving their parents, people certainly fill the food vessels to offer them nourishment and arrange their mats and bedding to attend to their needs. Yet the heart goes beyond these things: carrying out their parents’ wishes, they allow neither their demeanor and speech nor their hearing and sight to run counter to them; understanding their parents’ intentions, they cherish their own skin and hair and even the trees their parents planted. Could this possibly be a pretense put on in smiles and outward appearance? It is simply the manifestation of a sincere heart. How could an emperor’s service to Heaven differ from this?

In caring for their children, people certainly admonish and instruct them at appropriate times to encourage them, and personally endure toil and exhaustion to lead them by example. Yet the heart goes beyond these things: planning for their comfort, they ensure that housing, clothing, and grain are fully provided; guarding against illness, they make ready needles, stone lancets, decoctions, and heat treatments [?]. Could this possibly be a pretense put on in smiles and outward appearance? It is simply the manifestation of a sincere heart. How could an emperor’s protection of the people differ from this?

Serving Heaven rests on reverence; protecting the people rests on diligence. If there is outward form without substance, then serving one’s parents amounts merely to providing rich and sweet foods in vessels and attending to the positioning of their feet on mats and bedding [?]; protecting one’s children amounts merely to repeated admonitions and instructions…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
勞瘁之悁悁而已而曰我爲孝子我爲慈
父豈不妄哉知此則我
祖宗之所以
敬天勤民與我
皇上之所以承
休光
訓可得敷揚其實矣詩曰時邁其邦昊天其
子之則夫敬以事之子道宜爾而莫大於
郊祀記曰因名山升中於天因吉土饗帝
===
于郊蓋言敬也是故因丘掃地尚其質也
陶匏藁鞂象其性也疏布素車尊其樸也
鎮圭繅藉重其事也五采五就繁其飾也
龍旂日月明其道也黃鍾大呂極其變也
大裘龍袞備其物也豈徒以文已乎書曰
元后作民父母則夫勤以保之父道宜爾
而莫大於耕藉記曰孟春之月乃擇元辰
親載耒耜帥公卿諸侯大夫躬耕於南郊
蓋言勤也是故覘土省脈以若利也占正
punctuated: 勞瘁之悁悁而已，而曰「我爲孝子，我爲慈父」，豈不妄哉？知此，則我祖宗之所以敬天勤民，與我皇上之所以承休光訓，可得敷揚其實矣。《詩》曰：「時邁其邦，昊天其子之。」則夫敬以事之，子道宜爾，而莫大於郊祀。《記》曰：「因名山升中於天，因吉土饗帝于郊。」蓋言敬也。是故因丘掃地，尚其質也；陶匏藁鞂，象其性也；疏布素車，尊其樸也；鎮圭繅藉，重其事也；五采五就，繁其飾也；龍旂日月，明其道也；黃鍾大呂，極其變也；大裘龍袞，備其物也。豈徒以文已乎？《書》曰：「元后作民父母。」則夫勤以保之，父道宜爾，而莫大於耕藉。《記》曰：「孟春之月，乃擇元辰，親載耒耜，帥公卿諸侯大夫，躬耕於南郊。」蓋言勤也。是故覘土省脈，以若利也；占正
translation_en:
…and merely anxious exertion. Yet to say, “I am a filial son; I am a loving father”—would this not be presumptuous? Understanding this, we can expound the substance of how our imperial ancestors revered Heaven and labored for the people, and how our present emperor carries forward their blessed and glorious instructions [?]. The Book of Odes says: “He makes timely tours of his states; august Heaven treats him as its son.” To serve Heaven reverently is thus fitting conduct for a son, and nothing is more important than the suburban sacrifice. The Book of Rites says: “At famous mountains, one ascends to report achievements to Heaven; on auspicious ground, one offers sacrifice to the Supreme Lord in the suburbs.” This speaks of reverence. Thus, using a hill and sweeping the ground esteems simplicity; earthenware vessels, gourd vessels, and straw mats embody natural qualities; coarse cloth and an unadorned carriage honor plainness; the guardian jade tablet and its patterned silk pad give weight to the occasion; the five colors and fivefold ornamentation enrich its adornment; dragon banners bearing the sun and moon make manifest its Way; the Huangzhong and Dalü musical pitches bring its variations to their fullest expression; and the great fur robe and dragon-patterned ceremonial robe complete its ritual furnishings. Could these be merely matters of outward form?

The Book of Documents says: “The sovereign acts as father and mother to the people.” To protect them diligently is thus fitting conduct for a father, and nothing is more important than plowing the ritual field. The Book of Rites says: “In the first month of spring, an auspicious day is chosen. The ruler personally carries the plowing implements in his carriage and leads the Three Dukes, Nine Ministers, regional lords, and grand masters in plowing in person in the southern suburbs.” This speaks of diligence. Thus, inspecting the soil and examining its veins accords with favorable conditions; divining the proper…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
告協以順時也卽齋祗祓以昭休也薦鬯
薦醴以致潔也第胙序班以明帥也陳饗
散牢以逮勞也廩籍鍾藏以登入也遍徇
紀功以播勸也豈徒以文已乎三代以還
斯道不暢非無英辟未有殊尤絕迹可見
於今者也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝神武開基
世宗肅皇帝光華紹統
天德高明
===
聖學純邃孜孜三重因革百王相後先而典
禮大備焉洪武元年首
定祀
天圜丘祀
地方丘之禮十年感京房之說而始合嘉靖間
從言官之請而又分彬彬乎其竝盛哉今
繹思之其合也謂父母共牢而食也其分
也謂陰陽以類而求也義各有攸取矣洪
武元年首
punctuated:
告協以順時也，卽齋祗祓以昭休也，薦鬯薦醴以致潔也，第胙序班以明帥也，陳饗散牢以逮勞也，廩籍鍾藏以登入也，遍徇紀功以播勸也。豈徒以文已乎？三代以還，斯道不暢，非無英辟，未有殊尤絕迹可見於今者也。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝神武開基，世宗肅皇帝光華紹統，天德高明，聖學純邃，孜孜三重，因革百王，相後先而典禮大備焉。洪武元年，首定祀天圜丘、祀地方丘之禮。十年，感京房之說而始合；嘉靖間，從言官之請而又分。彬彬乎其竝盛哉！今繹思之，其合也，謂父母共牢而食也；其分也，謂陰陽以類而求也。義各有攸取矣。洪武元年，首
translation_en:
… announcing a favorable concurrence, thereby conforming to the proper season; entering ritual abstinence and reverently undergoing purification, thereby manifesting auspiciousness; presenting aromatic sacrificial wine and sweet wine, thereby achieving purity; ranking the portions of sacrificial meat and ordering the ranks, thereby making leadership manifest; setting out feasts and distributing sacrificial animals, thereby extending recompense to those who have labored; storing the produce of the imperial ploughing field in granaries [?], thereby bringing in the harvest; and making proclamations everywhere and recording achievements, thereby spreading encouragement. Could these things be merely outward embellishment? Since the Three Dynasties, this Way has not flourished. There have indeed been illustrious rulers, but none whose outstanding and unsurpassed achievements remain visible today.
We profoundly reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the dynasty through his divine martial prowess, and Emperor Shizong Su gloriously succeeded to its rule. Their heavenly virtue was lofty and luminous, their sagely learning pure and profound. Diligently attending to the three weighty matters of government, they retained or altered the institutions of the many kings of antiquity. Following one another, they brought ceremonial institutions to full completion. In the first year of Hongwu, rites were first established for sacrificing to Heaven at the Round Mound and to Earth at the Square Mound. In the tenth year, inspired by Jing Fang’s explanation, the sacrifices were first combined. During the Jiajing reign, they were separated again in response to a request from remonstrance officials. How splendidly both arrangements flourished! Reflecting on them now, combining the sacrifices meant that father and mother shared the same sacrificial offering at their meal; separating them meant that yin and yang were approached according to their respective kinds. Each arrangement thus had its own grounds in principle. In the first year of Hongwu, first …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
定耕籍田享先農之禮八年罷
仁祖之配嘉靖中申歲祭之典秩秩乎其繼美
哉今繹思之初上祀後中祀非略也初有
配後無配非簡也義固殺於
郊矣然而
敬勤之實則不盡於是者
太祖勅禮官議
郊曰聖帝明王嚴於祭祀内致誠敬外致儀文
諒哉諒哉愚嘗竊窺其實於文之外矣
===
謹巳答眷示艱難於去疾
脩人合道語類應於存仁水旱
懼刑罰失中災異
慮聞奏匪實
藁席草履不縠於監門
捧榼進蔬實勞於韋布他如
謨猷經紀
號令文章何者非
敬天之實也奚但籩豆享薦之豐齊明儼恪之
punctuated:
定耕籍田、享先農之禮，八年罷仁祖之配。嘉靖中申歲祭之典，秩秩乎其繼美哉！今繹思之，初上祀，後中祀，非略也；初有配，後無配，非簡也。義固殺於郊矣。然而敬勤之實，則不盡於是者。太祖勅禮官議郊曰：「聖帝明王嚴於祭祀，内致誠敬，外致儀文。」諒哉！諒哉！愚嘗竊窺其實於文之外矣。

謹巳答眷，示艱難於去疾；脩人合道，語類應於存仁。水旱，懼刑罰失中；災異，慮聞奏匪實。藁席草履，不縠於監門；捧榼進蔬，實勞於韋布。他如謨猷經紀、號令文章，何者非敬天之實也？奚但籩豆享薦之豐、齊明儼恪之
translation_en:
…established the rites for plowing the imperial field and sacrificing to the First Farmer. In the eighth year of Hongwu, the associated worship of Renzu was discontinued. During the Jiajing era, the regulations for annual sacrifices were reaffirmed. How orderly was this continuation of the splendid precedent! Reflecting on this now: the rite was initially a major sacrifice and later a medium sacrifice, but this was no neglect; initially there was an associated recipient of worship and later none, but this was no undue simplification. Its proper ritual standing was indeed below that of the suburban sacrifices. Yet the substance of reverence and diligence was not exhausted by these arrangements. When Taizu commanded the ritual officials to deliberate on the suburban sacrifices, he said: “Sage emperors and enlightened kings are exacting in their sacrifices: inwardly they perfect sincerity and reverence; outwardly they perfect ceremonial forms.” How true! How true! I have ventured to discern their substance beyond their outward forms.

By guarding his own conduct, he requited Heaven’s favor, explaining the hardships to Quji [?]; by cultivating human affairs in accordance with the Way, he spoke similarly in response to Cunren [?]. When floods or droughts occurred, he feared that punishments had missed the proper balance; when calamities and anomalies appeared, he worried that reports submitted to him were untrue. With straw mats and straw sandals, he acted thus toward the gatekeeper [?]; carrying a food vessel and presenting vegetables, he personally exerted himself for men in plain cloth. As for his plans and arrangements, his commands and writings—which of these was not a substantive expression of reverence for Heaven? How could this consist merely in the abundance of offerings presented in bamboo and wooden vessels, or in the purity, solemnity, and reverence of …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
秉哉
列聖相傳率由兹典
世宗纘緒
郊祀維新此
欽天記頌所爲述也是故
祈報重於春秋
禱祠切於暵溢一霾示儆脩省惟虔一隅告
祲驅除惟駛皇皇乎
敬天之實真與
===
太祖同揆者乎
太祖諭羣臣曰耕籍古禮也朕即位以來恒舉
行之惟欲使民盡力於田畝以遂生養非事
虛文也諒哉諒哉愚甞竊窺其實於文之外
矣
蠲租之詔歲下重其責於有司
種樹之令時申課其數於計吏
導太子歷田家之苦
命茂才專水利之司
punctuated:
秉哉！
列聖相傳，率由兹典。世宗纘緒，郊祀維新，此《欽天記頌》所爲述也。是故祈報重於春秋，禱祠切於暵溢。一霾示儆，脩省惟虔；一隅告祲，驅除惟駛。皇皇乎！敬天之實，真與太祖同揆者乎！
太祖諭羣臣曰：「耕籍，古禮也。朕即位以來，恒舉行之，惟欲使民盡力於田畝，以遂生養，非事虛文也。」諒哉！諒哉！愚甞竊窺其實於文之外矣。蠲租之詔歲下，重其責於有司；種樹之令時申，課其數於計吏；導太子歷田家之苦，命茂才專水利之司。
translation_en:
…the disposition maintained!

Successive sage emperors transmitted this tradition, all following these established rites. Shizong succeeded to the imperial line and renewed the suburban sacrifices to Heaven. This is what the Record and Eulogy of Reverence for Heaven (Qintian ji song) recounts. Thus prayers for blessings and offerings of thanksgiving received particular emphasis in spring and autumn, while supplications and sacrifices became especially urgent during droughts and floods. Whenever a haze gave warning, he cultivated himself and examined his conduct with utmost reverence; whenever an ominous influence was reported from any quarter, he hastened to dispel it. How magnificent! In the substance of his reverence for Heaven, did he not truly follow the same principles as Taizu?

Taizu instructed his assembled ministers: “Ploughing the ritual field is an ancient rite. Since ascending the throne, I have regularly performed it, solely because I wish the people to devote their efforts fully to their fields and thereby secure their livelihood and sustenance—not to pursue empty ceremony.” How true! How true! I, in my ignorance, have ventured to discern the substance beyond the outward forms. Each year he issued edicts remitting land taxes, laying a weighty responsibility upon the responsible officials. He repeatedly renewed orders for planting trees, holding accounting officials accountable for the numbers planted. He led the crown prince to experience the hardships of farming households and appointed men of outstanding ability to take special charge of water management.…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
恤刑而喻施鋤良苗必謹
賑歉而譬待哺惸獨恒先他如
品式綱維
裁成疆理何者非
勤民之實也奚但憤盈滿眚之觀震渝淳濯
之飭哉
列聖相承式遵
前烈
世宗臨御
===
耕籍聿脩此
祗穀先蠶壇所繼賦也是故亭殿構嚴於
太內薅刈心警於
豫遊
免稅勸農開其源於衣食
發帑施藥軫其念於顛連
矜憫無辜屢頒欽恤之詔
慎評庶職特嚴貪虐之條燁燁乎
勤民之實真與
punctuated:
恤刑而喻施鋤，良苗必謹；賑歉而譬待哺，惸獨恒先。他如品式綱維，裁成疆理，何者非勤民之實也？奚但憤盈滿眚之觀、震渝淳濯之飭哉？
列聖相承，式遵前烈。世宗臨御，耕籍聿脩，此祗穀先蠶壇所繼賦也。是故亭殿構嚴於太內，薅刈心警於豫遊；免稅勸農，開其源於衣食；發帑施藥，軫其念於顛連；矜憫無辜，屢頒欽恤之詔；慎評庶職，特嚴貪虐之條。燁燁乎！勤民之實，真與
translation_en:
…In showing compassion in punishment, he used the analogy of hoeing: good seedlings must be carefully protected. In relieving famine, he likened the hungry to those awaiting food, always giving priority to the bereft and solitary. Other measures included establishing standards and maintaining order, and defining and regulating territorial boundaries. Which of these was not a concrete expression of care for the people? How could this have consisted merely in displays of anger at arrogance and warnings that fullness brings calamity, or injunctions to reform through fear and cleanse oneself thoroughly [?]?
Successive sage emperors followed one another, taking the meritorious achievements of their predecessors as their model. When Shizong occupied the throne, he renewed the rite of plowing the imperial field. This was what the composition on the Altars of Reverence for Grain and the First Silkworm continued to celebrate [?]. Thus, while imposing pavilions and halls were built within the imperial palace, even during his leisurely excursions his mind remained alert to the labors of weeding and harvesting. By remitting taxes and encouraging agriculture, he opened up the sources of clothing and food; by releasing treasury funds and dispensing medicines, he showed his concern for those in distress. Pitying the innocent, he repeatedly issued decrees enjoining reverent care in administering punishments. Carefully assessing officials in their various posts, he made the provisions against corruption and oppression especially strict. How resplendent! These concrete expressions of care for the people truly accorded with …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
太祖同符者乎夫其
肇統握符隆升廣被若彼而
紹光闡繹昭登淪洽若此是以
玄祉繁昌黔心闓懌
聿懷之福保受於無疆
丕冒之治蟠極而不替也肆我
皇上嗣服凝圖他務未遑首郊
上帝先是嚴飈振威陰雲翳空凜乎栗矣至期
和氣暄煦星月輝爛風伯清塵雲師斂靄
===
何以故哉
聖敬潛孚
天心孚佑炳炳乎其不爽也迨
耕南甸
三推肇加千畝俶載希乎覯矣然而髦士承
旂都民驤首閭閻歡而動地耒耜奮而彌
野何以故哉
湛恩洪龐
休烈液洽奕奕乎其莫競也然而
punctuated:
太祖同符者乎！夫其肇統握符，隆升廣被若彼，而紹光闡繹，昭登淪洽若此，是以玄祉繁昌，黔心闓懌，聿懷之福保受於無疆，丕冒之治蟠極而不替也。肆我皇上嗣服凝圖，他務未遑，首郊上帝。先是，嚴飈振威，陰雲翳空，凜乎栗矣。至期，和氣暄煦，星月輝爛，風伯清塵，雲師斂靄。何以故哉？聖敬潛孚，天心孚佑，炳炳乎其不爽也。

迨耕南甸，三推肇加，千畝俶載，希乎覯矣。然而髦士承旂，都民驤首，閭閻歡而動地，耒耜奮而彌野。何以故哉？湛恩洪龐，休烈液洽，奕奕乎其莫競也。然而
translation_en:
…truly accords with Taizu! His founding of the dynastic succession and grasping of the mandate rose to such heights and spread so widely; the continuation of his glory and unfolding of his legacy have shone forth and penetrated so thoroughly. Thus blessings from Heaven flourish abundantly, and the hearts of the common people rejoice. Blessings that draw the people close are preserved and received without limit, while a government that shelters all extends to the furthest bounds and never declines. Now Our Emperor has succeeded to the throne and secured the dynastic enterprise. Before attending to other affairs, he first offered the suburban sacrifice to the Supreme Lord. Beforehand, fierce winds displayed their might, and dark clouds obscured the sky: how chilling and fearful it was! When the appointed time arrived, the air was mild and warm, the stars and moon shone brilliantly, the Wind Earl swept away the dust, and the Cloud Master gathered in the mist. Why was this so? His Majesty’s reverence silently inspired trust, and Heaven’s heart faithfully bestowed its protection. How manifestly this response proved unfailing!

When he came to plough the southern fields, he began by pushing the plough three times, inaugurating work on the thousand-mu field—a rare sight indeed! Distinguished scholars followed the banners, and the capital’s people craned their necks. The rejoicing of the neighborhoods shook the earth, and ploughs were vigorously wielded throughout the fields. Why was this so? His profound beneficence was vast and abundant, and the influence of his splendid achievements spread everywhere. How glorious and beyond all rivalry it was! Yet…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
皇上方覽三五之鴻猷弘
祖宗之茂實
順四時
調三光
恤鰥寡
存孤獨
起滯亨屯
鼎新革故邇因
京輔旱澇屢
===
勅羣臣省禱河夫之艱京商之困
特加惠焉仰覩
敬勤之實殆如子之於親承其志體其意父之
於子圖其安防其疾不徒笑貌為者此
太祖
世宗之所以格
上下而被四表也將使淳和益鬯
眷渥彌崇偕覆載以常新保億兆于永固矣而
執事謂郊籍大典也惟
punctuated: 皇上方覽三五之鴻猷，弘祖宗之茂實，順四時，調三光，恤鰥寡，存孤獨，起滯亨屯，鼎新革故。邇因京輔旱澇，屢勅羣臣省禱。河夫之艱、京商之困，特加惠焉。仰覩敬勤之實，殆如子之於親，承其志，體其意；父之於子，圖其安，防其疾，不徒笑貌為者。此太祖、世宗之所以格上下而被四表也。將使淳和益鬯，眷渥彌崇，偕覆載以常新，保億兆于永固矣。而執事謂郊籍大典也，惟
translation_en: … His Majesty is now contemplating the grand designs of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors and extending the substantial achievements of his imperial ancestors. He accords with the four seasons, harmonizes the three luminaries, cares for widowers and widows, sustains orphans and the solitary, raises up those whose advancement has stalled, brings relief to those in adversity, and institutes renewal by reforming the old. Recently, because of droughts and floods in the capital region, he repeatedly commanded his ministers to examine their conduct and offer prayers. He bestowed particular favors to relieve the hardships of river laborers and the distress of merchants in the capital. Looking reverently upon these concrete manifestations of reverence and diligence, we see something akin to a son’s relationship with his parents: carrying forward their aspirations and entering into their intentions; or a father’s relationship with his children: planning for their security and guarding against their ailments. These are not merely outward displays of smiles and demeanor. It was through this that Taizu and Shizong reached Heaven above and Earth below and extended their influence to the four extremities. His Majesty will cause pure harmony to flow still more freely and gracious favor to grow still more abundant, renewing them continually alongside Heaven, which covers, and Earth, which sustains, and securing lasting stability for the countless multitudes. Yet you, honored examiner, say that the suburban sacrifices and the ceremonial ploughing are great rites, and that only …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
盛德之君能行之愚則以為知本焉書曰德盛
不狎侮不狎侮則敬故能敬
天口代天言罔不臧也身代天事罔不欽也天
有日月法其明以理萬幾天有雨露法其
恩以澤萬民天有雷霆法其威以懾羣慝
無鉅無小不敢馳驅而
天無不敬矣書曰懋德無時逸豫不逸豫則勤
故能勤民民之饑猶巳饑之也民之溺猶
巳溺之也生養未遂導民以遂之倫理未
===
明敎民以明之爭奪未息治民以息之勞
心焦思不敢遑暇而民無不勤矣
皇上春秋鼎盛
德將日新
業將日大有不弘裕矣乎愚也何知同億兆
之民囿
覆載之中而日鼓舞焉耳烏能揚厲萬一哉雖
然天視自我民視天聽自我民聽勤民又
敬天之本也夫天之愛民甚矣民安則天心悅
punctuated:
盛德之君能行之，愚則以為知本焉。《書》曰：「德盛不狎侮。」不狎侮則敬，故能敬天。口代天言，罔不臧也；身代天事，罔不欽也。天有日月，法其明以理萬幾；天有雨露，法其恩以澤萬民；天有雷霆，法其威以懾羣慝。無鉅無小，不敢馳驅，而天無不敬矣。《書》曰：「懋德無時逸豫。」不逸豫則勤，故能勤民。民之饑，猶巳饑之也；民之溺，猶巳溺之也。生養未遂，導民以遂之；倫理未明，敎民以明之；爭奪未息，治民以息之。勞心焦思，不敢遑暇，而民無不勤矣。
皇上春秋鼎盛，德將日新，業將日大，有不弘裕矣乎？愚也何知？同億兆之民囿覆載之中，而日鼓舞焉耳，烏能揚厲萬一哉？雖然，天視自我民視，天聽自我民聽，勤民又敬天之本也。夫天之愛民甚矣，民安則天心悅，
translation_en:
…a sovereign of abundant virtue can carry them out; in my humble view, this means understanding the root. The Book of Documents says: “When virtue is abundant, there is no contemptuous treatment of others.” To refrain from contempt is to be reverent, and thus one can revere Heaven. Speaking on Heaven’s behalf, one says nothing that is not good; acting on Heaven’s behalf, one does nothing without reverence. Heaven has the sun and moon: one emulates their brightness in managing the myriad affairs of government. Heaven has rain and dew: one emulates its bounty in benefiting all the people. Heaven has thunder: one emulates its majesty in overawing the hosts of evildoers. In matters great and small, one dares not act impetuously [?], and thus reveres Heaven in every respect. The Book of Documents says: “Exert yourself in virtue; at no time indulge in ease.” To shun ease is to be diligent, and thus one can labor diligently for the people. When the people hunger, it is as though one had caused their hunger; when they drown, it is as though one had caused their drowning. Where their livelihood and nurture remain unfulfilled, guide them toward fulfillment; where ethical relationships remain unclear, teach them to understand; where contention and strife persist, govern them so as to bring these to an end. Exerting one’s mind and taxing one’s thoughts, one dares not take leisure, and thus labors for the people in every respect.
His Majesty is in the prime of life. His virtue will be renewed daily, and his achievements will grow daily: how could these fail to become vast and abundant? What do I, in my ignorance, know? Together with the countless millions of the people, I dwell within the embrace of Heaven and Earth, rejoicing day after day—that is all. How could I extol even one ten-thousandth of his accomplishments? Nevertheless, “Heaven sees through what our people see; Heaven hears through what our people hear.” Diligent care for the people is itself the root of reverence for Heaven. Heaven’s love for the people is indeed profound. When the people are at peace, Heaven’s heart is pleased…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
而順氣達焉弗安則天心慍而戾氣應焉
正如親之憂喜一隨子之苦樂是故孝子
事親愛而愛之敬而敬之何者志意之所
存也今夫第宅絲粟父母所以貽其子也
子有堂室甘毳父母不沾沾然喜哉人君
於民敦素儉節嗜欲戒竭澤之漁使民阜
於其財凡以祈天之我悅也箴石湯焫父
母所以防其子也子有疾痛疴癢父母不
戚戚然憂哉人君於民守鎮靜慎興作監
===
東野之御使民足於其力凡以祈天之不
我慍也是故聖王之治天不愛道地不愛
寶休徵嘉祥輝映瑶簡無他民心之所感
也書曰欲王以小民受天永命敢以是爲
當宁獻
第二問
陳瑛
同考試官教諭許批教儲之法莫詳于賈誼
之書子能誦述
punctuated:
而順氣達焉；弗安，則天心慍而戾氣應焉。正如親之憂喜，一隨子之苦樂。是故孝子事親，愛而愛之，敬而敬之。何者？志意之所存也。今夫第宅絲粟，父母所以貽其子也。子有堂室甘毳，父母不沾沾然喜哉？人君於民，敦素儉，節嗜欲，戒竭澤之漁，使民阜於其財，凡以祈天之我悅也。箴石湯焫，父母所以防其子也。子有疾痛疴癢，父母不戚戚然憂哉？人君於民，守鎮靜，慎興作，監東野之御，使民足於其力，凡以祈天之不我慍也。是故聖王之治，天不愛道，地不愛寶，休徵嘉祥，輝映瑶簡。無他，民心之所感也。《書》曰：「欲王以小民受天永命。」敢以是爲當宁獻。
第二問
陳瑛
同考試官教諭許批：教儲之法，莫詳于賈誼之書。子能誦述
translation_en:
…and harmonious vital forces circulate. When the people are not at peace, Heaven’s heart is angered, and baleful forces respond. This is just like parents, whose sorrow and joy follow entirely their children’s suffering and happiness. Thus, in serving his parents, a filial son loves what they love and respects what they respect. Why? Because these are the objects of their hearts and intentions. Houses, silk, and grain are what parents leave to their children. When their children have dwellings, fine food, and soft clothing, are the parents not filled with delight? In governing the people, the ruler promotes simplicity and frugality, restrains his appetites and desires, and guards against fishing by draining the marsh dry, enabling the people to enjoy abundant resources. All this is to seek Heaven’s pleasure in him. Needles, medicinal stones, decoctions, and moxibustion are the means by which parents safeguard their children. When their children suffer sickness, pain, ailments, or itching, are the parents not deeply distressed? In governing the people, the ruler maintains tranquillity, exercises caution in undertaking projects, and takes warning from Dongye’s handling of his horses, ensuring that the people retain sufficient strength. All this is to seek freedom from Heaven’s anger toward him. Thus, under the rule of sage kings, Heaven does not withhold its Way, nor Earth its treasures; favorable signs and auspicious portents shine forth in the precious records. There is no other cause: they are responses elicited by the hearts of the people. The Book of Documents says: “May the king, through the common people, receive Heaven’s enduring mandate.” I venture to offer this to Your Majesty.
Second Question
Chen Ying 陳瑛
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: No book sets out methods for educating the heir apparent more fully than that of Jia Yi. You are able to recite and expound it…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
憲章裨助講讀是有賈生之志者
同考試官教諭朱批敷對明切末以身法家法爲
獻忠愛可錄
考試官教授夏批條答詳悉忠愛藹然
考試官教授師批敷對詳明詞意懇到
帝王有以衍萬世之鴻圖必有以培天下
之大本大本者天命之所凝承人心之所
繫屬其關於天下萬世至重也是以聖王
重之豫爲訓迪之方慎其輔導之選俾青
===
宮之中前後左右莫非正人學習聽聞無
非正事則薰陶涵育緝熙光明敦元良之
體具知臨之宜所以聯天人之交紹神明
之統衍億萬載無疆之休者端在是矣今
夫萬彙之生莫不有本本培而後能固固
然後凝然懋樹而況太子者天下之本也
神器賴以附屬社稷賴以奠安豈非帝王
之所慎重者哉昔漢賈誼最號通達國體
上書漢文曰太子之善在於早諭教與選
punctuated:
憲章，裨助講讀，是有賈生之志者。

同考試官教諭朱批：敷對明切，末以身法、家法爲獻，忠愛可錄。

考試官教授夏批：條答詳悉，忠愛藹然。

考試官教授師批：敷對詳明，詞意懇到。

帝王有以衍萬世之鴻圖，必有以培天下之大本。大本者，天命之所凝承，人心之所繫屬，其關於天下萬世至重也。是以聖王重之，豫爲訓迪之方，慎其輔導之選，俾青宮之中，前後左右，莫非正人，學習聽聞，無非正事。則薰陶涵育，緝熙光明，敦元良之體，具知臨之宜，所以聯天人之交，紹神明之統，衍億萬載無疆之休者，端在是矣。今夫萬彙之生，莫不有本，本培而後能固，固然後凝然懋樹。而況太子者，天下之本也，神器賴以附屬，社稷賴以奠安，豈非帝王之所慎重者哉？昔漢賈誼最號通達國體，上書漢文曰：「太子之善，在於早諭教與選
translation_en:
…take them as guiding principles and use them to assist instruction through lectures and readings: this shows that you share Master Jia’s aspirations.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “Your response is clear and incisive. At the end you offer advice on personal conduct and the regulation of the family. Your loyalty and devotion merit recognition.”

Comment by Examiner Xia, Professor: “Your answers address the points fully and in detail, abounding in loyalty and devotion.”

Comment by Examiner Shi, Professor: “Your response is detailed and clear; its language and meaning are earnest and thorough.”

If emperors and kings are to extend their grand design through ten thousand generations, they must nurture the great foundation of the realm. This great foundation is where Heaven’s mandate is concentrated and received, and where the people’s hearts find their allegiance. Its importance to the realm throughout ten thousand generations is paramount. Thus the sage kings gave it great weight: they prepared methods of instruction in advance and carefully selected those who would assist and guide the heir. They ensured that within the crown prince’s palace, everyone before and behind him, to his left and right, was upright, and everything he studied, heard, and learned was proper. Through such formative influence and cultivation, his virtue would grow ever brighter; his character as the foremost worthy would be strengthened, and he would possess the qualities appropriate to ruling with wisdom. The means of joining Heaven and humanity, continuing the sacred succession, and extending boundless blessings through countless ages lie precisely here.

Now, of all the myriad things that live, none lacks a root. Only when its root is nurtured can it become firm; only once firm can it stand securely and flourish. How much more does this apply to the crown prince, who is the foundation of the realm! The sacred vessel of sovereignty depends on him for its continuity, and the altars of soil and grain depend on him for their stability. How could he fail to be an object of the emperors’ and kings’ utmost care? In former times, Jia Yi of the Han was especially renowned for understanding the essentials of government. title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
左右夫早諭教者養其蒙也蒙養端則聖
功成矣選左右者重其輔也輔導賢則后
德豫矣是其爲國家根本慮至深遠也甞
試言之士庶人之有家者欲其子之克家
也必孜孜俶俶教以義方弗納於邪尤擇
其才者賢者以師之友之然後其子克肖
有以保家業于不墜夫天下大器矣啻一
家而太子之所係奚啻士庶人子乎此其
爲計又當何如也三王家天下世有哲后
===
其克守成業號稱盛治者豈獨其嗣子性
質之靈異哉蓋亦有訓誨之功賢人之輔
焉是故有典有則禹之訓也伯益輔之三
風十愆湯之訓也伊尹輔之顯謨承烈文
武之訓也周召輔之此所以有敬承之啓
一德之太甲宥密之成王率循之康王卓
然稱繼世之明主而長治久安賴之矣三
代而下唐有帝範有戒子篇宋有元良述
有承華要略非不教也而鮮道德仁義之
punctuated:
左右。夫早諭教者，養其蒙也；蒙養端，則聖功成矣。選左右者，重其輔也；輔導賢，則后德豫矣。是其爲國家根本慮至深遠也。甞試言之：士庶人之有家者，欲其子之克家也，必孜孜俶俶，教以義方，弗納於邪，尤擇其才者賢者以師之友之，然後其子克肖，有以保家業于不墜。夫天下大器矣，啻一家，而太子之所係，奚啻士庶人子乎？此其爲計又當何如也？三王家天下，世有哲后。其克守成業，號稱盛治者，豈獨其嗣子性質之靈異哉？蓋亦有訓誨之功、賢人之輔焉。是故有典有則，禹之訓也，伯益輔之；三風十愆，湯之訓也，伊尹輔之；顯謨承烈，文武之訓也，周召輔之。此所以有敬承之啓、一德之太甲、宥密之成王、率循之康王，卓然稱繼世之明主，而長治久安賴之矣。

三代而下，唐有《帝範》，有《戒子篇》；宋有《元良述》，有《承華要略》。非不教也，而鮮道德仁義之
translation_en:
…those attending him. To instruct him early is to nurture him while his understanding is still unformed; if this nurture is correct, the work of forming a sage will be accomplished. To select his attendants is to attach importance to those who assist him; if his guides are worthy, his virtue as a ruler will be prepared in advance. Such concern for the foundations of the state reaches very deep and far.

Let me explain. When gentlemen and commoners with households wish their sons to sustain their families, they must labor diligently, teaching them the ways of righteousness and keeping them from straying into evil. Above all, they select talented and worthy men to serve as their teachers and companions. Only then can their sons live up to their fathers and preserve the family inheritance from decline. All under Heaven is a great vessel—merely a single household [?]—and how could the responsibilities bound up with the crown prince be merely those of a gentleman’s or commoner’s son? What planning, then, should be devoted to him?

The Three Kings made rule over All under Heaven hereditary within their houses, and enlightened sovereigns appeared generation after generation. That their successors preserved the established inheritance and won renown for flourishing government was surely not due solely to their exceptional natural endowments. It also owed much to instruction and the assistance of worthy men. Thus, having established norms and standards was the teaching of Yu, with Bo Yi providing assistance; the warnings against the three pernicious habits and ten transgressions were the teaching of Tang, with Yi Yin providing assistance; and illustrious counsels and the continuation of glorious achievements were the teaching of Kings Wen and Wu, with the Dukes of Zhou and Shao providing assistance. Hence there arose Qi, who reverently carried on his inheritance; Tai Jia, whose virtue was single-minded; King Cheng, who was magnanimous and tranquil; and King Kang, who followed established precedents. They stood out as enlightened hereditary rulers, upon whom enduring good government and lasting peace depended.

After the Three Dynasties, the Tang had the Model for Emperors (Di fan) and the Admonitions to a Son (Jie zi pian); the Song had the Account of the Heir Apparent (Yuanliang shu) and the Essentials for the Heir Apparent (Chenghua yaolüe). It was not that instruction was lacking, yet there was little in it of the Way, virtue, benevolence, and righteousness…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
實其所以教之者無其本晉置六傅漢開
博望唐闢崇賢吳延四友非不置左右也
而無啓迪箴規之益其所以輔之者非其
人毋怪乎君德之有歉而治之不古若也
何足以廑執事之問哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝龍飛淮甸統有寰宇
正位之初未遑他務首以
儲嗣爲重不令作中書令建
大本堂以處之謂教之不可不早也
===
親灑
宸翰作
儲君昭鑒錄採摭歷代帝王善可爲法惡可
爲戒者載爲一書
賜東宮以及
諸王使明治亂之故達禍福之原極其詳備
與三王之謨訓同一眞切矣又以左右之
不可不愼也
親擢勲舊兼
punctuated:
實。其所以教之者無其本。晉置六傅，漢開博望，唐闢崇賢，吳延四友，非不置左右也，而無啓迪箴規之益，其所以輔之者非其人。毋怪乎君德之有歉，而治之不古若也。何足以廑執事之問哉！
洪惟我太祖高皇帝龍飛淮甸，統有寰宇。正位之初，未遑他務，首以儲嗣爲重，不令作中書令，建大本堂以處之，謂教之不可不早也。親灑宸翰，作《儲君昭鑒錄》，採摭歷代帝王善可爲法、惡可爲戒者，載爲一書，賜東宮以及諸王，使明治亂之故，達禍福之原，極其詳備，與三王之謨訓同一眞切矣。又以左右之不可不愼也，親擢勲舊兼
translation_en:
…substance. The instruction they provided lacked its foundation. The Jin appointed six tutors; the Han opened the Bowang establishment; the Tang established Chongxian Hall; and Wu invited the Four Friends. It was not that they failed to appoint attendants, but these brought no benefit through enlightenment, admonition, or correction: those chosen to assist were not the right men. It is no wonder that the rulers’ virtue was deficient and their government fell short of antiquity. How could these examples merit the concern expressed in your question?
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao rose like a dragon in the Huai region and united all under Heaven. At the outset of his reign, before he had leisure for other affairs, he made the heir apparent his foremost concern. He did not have him serve as Director of the Secretariat, but built Daben Hall to house him, holding that his education must begin early. With his own imperial brush he composed the Record of Illuminating Examples for the Heir Apparent (Chujun zhaojian lu), selecting deeds of emperors of successive dynasties—the good that could serve as models and the evil that could serve as warnings—and compiling them into a single book. He bestowed it upon the crown prince and the princes, so that they would understand the causes of order and disorder and comprehend the origins of calamity and good fortune. Exhaustively detailed and comprehensive, it was as earnest and pertinent as the counsels and instructions of the Three Kings. Moreover, considering that the selection of attendants required the utmost care, he personally promoted longstanding meritorious servants to serve concurrently as…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
東宮官屬李善長徐達常遇春爲三少鄧愈
湯和爲諭德章溢爲賛善而又擢起居注
魏觀爲侍書選國子生王璞爲侍讀召桂
彥良爲正字皆一時之名德正士庶幾乎
益尹周召之流矣甞莊誦
太祖之諭太子有曰天子之子與公卿士庶人
之子異爾若不能正心脩德宗廟社稷有所
不保天下生靈皆受其殃可不懼哉又
諭詹同曰朕今立東宮取廷臣勳德老成兼職
===
老成舊人動有典則若新進之賢亦選擇參
用又
諭陶凱曰朕欲令省臺都督府兼東宮之職庶
父子一體君臣一心又
諭梁賢等曰朕命卿等輔導太子必先養其德
性使進於高明凡帝王之道禮樂稼穡往古
成敗之事皆當與之論說積久以化他日爲
政自然合道嗚呼大哉
皇言眞有以爲萬世子孫之法而陋漢唐宋以
punctuated:
東宮官屬，李善長、徐達、常遇春爲三少，鄧愈、湯和爲諭德，章溢爲賛善，而又擢起居注魏觀爲侍書，選國子生王璞爲侍讀，召桂彥良爲正字，皆一時之名德正士，庶幾乎益、尹、周、召之流矣。
甞莊誦太祖之諭太子，有曰：「天子之子與公卿士庶人之子異，爾若不能正心脩德，宗廟社稷有所不保，天下生靈皆受其殃，可不懼哉？」又諭詹同曰：「朕今立東宮，取廷臣勳德老成兼職。老成舊人動有典則，若新進之賢，亦選擇參用。」又諭陶凱曰：「朕欲令省臺都督府兼東宮之職，庶父子一體，君臣一心。」又諭梁賢等曰：「朕命卿等輔導太子，必先養其德性，使進於高明。凡帝王之道、禮樂稼穡、往古成敗之事，皆當與之論說，積久以化，他日爲政，自然合道。」嗚呼！大哉皇言！眞有以爲萬世子孫之法，而陋漢唐宋以
translation_en:
…as officials of the Eastern Palace: Li Shanchang, Xu Da, and Chang Yuchun served as the Three Junior Guardians; Deng Yu and Tang He as Admonishers; and Zhang Yi as Counselor. He further promoted the Imperial Diarist Wei Guan to Calligraphy Attendant, selected the National University student Wang Pu as Reader-in-waiting, and summoned Gui Yanliang to serve as Orthographer. All were upright men renowned in their day for virtue, approaching the stature of Yi, Yi Yin, and the Dukes of Zhou and Shao.
