I once reverently recited Taizu’s instructions to the crown prince, which included these words: “The son of the Son of Heaven differs from the sons of dukes, ministers, gentlemen, and commoners. If you cannot rectify your mind and cultivate virtue, the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain may not be preserved, and all living people under Heaven will suffer the calamity. Can you fail to fear this?” He also instructed Zhan Tong: “Now that I have established the Eastern Palace, I am choosing court ministers of merit, virtue, maturity, and experience to hold concurrent posts there. Mature and experienced servants follow established standards in all their actions. Worthy men newly entering service will also be selected to serve alongside them.” He further instructed Tao Kai: “I wish to have officials of the Secretariat, the Censorate, and the Chief Military Commission hold concurrent posts in the Eastern Palace, so that father and son may form one body, and ruler and ministers share one mind.” He also instructed Liang Xian and the others: “In ordering you to assist and guide the crown prince, I require you first to nurture his moral nature and lead him toward loftiness and enlightenment. The Way of emperors and kings, rites and music, sowing and reaping, and the successes and failures of antiquity—all these you should discuss and explain to him. Through sustained effort over time, he will be transformed; when he governs in the future, he will naturally accord with the Way.” Ah, how great are these imperial words! They truly provide a model for descendants through ten thousand generations, and make the Han, Tang, and Song appear inferior, as…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
不足觀者矣迨我
成祖文皇帝則有
文華寶鑑之作爰稽自古以來嘉言善行有
益於
儲敎者輯爲成書又取
皇祖昭鑒錄而增益焉
宣宗章皇帝製帝訓五十篇以示
皇太子自君德以至藥餌其目二十有五
憲宗純皇帝製文華大訓四卷以賜
===
皇太子自進學以至明治其大綱有四是三
書之旨雖有詳略而孰非
太祖訓迪儲貳之意哉
成祖於東宮之屬則選蹇義金忠丘福黃淮胡
廣等充之
宣宗於東宮之屬則選楊士奇楊榮王直王英
等充之
憲宗於東宮之屬則選彭華周經等充之是三
朝之臣雖有不同而孰非
punctuated:
不足觀者矣。迨我成祖文皇帝，則有《文華寶鑑》之作，爰稽自古以來嘉言善行有益於儲敎者，輯爲成書，又取皇祖《昭鑒錄》而增益焉。宣宗章皇帝製《帝訓》五十篇，以示皇太子，自君德以至藥餌，其目二十有五。憲宗純皇帝製《文華大訓》四卷，以賜皇太子，自進學以至明治，其大綱有四。是三書之旨，雖有詳略，而孰非太祖訓迪儲貳之意哉？
成祖於東宮之屬，則選蹇義、金忠、丘福、黃淮、胡廣等充之。宣宗於東宮之屬，則選楊士奇、楊榮、王直、王英等充之。憲宗於東宮之屬，則選彭華、周經等充之。是三朝之臣，雖有不同，而孰非
translation_en:
…unworthy of consideration. When the reign of our Emperor Chengzu Wen arrived, the Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor (Wenhua baojian) was composed. Worthy sayings and exemplary deeds from antiquity onward that would benefit the education of the heir apparent were examined and compiled into a book; the imperial ancestor’s Record of Illustrious Examples (Zhaojian lu) was also drawn upon to augment it. Emperor Xuanzong Zhang composed fifty chapters of Imperial Instructions (Dixun) to instruct the crown prince. Its twenty-five subjects ranged from the ruler’s virtue to medicines. Emperor Xianzong Chun composed the Great Instructions of Literary Splendor (Wenhua daxun) in four juan and bestowed it upon the crown prince. Its four principal divisions ranged from advancing in learning to understanding governance. Although these three books differ in their degree of detail, which does not embody Taizu’s intention to instruct and guide the heir apparent?
For the staff of the Eastern Palace, Chengzu selected Jian Yi, Jin Zhong, Qiu Fu, Huang Huai, Hu Guang, and others. Xuanzong selected Yang Shiqi, Yang Rong, Wang Zhi, Wang Ying, and others. Xianzong selected Peng Hua, Zhou Jing, and others. Although the ministers of these three reigns differed, which did not…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
太祖愼選左右之意哉是以
聖子
神孫後先繼起洪猷懿軌奕葉相輝故能祈天
永命而垂有道之長也猗歟休哉我
皇上德邁三代法宗
列祖而於燕翼之謀尤惓惓焉方今
皇太子英齡已長慧性漸開
正位東宮非若襁褓時也頃者禮臣援彞章
以出講
請
皇上俞以十齡則有就學期矣天下臣民罔不
喁喁然仰
前星而鼓舞慶麟趾而謳歌思見
睿德之成
國本之正而有以長我子孫也則夫敎
皇太子以重天下之本是誠今日之不可緩
者而進陳訓典愼選宮寮
廟廊之上當蚤有以處此矣乃執事尤欲敷
punctuated: 太祖愼選左右之意哉？是以聖子神孫，後先繼起，洪猷懿軌，奕葉相輝，故能祈天永命，而垂有道之長也。猗歟休哉！我皇上德邁三代，法宗列祖，而於燕翼之謀尤惓惓焉。方今皇太子英齡已長，慧性漸開，正位東宮，非若襁褓時也。頃者禮臣援彞章，以出講請，皇上俞以十齡，則有就學期矣。天下臣民罔不喁喁然仰前星而鼓舞，慶麟趾而謳歌，思見睿德之成、國本之正，而有以長我子孫也。則夫敎皇太子以重天下之本，是誠今日之不可緩者。而進陳訓典，愼選宮寮，廟廊之上當蚤有以處此矣。乃執事尤欲敷
translation_en:
…Taizu’s intention to choose carefully those attending him? Thus sage sons and divine grandsons succeeded one another, their grand designs and admirable precedents illuminating successive generations. Hence they could pray to Heaven for an enduring mandate and perpetuate the longevity of a dynasty possessing the Way. Ah, how glorious!

Our Emperor’s virtue surpasses that of the Three Dynasties, and he takes his imperial ancestors as his models. He is especially solicitous in planning for the welfare of his descendants. Now the Crown Prince has grown in years, and his intelligence is gradually unfolding. He occupies his proper position in the Eastern Palace and is no longer an infant in swaddling clothes. Recently, the officials responsible for rites cited established regulations in requesting that he come forth to attend lectures. The Emperor approved this for the age of ten, so a time has been set for him to begin his studies. Throughout the realm, officials and commoners eagerly gaze up at the Foremost Star—the Crown Prince—and rejoice; they celebrate the ‘qilin’s footprints,’ the auspicious imperial offspring, in song. They long to see his sagely virtue perfected and the foundation of the state set upright, thereby securing the continuance of our descendants.

Thus educating the Crown Prince, so as to give due weight to the foundation of the realm, truly admits of no delay today. As for presenting instructional canons and carefully selecting officials of the Eastern Palace, those at court ought to make provision for these matters early. Yet you, honored examiner, further wish for an exposition…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
陳以資講讀愚生竊謂教諭左右之言宋
儒朱熹甞以為萬世不易之定論則愚之
拳拳忠獻於
今日以為凝固天人之助者寧復有出於斯二
者乎然草茅一念忠愛之悃誠有不能已
者蓋諭教之道不但春誦夏絃而已
國家大政孰非當素講者乎殆必因章奏之
入
示以機宜隨日用所行
===
指其樞要諸凡四方水旱九邊夷情人物忠邪
閭閻疾苦莫不纖析而縷舉之將見
訏謨郚議日聞乎
德言
睿智聰明自成乎天性矣左右之選不但賢
士大夫而已
內廷瞽御豈非其尤切者乎又必於
東宮伴讀近侍謹擇其忠正誠直者以充如
剪桐之戲隨事箴規折柳之娛及時戒止
punctuated:
陳以資講讀，愚生竊謂教諭左右之言，宋儒朱熹甞以為萬世不易之定論。則愚之拳拳忠獻於今日，以為凝固天人之助者，寧復有出於斯二者乎？然草茅一念忠愛之悃，誠有不能已者。蓋諭教之道，不但春誦夏絃而已，國家大政，孰非當素講者乎？殆必因章奏之入，示以機宜；隨日用所行，指其樞要。諸凡四方水旱、九邊夷情、人物忠邪、閭閻疾苦，莫不纖析而縷舉之。將見訏謨郚議，日聞乎德言，睿智聰明，自成乎天性矣。

左右之選，不但賢士大夫而已，內廷瞽御，豈非其尤切者乎？又必於東宮伴讀近侍，謹擇其忠正誠直者以充。如剪桐之戲，隨事箴規；折柳之娛，及時戒止。
translation_en:
…set these matters forth to assist instruction through lectures and reading. I, an unworthy student, humbly submit that the Song scholar Zhu Xi regarded the statement concerning instruction and those attending the prince as a definitive judgment that would remain unchanged for ten thousand generations. Could the earnest, loyal counsel I offer today, to help secure the bonds between Heaven and humanity, possibly go beyond these two matters? Yet the sincere loyalty and affection of one dwelling among the common people cannot be suppressed. For instruction consists of more than recitation in spring and music in summer. Which of the great affairs of state should not be discussed beforehand? Whenever memorials come in, the prince must surely be shown the circumstances and appropriate responses; in the conduct of daily affairs, their essential points must be explained. Floods and droughts throughout the realm, conditions among the non-Chinese peoples along the Nine Frontier Commands, loyalty and wickedness in men, and the sufferings of ordinary households—all must be analyzed minutely and enumerated in detail. Then grand plans and weighty deliberations [?] will daily reach his ears through virtuous discourse, and sagacity and discernment will develop naturally from his Heaven-endowed nature.

The selection of those attending him concerns more than worthy scholar-officials. Are not the blind musicians and attendants of the inner court especially consequential? The Eastern Palace’s study companions and close attendants must also be carefully chosen for their loyalty, uprightness, sincerity, and integrity. In such play as cutting a paulownia leaf, they should offer admonition as the occasion arises; in such amusements as breaking willow branches, they should promptly caution him and put a stop to it…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
諸凡得於進講者莫不詳悉而發明之則
服習於內旣無扞格之虞而獻納於外自
覺容受之易矣雖然猶有進焉書曰王懋
昭大德建中于民以義制事以禮制心垂
裕後昆言身法也詩曰豐水有芑武王豈
不仕詒厥孫謀以燕翼子言家法也則夫
端表儀之樹弘藝極之陳嚴警覺之方立
輔翼之準亦惟人主握其機耳今我
皇上敬德日新身律聲度深宮燕閒之中潛移
默啓必有出於諭敎左右之外者豈愚生
所能仰窺其萬一哉敢以是為明問復
第三問
周良寅
同考試官敎諭王批儒者必歸本道德方為正學是篇發
得此意透徹於名實真似之間剖析詳明宜登潛心大業者耶宜錄以式
同考試官學正黃批是作品評儒術揚確古今錙兩不
爽其學識從可占矣
考試官敎授夏批議論精詳
punctuated:
諸凡得於進講者，莫不詳悉而發明之，則服習於內，旣無扞格之虞，而獻納於外，自覺容受之易矣。雖然，猶有進焉。《書》曰：「王懋昭大德，建中于民，以義制事，以禮制心，垂裕後昆。」言身法也。《詩》曰：「豐水有芑，武王豈不仕？詒厥孫謀，以燕翼子。」言家法也。則夫端表儀之樹，弘藝極之陳，嚴警覺之方，立輔翼之準，亦惟人主握其機耳。今我皇上敬德日新，身律聲度，深宮燕閒之中，潛移默啓，必有出於諭敎左右之外者，豈愚生所能仰窺其萬一哉？敢以是為明問復。
第三問
周良寅
同考試官敎諭王批：「儒者必歸本道德，方為正學。是篇發得此意透徹，於名實真似之間，剖析詳明。宜登潛心大業者耶？宜錄以式。」
同考試官學正黃批：「是作品評儒術，揚確古今，錙兩不爽，其學識從可占矣。」
考試官敎授夏批：「議論精詳。」
translation_en:
…Everything learned in the lectures should be explained fully and elucidated. Then, as he becomes accustomed to these teachings within the palace, there will be no fear of resistance; and he will naturally find it easy to accept counsel offered from outside. Yet there is a further point. The Book of Documents says: “Let the king strive to make his great virtue shine forth and establish the mean among the people; regulate affairs by righteousness and the mind by ritual propriety, leaving abundance to later descendants.” This speaks of setting an example through one’s own person. The Book of Odes says: “The Feng River has its white millet. Did King Wu not serve? He bequeathed plans to his descendants, to bring peace to and shelter his children.” This speaks of setting an example within the family. Thus, establishing an upright model of conduct, setting forth broad standards of accomplishment, making admonition and awakening rigorous, and establishing rules for guidance and support—all these depend upon the ruler’s grasp of the decisive means.
Our present Emperor reveres virtue and renews himself daily, making his own person a rule and his utterances a standard. In the leisure of the inner palace, his imperceptible influence and silent instruction must extend beyond what he expressly teaches his attendants. How could an ignorant student such as I discern even the smallest fraction of this? I venture to offer this in reply to your discerning question.
Third Policy Question
Zhou Liangyin
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “A Confucian scholar must ultimately ground himself in moral virtue for his learning to be orthodox. This essay brings out that meaning thoroughly, analyzing clearly and in detail the distinctions between name and reality, the genuine and the merely apparent. Surely he deserves advancement as one who devotes himself to the great undertaking [?]. This should be recorded as a model.”
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “This essay evaluates Confucian learning and critically weighs past and present [?], without the slightest error in the balance. From it one can judge his learning and discernment.”
Examiner Xia, Professor, comments: “The argument is precise and thorough.”

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授帥批識見甚正
儒道之寄也道一而已矣儒有二乎哉儒
之爲道根乎身心性情通乎天地民物至
醇而不雜至正而不偏至大而不迂蘊之
足以凝會聖眞發之足以恢張王化天下
不可一日無道則亦不可一日無儒故所
貴乎儒者非徒以其冠儒冠服儒服名儒
名巳也當必有繼往開來之實而後稱其
爲儒也如以其冠其服其名而巳則執途
===
之人而冠以章甫服以縫掖而名之曰儒
其果儒也耶使儒而果若斯也則亦何望
於聖學何裨於化理乎故學儒者必要諸
道而後從違之極定命儒者必稽諸道而
後是非之辨明今執事發策而以儒行爲
問顧海邦非多儒者而愚也生長
右儒之世涵濡
聖化仰止前脩亦既有日矣敢無言以復儒之
名何始乎三代而上未甞無儒而不以儒
punctuated:
考試官敎授帥批：識見甚正。
儒，道之寄也。道一而已矣，儒有二乎哉？儒之爲道，根乎身心性情，通乎天地民物，至醇而不雜，至正而不偏，至大而不迂。蘊之，足以凝會聖眞；發之，足以恢張王化。天下不可一日無道，則亦不可一日無儒。故所貴乎儒者，非徒以其冠儒冠、服儒服、名儒名巳也，當必有繼往開來之實，而後稱其爲儒也。如以其冠、其服、其名而巳，則執途之人而冠以章甫，服以縫掖，而名之曰儒，其果儒也耶？使儒而果若斯也，則亦何望於聖學，何裨於化理乎？故學儒者，必要諸道，而後從違之極定；命儒者，必稽諸道，而後是非之辨明。今執事發策而以儒行爲問，顧海邦非多儒者，而愚也生長右儒之世，涵濡聖化，仰止前脩，亦既有日矣，敢無言以復？儒之名何始乎？三代而上，未甞無儒，而不以儒
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Shuai, Professor: His understanding is thoroughly sound.

The Confucian scholar is the repository of the Way. The Way is one and nothing more; could there be two kinds of Confucian scholars? The Way practiced by the Confucian scholar is rooted in the person, mind, nature, and feelings, and extends to Heaven and Earth, the people, and all things. It is utterly pure and unmixed, utterly correct and impartial, utterly comprehensive without being impractical. Stored within, it suffices to bring together the true essence of sagehood; expressed outwardly, it suffices to extend the transforming influence of kingly rule. If the world cannot go a single day without the Way, neither can it go a single day without Confucian scholars. Thus, what we value in Confucian scholars is not merely that they wear a scholar’s cap and robes and bear a scholar’s name. They must possess the substance of carrying forward the past and opening the way for the future before they deserve to be called Confucian scholars. If it were merely a matter of cap, robes, and name, one could take a person from the road, put a zhangfu ceremonial cap on him, dress him in broad-sleeved robes, and call him a Confucian scholar. Would he really be one? If Confucian scholars were indeed like this, what could one expect of them in the learning of the sages, and what benefit could they bring to moral transformation and good government? Thus, those who study to become Confucian scholars must judge by the Way before they can establish the ultimate standard for what to follow and what to reject. Those who designate others as Confucian scholars must examine them against the Way before the distinction between right and wrong becomes clear.

Now you, honored examiners, have issued a policy question asking about the conduct of Confucian scholars. Although this coastal region does not abound in such scholars, I, unworthy though I am, have grown up in an age that honors Confucian learning, steeped in the sage sovereign’s transforming influence. I have long looked up to the worthy men of earlier times. How could I dare offer no words in reply? When did the designation “Confucian scholar” begin? During the Three Dynasties and earlier, there were never no Confucian scholars, yet they were not called Confucian scholars …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
名心儒者之心道儒者之道夫人是也不
可得而名也何也國多弱子勇士之名始
彰人皆貪夫廉士之名乃見故名不生於
有而生於無也無儒之名儒之盛也儒名
起而實則衰矣然則儒之名其濫觴於叔
季之世乎粤自周官太宰以九兩繫萬民
而儒因以著今攷其目曰牧以地得民也
長以貴得民也師以賢得民也儒以道得
民也宗以族得民也主以利得民也吏以
===
治得民也友以任得民也藪以多得民也
夫儒而與主吏牧長並稱固以儒道貫乎
九兩之中而為聯屬人心之本也儒之道
不其重哉漢班固作藝文志有九家之論
而儒居其一今攷其說曰儒家出於司徒
之官也道家出於史官也陰陽家出於羲
和之官也法家出於理官也名家出於禮
官也墨家出於清廟之官也縱横家出於
行人之官也雜家出於議官也農家出於
punctuated:
名。心儒者之心，道儒者之道，夫人是也，不可得而名也。何也？國多弱子，勇士之名始彰；人皆貪夫，廉士之名乃見。故名不生於有，而生於無也。無儒之名，儒之盛也；儒名起，而實則衰矣。然則儒之名，其濫觴於叔季之世乎？粤自《周官》太宰以九兩繫萬民，而儒因以著。今攷其目曰：牧以地得民也，長以貴得民也，師以賢得民也，儒以道得民也，宗以族得民也，主以利得民也，吏以治得民也，友以任得民也，藪以多得民也。夫儒而與主、吏、牧、長並稱，固以儒道貫乎九兩之中，而為聯屬人心之本也。儒之道，不其重哉！

漢班固作《藝文志》，有九家之論，而儒居其一。今攷其說曰：儒家出於司徒之官也，道家出於史官也，陰陽家出於羲和之官也，法家出於理官也，名家出於禮官也，墨家出於清廟之官也，縱横家出於行人之官也，雜家出於議官也，農家出於
translation_en:
…by that name. They had the minds of Confucian scholars and followed the Way of Confucian scholars. Everyone was like this, so no distinctive name could be given them. Why? Only when a country has many weaklings does the name “brave warrior” become conspicuous; only when everyone is greedy does the name “incorruptible gentleman” appear. Thus a name arises not from a quality’s presence, but from its absence. The absence of the name “Confucian scholar” marked the flourishing of Confucian scholars; when the name arose, the substance had declined. Did the designation “Confucian scholar,” then, originate in an age of decline? In the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), the Grand Steward bound the myriad people together through the nine bonds, and Confucian scholars thereby gained explicit recognition. Examining its enumeration, we find: regional rulers win the people through land; chiefs win the people through noble rank; teachers win the people through worthiness; Confucian scholars win the people through the Way; lineage heads win the people through kinship; masters win the people through material benefits; officials win the people through governance; friends win the people through mutual responsibility; and keepers of marshlands win the people through their abundant resources. Confucian scholars are named alongside masters, officials, regional rulers, and chiefs precisely because the Confucian Way runs through all nine bonds and provides the foundation for joining people’s hearts together. How weighty is the Way of Confucian scholars!

When Ban Gu of the Han compiled the Treatise on Literature (Yiwenzhi), he discussed nine schools, with the Confucians occupying one place among them. Examining his account, we find: the Confucian school originated in the office of the Minister of Education; the Daoist school originated among historiographers; the Yin-Yang school originated in the offices of Xi and He; the Legalist school originated among judicial officials; the School of Names originated among ritual officials; the Mohist school originated among officials of the Pure Temple; the School of Diplomatic Strategists originated among envoys; the Eclectic school originated among deliberative officials; and the Agriculturalist school originated in …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
農稷之官也小說家出於稗官也夫儒而
與陰陽農雜槩列殆不知儒道精粹渾全
非一家一官所能限也固之言不其謬哉
仲尼侍魯君述儒行備矣曰自立豫養曰
近人剛毅曰憂思寬裕曰特立獨行信哉
更僕未易數也或謂誇與太過似非聖經
其殆䰷鰠測海乎楊雄著法言述儒効備
矣曰周公一用而四海皇皇奠枕於京曰
孔子一用而齊人章章歸其侵疆信哉功
===
効不可誣也然以二聖勳業妄加指數其
殆斥鷃窺天乎洙泗以還道術棼裂儒學
蓋失傳矣隱柴桑而述八儒者陶潛也謂
子思爲蓽門圭竇以道自樂之儒子張爲
大讓小讓以儀自飭之儒顏氏傳詩爲諷
諫之儒孟氏傳書爲疏通知遠之儒漆雕
氏傳禮爲恭儉莊敬之儒仲梁氏傳樂爲
移風易俗之儒樂正氏傳春秋爲屬辭比
事之儒公孫氏傳易爲潔淨精微之儒夫
punctuated:
農稷之官也；小說家出於稗官也。夫儒而與陰陽、農、雜槩列，殆不知儒道精粹渾全，非一家一官所能限也。固之言不其謬哉？
仲尼侍魯君，述儒行備矣。曰自立豫養，曰近人剛毅，曰憂思寬裕，曰特立獨行。信哉，更僕未易數也！或謂誇與太過，似非聖經，其殆䰷鰠測海乎？楊雄著《法言》，述儒効備矣。曰周公一用，而四海皇皇，奠枕於京；曰孔子一用，而齊人章章，歸其侵疆。信哉，功効不可誣也！然以二聖勳業妄加指數，其殆斥鷃窺天乎？
洙泗以還，道術棼裂，儒學蓋失傳矣。隱柴桑而述八儒者，陶潛也。謂子思爲蓽門圭竇、以道自樂之儒；子張爲大讓小讓、以儀自飭之儒；顏氏傳《詩》，爲諷諫之儒；孟氏傳《書》，爲疏通知遠之儒；漆雕氏傳《禮》，爲恭儉莊敬之儒；仲梁氏傳《樂》，爲移風易俗之儒；樂正氏傳《春秋》，爲屬辭比事之儒；公孫氏傳《易》，爲潔淨精微之儒。夫
translation_en:
…the officials responsible for agriculture and grain; the school of minor tales arose from the petty officials. To rank the Confucians indiscriminately alongside the Yin-Yang, Agricultural, and Miscellaneous schools is surely to fail to understand that the Confucian Way is pure in its essence and wholly comprehensive: no single school or office can encompass it. Are not Ban Gu’s words mistaken?
When Zhongni attended the ruler of Lu, he described the conduct of Confucians comprehensively. He spoke of establishing oneself and nurturing oneself in advance; of being approachable, firm, and resolute; of anxious reflection and generous forbearance; and of standing apart and acting independently. Indeed, even with servants relieving one another, such qualities could not readily be enumerated! Some say that this account is extravagant and excessive, and seems not to be a sage’s canonical teaching. Is this not like shellfish attempting to fathom the sea [?]? In writing Model Sayings (Fayan), Yang Xiong described the achievements of Confucians comprehensively. He said that once the Duke of Zhou was employed, all within the Four Seas flourished magnificently, resting securely in the capital; and that once Confucius was employed, the people of Qi conspicuously returned the territory they had encroached upon. Indeed, these accomplishments cannot be denied! Yet presumptuously to reckon up the achievements of these two sages—is this not like a little quail peering at the heavens?
Since the days of the Zhu and Si rivers, the Way and its arts have fragmented into confusion, and the transmission of Confucian learning has, it seems, been lost. It was Tao Qian, living in retirement at Chaisang, who described eight types of Confucians. He called Zisi a Confucian who lived behind a brushwood gate and a small, pointed wall opening, finding joy in the Way; Zizhang, a Confucian who yielded in matters great and small and disciplined himself through ceremonial deportment; the Yan lineage, transmitters of the Book of Odes, Confucians of indirect remonstrance; the Meng lineage, transmitters of the Book of Documents, Confucians of broad understanding and knowledge of the distant past; the Qidiao lineage, transmitters of the rites, Confucians of humility, frugality, dignity, and reverence; the Zhongliang lineage, transmitters of music, Confucians who transformed prevailing practices and customs; the Yuezheng lineage, transmitters of the Spring and Autumn Annals, Confucians who linked statements and compared events; and the Gongsun lineage, transmitters of the Book of Changes, Confucians of purity and subtle discernment. Now …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
子思子張親承聖教者取釋經諸儒而並
之是容彭而班殤子也其所評隲果當哉
令蘭陵而賤三儒者荀况也謂弟佗其冠
神禫其辭禹行而舜趨子張氏賤儒也正
其衣冠齊其顏色慊然而終日不言子夏
氏賤儒也偷懦憚事無廉恥而嗜飲食曰
君子固不用力子游氏賤儒也夫游夏子
張同具聖禮者以衣冠飲食而賤之是白
璧而蒙青蠅也其所譏詆何妄哉漢史立
===
儒林傳載丁寬而下諸人而潜心大業若
董仲舒者乃獨不與豈丁寬輩賢於仲舒
耶蓋漢以訓詁為儒而仲舒以正誼明道
為心以計功謀利為戒似不專於訓詁者
史氏捨而不錄宜矣唐史立儒學傳載徐
文遠而下諸人而學本六經若韓愈者乃
又見遺豈文遠輩優於愈耶蓋唐以辨博
為儒而愈以起衰濟溺為期以闢邪崇正
為任似不事於辨博者史氏置而不及宜
punctuated:
子思、子張，親承聖教者，取釋經諸儒而並之，是容彭而班殤子也。其所評隲果當哉？令蘭陵而賤三儒者，荀况也。謂弟佗其冠，神禫其辭，禹行而舜趨，子張氏賤儒也；正其衣冠，齊其顏色，慊然而終日不言，子夏氏賤儒也；偷懦憚事，無廉恥而嗜飲食，曰「君子固不用力」，子游氏賤儒也。夫游、夏、子張，同具聖禮者，以衣冠飲食而賤之，是白璧而蒙青蠅也。其所譏詆何妄哉！

漢史立《儒林傳》，載丁寬而下諸人，而潜心大業若董仲舒者，乃獨不與。豈丁寬輩賢於仲舒耶？蓋漢以訓詁為儒，而仲舒以正誼明道為心，以計功謀利為戒，似不專於訓詁者，史氏捨而不錄，宜矣。

唐史立《儒學傳》，載徐文遠而下諸人，而學本六經若韓愈者，乃又見遺。豈文遠輩優於愈耶？蓋唐以辨博為儒，而愈以起衰濟溺為期，以闢邪崇正為任，似不事於辨博者，史氏置而不及，宜
translation_en:
…Zisi and Zizhang personally received the Sage’s teachings. To take the various scholars who explicated the classics and rank them alongside these two is to place Pengzu together with children who died in infancy [?]. Were his assessments really appropriate? It was Xun Kuang, magistrate of Lanling, who disparaged three groups of Confucians. He said: “With dangling caps [?] and strange, extravagant words [?], walking like Yu and hastening like Shun—these are the base Confucians of Zizhang’s school. Straightening their robes and caps, composing their expressions, and remaining reserved and silent all day—these are the base Confucians of Zixia’s school. Indolent and timid, shrinking from affairs, lacking integrity and shame, yet fond of food and drink, and saying, ‘A gentleman certainly does not exert himself’—these are the base Confucians of Ziyou’s school.” Now Ziyou, Zixia, and Zizhang all possessed the Sage’s ritual propriety. To disparage them on account of clothing, caps, food, and drink is to let blue flies sully white jade. How reckless were his slanders!

The history of the Han established “Biographies of Confucian Scholars,” recording Ding Kuan and those who followed him; yet someone like Dong Zhongshu, who devoted himself to the great undertaking, was alone excluded. Could Ding Kuan and his fellows have been worthier than Zhongshu? The Han regarded textual exegesis as defining Confucian scholarship, whereas Zhongshu set his heart on rectifying righteousness and illuminating the Way, warning against calculating achievements and seeking profit. He apparently did not specialize in textual exegesis, so it was only fitting that the historians should omit him from their account!

The history of the Tang established “Biographies of Confucian Learning,” recording Xu Wenyuan and those who followed him; yet someone like Han Yu, whose learning was rooted in the Six Classics, was again omitted. Could Wenyuan and his fellows have been superior to Yu? The Tang regarded argumentative skill and broad learning as defining Confucian scholarship, whereas Yu aimed to revive what had declined and rescue what was drowning, taking as his responsibility the rejection of heterodoxy and the exaltation of orthodoxy. He apparently did not devote himself to argumentative skill and broad learning, so it was only fitting that the historians should set him aside and leave him unmentioned…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
矣至儒林傳之作于宋紀聶崇義邢昺諸
人而又作道學傳以紀濂洛關閩諸賢可
謂詳矣于時精於稽古得中原文献之傳
若呂伯恭精於涵養謹屋漏夢寐之際若
陸子靜與程朱同一學術者而道學傳顧
亦遺焉豈非以伯恭之學傷於巧子靜之
學流於禪造詣未醇未足與諸賢爲伍歟
此固史氏別傳之微意也詎謂道自道儒
自儒乃岐而二之哉嗚呼自學儒者之不
===
愼其趨而儒之途始雜自論儒者之不稽
其實而儒之名始卑魚目能混珠而槩謂
珠之不足珍非也燕石能亂玉而槩謂玉
之不足貴非也曲士類儒而槩謂儒之不
足重非也故嘗合而觀之周公達而在上
而儒道行孔子窮而在下而儒道明萬世
儒者之的也後之爲儒者希周焉耳希孔
焉耳希周而周希孔而孔所得雖殊所趨
皆正猶飲河焉多寡異受而各充其量也
punctuated:
矣。至儒林傳之作于宋，紀聶崇義、邢昺諸人，而又作道學傳，以紀濂洛關閩諸賢，可謂詳矣。于時精於稽古，得中原文献之傳若呂伯恭，精於涵養，謹屋漏夢寐之際若陸子靜，與程朱同一學術者，而道學傳顧亦遺焉。豈非以伯恭之學傷於巧，子靜之學流於禪，造詣未醇，未足與諸賢爲伍歟？此固史氏別傳之微意也，詎謂道自道、儒自儒，乃岐而二之哉？
嗚呼！自學儒者之不愼其趨，而儒之途始雜；自論儒者之不稽其實，而儒之名始卑。魚目能混珠，而槩謂珠之不足珍，非也；燕石能亂玉，而槩謂玉之不足貴，非也；曲士類儒，而槩謂儒之不足重，非也。故嘗合而觀之：周公達而在上，而儒道行；孔子窮而在下，而儒道明。萬世儒者之的也。後之爲儒者，希周焉耳，希孔焉耳。希周而周，希孔而孔，所得雖殊，所趨皆正。猶飲河焉，多寡異受，而各充其量也。
translation_en:
…indeed. When the Biographies of Confucian Scholars were compiled for the Song, they recorded Nie Chongyi, Xing Bing, and others; separate Biographies of Scholars of the Way were also compiled to record the worthies of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min. This may be called comprehensive. Yet there were men of that age such as Lü Bogong, who excelled in investigating antiquity and inherited the textual and scholarly traditions of the Central Plain, and Lu Zijing, who excelled in nurturing his moral nature and remained vigilant even in the privacy of his chamber and in his dreams. Though their learning belonged to the same tradition as that of the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi, the Biographies of Scholars of the Way nevertheless omitted them. Was this not because Bogong’s learning was marred by cleverness and Zijing’s learning strayed into Chan Buddhism, so that their attainments were not yet pure enough to place them among those worthies? This was surely the historians’ subtle intention in assigning them separate biographies. How could it mean that the Way and Confucian learning were distinct things, to be divided into two?
Alas! It was because those studying Confucian learning were careless about the direction they pursued that the paths of Confucian learning first became confused; it was because those judging Confucian scholars failed to examine their actual qualities that the name of Confucian scholar first fell into disrepute. Fish eyes can be mistaken for pearls, but it is wrong to declare on that account that pearls are unworthy of being treasured. Stones from Yan can be mistaken for jade, but it is wrong to declare on that account that jade is unworthy of esteem. Narrow-minded scholars may resemble Confucian scholars, but it is wrong to declare on that account that Confucian scholars are unworthy of respect. Thus I have considered these things together: the Duke of Zhou enjoyed success and occupied a high position, and the Confucian Way was put into practice; Kongzi encountered adversity and remained in a lowly position, and the Confucian Way was made clear. They are the models for Confucian scholars for all ages. Those who become Confucian scholars in later times need only aspire to be like the Duke of Zhou or Kongzi. By aspiring to the Duke of Zhou, they become like him; by aspiring to Kongzi, they become like him. Although their attainments differ, the direction they pursue is in every case correct. It is like drinking from a river: each takes a different amount, whether much or little, yet each fills his own capacity.

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
猶趨塗焉遐邇異至而各要其歸也故周
張游夏近師周孔而得儒之精者也濂洛
關閩遠宗周孔而得儒之正者也董子儒
之度越者也韓子儒之醇而未免于疵者
也伯恭子靜儒之未粹者也仲梁樂正公
孫諸氏儒之羽翼者也丁寛文遠邢昺崇
義諸家儒之宮牆外望者也彼班之駁雜
陶之放逸荀與楊擇焉而不精蓋似周非
周似孔非孔似儒非儒者也又烏足以談
===
儒哉而要之儒非絕德也仁義禮智儒之
道也君臣父子儒之倫也孝弟忠信儒之
用也視聽言動儒之功也禮樂文章儒之
具也經綸康濟儒之施也易知簡能儒固
若是焉止矣為周為孔儒亦率是焉止矣
乃世之儒者喜為非常之習以謏聞動衆
或者不察往往羣起而慕效之以為儒道
固當如是嗟乎其果儒耶非耶自今言之
儒者非無文而文即道也聱牙若奇剽竊
punctuated:
猶趨塗焉，遐邇異至，而各要其歸也。故周、張、游、夏，近師周、孔而得儒之精者也；濂、洛、關、閩，遠宗周、孔而得儒之正者也。董子，儒之度越者也；韓子，儒之醇而未免于疵者也；伯恭、子靜，儒之未粹者也；仲梁、樂正、公孫諸氏，儒之羽翼者也；丁寛、文遠、邢昺、崇義諸家，儒之宮牆外望者也。彼班之駁雜，陶之放逸，荀與楊擇焉而不精，蓋似周非周，似孔非孔，似儒非儒者也，又烏足以談儒哉？

而要之，儒非絕德也。仁義禮智，儒之道也；君臣父子，儒之倫也；孝弟忠信，儒之用也；視聽言動，儒之功也；禮樂文章，儒之具也；經綸康濟，儒之施也。易知簡能，儒固若是焉止矣；為周為孔，儒亦率是焉止矣。乃世之儒者，喜為非常之習，以謏聞動衆。或者不察，往往羣起而慕效之，以為儒道固當如是。嗟乎！其果儒耶？非耶？自今言之，儒者非無文，而文即道也。聱牙若奇，剽竊
translation_en:
…It is likewise as with traveling along a road: some reach farther than others, but each seeks to arrive at his destination. Thus Zhou [?], Zhang, You, and Xia learned directly from the Duke of Zhou and Confucius and grasped the essence of Confucian learning; the traditions of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min followed the Duke of Zhou and Confucius across the intervening ages and grasped its orthodox principles. Master Dong was an outstanding Confucian; Master Han was a substantially pure Confucian, though not free from flaws. Bogong and Zijing were Confucians whose learning had not attained purity. The Zhongliang, Yuezheng, Gongsun, and other lineages served as wings supporting Confucian learning. Ding Kuan, Wenyuan, Xing Bing, Chongyi, and other scholars gazed from outside the walls of its palace. As for Ban’s mixed and inconsistent learning, Tao’s unrestrained abandonment of convention, and Xun and Yang’s insufficiently discerning selection of teachings, these resembled the Duke of Zhou without truly being like him, resembled Confucius without truly being like him, and resembled Confucians without truly being Confucians. How could they qualify to discuss Confucian learning?

In essence, however, being a Confucian does not require extraordinary virtue. Benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom constitute the Confucian Way; ruler and minister, father and son constitute its human relationships. Filial devotion, fraternal respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness are its practical expression; seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting are the work of its cultivation. Rites, music, and literary expression are its instruments; ordering affairs and bringing peace and relief to the people are its application. Easy to understand and simple to practice: being a Confucian amounts to just this. To become like the Duke of Zhou or Confucius likewise requires only following these things. Yet the Confucians of the present age delight in unconventional practices, stirring the multitude with their meager learning. Some fail to examine them critically and repeatedly flock to admire and imitate them, supposing that the Confucian Way must indeed be like this. Alas! Are they truly Confucians, or are they not? Speaking of the present, Confucians do not lack literary expression, but that expression is itself the Way. Awkward, grating diction passes for originality; plagiarism…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
若該鄙俚若淺馳騖若廣其果儒耶非耶
儒者非無行而行即道也擎曲若恭矯違
若廉誕謾若信賣直若忠其果儒耶否耶
儒者非無出處而出處即道也堅僻若高
三謁若通撫扼若烈猖狂若敢其果儒耶
非耶若是者彼固挾此以自托于儒者之
林天下亦或以儒名之而不知其去乎儒
也奚啻千里真似之際可不慎所趨哉雖
然水必寒而火必熱真也莠疑苗而紫疑
===
朱似也真似雜陳鮮不悅其似而棄其真
故士之業儒者亦恒苦于真之難售而競
趨于似之易投也何也好尚故也世誠識
真人皆抱其真以需進時方悅似人皆飾
其似以媒通倡感之機夫固有所係之矣
方今
聖天子在上右文崇教飭經表俗海內之士欣
欣嚮風家周孔而戶程朱固知真儒碩彥
霧集雲蒸足以闡聖真而揚
punctuated:
若該，鄙俚若淺，馳騖若廣，其果儒耶？非耶？儒者非無行，而行即道也。擎曲若恭，矯違若廉，誕謾若信，賣直若忠，其果儒耶？否耶？儒者非無出處，而出處即道也。堅僻若高，三謁若通，撫扼若烈，猖狂若敢，其果儒耶？非耶？若是者，彼固挾此以自托于儒者之林，天下亦或以儒名之，而不知其去乎儒也奚啻千里！真似之際，可不慎所趨哉？雖然，水必寒而火必熱，真也；莠疑苗而紫疑朱，似也。真似雜陳，鮮不悅其似而棄其真。故士之業儒者，亦恒苦于真之難售，而競趨于似之易投也。何也？好尚故也。世誠識真，人皆抱其真以需進；時方悅似，人皆飾其似以媒通。倡感之機，夫固有所係之矣。
方今聖天子在上，右文崇教，飭經表俗，海內之士欣欣嚮風，家周孔而戶程朱。固知真儒碩彥，霧集雲蒸，足以闡聖真而揚
translation_en:
…as though comprehensive; vulgar and coarse, as though plain and accessible; ranging restlessly, as though broad in learning—are they truly Confucian scholars, or not? Confucian scholars certainly have their conduct, and that conduct is itself the Way. Affected deference [?] passes for respect, contrived nonconformity for integrity, extravagant falsehood for trustworthiness, and the ostentatious display of bluntness for loyalty—are they truly Confucian scholars, or not? Confucian scholars certainly make choices about entering office or withdrawing, and those choices are themselves the Way. Stubborn eccentricity passes for loftiness, repeated calls on patrons [?] for adaptability, breast-beating indignation [?] for ardor, and reckless abandon for courage—are they truly Confucian scholars, or not? Such men rely on these things to claim a place among Confucian scholars. The world may also call them Confucian scholars, unaware that they are more than a thousand miles removed from true Confucian learning! At the boundary between the genuine and its semblance, can one fail to take care about what one pursues? Yet water is necessarily cold and fire necessarily hot: these are genuine qualities. Weeds are mistaken for grain shoots, and purple for vermilion: these are deceptive semblances. When the genuine and its semblance are displayed together, few fail to delight in the semblance and discard the genuine. Thus scholars pursuing Confucian learning also constantly suffer because the genuine is difficult to find acceptance for, and compete in pursuing the semblance because it readily wins favor. Why is this? Because of prevailing tastes. If the world truly recognized the genuine, everyone would hold fast to what was genuine in himself and await advancement. When the age delights in semblances, everyone embellishes his semblance to secure access to office. The dynamic by which an example is set and others respond assuredly depends on something.
Now our sagely Son of Heaven reigns above, honoring literary learning and exalting instruction, setting the canonical norms in order and providing an example for popular customs. Scholars throughout the realm joyfully turn toward his influence; every family follows Zhou and Confucius, and every household Cheng and Zhu. We assuredly know that true Confucian scholars and men of outstanding worth gather like mist and rise like clouds, sufficient to elucidate the sages’ true teaching and spread …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
王化矣然愚又有進焉周也貴士則士亦自
貴而道德仁義之儒出秦也賤士則士亦
自賤而縱橫捭闔之儒顯信乎儒道之汙
隆轉移變化其機在上而不在下矣任風
教之責者無亦知所隆重以來真儒哉
第四問
林奇石
同考試官教諭趙批寬嚴竝施不膠不縱
國家法令之設本如是是篇能發揮此意而末復責成于行法者具見經緯之學
===
同考試官教諭王批以正與通立意而全篇無一經生
套語文之佳者
考試官教授夏批問目外更能推廣通儒也
考試官教授帥批殆閑習法令者
法者聖人所以整齊宇內攝一羣生至正
至通之道也何謂至正本天理之公究人
情之極為嚴為寬有倫有要萬世莫能易
也何謂至通奉天理以推遷緣人情以順
應或嚴或寬趨時妙用萬世亦莫能易也
punctuated:
王化矣。然愚又有進焉：周也貴士，則士亦自貴，而道德仁義之儒出；秦也賤士，則士亦自賤，而縱橫捭闔之儒顯。信乎，儒道之汙隆、轉移變化，其機在上而不在下矣。任風教之責者，無亦知所隆重以來真儒哉？

第四問
林奇石

同考試官教諭趙批：寬嚴竝施，不膠不縱，國家法令之設本如是。是篇能發揮此意，而末復責成于行法者，具見經緯之學。

同考試官教諭王批：以正與通立意，而全篇無一經生套語，文之佳者。

考試官教授夏批：問目外更能推廣，通儒也。

考試官教授帥批：殆閑習法令者。

法者，聖人所以整齊宇內、攝一羣生，至正至通之道也。何謂至正？本天理之公，究人情之極，為嚴為寬，有倫有要，萬世莫能易也。何謂至通？奉天理以推遷，緣人情以順應，或嚴或寬，趨時妙用，萬世亦莫能易也。
translation_en:
…the transforming influence of royal rule. Yet I venture to add a further point. Under the Zhou, scholars were esteemed, so scholars also esteemed themselves, and Confucians devoted to the Way, virtue, benevolence, and righteousness emerged. Under the Qin, scholars were despised, so scholars also debased themselves, and Confucians skilled in political maneuvering and persuasion rose to prominence. Indeed, the decline and flourishing of the Confucian Way, its shifts and transformations, are set in motion by those above, not those below. Should not those responsible for moral instruction know what to honor and esteem, so as to attract true Confucians?

Fourth Question
Lin Qishi 林奇石

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “Leniency and severity should both be applied, without rigidity or laxity: this is precisely the original purpose of the state's establishment of laws and ordinances. This essay develops that idea and, at its conclusion, further holds those who administer the law responsible for its fulfillment. It fully displays learning suited to ordering affairs.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “It takes rectitude and adaptability as its central idea, yet throughout the essay there is not a single stock phrase of the conventional classical scholar. A fine piece of writing.”

Comment by Examiner Xia, Professor: “He can extend the discussion beyond the scope of the question itself—a broadly learned Confucian.”

Comment by Examiner Shuai, Professor: “He seems well versed in laws and ordinances.”

Law is the means by which the sages bring order to all under Heaven and unite the multitude of living people under their governance; it is a way of utmost rectitude and utmost adaptability. What is meant by utmost rectitude? Grounded in the impartiality of Heaven's principle and fully fathoming human dispositions, it employs severity and leniency with due order and guiding essentials: this cannot be changed for ten thousand generations. What is meant by utmost adaptability? Upholding Heaven's principle as circumstances change and responding appropriately in accordance with human dispositions, it employs severity or leniency as needed, adapting to the times with consummate skill: this too cannot be changed for ten thousand generations.

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
惟用法者不達其原徒知嚴之爲正而任
法以逞於是文致之風起操切之政行糾
如束薪急如絞繩而賢者或不免矣不知
寬之未始非正也徒知寬之爲通而弛法
以徇於是綱解而不張防決而不止網漏
於吞舟禁疎於出柙而不肖者或倖免矣
不知嚴之未始非通也正以示之而人有
所循通以行之而人有所措則法令恊中
古今稱盛治者此也執事發策以法令下
===
詢承學寧非有感于古今之不相及而思
所以善其法於不窮也歟請因明問而敬
陳之今夫天以陽生萬物而不能不肅之
以陰聖王以仁育萬民而不能不正之以
義於是乎法令制焉蓋人心不齊則亂人
情不一則散法令者所以整齊其亂而懾
一其散之具也是故峻如峭壁深如重淵
不可越也疾如衝風砉如震雷不可禦也
固如是其嚴也持鑑察形因足施屨不爲
punctuated:
惟用法者不達其原，徒知嚴之爲正，而任法以逞，於是文致之風起，操切之政行，糾如束薪，急如絞繩，而賢者或不免矣。不知寬之未始非正也。徒知寬之爲通，而弛法以徇，於是綱解而不張，防決而不止，網漏於吞舟，禁疎於出柙，而不肖者或倖免矣。不知嚴之未始非通也。正以示之，而人有所循；通以行之，而人有所措，則法令恊中。古今稱盛治者，此也。
執事發策，以法令下詢承學，寧非有感于古今之不相及，而思所以善其法於不窮也歟？請因明問而敬陳之。今夫天以陽生萬物，而不能不肅之以陰；聖王以仁育萬民，而不能不正之以義。於是乎法令制焉。蓋人心不齊則亂，人情不一則散。法令者，所以整齊其亂，而懾一其散之具也。是故峻如峭壁，深如重淵，不可越也；疾如衝風，砉如震雷，不可禦也。固如是其嚴也。持鑑察形，因足施屨，不爲
translation_en:
Yet those who apply the law fail to grasp its source. Knowing only that severity constitutes rectitude, they wield the law to indulge their own will. Thus a habit of contriving charges arises, and oppressive government prevails. Restraints tighten like bundles of firewood and press like twisted ropes, so that even worthy people sometimes cannot escape punishment. Such officials do not understand that leniency, too, can accord with rectitude. Knowing only that leniency constitutes adaptability, they relax the law to accommodate others. Thus the guiding cords slacken and are never drawn taut; the embankments breach and the flow is never stopped. The net lets through fish large enough to swallow a boat, and prohibitions leave openings through which caged beasts escape. Even the unworthy may consequently escape punishment by good fortune. Such officials do not understand that severity, too, can accord with adaptability. Show people rectitude, and they have something to follow; apply the law with adaptability, and they have a basis on which to act. Then laws and ordinances accord with the proper mean. This is what has been praised, in antiquity and today, as flourishing government.
You gentlemen have issued a policy question on laws and ordinances, condescending to consult us students. Surely you are moved by the failure of the present to measure up to antiquity, and seek a way to perfect the law for all time? Allow me respectfully to set forth my views in response to your discerning question. Heaven brings forth the myriad things through yang, yet cannot dispense with the restraining force of yin. The sage kings nurture the myriad people through benevolence, yet cannot dispense with rectifying them through righteousness. Hence laws and ordinances were established. For when people’s minds are not aligned, disorder results; when their dispositions are not united, they become dispersed. Laws and ordinances are the instruments by which this disorder is brought into order and this dispersal is overawed into unity. Thus they are steep as sheer cliffs and deep as successive abysses: they cannot be crossed. They are swift as a rushing wind and resounding as thunder: they cannot be resisted. Such, indeed, is their severity. Holding up a mirror to examine a form, fitting the shoe to the foot—this does not constitute …

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
徇也以仁勝義屈法全恩不爲私也又如
是其寬也寬嚴互用操縱異宜不求劍於
刻舟此之謂通不毀方以爲圓此之謂正
朝廷之所以常尊世道之所以常治是故聖
人重之也韓非子曰人臣循令而從事案
法而治官故君者置法而出令者也臣者
守法而共令者也臣以守法共令爲職則
雖米鹽之細猶當奉之惟謹而況城郭乎
虜寇乎巨獄乎筦庫乎臣以守法共令爲
===
盡職則雖米鹽之細猶當請而後行而況
廢營繕乎縱強寇乎燒獄詞乎用庫錢乎
乃古之豪傑有不然者出宰百里不繕城
郭尹鐸爲之居守鴈門縱虜入寇李牧爲
之梁事按實輒燒獄詞田叔爲之筦庫雜
錢輒以自用明道爲之彼四子者豈不知
法令之當守哉顧守法則功不可收事不
可濟通之則功收事濟而君之法令固在
也是故不繕非法五日告完何嫌□□□
punctuated:
徇也；以仁勝義，屈法全恩，不爲私也。又如是其寬也。寬嚴互用，操縱異宜，不求劍於刻舟，此之謂通；不毀方以爲圓，此之謂正。朝廷之所以常尊，世道之所以常治，是故聖人重之也。韓非子曰：「人臣循令而從事，案法而治官。」故君者，置法而出令者也；臣者，守法而共令者也。臣以守法共令爲職，則雖米鹽之細，猶當奉之惟謹，而況城郭乎？虜寇乎？巨獄乎？筦庫乎？臣以守法共令爲盡職，則雖米鹽之細，猶當請而後行，而況廢營繕乎？縱強寇乎？燒獄詞乎？用庫錢乎？
乃古之豪傑有不然者：出宰百里，不繕城郭，尹鐸爲之；居守鴈門，縱虜入寇，李牧爲之；梁事按實，輒燒獄詞，田叔爲之；筦庫雜錢，輒以自用，明道爲之。彼四子者，豈不知法令之當守哉？顧守法則功不可收，事不可濟；通之則功收事濟，而君之法令固在也。是故不繕非法，五日告完，何嫌□□□
translation_en:
…indulgence; letting benevolence prevail over righteousness and bending the law to preserve gracious treatment does not constitute favoritism. Such, too, is its leniency. Leniency and severity are used in alternation; restraint and latitude each have their appropriate circumstances. One does not seek a sword by a notch cut in a boat: this is called adaptability. One does not destroy the square to make a circle: this is called rectitude. These are what keep the court perpetually honored and the world perpetually well governed; hence the sages attach great importance to them. Han Feizi said: “Ministers follow commands in conducting affairs and administer their offices according to law.” Thus the ruler establishes laws and issues commands, while ministers uphold the laws and obey the commands. If ministers take upholding laws and obeying commands as their duty, then even in matters as trifling as rice and salt they should observe them with the utmost care. How much more so with city walls, enemy raids, major criminal cases, and treasuries! If ministers regard upholding laws and obeying commands as the fulfillment of their duty, then even in matters as trifling as rice and salt they should request authorization before acting. How much more so before abandoning construction and repairs, giving powerful raiders free rein, burning judicial records, or spending treasury funds!
Yet there were outstanding men of antiquity who acted otherwise. Governing a district a hundred li across, Yin Duo left its city walls unrepaired. Holding command at Yanmen, Li Mu allowed enemy forces to enter and raid. Having investigated and established the facts of the Liang affair, Tian Shu promptly burned the judicial records. Mingdao freely used miscellaneous treasury funds on his own authority. Could these four men have been unaware that laws and commands ought to be upheld? They recognized, however, that strict adherence to the law would prevent results from being achieved and affairs from being brought to completion. By applying it flexibly, they achieved results and accomplished their tasks, while the ruler’s laws and commands remained intact. Thus, leaving the walls unrepaired contravened the law, yet their completion was reported in five days: what grounds were there for suspecting [three illegible characters] [?]…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
寇非法卒以斃胡何嫌於弱故縱非法上
全太后何嫌於擅自用非法補助民力何
嫌於專向使鐸而無見於政教之脩牧而
無見於成功之偉叔而無見於母子之倫
明道而無見於民命之重則君之法君之
令亦凜凜然與天下共守矣故略其迹而
究其心雖謂四子能守法焉可也如韓非
子所云則雖謂四子越法焉亦可也方
今政令昭明紀法森布二百餘年無狂譎之夫
===
干誖之衆此成周之所以致刑措矣然慷
慨憤激之士一或不當少有詿誤即不免
焉是使尹鐸李牧難以成功而田叔明道
無以免咎也彼躬犯姦臧罪罹罔赦棄之
如豚鼠耳下不挂於吏議上得逭乎邦刑
兎脫網而雉罹羅謂法之無弊不可也愚
甞聞造父之御車矣或急其箠或舒其轡
急則下乗得齊舒則驥足易騁也是以二
十四蹄周旋進退莫不中節若其跛曳不
punctuated:
寇非法，卒以斃胡，何嫌於弱？故縱非法，上全太后，何嫌於擅？自用非法，補助民力，何嫌於專？向使鐸而無見於政教之脩，牧而無見於成功之偉，叔而無見於母子之倫，明道而無見於民命之重，則君之法、君之令，亦凜凜然與天下共守矣。故略其迹而究其心，雖謂四子能守法焉可也。如韓非子所云，則雖謂四子越法焉亦可也。
方今政令昭明，紀法森布，二百餘年無狂譎之夫、干誖之衆，此成周之所以致刑措矣。然慷慨憤激之士，一或不當，少有詿誤，即不免焉。是使尹鐸、李牧難以成功，而田叔、明道無以免咎也。彼躬犯姦臧，罪罹罔赦，棄之如豚鼠耳，下不挂於吏議，上得逭乎邦刑。兎脫網而雉罹羅，謂法之無弊不可也。
愚甞聞造父之御車矣，或急其箠，或舒其轡。急則下乗得齊，舒則驥足易騁也。是以二十四蹄，周旋進退，莫不中節。若其跛曳不
translation_en:
…[allowing] raiders to enter was unlawful, yet it ultimately brought about the destruction of the Hu: why suspect weakness? Deliberately letting offenders go was unlawful, yet it preserved the Empress Dowager’s standing: why suspect unauthorized action? Using funds at one’s own discretion was unlawful, yet it supplemented the people’s resources: why suspect arbitrary conduct? Had Yin Duo lacked insight into the cultivation of government and moral instruction, Li Mu into the greatness of the achievement to be secured, Tian Shu into the proper relationship between mother and son, and Mingdao into the weightiness of the people’s lives, they too would have stood in awe of their ruler’s laws and commands and observed them together with all under Heaven. Thus, if we set aside their outward actions and examine their intentions, we may indeed say that these four men knew how to uphold the law. Judged by what Han Feizi says, however, we may also say that these four men transgressed the law.
At present, governmental commands are clear and manifest, and regulations and laws stand in imposing array. For more than two hundred years there have been no reckless, deceitful men or rebellious multitudes. This is how the Zhou dynasty in its flourishing age reached the point where punishments could be laid aside. Yet men of ardent spirit and righteous indignation, if they act improperly in even one instance or incur the slightest error, cannot escape punishment. This makes it difficult for men like Yin Duo and Li Mu to achieve success, and leaves men like Tian Shu and Mingdao unable to avoid blame. As for those who themselves commit wrongdoing and corruption, incurring crimes beyond pardon, they deserve simply to be cast aside like pigs and rats. Yet below they do not become subject to official censure, and above they manage to evade the punishments of the state. The hare escapes the net while the pheasant is caught in the snare: one cannot say that the law is free of defects.
I have heard how Zaofu drove his chariot: at times he urged the horses on with his whip; at times he slackened his reins. By urging them on, he brought the inferior horses into line; by slackening the reins, he allowed the fine steeds to gallop freely. Thus all twenty-four hooves, whether wheeling, advancing, or retreating, invariably kept the proper rhythm. But if they limped and dragged, failing to…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
前馳驟先蹶則亦斥之焉耳又嘗聞匏巴
之鼓瑟矣或促其柱或疏其越促則清聲
易發疏則雅韻得成也是以二十四絃抑
揚高下莫不中律若沾懣不調宮商不應
則亦更之焉耳今慷慨有欯至之辜是雅
韻壞於促柱而逸足困於急箠也姦罪無
必然之罰是沾懣不廢於匏巴跛曳獲容
於造父也不相權矣昔
高皇帝立法制令破拘攣之見申畫一之條以
===
為整齊攝一之術因言而授事因事而責
功功當其事事當其言則賞功不當其事
事不當其言則誅其功然其事不然無寧
因事而廢功其事然其言不然無寧因言
而廢事行不測之賞藹然如雨露疏賤不
遺行不測之誅凜然如雷霆親貴莫逃也
倏寬倏嚴至通至正此
聖人之微權萬世不能易矣執事慨豪傑姦罔
兩不得平欲求救弊之方可無參伍於其
punctuated: 前，馳驟先蹶，則亦斥之焉耳。又嘗聞匏巴之鼓瑟矣：或促其柱，或疏其越；促則清聲易發，疏則雅韻得成也。是以二十四絃，抑揚高下，莫不中律。若沾懣不調，宮商不應，則亦更之焉耳。今慷慨有欯至之辜，是雅韻壞於促柱，而逸足困於急箠也；姦罪無必然之罰，是沾懣不廢於匏巴，跛曳獲容於造父也。不相權矣！昔高皇帝立法制令，破拘攣之見，申畫一之條，以為整齊攝一之術。因言而授事，因事而責功；功當其事，事當其言，則賞；功不當其事，事不當其言，則誅。其功然，其事不然，無寧因事而廢功；其事然，其言不然，無寧因言而廢事。行不測之賞，藹然如雨露，疏賤不遺；行不測之誅，凜然如雷霆，親貴莫逃也。倏寬倏嚴，至通至正，此聖人之微權，萬世不能易矣。執事慨豪傑、姦罔兩不得平，欲求救弊之方，可無參伍於其
translation_en:
…forward, and stumble as soon as they gallop, then they too are simply rejected. I have also heard of Pao Ba’s playing the se zither: sometimes he brought its bridges closer together, and sometimes he widened its sound apertures [?]. With closer spacing, clear notes readily issued; with wider spacing, refined harmonies could be achieved. Thus all twenty-four strings, rising and falling, high and low, accorded with the musical standards. If the sound was sluggish and muffled [?], out of tune, and the gong and shang notes failed to respond to one another, he would simply change it.

Now, when spirited men incur the guilt of “欯至” [?], this is like refined harmonies being spoiled by crowding the bridges, or a fleet horse being hampered by urgent whipping. When criminal wrongdoing carries no certain punishment, this is like Pao Ba failing to discard muffled, discordant sounds, or Zaofu tolerating lame, dragging horses. These measures are not properly balanced!

Formerly, Emperor Gao established laws and promulgated ordinances, breaking through constricted views and setting forth uniform provisions as a means of bringing order and unity. He assigned tasks according to a man’s words and demanded results according to his tasks. If the achievement matched the task and the task matched the words, he rewarded him; if the achievement did not match the task and the task did not match the words, he punished him. If the achievement was acceptable but the undertaking was not, he would rather disregard the achievement on account of the undertaking; if the undertaking was acceptable but the words were not, he would rather disregard the undertaking on account of the words. He bestowed rewards beyond expectation, gracious as rain and dew, overlooking neither the distant nor the lowly. He inflicted punishments beyond expectation, fearsome as thunder, from which neither his intimates nor the eminent could escape. Now lenient, now stern, utterly discerning and utterly just: such was the sage’s subtle weighing of circumstances, which cannot be altered in ten thousand generations.

You, sir, lament that neither outstanding men nor deceitful wrongdoers receive equitable treatment, and wish to find a remedy for these abuses. Can you dispense with comparing and examining the circumstances among…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
間哉天下人品大槩有三中亡論巳上卽
豪傑下卽姦罔二者聖世所宜盡心也廣
聰明責名實循參驗定低昻果皆當乎抑
不然乎豪傑信矣暴其心而賞之可也不
以一眚掩使後圖焉可也抑其銳姑困之
可也然而不能何也曰嚴也以爲是法之
正爾姦罔信矣褫其冠使不得與薦紳齒
可也屛而遠之可也戮而肆之可也然而
不能何也曰寛也以爲是法之通爾謂寛
===
非正弊也謂嚴非通弊也嚴或加於豪傑
寛或施於姦罔弊之弊也
國家立法制令之意必不然矣雖然豪傑易
知也而似是而非者難識也曰飲醇醪略
不事事慧辯高談猥自解脫非智也中情
脆怯奉頭而竄借言處女以誤敵人非謀
也撓清爲濁利在得魚滅迹爲姦自謂不
察非公也鶉衣糗食矯情似潔外假公名
內營私計非廉也此四者下之倖逃乎數
punctuated:
間哉？天下人品大槩有三，中亡論巳，上卽豪傑，下卽姦罔。二者，聖世所宜盡心也。廣聰明，責名實，循參驗，定低昻，果皆當乎？抑不然乎？豪傑信矣，暴其心而賞之可也，不以一眚掩，使後圖焉可也，抑其銳姑困之可也。然而不能，何也？曰嚴也，以爲是法之正爾。姦罔信矣，褫其冠，使不得與薦紳齒可也，屛而遠之可也，戮而肆之可也。然而不能，何也？曰寛也，以爲是法之通爾。謂寛非正，弊也；謂嚴非通，弊也。嚴或加於豪傑，寛或施於姦罔，弊之弊也。
國家立法制令之意必不然矣。雖然，豪傑易知也，而似是而非者難識也。曰飲醇醪，略不事事，慧辯高談，猥自解脫，非智也；中情脆怯，奉頭而竄，借言處女以誤敵人，非謀也；撓清爲濁，利在得魚，滅迹爲姦，自謂不察，非公也；鶉衣糗食，矯情似潔，外假公名，內營私計，非廉也。此四者，下之倖逃乎數
translation_en:
…among these possibilities? Broadly speaking, people in the world fall into three grades. Leaving the middle grade aside, those above are outstanding men, and those below are treacherous deceivers. Both deserve the fullest attention in an age of sage rule. Broaden what one hears and sees, hold reputations accountable to actual conduct, proceed through comparison and verification, and determine advancement or demotion: are all these judgments truly appropriate, or are they not? Once someone is confirmed to be an outstanding man, one may make his intentions manifest and reward him; one may refrain from letting a single fault obscure his merits and allow him to strive for future achievement; or one may curb his impetuosity and subject him to hardship for a time. Yet why are officials unable to do so? Because of severity: they suppose this alone constitutes the proper application of the law. Once someone is confirmed to be a treacherous deceiver, one may strip him of his official cap and deny him a place among the ranks of officials; one may expel and banish him; or one may execute him and expose his corpse. Yet why are officials unable to do so? Because of leniency: they suppose this alone constitutes the flexible application of the law. To say that leniency cannot be proper is an error; to say that severity cannot be flexible is an error. To impose severity upon outstanding men, or extend leniency to treacherous deceivers, is the worst error of all.
Surely this cannot be the state's intention in establishing laws and issuing ordinances. Nevertheless, outstanding men are easy to recognize, while those who seem worthy but are not are difficult to discern. Drinking strong wine and attending to virtually no business, then using clever arguments and lofty talk brazenly to excuse oneself—this is not wisdom. Being inwardly weak and timid, fleeing with one's hands over one's head, and invoking the claim that one appears like a maiden in order to deceive the enemy—this is not strategy. Stirring clear water until it is muddy for the advantage of catching fish, concealing one's tracks while practicing treachery, and imagining that one will escape detection—this is not impartiality. Wearing ragged clothes and eating dry grain, affecting purity through a false display, outwardly borrowing the name of public service while inwardly pursuing private schemes—this is not incorruptibility. Those who practice these four things may, at the lower end, luckily escape being counted among… [?]

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
罔之議上之謬托干豪傑之名所當審也
人主運遠照之明察近似之迹而以行至正至
通之法幾矣姦罔易知也而似非而是者
難識也是故以繕城郭不爲尹鐸美矣徐
考之城果高乎池果深乎兵卒盡城守乎
寇至不鳥獸遯乎以禦寇賊不爲李牧美
矣徐考之果能戰乎不畫城自保使自來
去乎不虔劉我赤子乎不飾虛功以邀爵
賞乎以治獄訟不爲田叔美矣徐考之不
===
朴擊賣請乎不勢奪乎人不故出入乎不
囊贖鍰爲己利乎文不增損爲己便乎以
司府庫不爲明道美矣徐考之不狗盜乎
出納不輕重乎不私竄抵乎此四者上之
不能與豪傑同功下之不得與姦罔同罪
旣逃乎法而反以令名終罪浮於顯戮者
也所當審也
人主運遠照之明察近似之迹而以行至正至
通之法幾矣抑愚又有說焉制令在君行
punctuated:
罔之議，上之謬托干豪傑之名，所當審也。人主運遠照之明，察近似之迹，而以行至正至通之法，幾矣。姦罔易知也，而似非而是者難識也。是故以繕城郭不爲尹鐸美矣，徐考之：城果高乎？池果深乎？兵卒盡城守乎？寇至不鳥獸遯乎？以禦寇賊不爲李牧美矣，徐考之：果能戰乎？不畫城自保，使自來去乎？不虔劉我赤子乎？不飾虛功以邀爵賞乎？以治獄訟不爲田叔美矣，徐考之：不朴擊賣請乎？不勢奪乎人？不故出入乎？不囊贖鍰爲己利乎？文不增損爲己便乎？以司府庫不爲明道美矣，徐考之：不狗盜乎？出納不輕重乎？不私竄抵乎？此四者，上之不能與豪傑同功，下之不得與姦罔同罪，旣逃乎法，而反以令名終，罪浮於顯戮者也，所當審也。人主運遠照之明，察近似之迹，而以行至正至通之法，幾矣。
抑愚又有說焉：制令在君，行
translation_en:
…the charge of deception; at the higher end, they falsely lay claim to the name of outstanding men. These are matters that require scrutiny. If the ruler exercises his far-reaching discernment, examines appearances that closely resemble the real thing, and thereby applies laws of utmost rectitude and adaptability, he will come close to the ideal.
Wickedness and deception are easy to recognize, but what seems wrong yet is right is difficult to discern. Thus, in repairing city walls, a man may not attain Yin Duo’s excellence. Examine him carefully: are the walls truly high? Is the moat truly deep? Do all the soldiers defend the walls? When bandits arrive, do they refrain from scattering like birds and beasts? In repelling bandits, a man may not attain Li Mu’s excellence. Examine him carefully: can he actually fight? Does he refrain from merely marking out a city for his own protection and letting the enemy come and go at will? Does he refrain from slaughtering our innocent people? Does he refrain from fabricating military achievements to seek ranks and rewards?
In handling criminal cases and lawsuits, a man may not attain Tian Shu’s excellence. Examine him carefully: does he refrain from beating people and selling favors to petitioners [?]? Does he refrain from using his power to seize things from others? Does he refrain from deliberately acquitting the guilty or convicting the innocent? Does he refrain from pocketing redemption fines for his own profit? Are documents left without additions or deletions made for his own convenience? In administering treasuries and storehouses, a man may not attain Mingdao’s excellence. Examine him carefully: does he refrain from furtive theft? Are receipts and disbursements free from manipulation of weights or amounts? Does he refrain from secretly altering accounts to offset shortages [?]?
These four kinds of men cannot, at the higher end, share the achievements of outstanding men; at the lower end, they cannot be assigned the same guilt as the wicked and deceitful. Having escaped the law, they instead end their days with a fine reputation, though their guilt exceeds that of men publicly executed. These are matters that require scrutiny. If the ruler exercises his far-reaching discernment, examines appearances that closely resemble the real thing, and thereby applies laws of utmost rectitude and adaptability, he will come close to the ideal.
Yet I, in my ignorance, have something further to say: issuing ordinances rests with the ruler; carrying them out…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
令在臣議法在君守法在臣法令之弊豈
法令之不善哉用之者或失其道也用法
令之吏宜何如其平若衡其明若鑑其仁
恕若徐有功其剛正若包孝肅其罪也果
麗于法耶則雖弄臣豪奴不得以私愛奪
而又何姦罔者之幸脫也其罪也果不當
抵法耶則雖犯蹕盜環不得以私怒加而
何豪傑者之濫及也若是則嚴用之而不
以爲苛寬用之而不以爲縱正用之而豪
===
傑不束於深文通用之而姦罔莫逃於法
外縱横闔闢無施不可而
祖宗之法雖萬世共守之可也又烏乎弊哉故
曰制而用之存乎法推而行之存乎人
第五問
余一愚
同考試官教諭朱 批 查米練客兵不可驟遣此議
極中時宜至論簡練二法尤鑿鑿可裨實用非拘方之士也
同考試官教諭李 批 論時事者不激即泛是篇言
punctuated:
令在臣，議法在君，守法在臣。法令之弊，豈法令之不善哉？用之者或失其道也。用法令之吏宜何如？其平若衡，其明若鑑，其仁恕若徐有功，其剛正若包孝肅。其罪也果麗于法耶？則雖弄臣豪奴，不得以私愛奪，而又何姦罔者之幸脫也？其罪也果不當抵法耶？則雖犯蹕盜環，不得以私怒加，而何豪傑者之濫及也？若是，則嚴用之而不以爲苛，寬用之而不以爲縱，正用之而豪傑不束於深文，通用之而姦罔莫逃於法外，縱横闔闢，無施不可，而祖宗之法雖萬世共守之可也，又烏乎弊哉？故曰：「制而用之存乎法，推而行之存乎人。」

第五問
余一愚

同考試官教諭朱批：查米練客兵不可驟遣，此議極中時宜。至論簡練二法，尤鑿鑿可裨實用，非拘方之士也。

同考試官教諭李批：論時事者不激即泛，是篇言
translation_en:
…carrying out ordinances rests with ministers; deliberating upon laws rests with the ruler, and observing them rests with ministers. Are abuses in laws and ordinances really due to their being unsound? Those who apply them sometimes depart from the proper way. What should officials who apply laws and ordinances be like? As impartial as a balance, as discerning as a mirror, as humane and forgiving as Xu Yougong, and as firm and upright as Bao Xiaosu. Does an offense truly fall under the law? Then even for court favorites or overbearing servants, private affection must not override it. How, then, could deceitful lawbreakers escape through good fortune? Does an offense truly not warrant punishment under the law? Then even for someone who violates the restrictions surrounding the imperial procession or steals a ring, private anger must not increase the penalty. How, then, could outstanding men be indiscriminately implicated? In this way, strict application will not be deemed harsh, and lenient application will not be deemed indulgent. With correct application, outstanding men will not be fettered by strained interpretations of the statutes; with adaptable application, deceitful lawbreakers will find no escape beyond the law. Whether extending or restricting, opening or closing, every application will be appropriate. The laws of the imperial ancestors could then be observed by all for ten thousand generations. What abuses could there be? Thus it is said: “Establishing institutions and putting them to use depends on laws; extending them and carrying them into effect depends on people.”

Fifth Question
Yu Yiyu

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: The discussion of checking grain supplies and training troops from outside the province [?], and the argument that these troops must not be abruptly sent away, are most appropriate to present circumstances. His discussion of the two methods of selection and training is particularly concrete and could assist practical implementation. He is no scholar bound by fixed formulas.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Those who discuss current affairs are either intemperate or vague. The language of this essay…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
辭剴切經畫老成可式
考試官敎授夏批條答詳明
考試官敎授帥批此必熟知時務者
執事策諸生而終及練兵之計蓋欲攘寇
安民爲閩中遠慮甚盛心也顧豎儒非夙
諳武備其何以攄一得復明問試卽所聞
于故老者陳之夫八閩之地昔稱海濱鄒
魯以士人喜談詩書而不言兵也粵考形
勢則延建邵汀阻山依谷福興泉漳帶海
===
襟江故
國初都司衞所郡縣相錯並設而於銅山浯
嶼南日小埕諸要害處水寨星列墩堠鱗
次非以外接島夷內聯峒箐故爲計特周
且悉耶承平旣久法度漸弛頃歲一二猾
寇弄兵潢池黠夷乘之擣虛深入甲腐而
不可張兵鈍而不足試束手待斃嗟乎戚
矣當事者慘目戒心權宜拯解策先募兵
此猶驟病之夫危在旦夕顧視其家乃無
punctuated:
辭剴切，經畫老成，可式。
考試官敎授夏批：條答詳明。
考試官敎授帥批：此必熟知時務者。
執事策諸生，而終及練兵之計，蓋欲攘寇安民，爲閩中遠慮，甚盛心也。顧豎儒非夙諳武備，其何以攄一得，復明問？試卽所聞于故老者陳之。夫八閩之地，昔稱海濱鄒魯，以士人喜談詩書而不言兵也。粵考形勢，則延建邵汀阻山依谷，福興泉漳帶海襟江。故國初都司衞所郡縣相錯並設，而於銅山浯嶼南日小埕諸要害處，水寨星列，墩堠鱗次，非以外接島夷，內聯峒箐，故爲計特周且悉耶？承平旣久，法度漸弛。頃歲一二猾寇弄兵潢池，黠夷乘之，擣虛深入。甲腐而不可張，兵鈍而不足試，束手待斃。嗟乎，戚矣！當事者慘目戒心，權宜拯解，策先募兵。此猶驟病之夫，危在旦夕，顧視其家，乃無
translation_en:
…its language is incisive and pertinent, and its planning mature and seasoned: it can serve as a model.
Examiner Xia, Prefectural School Instructor, comments: The answers to the individual points are detailed and clear.
Examiner Shuai, Prefectural School Instructor, comments: This must be someone thoroughly familiar with current affairs.
You, honored officials, have questioned the candidates and concluded by addressing plans for training troops. Surely you wish to repel bandits and bring peace to the people, taking thought for Fujian’s long-term welfare. Yours is a most generous concern. Yet I, a mere bookish scholar, have no longstanding familiarity with military preparations. How can I set forth even one useful insight in answer to your discerning question? Let me present what I have heard from the elders. The land of the Eight Min was formerly called the Zou and Lu of the seacoast, because its scholars delighted in discussing the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents rather than military matters. Examining its terrain, we find that Yanping, Jianning, Shaowu, and Tingzhou are protected by mountains and lie along valleys, while Fuzhou, Xinghua, Quanzhou, and Zhangzhou border the sea and embrace rivers. Thus, at the founding of the dynasty, Regional Military Commissions, guards, and battalions were established interspersed with prefectures and counties. At strategic places such as Tongshan, Wuyu, Nanri, and Xiaocheng, naval stockades were scattered like stars, and watchtowers stood in close succession like scales. Was this not because the region faced island barbarians abroad and adjoined mountain caves and bamboo thickets inland, requiring exceptionally comprehensive and thorough planning? After prolonged peace, laws and institutions gradually grew lax. In recent years, a few cunning bandits took up arms like rebels in a mere stagnant pool; crafty barbarians seized the opportunity to strike at undefended places and penetrate deep inland. Armor had rotted and could no longer be put on; weapons were blunt and unfit for use. With hands tied, people awaited death. Alas, how grievous! Those responsible, appalled by what they saw and alarmed at heart, resorted to expedients to bring relief, making troop recruitment their first measure. This was like a man suddenly stricken with illness, his life hanging in the balance, who looks about his household only to find that it has no…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
宿艾汲汲然裹糧求巳于秦越人計也是
時攘臂先登摧鋒陷敵東支西吾不至大
壞皆客兵力耳然購募必重犒賚必厚鎧
仗必給需求必煩驛遞必擾亦勢之不得
不然者昔李泌謂兵不土著又無宗族不
自顧惜客兵其可久哉而建議者遂持練
土兵之計以爲募兵當在昔日練兵當在
今日夫病勢亟而利用召醫勢稍緩而利
在蓄艾亦計也然土兵非始于今日也自
===
成周時而此制已權輿矣成周之制居則
爲比閭族黨州鄉之民行則爲伍兩卒旅
軍師之衆夫其居也乃所以爲農而其出
也卽所以爲兵是農亦兵而兵亦農也非
卽土兵之意乎始壞於齊之內政家一人
繼壞於晉之州兵家五人而後兵農異途
耕戰殊業矣漢制材官騎士皆家人子起
田中者爲之雖未必盡合於周官而亦用
農爲兵之遺也漢世所以威行八埏鞭撻
punctuated:
宿艾，汲汲然裹糧求巳于秦越人，計也。是時攘臂先登，摧鋒陷敵，東支西吾，不至大壞，皆客兵力耳。然購募必重，犒賚必厚，鎧仗必給，需求必煩，驛遞必擾，亦勢之不得不然者。昔李泌謂兵不土著，又無宗族，不自顧惜。客兵其可久哉？而建議者遂持練土兵之計，以爲募兵當在昔日，練兵當在今日。夫病勢亟而利用召醫，勢稍緩而利在蓄艾，亦計也。然土兵非始于今日也，自成周時而此制已權輿矣。
成周之制，居則爲比閭族黨州鄉之民，行則爲伍兩卒旅軍師之衆。夫其居也，乃所以爲農；而其出也，卽所以爲兵。是農亦兵，而兵亦農也，非卽土兵之意乎？始壞於齊之內政家一人，繼壞於晉之州兵家五人，而後兵農異途，耕戰殊業矣。漢制材官騎士，皆家人子起田中者爲之，雖未必盡合於周官，而亦用農爲兵之遺也。漢世所以威行八埏，鞭撻
translation_en:
…aged moxa, and hastily packing provisions to seek a cure [?] from Qin Yueren: this, too, was a practical expedient. At that time, those who bared their arms and led the assault, broke the enemy’s vanguard and penetrated his ranks, and held the line here and there [?], preventing utter collapse, accomplished this entirely through the strength of troops recruited from elsewhere. Yet recruitment necessarily required substantial payments, rewards had to be generous, armor and weapons had to be supplied, requisitions inevitably became burdensome, and the postal relay service inevitably suffered disruption. These, too, were unavoidable consequences of the circumstances. Li Mi once said that soldiers who were not locally rooted and had no kin groups nearby did not take care to preserve their own lives. Could reliance on troops from elsewhere endure? Those making proposals therefore advocated training local troops, arguing that recruiting troops had been appropriate earlier, while training them was appropriate now. When an illness is critical, it is advantageous to summon a physician; when its severity has somewhat abated, the advantage lies in storing moxa. This, too, is a practical expedient. Yet local troops did not originate today: this institution had already begun in the time of the established Zhou dynasty.
Under the Zhou system, at home the people belonged to the residential groupings of bi, lü, zu, dang, zhou, and xiang; on campaign they formed the military units of wu, liang, zu, lü, jun, and shi. Their organization at home enabled them to farm, while their mobilization enabled them to serve as soldiers. Thus farmers were also soldiers, and soldiers also farmers. Was this not precisely the principle of local troops? The system first deteriorated under Qi’s domestic arrangements, which took one man from each household, and deteriorated further under Jin’s system of regional troops, which took five men from each household [?]. Thereafter soldiers and farmers followed separate paths, and cultivation and warfare became distinct occupations. Under the Han system, the infantry and cavalry were all sons of ordinary households drawn from the fields. Although this did not necessarily accord in every respect with the Offices of Zhou, it nevertheless preserved something of the practice of employing farmers as soldiers. This was how, in Han times, imperial might reached the eight bounds of the earth and scourged…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
四夷與唐李抱眞守懷州三丁籍一蠲其
徭役給以弓矢官無廩餼各精技射名曰
澤潞步兵而勇敢爲諸道最李德裕守西
川率戶二百取一緩則農急則戰名曰雄
邊子弟而南詔不敢犯塞悉怛謀降他若
晉齊王之武定軍宋慶曆之保毅軍宣毅
軍景德之廣銳軍治平之義勇軍此皆兵
之出於民而隸之州縣者也非土兵績効
章章耶夫土兵所以勝於客兵者非謂其
===
智勇獨先而技藝獨精也亦非謂其轉餉
較易而鈔掠較省也以其有父兄室家之
念祖宗丘隴之思其心固較客兵異也凡
用兵者用其心耳驅土人以禦寇是俾之
自衛家室自樊丘隴心固戀戀向也夫昏
夜貯物於衢以他人守卽股枕臥矣守以
主者則盻盻然中宵張睫焉何者心之繫
與否也此非土客二兵大辨耶土兵之在
今日有三曰保甲曰弓兵曰機兵保甲之
punctuated:
四夷，與唐李抱眞守懷州，三丁籍一，蠲其徭役，給以弓矢，官無廩餼，各精技射，名曰澤潞步兵，而勇敢爲諸道最。李德裕守西川，率戶二百取一，緩則農，急則戰，名曰雄邊子弟，而南詔不敢犯塞，悉怛謀降。他若晉齊王之武定軍，宋慶曆之保毅軍、宣毅軍，景德之廣銳軍，治平之義勇軍，此皆兵之出於民而隸之州縣者也，非土兵績効章章耶？
夫土兵所以勝於客兵者，非謂其智勇獨先而技藝獨精也，亦非謂其轉餉較易而鈔掠較省也。以其有父兄室家之念，祖宗丘隴之思，其心固較客兵異也。凡用兵者，用其心耳。驅土人以禦寇，是俾之自衛家室，自樊丘隴，心固戀戀。向也，夫昏夜貯物於衢，以他人守，卽股枕臥矣；守以主者，則盻盻然中宵張睫焉。何者？心之繫與否也。此非土客二兵大辨耶？土兵之在今日有三：曰保甲，曰弓兵，曰機兵。保甲之
translation_en:
…the barbarians of the four quarters. And when Li Baozhen of the Tang governed Huaizhou, he enrolled one man out of every three adult males, exempted them from corvée service, and supplied them with bows and arrows. The government provided no grain allowances; each became proficient in archery. Called the Zelu Infantry, they surpassed the troops of all other circuits in courage. When Li Deyu governed Xichuan, he took one man from every two hundred households. In quiet times they farmed; in emergencies they fought. They were called the Stalwart Frontier Sons, and Nanzhao dared not violate the frontier, while Xi Damou surrendered. Other examples include the Wuding Army of the Prince of Qi of the Jin, the Baoyi and Xuanyi armies of the Song’s Qingli era, the Guangrui Army of the Jingde era, and the Yiyong Army of the Zhiping era. These were all troops drawn from the common people and placed under prefectural and county jurisdiction. Are these not conspicuous demonstrations of the achievements of local troops?
The superiority of local troops over troops brought in from elsewhere does not mean that they alone excel in intelligence and courage or possess exceptional martial skills. Nor does it mean merely that their provisions are easier to transport or that they commit less plunder. Rather, they care for their fathers, elder brothers, wives, and families, and cherish the graves of their ancestors. Their disposition is therefore inherently different from that of troops brought in from elsewhere. Employing soldiers is simply a matter of engaging their hearts. To mobilize local men to resist raiders is to have them defend their own households and protect their own ancestral graves: their hearts are firmly attached to these. Suppose goods were left in a thoroughfare at night. If someone else were set to guard them, he would lie down with his head pillowed on his thigh; if their owner guarded them, he would remain watchful, his eyes wide open through the night. Why? It is a matter of whether his heart is engaged. Is this not the great distinction between local troops and troops brought in from elsewhere? Today there are three kinds of local troops: the baojia mutual-responsibility militia, archer troops, and mobile troops. As for the baojia…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
法歲檄有司編什伍置尺籍脩鉏挺止矣
保甲其可恃乎弓兵額數旣單近復裁減
供追呼走鄉聚逐鷄豚止矣弓兵其可使
乎機兵時有調發常自負爲公家出力守
令閱視則擐甲而趨持干而倚羣呼迭鬨
若將爲戲止矣緩急其可賴乎若此者皆
羸夫弱子朽甲斷戟聰明不足赴旗皷强
銳不足犯死傷見敵卽望風走當事者以
爲脆弱宜也然往歲寇在吳閩人旣爲兵
===
於吳已而寇在越閩人又爲兵於越繼寇
在閩則閩人不自兵而吳越人反爲兵於
閩豈閩人强於吳越而獨弱於桑梓里哉
無以練之故也夫土兵未練而遽曰客兵
可去一旦寇起倉卒何以應之所謂見兎
而顧犬臣竊懼其晚也故爲今之計莫若
預練土兵而練之之法有三一曰定經制
二曰嚴教習三曰明賞罰此皆今日之不
可不講者夫兵制不定則衆寡不均兵籍
punctuated:
法，歲檄有司編什伍，置尺籍，脩鉏挺，止矣。保甲其可恃乎？弓兵額數旣單，近復裁減，供追呼，走鄉聚，逐鷄豚，止矣。弓兵其可使乎？機兵時有調發，常自負爲公家出力。守令閱視，則擐甲而趨，持干而倚，羣呼迭鬨，若將爲戲，止矣。緩急其可賴乎？若此者，皆羸夫弱子，朽甲斷戟，聰明不足赴旗皷，强銳不足犯死傷，見敵卽望風走。當事者以爲脆弱，宜也。然往歲寇在吳，閩人旣爲兵於吳；已而寇在越，閩人又爲兵於越；繼寇在閩，則閩人不自兵，而吳越人反爲兵於閩。豈閩人强於吳越，而獨弱於桑梓里哉？無以練之故也。
夫土兵未練，而遽曰客兵可去，一旦寇起倉卒，何以應之？所謂見兎而顧犬，臣竊懼其晚也。故爲今之計，莫若預練土兵，而練之之法有三：一曰定經制，二曰嚴教習，三曰明賞罰。此皆今日之不可不講者。夫兵制不定，則衆寡不均；兵籍
translation_en:
…the procedure amounts merely to sending annual written orders to the responsible officials to organize households into groups of ten and five, establish military registers, and put hoes and clubs in repair. Can the baojia household militia be relied upon? The authorized complement of archer constables was already small and has recently been reduced further. They merely serve to pursue and summon people, run about the villages, and chase chickens and pigs. Can these archer constables be put to use? The local militia troops known as jibing are occasionally mobilized and constantly pride themselves on exerting themselves for the government. When prefects and magistrates inspect them, they hurry forward wearing armor, then stand leaning on their shields, shouting together and raising successive uproars, as though merely putting on a game. Can they be depended upon in an emergency? Such men are all frail fellows and weak youths, with rotting armor and broken halberds. Their hearing and sight are not keen enough to respond to flags and drums, nor are their strength and courage sufficient to brave death and injury. At the sight of the enemy they flee before the onslaught. It is understandable that those in charge consider them weak. Yet in former years, when raiders were in Wu, men of Min served as soldiers in Wu; later, when raiders were in Yue, men of Min again served as soldiers in Yue. Subsequently, when raiders were in Min, the men of Min did not themselves take up arms, while men of Wu and Yue instead served as soldiers in Min. Could men of Min be strong in Wu and Yue, yet weak only in their native villages? The reason is that no means have been provided to train them.
If local troops have not yet been trained, but one abruptly declares that troops recruited from elsewhere can be dismissed, how will we respond when raiders suddenly rise? This is what is called looking back for the hound only after seeing the hare; your servant fears that it will be too late. Thus the best course now is to train local troops in advance. There are three methods for training them: first, establish a regular military organization; second, enforce rigorous instruction and drill; third, make rewards and punishments clear. All these are matters that must be addressed today. If military organization is not fixed, troop strengths will be uneven; if the military registers…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
不覈則强弱不分操練之術安從施耶今
宜倣新
題事例查照弘治年間舊規大縣該兵幾何
中縣該兵幾何悉復前額嚴加挑選老者
遣之弱者汰之虛者補之冒者正之影射
必稽占役必禁逋逃必復部隊必全版築
迎送勿以干預文吏詰查不得漁擾規畫
周而後練習可加故曰經制之不可不定
者此也兵家之法超忽變化目駭耳廻苟
===
非素閑臨敵必亂今宜於戈矛之用礮石
之制决拾之方營陣之規具有成法者購
募良師以一教十以十教百其執技也長
短步騎靡用弗適其成列也縱橫首尾隨
變輒應技藝既精膽氣自壯聞敵而躍然
思赴見敵而羣然爭前矣故曰教習之不
可不嚴者此也夫鋒鏑注目而士弗却矢
鏃貫顱而兵不動者賞罰素明耳練習之
時號令不明賞不信罰不必則驅之臨陣
punctuated:
不覈，則强弱不分，操練之術安從施耶？今宜倣新題事例，查照弘治年間舊規，大縣該兵幾何，中縣該兵幾何，悉復前額，嚴加挑選：老者遣之，弱者汰之，虛者補之，冒者正之。影射必稽，占役必禁，逋逃必復，部隊必全。版築迎送，勿以干預；文吏詰查，不得漁擾。規畫周而後練習可加，故曰經制之不可不定者，此也。
兵家之法，超忽變化，目駭耳廻。苟非素閑，臨敵必亂。今宜於戈矛之用、礮石之制、决拾之方、營陣之規，具有成法者，購募良師，以一教十，以十教百。其執技也，長短步騎，靡用弗適；其成列也，縱橫首尾，隨變輒應。技藝既精，膽氣自壯，聞敵而躍然思赴，見敵而羣然爭前矣。故曰教習之不可不嚴者，此也。
夫鋒鏑注目而士弗却，矢鏃貫顱而兵不動者，賞罰素明耳。練習之時，號令不明，賞不信，罰不必，則驅之臨陣
translation_en:
…are not scrutinized, the strong and weak cannot be distinguished; how, then, can methods of military drill be applied? We should now follow the recently memorialized precedents and consult the old regulations of the Hongzhi reign: how many soldiers a large county must supply, and how many a medium-sized county must supply. All former quotas should be restored, and selection made rigorous: discharge the old, weed out the weak, fill vacant places, and rectify fraudulent registrations. Evasion through nominal affiliation must be investigated; appropriation of soldiers for private service must be prohibited; deserters must be brought back; and units must be kept at full strength. Construction labor and duties of welcoming and escorting officials must not interfere with training. Civil officials conducting inspections must not extort from or harass the soldiers. Only once arrangements are comprehensive can training be undertaken. This is why the military establishment must be put on a definite footing.
Military methods change with bewildering speed, startling the eyes and confusing the ears. Unless soldiers are thoroughly accustomed to them beforehand, they will inevitably fall into confusion when confronting the enemy. We should now recruit skilled instructors in all matters for which established methods exist: the use of dagger-axes and spears, the handling of cannon and stone projectiles, archery techniques using thumb rings and armguards, and the rules of encampment and battle formation. Let one teach ten, and ten teach a hundred. In exercising their skills, whether with long or short weapons, on foot or on horseback, they should be proficient in every application. When forming ranks, whether lengthwise or across, at the front or rear, they should respond immediately to every change. Once their skills are perfected, their courage will naturally grow. On hearing of the enemy, they will eagerly wish to engage; on seeing the enemy, they will vie with one another to advance. This is why instruction and practice must be rigorous.
When blades and arrowheads threaten their eyes yet the men do not retreat, and arrowheads pierce skulls yet the troops remain unshaken, it is simply because rewards and punishments have long been clearly established. If, during training, commands are unclear, rewards unreliable, and punishments uncertain, then when the men are driven into battle…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
必不前矣此孫武所以加刑於莊賈也今
宜重之以將領之職假之以便宜之權愆
期後至必刑踰行越伍必刑旌旗金鼓不
如敎必刑坐作進退不如法必刑其若于
訓者什伯之長以次遞進且有厚賚由是
而率以赴敵則人知進有殊賞退有嚴誅
孰不捐軀以自効哉故曰賞罰之不可不
明者此也三者旣舉而又責成於有司守
令以此爲盡職臺臣以此爲殿最則挾鼎
===
超距之人出攕蛟射鵰之技進而人咸奮
武隊咸稱强矣夫一人敎成然後客兵可
去一人也一隊敎成然後客兵可去一隊
也旋敎旋去不二三年而客兵可以盡遣
客兵之餉可以盡蠲蓋以機兵而代客兵
以軍餉而爲工食正相乘矣况所省又不
訾乎不然艾不素蓄遠方之醫終不可謝
卽使儲金若丘積粟如山江河之大其能
當漏卮哉故議兵者率以是爲憂於是有
punctuated:
必不前矣。此孫武所以加刑於莊賈也。今宜重之以將領之職，假之以便宜之權。愆期後至必刑，踰行越伍必刑，旌旗金鼓不如敎必刑，坐作進退不如法必刑。其若于訓者，什伯之長以次遞進，且有厚賚。由是而率以赴敵，則人知進有殊賞，退有嚴誅，孰不捐軀以自効哉？故曰賞罰之不可不明者，此也。三者旣舉，而又責成於有司，守令以此爲盡職，臺臣以此爲殿最，則挾鼎超距之人出，攕蛟射鵰之技進，而人咸奮武，隊咸稱强矣。
夫一人敎成，然後客兵可去一人也；一隊敎成，然後客兵可去一隊也。旋敎旋去，不二三年，而客兵可以盡遣，客兵之餉可以盡蠲。蓋以機兵而代客兵，以軍餉而爲工食，正相乘矣，况所省又不訾乎？不然，艾不素蓄，遠方之醫終不可謝。卽使儲金若丘，積粟如山，江河之大，其能當漏卮哉？故議兵者率以是爲憂，於是有
translation_en:
…they will certainly fail to advance. This is why Sun Wu inflicted punishment upon Zhuang Jia [?: the episode conventionally concerns Sima Rangju]. Now commanders should be invested with the weight of military office and granted authority to act as circumstances require. Those who miss the appointed time and arrive late must be punished; those who stray from their ranks and files must be punished; those who fail to follow instructions conveyed by banners, gongs, and drums must be punished; and those whose sitting, rising, advancing, and retreating do not conform to regulations must be punished. Those who obey instructions [?] should be advanced successively through the posts of leaders of tens and hundreds, and also receive generous rewards. If they are then led against the enemy, everyone will know that advancing brings exceptional rewards and retreating brings severe punishment. Who would not risk his life to render service? This is what is meant by saying that rewards and punishments must be clearly established. Once these three measures have been implemented, responsibility for their success must also be assigned to the officials concerned. Prefects and magistrates should regard this as the fulfillment of their duties, and censorial officials should use it to assess their performance as inferior or superior. Then men capable of lifting tripods and leaping great distances will emerge, skills in striking down dragons [?] and shooting eagles will develop, every man will display martial prowess, and every unit will be acclaimed as strong.
Only after one man has been fully trained can one soldier brought in from elsewhere be dismissed; only after one unit has been fully trained can one such unit be dismissed. As training proceeds, dismissals can follow. Within two or three years, all the outside troops can be sent away, and the levies for their provisions can be entirely remitted. Local defense soldiers would replace outside troops, and military provisioning funds would become wages: the one would precisely serve the purposes of the other. How much more compelling, then, are the immeasurable savings! Otherwise, if moxa has not been stored beforehand, the physician from afar can never be dispensed with. Even if gold were stored in mounds and grain piled into mountains, could resources as vast as rivers withstand a leaking cup? Thus those who discuss military affairs generally regard this as a source of concern, and consequently there have arisen…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
閒田之論寺租之說夫全閩升斗之地盡
入版圖無復閒田可供召募而寺租雖多
悉充軍餉又安有奇贏給土兵哉二說蓋
不可行也宋咸平中王元之言於朝曰福
建等郡酌民户衆寡城池大小並許置本
城守捉軍士習弓劔葺城壘夫抽取于民
非土兵邪元之欲行之於宋顧不可行之
於今邪抑有說焉曩者寇犯閩境其爲嚮
導而來者多土人也蓋遊手之徒囂然好
===
逞中有魁黠者起而倡之往往相率從亂
大抵寇盜最可慮者其中有魁黠也魁黠
在中未易卒制周亞夫征吳楚急索劇孟
誠慮之也乃今用土兵則草萊之魁黠具
可籠取束縛之而銷亡外寇之術固寓焉
此又練兵之一益也雖然謀國之要不在
立法而在得人守懷州者得一抱真焉則
澤潞孱丁皆爲勇敢矣守西川者得一德
裕焉則劔南子弟可以雄邊矣故愚之所
punctuated:
閒田之論、寺租之說。夫全閩升斗之地盡入版圖，無復閒田可供召募；而寺租雖多，悉充軍餉，又安有奇贏給土兵哉？二說蓋不可行也。宋咸平中，王元之言於朝曰：「福建等郡，酌民户衆寡、城池大小，並許置本城守捉軍士，習弓劔，葺城壘。」夫抽取于民，非土兵邪？元之欲行之於宋，顧不可行之於今邪？

抑有說焉。曩者寇犯閩境，其爲嚮導而來者，多土人也。蓋遊手之徒，囂然好逞，中有魁黠者起而倡之，往往相率從亂。大抵寇盜最可慮者，其中有魁黠也。魁黠在中，未易卒制。周亞夫征吳楚，急索劇孟，誠慮之也。乃今用土兵，則草萊之魁黠具可籠取，束縛之，而銷亡外寇之術固寓焉。此又練兵之一益也。

雖然，謀國之要，不在立法，而在得人。守懷州者，得一抱真焉，則澤潞孱丁皆爲勇敢矣；守西川者，得一德裕焉，則劔南子弟可以雄邊矣。故愚之所
translation_en:
…proposals concerning idle land and suggestions concerning rents from Buddhist monasteries. Yet throughout Fujian, every tiny parcel of land is already entered in the territorial registers; no idle land remains available to support recruitment. And although monastery rents are substantial, they are entirely devoted to military pay: how could there be any surplus to provide for local troops? Neither proposal, then, is practicable. During the Xianping reign of the Song, Wang Yuanzhi told the court: “The prefectures of Fujian and elsewhere should all be permitted, according to the number of civilian households and the size of their walled cities, to establish troops to guard their own cities, train in archery and swordsmanship, and repair the walls and fortifications.” Men levied from the populace—are these not local troops? Yuanzhi wished to implement this under the Song; could it really not be implemented today?

There is also another consideration. Previously, when raiders invaded Fujian, many of those who came as their guides were local people. Idle fellows are boisterous and eager to assert themselves; when cunning ringleaders arise among them and take the lead, they often follow one another into rebellion. Generally, the most troubling thing about raiders and bandits is the presence of such ringleaders among them. With these men in their midst, they cannot easily be subdued at short notice. When Zhou Yafu campaigned against Wu and Chu, he urgently sought out Ju Meng precisely out of this concern. If local troops are now employed, the cunning leaders among the common people can all be drawn in and placed under restraint; a means of eliminating raiders from outside is thus inherent in this policy. This is another benefit of training troops.

Nevertheless, the essential task in planning for the state lies in securing the right men, rather than in establishing regulations. Obtain a Baozhen to defend Huaizhou, and even the weak men of Ze and Lu will all become brave fighters; obtain a Deyu to defend Xichuan, and the young men of Jiannan can make the frontier strong. Thus, what I, in my humble judgment…

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
陳者皆自其救偏補弊者言之而究其本
則固存乎其人耳子朱子有言曰聖王制
禦夷狄之道其具不在兵食而在綱紀愚
則曰今日整飭八閩之方其具不在兵食
而在守令執事以爲何如
punctuated: 陳者，皆自其救偏補弊者言之，而究其本，則固存乎其人耳。子朱子有言曰：「聖王制禦夷狄之道，其具不在兵食，而在綱紀。」愚則曰：「今日整飭八閩之方，其具不在兵食，而在守令。」執事以爲何如？
translation_en: …what I have set forth has all been concerned with correcting imbalances and remedying abuses; yet, on examining the root of the matter, it surely rests with the men entrusted with the task. Master Zhu Xi once said: “In the sage kings’ way of controlling the Yi and Di peoples, the essential means lay not in troops and provisions, but in the governing order.” I would humbly say: “In putting the Eight Min regions of Fujian in order today, the essential means lie not in troops and provisions, but in prefects and district magistrates.” What is your judgment, honored examiners?

title: 隆慶四年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄後序
隆慶庚午秋福建當賓興御
史蒙詔申飭規條視昔益虔
益密事竣大勳不佞從諸執
事後例得敘諸末簡竊謂賢
哲之生受才於天鍾氣於地
而應用於
===
君天運會則昌地形靈則傑而
君道盛則得以竟其所施此古今
大較也八閩古揚州域吻海
派江孤峯危嶽秀美甲天下
逸氣所鍾豈獨鹽鐵金沙素
馨長竹已哉其間洪猷偉器
後先繼鳴或慷慨憂時孤直
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄後序

隆慶庚午秋，福建當賓興，御史蒙詔申飭規條，視昔益虔益密。事竣，大勳不佞從諸執事後，例得敘諸末簡。竊謂賢哲之生，受才於天，鍾氣於地，而應用於君。天運會則昌，地形靈則傑，而君道盛則得以竟其所施，此古今大較也。八閩古揚州域，吻海派江，孤峯危嶽，秀美甲天下。逸氣所鍾，豈獨鹽鐵金沙、素馨長竹已哉？其間洪猷偉器，後先繼鳴，或慷慨憂時，孤直
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination
